body.text: ācāryakamalaśīlaviracitayā
body.translated_text: Composed by <s>Ācārya Kamalaśīla</s>

body.text:
āryaprajñāpāramitāyā vajracchedikāyā
vistṛtaṭīkayā sahitam
body.translated_text: The <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā Vajracchedikā</s> (Noble Perfection of Wisdom, the Diamond Cutter), accompanied by the extensive commentary (<s>vistṛtaṭīkā</s>)

body.text: namo mañcuśriye kumārabhūtāya
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful one (<s>kumārabhūta</s>).

body.text: maṅgalācaraṇam
body.translated_text: Auspicious invocation (<s>maṅgalācaraṇam</s>).

children.text: kāyaḥ prasiddhaḥ paridṛśyamāno janeṣu sarveṣu sphuṭaṃ tathāpi |
children.translated_text: The body (<s>kāya</s>), well-known and clearly seen among all people, yet

children.text: svabhāvato vastutayā na prāpto nidarśitaḥ so 'pi ca prāptihetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: not attained in reality by its own nature — even that has been shown to be the cause of attainment. //

children.text: phalasya śreṣṭhasya ca nityabhūtaparamasya cāgryasya jinaiḥ samastaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Of the most excellent fruit, eternal, supreme, and foremost, [as taught] by all the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones),
therefore I constantly pay homage with my heart to her — the mother of all <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times. // 1 //

children.text: alpīyasābhyāsabalena yasyāḥ, mahānti puṇyāni hi sañcinoti |
children.translated_text: By the power of even a little practice of her, one accumulates great merits,

children.text: utkhātamūlāni ca pāpakāni, sarvāṇi cāpādayati kṣaṇena ||
children.translated_text: and sins are uprooted at their very root, and all [attainments] are accomplished in an instant.
Therefore, for the purpose of long contemplation of her, I shall teach the path according to my own ability,
as instructed by the <s>guru</s> (teacher), well-examined, following my own understanding. // 2 //

body.text: tatrādau sūtraṃ vyācikhyāsuḥ sādhyavasāya (viṣaya-) grahaṇādau śrotṝṇāmavatāraṇārthaṃ prayojanamāha | na hi prayojanamantareṇa prekṣāvān kvacit pravartate | tadanantaraṃ prayojanopāyamupadarśayitumabhidheyastāvad vakṣyate, (yato hi) abhidheyarahitaṃ sūtraṃ daśadāḍimānītyādivākyavanneṣṭaprayojanaṃ sādhayati | tataḥ saukaryeṇa tadabhidheyagrahaṇārthaṃ piṇḍārtho vakṣyate |
body.translated_text: Here, at the outset, wishing to explain the <s>sūtra</s>, he states the purpose — for the sake of introducing the listeners through grasping the topic at the beginning. For no wise person engages in anything without a purpose. Next, to show the means to that purpose, the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) will first be stated; for a <s>sūtra</s> devoid of subject matter, like the sentence 'ten pomegranates,' does not accomplish the desired purpose. Then, for ease in grasping that subject matter, the summary meaning (<s>piṇḍārtha</s>) will be stated.

body.text: tadanantaraṃ samāsārthapratipattaye padārtho 'bhidhāsyate | tataḥ kramasyāvirodhaṃ nidarśayituṃ padānāmanusandhirdarśayiṣyate | tadanantaraṃ pūrvāparayuktivirodhāpanodanāya codakaṃ prati samādhānaṃ vakṣyata ityeva nyāyaḥ | tatra vajracchedikā iti sūtrasya nāmadheyam | anenaiva tāvad abhidheyaḥ prayojanaṃ cābhidhīyete |
body.translated_text: Next, for understanding the summary meaning, the word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>) will be explained. Then, to show the non-contradiction of the sequence, the connection of words (<s>anusandhi</s>) will be demonstrated. Next, to remove the contradiction between prior and subsequent reasoning, the resolution to the objection will be stated — this is the proper method. Here, 'Vajracchedikā' (Diamond Cutter) is the name of the <s>sūtra</s>. By this very [name], both the subject matter and the purpose are expressed.

body.text: atra dvidhā vajracchedikā | sūkṣmakleśajñeyāvaraṇāni vajravaddurbhedyāni, teṣāṃ chedanāt | etenāsya (granthasya) āvaraṇadvayaprahāṇaṃ tāvat prayojanaṃ nirdiṣṭam | athavā chedanaṃ hi vajrākārasādṛśyena vajravaditi | vajrasya hi ubhe śikhare sthūle madhyaṃ ca sūkṣmam | tathaiveyaṃ prajñāmitāpyādāvadhimukticaryābhūmim ante ca buddhabhūmiṃ vistareṇa nirdiśati | sūkṣmeṇa tāvanmadhyabhāgena śūddhādhyāśayabhūmiṃ nirdiśati | ata eveyaṃ vajrākāravaditi | etena bhūmitritayamasyāḥ (vajracchedikāyāḥ) abhidheyo nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, 'Vajracchedikā' is [understood] in two ways. The subtle afflictive and cognitive obscurations (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s> and <s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) are hard to break like a <s>vajra</s> (diamond); because it cuts through them. By this, the purpose of this treatise is indicated as the abandonment of the two obscurations. Or, the cutting is 'like a <s>vajra</s>' due to its resemblance to the shape of a <s>vajra</s>. For a <s>vajra</s> has both ends thick and the middle thin. Likewise, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too extensively teaches the stage of devotional practice (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>) at the beginning and the <s>Buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha stage) at the end; and with its thin middle portion, it teaches the stage of pure superior aspiration (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>). Therefore, it is 'like the shape of a <s>vajra</s>.' By this, the three stages (<s>bhūmitraya</s>) are indicated as the subject matter of this <s>Vajracchedikā</s>.

body.text: piṇḍārthastu saṃkṣepeṇa pañcadhā, tadyathā- nidānam, upodghātaḥ, buddhavaṃśānupacchedaḥ pratipattilakṣaṇam, tatsthānañca |
body.translated_text: The summary meaning (<s>piṇḍārtha</s>) is briefly fivefold, namely: (1) the background (<s>nidāna</s>), (2) the introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>), (3) the non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s> lineage (<s>buddhavaṃśānupaccheda</s>), (4) the characteristic of practice (<s>pratipattilakṣaṇa</s>), and (5) its domain (<s>sthāna</s>).

body.text: tatra nidānaṃ tu sūtrārambhanimittam, taccāpi evaṃ mayā śrutam ityārabhya tena khalu āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ ityetāvatparyantaṃ deśitam | tasya ca saṅgītikārairātmaprāmāṇyapratipādanāyoktatvāt | evaṃ sutrāntareṣvapi vācyam |
body.translated_text: The background (<s>nidāna</s>) is the occasion for the commencement of the <s>sūtra</s>; it is taught from 'Thus have I heard' (<s>evaṃ mayā śrutam</s>) up to 'then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.' And since this was stated by the compilers of the council (<s>saṅgītikāra</s>) for establishing their own authority, the same should be said in other <s>sūtras</s> as well.

body.text: upodghātastāvat prakaraṇena sūtrārthavyutpādanārthaṃ saṃyujyate | aprastutābhidhānena sarvam asamañjasaṃ syāditi tannirākartuṃ sarvatrāpi prakaraṇena yojyam | atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirutthāyāsanāt ityādinā tannirdiṣṭam | buddhavaṃśānupacchedo 'pi ca tenaiva darśitaḥ | āryasubhūtinā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ buddhavaṃśānupacchedakatvena viditvā yathā buddhavaṃśānupacchedo bhavet tathaivādau saṃsthāpitā |
body.translated_text: The introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>) is joined with the topic for the purpose of elucidating the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. To remove the unsuitability that would result from stating something irrelevant, [the text] should everywhere be connected with the topic. This is indicated by [the passage beginning] 'Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, rising from his seat.' The non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s> lineage (<s>buddhavaṃśānupaccheda</s>) is also shown by that very [passage]. The Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, having understood this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as that which ensures the non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s> lineage, established it at the outset precisely so that the <s>Buddha</s> lineage would continue uninterrupted.

body.text: pratipattilakṣaṇaṃ tu bodhisattvayānasamprasthitena kathaṃ sthātavyam? ityādinā proktam |
body.translated_text: The characteristic of practice (<s>pratipattilakṣaṇa</s>) is expressed by [the question:] 'How should one who has set out in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle abide?'

body.text: tasya pratipattilakṣaṇasya sthānaṃ tāvat kasmin viṣaye bodhisattvena sthātavyam? pratipattavyam? cittaṃ pragrahītavyam? yadetat tattasya sthānamiti | tadapi iha subhūte ! bodhisattvayānasamprasthitena evaṃ mayā ityādinārabhya tārakā timiram ityantimagāthāṃ yāvadabhihitam | pratipattilakṣaṇaṃ tasya sthānaṃ cetyetābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ bodhisattvānāmaśeṣakaraṇīyaparipūrṇatā samprakāśitā, ityeṣa tāvat piṇḍārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The domain (<s>sthāna</s>) of that characteristic of practice is: 'In what object should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> abide? Practice? Take hold of the mind?' — that is its domain. This too is expressed from 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, by one who has set out in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, thus by me' up to the final verse on 'a star, a visual aberration.' Through the characteristic of practice and its domain, the complete fulfillment of all that is to be done by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is illuminated — this is the summary meaning (<s>piṇḍārtha</s>).

body.text: nidānam :
body.translated_text: The background (<s>nidāna</s>):

body.text: padārthādayaśceme sāmpratamabhidhīyante- tatra evam iti śabdo 'bhyupagamādinānārtheṣu dṛśyate | atra prakaraṇādibalena saṃnnidhāpitārtho grāhyaḥ | ayaṃ hi vakṣyamāṇasakalasūtrārthaṃ vyavasthāpayati | mayā ityanyavyavacchedena arthasya sākṣācchravaṇaṃ nirdiśyate | ātmanaiva śrutaṃ na śravaṇaparamparāyātamityarthaḥ | śrutam ityadhigamo niṣedhyate | tathāgatād ṛte nānye svatastāthābhūtadharmādhigamavanto bhavanti | etenānāptapvaṃ nirākriyate | ekasmin samaye iti ekasmin kāle, sarvakālamevaṃvidhadharmaratnaśravaṇaṃ durlabhamityākhyātam | (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 99

children.text: ) yadvā svagataṃ bāhuśrutyamupadarśitam | ekasmin kāle idaṃ śrutamanyadā anyadapi śrutamiti darśyate | atha vā, ekasmin samaye bhagavān viharati sma ityuttareṇa sambadhyate | aparimitāvineyānāṃ teṣāṃ hitāya anyadā anyatra viharati sma iti pratipādyate | kleśaskandhamṛtyudevaputrarūpāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ mārāṇāṃ bhañjakatvānnirūktayā bhagavān iti smaryate | atha vā īśvaryādimattvāt 'bhagavān'; ityucyate | yathoktam-
children.translated_text: Or, one's own extensive learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>) is indicated. 'At one time this was heard; at another time, that too was heard' — this is shown. Or, '<s>ekasmin samaye</s>' is connected with what follows: 'the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling.' It is conveyed that for the benefit of limitless beings to be trained (<s>vineya</s>), he dwelt at other times in other places. He is remembered as '<s>Bhagavān</s>' (the Blessed One) by etymology because he is the destroyer of the four <s>Māras</s> — of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), death (<s>mṛtyu</s>), and <s>Devaputra</s>. Or, he is called '<s>Bhagavān</s>' because he possesses sovereignty and other [qualities]. As it is said:

body.translated_text: The word-meanings (<s>padārtha</s>) and so forth are now explained. Here, the word '<s>evam</s>' ('thus') is seen in various meanings such as acceptance. In this context, the meaning established by the force of the topic and other [factors] should be taken. For this [word] establishes the entire meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> that follows. By '<s>mayā</s>' ('by me'), through the exclusion of others, direct hearing of the teaching is indicated — the meaning is: heard by oneself, not received through a chain of hearsay. By '<s>śrutam</s>' ('heard'), realization (<s>adhigama</s>) is negated — apart from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, no others independently realize the true <s>dharmas</s>. By this, unreliability is refuted. By '<s>ekasmin samaye</s>' ('at one time') — at one time — it is declared that hearing such a jewel of <s>Dharma</s> is rare at all times.

children.translated_text: 'Of complete sovereignty, form, fame, glory,

children.text: jñānasyātha prayatnasya ṣaṇṇāṃ bhaga iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowledge, and effort — of these six, '<s>bhaga</s>' is the traditional [meaning].'

body.text: śrāvastī iti śravastestannāmakarṣerāśramatvācchrāvastī nagarī, tayopalakṣito deśaviśeṣo 'pi tatsambandhena śrāvastītyucyate | deśoktayā ayaṃ deśo 'pi caityabhūto 'bhidhīyate, tadyathā caityabhūtaḥ sa pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati ityatrāpyuktam | atha ca saṅgītikārairātmavacanānāmādeyatāpratipādanāyaitat sarvamuktam | lokapratyāyanārthaṃ tāvat [sa] pradeśaḥ sākāraḥ samṛddhaścetyuktaḥ, evaṃ sati paraiḥ grāhyaṃ bhavati vacanam, nānyathā tadādeyavacanamiti |
body.translated_text: <s>Śrāvastī</s> — because it was the hermitage of the king named <s>Śravasta</s>, [the place is called] <s>Śrāvastī</s> city; and the particular region marked by it is also called <s>Śrāvastī</s> by that association. By mentioning the place, this region too is declared to be a sacred site (<s>caityabhūta</s>), as it is said elsewhere: 'that spot of earth shall become a sacred site.' Moreover, all this was stated by the council compilers for establishing the trustworthiness of their own words. To gain the conviction of the world, the place is described as having definite features and being prosperous — for when it is so, the statement is accepted by others; otherwise the statement would not be trustworthy.

body.text: śrāvastīpradeśasya atyantaṃ vistīrṇatvāt kutra viharatīti sthānaniścayābhāvād jetavane ityuktam | 'jetṛ'; ityākhyasya rājakumārasya vanatvād jetavanamiti | tadapi tāvat kasyacidaprasiddhamiti sambhāvanāyām anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ityuktam | gṛhapati-anāthapiṇḍada ityanāthebhyo dayayā piṇḍadānena tathā prasiddhaḥ, sa khalu bhagavadarthaṃ nirantarayā ratnāni vikīrya jetuḥ rājaputrādārāmaṃ krītavān | rājaputrajetṛṇāpi tatra kācid bhūmirāvāsādibhiḥ samalaṅkṛtā, atastayostad vanamiti prasiddhiṃ gatam | kasyacidekasyopādānena abhipretadeśaviśeṣasyānavabodhāt padatrayamuktam | athavā śrāvastītyanena bahunāṃ madhye viharaṇāt parārthasampadabhihitā | jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāma ityanena (ca) vivekaviharaṇāt svārthasampat |
body.translated_text: Because the region of <s>Śrāvastī</s> is extremely vast, to determine where exactly [the <s>Bhagavān</s>] was dwelling, it is said 'in <s>Jetavana</s>' (Jeta's grove). Because it was the grove (<s>vana</s>) of the prince named <s>Jetṛ</s> (the Conqueror), it is called <s>Jetavana</s>. Since even that might be unknown to some, it is said 'in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.' The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> — so famous for giving alms (<s>piṇḍadāna</s>) with compassion to the destitute (<s>anātha</s>) — he purchased the park from the prince <s>Jetṛ</s> by spreading jewels over the ground continuously for the sake of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Prince <s>Jetṛ</s> too adorned some land there with dwellings and such; hence it became known as the [grove/park] of both of them. Because the intended particular place would not be understood from mentioning only one, three terms are stated. Or, by '<s>Śrāvastī</s>,' the accomplishment of others' welfare is expressed, since he dwelt among many; and by 'in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>,' the accomplishment of one's own welfare [is expressed], since he dwelt in seclusion.

body.text: atra kaḥ sākṣīti cintyamāne mahatābhikṣusaṃghena ityuktam | bhinnakleśā hi bhikṣavaḥ | mārādibhiḥ pratyarthibhirabhedyatvāt teṣāṃ samūhaḥ saṃghaḥ ityucyate | mahān bhikṣusaṃghastāvat bhūyastvena ānubhāveneti dvaividhyena, ānubhāvastāvad darśitaḥ | kathaṃ bhūyasvamiti ced? sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhiḥ (bhikṣu) śataiḥ ityādyucyate | tasmin samaye tāvatāmeva sattvāt | bhikṣusaṃghāt bodhisattvānāṃ bāhulyaṃ tu teṣāmevārthāya sūtrāṇāṃ bhāṣitatvāt | bodhau sattvamāśayo yeṣāṃ te 'bodhisattvāḥ'; | śrāvakeṣvapi bodhau sattvaṃ vidyate, atasteṣāṃ vyavacchedāya mahāsattvaiḥ ityāha | dharma-cittotpāda-adhimukti-adhyāśaya-sambhāra-kāla-sampratipattilakṣaṇaiḥ saptabhirmahattvairupetvād mahāsattvāḥ |
body.translated_text: When one considers 'Who is the witness here?', it is said 'with a great assembly of monks.' For monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>) are those whose afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) are broken. Because they cannot be divided by adversaries such as <s>Māra</s> and others, their group is called a <s>saṃgha</s> (assembly). 'A great assembly of monks' — this is first of all because the majority have direct experience.

body.text: tatra dharmahattvaṃ tu bodhisattvebhyaḥ śatasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitādivipuladharmāṇāṃ deśanāt | cittotpādamahattvaṃ tāvadanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittotpādāt |
body.translated_text: The greatness of the <s>Dharma</s> [is established] because extensive teachings such as the <s>Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> and others are taught to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The greatness of the arising of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>) is because of the generation of the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: adhimuktimahattvaṃ taminneva gambhīrodāra dharme 'dhimuktatvāt | āśayamahattvaṃ tu sarvasattvahitasukhotpādāśayāt | sambhāramahattvaṃ tāvadaparimitapuṇyajñānaṃsambharaṇāt | kālamahattvaṃ khalu tribhirasaṃkhyeyakalpairbodhiprāpteḥ | sampratipattimahattvaṃ hi anuttarasamyaksambodherniṣpādanāt |
body.translated_text: The greatness of conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) is because of conviction in that very profound and noble <s>Dharma</s>. The greatness of intention (<s>āśaya</s>) is because of the intention to produce benefit and happiness for all sentient beings. The greatness of accumulation (<s>sambhāra</s>) is because of the gathering of immeasurable merit and knowledge. The greatness of time (<s>kāla</s>) indeed, through three [incalculable aeons].

body.text: viharati iti caturbhirīryāpathaiḥ, athavā anuttareṇa brahma-deva-āryavihāreṇa viharati | sma iti vihṛtavāniti darśitam | tatra bhikṣusaṃghastu kṛtakṛtyatvād mṛdukāruṇikatvācca sarvakālaṃ tathāgatasya pādāntike niṣadyata iti viditvā syāsnutvasaṃdarśanārthaṃ pūrvamuktaḥ | bodhiasattvāstu aparimeyasattvārthakriyāsādhana-pariniṣpattau akṛtakāryatvāt, adhimātrakaruṇayā jagadarthakaraṇāya lokadhātuṣu viharaṇāt sarvakālaṃ bhagavataḥ pādāntike 'niṣīdanācca paścāduktāḥ | ata eva śrāvakasūtrānteṣu nocyante bodhisattvāḥ, na ca tāni (śrāvakasūtrāṇi) tadarthāni, aniyatāni ceti |
body.translated_text: 'Dwells' (<s>viharati</s>) — with the four deportments (<s>īryāpatha</s>), or [it means] he dwells in the unsurpassed dwelling of <s>Brahmā</s>, the gods, and the noble ones. '<s>Sma</s>' indicates that he had dwelt [in the past]. The assembly of monks, because of having accomplished their task and because of their gentle compassion, always [remains in] the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha iti tadanantaram | samaye iti niyate | etena niyatastāvat piṇḍakāla iti | kālaniyatatvaṃ tu asminneva kāle piṇḍapāto grahītavya iti, tadapi kimiti aparijñānāt tadarthaṃ pūrvāhṇaḥ iti vacanenābhidhīyate | pūrvāhṇañca kālasamayaśceti samāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Then' (<s>atha</s>) means immediately after that. 'At the time' (<s>samaye</s>) means at the appointed [time]. By this, the time for the alms-round is indeed fixed. The fixedness of time means 'alms-food should be collected at this very time.' And why? Because of the lack of complete knowledge [otherwise], this is indicated by the expression 'in the forenoon' (<s>pūrvāhṇa</s>).

body.text: upavasatāṃ pravajitānāṃ ca piṇḍakālopalambhena pūrvāhṇalakṣaṇaṃ bhagavatā deśitamekāntenetyavabodhanārthaṃ kālasamaye ityuktam | anyathā pūrvāhṇa ityetadvacanena tadaekāntatvanirdeśo nāvagamyate | bhagavatā svecchayā kṛtamiti sambhāvyamānatvād etat padatrayamuktamiti vā | nivāsya iti gṛhapraveśānurūpaṃ vastradhāraṇam | tadapi śikṣāsu śrotṛṇāṃ gauravasampādanārtham, anyathā svasyaiva vineyatvābhāve kathaṃ parasya vineyatā syāt | cīvaramādāya ityatra cīvarādānaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_103

children.text: ) tāvat prāvaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ draṣṭavyam, nāstyantasyāvakāśa iti | mahānagarī iti deśaviśeṣaḥ, śrāvastīmātravyavacchedārtham | kimarthaṃ bhagavān piṇḍāya prāvikṣat iti | śrāvakeṣvalpecchatāpravṛttiḥ, daridra-rogi-gṛhiṇī-vṛddhādiṣvanugrahaḥ, andhādibhyo netrādisamprāptiriti, vividhavismayahetūnāmanavarataṃ pradarśanena bhagavati ca pareṣāṃ prasādotpādanārthaṃ ityetānyaparimitāni prayojanānyavagantavyāni | kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ iti yaḥ khalu bhojanādibhaktakṛtyaṃ sampāditavān, sa evamucyate |
children.translated_text: ...the characteristic of the outer robe should be examined, since there is no room for doubt about this. 'Great city' is a specification of place, for the purpose of distinguishing [it as] <s>Śrāvastī</s> alone. Why did the <s>Bhagavān</s> enter [the city] for alms? [To demonstrate] the practice of contentment with few desires among the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples),

body.translated_text: In order to make it understood that 'the time for alms-food for renunciants and monastics is definitely taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as characterized by the forenoon,' it is said 'at the time of the [proper] hour.' Otherwise, by the mere expression 'forenoon,' the definitive indication of that [exclusivity] would not be understood. The <s>Bhagavān</s>...

body.text: alpakuśalamūlebhyo nirjātā api brahmādayaḥ kavalīkārāhāravināgānnaiva bhaktakṛtyaṃ kurvanti, tarhi acintyakuśalamūlanirjāto hi bhagavān (buddhaḥ) kathaṃ kuryāditi? tathā āryadharmasaṃgītau api bhāṣitam "tathāgatastu kṣutpipāsāvarjitaḥ mūtrapurīṣavirahito 'kṣīṇakāyaśca bhavati" iti | satyamevaitat tathāpi yadi bhagavataḥ sa kāyo na paramārthabhūtaḥ, tadā syāt sarvopālambhāvasaro 'pi, yadā tvayaṃ bhagavato nirmāṇakāyaḥ, evaṃvidhacaritapradarśanena veneyasattvāśayānurūpaṃ pravartate, tadā kathamumālambhāvakāśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Even <s>Brahmā</s> and others, though born from small roots of virtue, do not perform the act of eating since they are without morsels of material food; how then could the <s>Bhagavān</s> (<s>Buddha</s>), who is born from inconceivable roots of virtue, do so? Likewise, in the <s>Āryasamgītisūtra</s> also it is stated:

body.text: manuṣyabhāve eva vīryārambheṇa etādṛśamanuttarapadaṃ labhyata iti vineyānāmutsāhanārthaṃ manuṣyabhāvaṃ darśayitvā evaṃrūpaṃ piṇḍabhaktaṃ darśitavān | ye dāyakā dānapatayaḥ teṣu piṇḍaparikarmaprakāśanena praharṣaḥ samupajāyate | bhāgyavanto 'pi kiñcitkarmāvaraṇavaśāt pretādiṣu samupajātāḥ mahaujaskā yakṣādayaḥ bhagavatāṃ karanakhāmṛtena saṃspṛsṭaṃ paramākṣayadivyarasamādāya paribhuñjānāḥ paramasukhasaṃtṛptacetasa uttamāṃ samādhiṃ samavāpnuvanti | ataḥ aparimeyaṃ tāvad bhagavato bhaktakṛtyam |
body.translated_text: In order to inspire enthusiasm in those to be trained — [showing] that such an unsurpassed state is attained only through effort in the human condition — having displayed the human condition, he showed this form of alms-food. For the donors and patrons, [this is] for the purpose of illuminating the preparation of alms-food.

body.text: kena prakāreṇa bhaktakṛtyaṃ kṛtamiti cet? tadarthaṃ paścād ityādyāha | sarvamādāya tadanu yat piṇḍapātaṃ bhaktaṃ tat paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātam | pūrvametatsamādānaṃ tu śrāvakāṇāṃ dhūtaguṇeṣvavatāraṇārtham | bhaktamiti (bhakṣaṇakṛtyaṃ) sampāditamityarthaḥ | athavā paścāditi yad dvitīyavāramādānaṃ tat paścādbhaktam | tadeva paścādbhaktamapi piṇḍaścāpīti padayojanā | athavā apārahṇabhaktatvena yaḥ paribhujyate piṇḍaḥ sa evamucyate |
body.translated_text: If asked, 'In what manner was the act of eating performed?' — for that purpose he says 'afterward' and so on. Having collected everything, then, after [collecting] that alms-food — that is the after-meal alms-round. The prior collection [of food] is for the purpose of introducing the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) to the ascetic practices (<s>dhūtaguṇas</s>).

body.text: ataśca dhūtaguṇavattvāt vikālabhojanaparihṛtatvācca tadviorahitametad bhaktaṃ syādityarthaḥ | pratiśāmya iti pratiṣṭhāpyetyarthaḥ | tacca śakrādayastu bhagavadājñāmādātuṃ samudyatāstadantike sadaivopatiṣṭhante, kintu pravrajitāstu svayamevānutiṣṭhanta iti nidarśayituṃ bhagavatā svayaṃ pātracīvarapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ kṛtam, alabhyamānabhṛtyānāṃ mandabhāgyānāṃ daurmanasyaparihāṇārthamapīti |
body.translated_text: And therefore, because of possessing the ascetic practices and because of refraining from eating at improper times, this food would be free from that [fault] — this is the meaning. 'Having settled' (<s>pratiśāmya</s>) means 'having established.' And [as for his attendants], <s>Śakra</s> and others, ready to receive the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s command, always attend upon him in his presence.

body.text: aśucyābhāsaṃ satatasamitapākartuṃ kamaleṣu pādanikṣepaṇam, kriyāntrādyadhimuktasattvāśayānuvartanaṃ vā sarajaskapādābhyāṃ śayanāsanānāmanavamardanam iti śikṣāyāmādaraṃ darśayituṃ pādaprakṣālanaṃ draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: The washing of feet, in which he places his feet upon lotuses to continuously ward off the appearance of impurity — or [it should be understood as] conforming to the dispositions of beings who have conviction in ritual actions and so forth, and [as showing] respect for the training by not pressing down bedding and seats with dusty feet.

body.text: prajñapta evāsane iti devādibhiḥ prajñapte | ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya iti nātinamraṃ nātistabdhamityarthaḥ | kathaṃ dharmadeśanākāle bhagavān samāhitena īryāpathena (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_105

children.text: ) nyaṣīdaditi cet? samāhitaireva dharmo 'yaṃ jñātuṃ śrotuṃ vā śakyate nānyairiti samādhau yatnotpādāya lokāanāṃ pravartanāt |
children.translated_text: Because this <s>Dharma</s> can be known and heard only by those who are composed in meditation (<s>samādhi</s>), not by others — it is for the purpose of urging beings to make effort in meditation.

body.translated_text: 'On the very seat that was prepared' — prepared by gods and others. 'Holding the body upright' (<s>ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya</s>) means neither too bent nor too rigid. If asked, 'How did the <s>Bhagavān</s> sit with a composed deportment at the time of teaching the <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: pratimukhīṃ smṛtimupasthāpya iti pūrvaṃ bodhisattvāvasthāyāṃ tāvad anuttarapadaṃ prāpya yathā buddhavaṃśānupacchedaḥ syāttathāhaṃ kariṣye iti yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tat praṇidhānaṃ smaraṇābhimukhīkṛtamityarthaḥ | bhagavāṃstu buddhaḥ sadā samāhitaḥ sannapi sarvathā smṛtau viharati | asamayasmareṇa na kiñcit syāt | samaye praṇidhānasmaraṇaṃ hi saphalaṃ bhavati | samaye smareṇanāpi bhagavataḥ sadā samāhitatvaṃ na virudhyate |
body.translated_text: 'Having established mindfulness directed to the front' (<s>pratimukhīṃ smṛtim upasthāpya</s>) — previously, in the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage, having attained the unsurpassed state, the vow that was made — 'I shall act in such a way that the lineage of Buddhas will not be interrupted' — that vow has been brought to the forefront of recollection.

body.text: atha khalu saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ ityanena kimuktam? yatparimāṇena bhikṣusaṃghena saha bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma, sa sarvaḥ dharmadeśanākāle tatra naiva sannipatitaḥ | tribhyo 'dhikāstatra sannipatitā ityuktam | tacca saṅgītikāraiḥ parasampratyayotpānādanārthaṃ nirdiṣṭam | sannipatitaḥ iti sannihita eva | sanniṣaṇṇaḥ ityāsane upaviṣṭaḥ | loke prāyaḥ samānyapūrvakaṃ viśeṣaḥ sthāpyata iti lokaprasiddhyanurūpamubhayamāha | anyathā niṣaṇṇaḥ ityetāvatmātreṇa apyubhayamuktaṃ syāditi | uktā nidānapadārthāḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, what is meant by 'Now indeed a number of monks'? The entire community of monks with whom the Blessed One was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> was not assembled there at the time of the <s>Dharma</s> teaching. It is stated that more than three [of the standard number] had assembled there. And this was indicated by the compilers of the recitation (<s>saṅgītikāras</s>) for the purpose of generating trust in others. 'Assembled' (<s>sannipatitaḥ</s>) means present, nearby. 'Seated' (<s>sanniṣaṇṇaḥ</s>) means seated upon a seat. In the world, a particular [statement] is generally established after a general [one]; thus both are stated in conformity with common usage. Otherwise, by the word 'seated' (<s>niṣaṇṇaḥ</s>) alone, both meanings would have been expressed. The meanings of the introductory section (<s>nidānapadārtha</s>) have been stated.

body.text: upodghāto buddhavaṃśānupacchedaśca :
body.translated_text: The preface (<s>upodghāta</s>) and the unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage:

body.text: samprati upodghāto buddhavaṃśānupacchedaśca kathayiṣyete | paramāścaryamādarśayituṃ dvirabhidhānam | sugata iti sambodhanam | nairātmyadvayamārgeṇa (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 106

children.text: ) samyag gata iti suṣṭhurūpeṇa gataḥ sugataḥ surūpavaditi | athavā nikhilasavāsanāśeṣakleśajñeyāvaraṇāni prahāya gataḥ sugataḥ, sūpūrṇaghaṭavat | athavā apunarāvṛttyā gataḥ sugataḥ, sunaṣṭajvaravat | yāvataivānugrahītāḥ, tāvataivānuparigṛhītā ityarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: like one of beautiful form (<s>surūpa</s>). Or, having abandoned all affliction-obscurations (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and knowledge-obscurations (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) together with their residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), without remainder, he has gone — [hence] <s>Sugata</s>, like a well-filled vessel (<s>sūpūrṇaghaṭa</s>). Or, he has gone without return — [hence] <s>Sugata</s>, like a well-cured fever (<s>sunaṣṭajvara</s>). 'As many as were favored' means 'just that many were taken under protection' — that is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Now the preface and the unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage will be explained. The double statement [of certain phrases] is to show supreme wonder. '<s>Sugata</s>' is a form of address. [He is called] <s>Sugata</s> because he has gone (<s>gata</s>) well (<s>su</s>) — that is, gone in a good manner — by the path of the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmyadvaya</s>),

body.text: rājādayo 'pi āśritān prajādīn yathāśakti anuparigṛhṇanti kintvatra bhagavati āścaryamityāśaṅkākāyāṃ kimāścaryamiti tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena ityuktam | yathāvadvastutattvadeśanāt tathāgataḥ | athavā yathā pūrvakā nairātmyadva rgeṇa gatāḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇamadhigatāḥ, atrāpi tathā gatatvāt tathāgataḥ | sarvalokābhyarhaṇīyatvāt, arīṇāṃ kleśānāṃ vā hantṛtvād arhan | samastajñeyānāṃ samyagabodhāt samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | ebhiḥ padairbhagavataḥ prahāṇajñānarūpā sva-parārthasampadupadarśitā bhavanti |
body.translated_text: Kings and the like also protect their dependents — subjects and so forth — according to their ability. But in anticipation of the doubt 'what is wonderful about this in regard to the Blessed One?' it is said: 'by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>).' He is <s>Tathāgata</s> because of teaching the true nature of reality as it is. Or, just as the former [<s>Buddhas</s>] went by the path of twofold selflessness and attained the abandonment of affliction and knowledge obscurations, so too has he gone in that same way — hence <s>Tathāgata</s>. He is <s>Arhat</s> because he is worthy of veneration by all the world, and because he is the destroyer of enemies (<s>ari</s>), i.e., afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). He is <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> because of his perfect awakening to all knowable things. By these terms, the Blessed One's perfect attainment of his own and others' welfare, consisting of abandonment and knowledge, is shown.

body.text: etenaivamabhidhīyate- rājādīnāṃ prajādiṣvanugrahe tāvannaivāścaryam, yato hi te lābhasatkārādisvārthārthitayā parānanugṛhṇanti, bhagavatastāvat tathāgatatvenārhattvena samyagabhisambuddhya adhigatāśeṣasampattitayā yo 'nugrahaḥ sa khalvatra āścaryamityādarśitam | ṛte karuṇāṃ bhagavato 'nugrahe 'smin nāsti kiñcidanugrahakāraṇāntaramityanenābhihita eva bhavati bhagavān mahākāruṇikaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this the following is stated: There is indeed nothing wonderful about the favor of kings and the like toward their subjects, since they favor others out of desire for their own benefit such as gain, honor, and the rest. But in the case of the Blessed One, the favor [shown by one] who, as <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, and <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, has attained every perfection without remainder — that indeed is shown to be wonderful. By this it is implicitly stated that apart from compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), there is no other reason for the Blessed One's favor — [hence] the Blessed One is the Great Compassionate One (<s>mahākāruṇika</s>).

body.text: anuparigṛhītāḥ iti abhisambuddhena bhagavatā dharmacakrapravartanākāle paripakvakuśalamūlā bodhisattvā bhūmiṣvavatāritāḥ, dharmatāyāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ pratiṣṭhāpanena | parīnditāḥ iti aparipakvakuśalamūlānām ādikarmikāṇāmanugrahāya ta eva parīnditāḥ, dharmatāyāṃ bodhisattvān pratiṣṭhāpayitum | mama parinirvāṇapradarśanaṃ tu yuṣmāsvaprāptaguṇānāmadhigamāya, prāptānāṃ ca samyagaparihāṇāyeti | evamanugrahaparīndanetyubhābhyāṃ buddhavaṃśānupacchedaḥ samprakāśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Were taken under protection' (<s>anuparigṛhītāḥ</s>) means: when the Blessed One, having attained perfect awakening, turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) were ripened were established on the [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] stages (<s>bhūmi</s>) by establishing them in the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>). 'Were entrusted' (<s>parīnditāḥ</s>) means: for the benefit of beginners (<s>ādikarmika</s>) whose wholesome roots were not yet ripened, those very [advanced <s>Bodhisattvas</s>] were entrusted — to establish [further] <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the nature of reality. 'My display of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, however, is for those among you who have not yet attained [the necessary] qualities to attain them, and for those who have attained them not to decline from them.' Thus by both — favor (<s>anugraha</s>) and entrustment (<s>parīndana</s>) — the unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage is illuminated.

body.text: bodhisattveṣvanugrahastu pañcadhā samyag veditavyaḥ- kāla-viśeṣatā-udāratā-sthiṃratā-vyāpakatābhiḥ | tatra kālaḥ- janmajanmātaratvāt | viśeṣatā-tairthika-śrāvaka-pratyekabuddhebhyo 'nugraheṇa viśiṣṭatvāt | udāratā- anuttaratvāt tadanugrahasya | sthiratā- ātyantikatvāt | vyāpakatā- tadanugraheṇa tu sva- parasantatyorhitasampādanāt |
body.translated_text: The favor toward <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be properly understood in five aspects: in terms of time (<s>kāla</s>), distinctiveness (<s>viśeṣatā</s>), nobility (<s>udāratā</s>), firmness (<s>sthiratā</s>), and pervasiveness (<s>vyāpakatā</s>). Therein, time — because it extends from birth to birth. Distinctiveness — because it surpasses the favor shown by non-Buddhists (<s>tīrthika</s>), <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Nobility — because that favor is unsurpassed. Firmness — because it is ultimate and final. Pervasiveness — because through that favor, the welfare of both one's own and others' continuums (<s>santati</s>) is accomplished.

body.text: parīndanāpi tridhā samyag draṣṭavyā, āśraya-dharmatāprāpaṇa-jñapticavanaiḥ | kīdṛśastāvadāśrayaḥ? kalyāṇamitreṣu parīndanāt sā bhavatyavipraṇaṣṭā | kiṃ tāvad dharmatāprāpaṇam? anuparigṛhītā bodhisattvā dharmatayā parānanugrāhayanti | kiṃ tarhi jñaptivacanam? tvayā anye bodhisattvā anugrahītavyā ityājñāpitam, na tvanādarabhāvaḥ | upodghāta-buddhavaṃśānupacchedapadārthā uktāḥ |
body.translated_text: The entrustment (<s>parīndana</s>) too should be properly understood in three aspects: through the basis (<s>āśraya</s>), bringing to the nature of reality (<s>dharmatāprāpaṇa</s>), and the statement of instruction (<s>jñaptivacana</s>). What is the basis? Because the entrustment is to spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), it is not lost. What then is bringing to the nature of reality? The <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who were taken under protection cause others to be favored through the nature of reality. And what is the statement of instruction? [The <s>Buddha</s>] commanded: 'You should favor other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — this is not an expression of indifference. The meanings of the preface and unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage have been stated.

body.text: pratipattilakṣaṇam :
body.translated_text: The characteristic of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>):

body.text: pratipattilakṣaṇaṃ tāvaducyute- tadadhikāreṇa katham ityuktam | āryasubhūtiḥ khalu ṣaḍvidhaprayojanārthaṃ pṛṣṭavān | 1 saṃśayopacchedāya, 2 adhimuktisamutpādāya, 3 gambhīreṣvartheṣvavatāraṇāya, 4 avinivartanāya, 5 paramapramodasañjananāya, 6 saddharmasya cirasthityai ca |
body.translated_text: The characteristic of practice is now stated — with that authority, 'how' was asked. The noble <s>Subhūti</s> asked for a sixfold purpose: (1) for the cutting off of doubt, (2) for the generation of conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>), (3) for entry into profound meanings, (4) for non-regression, (5) for the generation of supreme joy, and (6) for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra prajñāpāramiteyaṃ kathaṃ buddhavaṃśasya anupacchedaṃ karotīti sandehakāriṇāṃ saṃśayopacchedanārtham | aparipakvasantatīnāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ puṇyabāhulyakhyāpanena prajñāpāramitāsu adhimuktisamutpādanārtham | paripakvasantatīnāṃ tāvad gambhīreṣvartheṣvavatāraṇārtham | abhūtapratipattiparibhūtānāṃ tadudgrahaṇadhāraṇayorvyāyacchatāṃ puṇyavāhulyābhikāṅkṣayā avinirvatanārtham | anugṛhīteṣu viśuddhādhyāśayeṣu svādhigatataddharmadarśanena paramapramodasañjananārtham | anāgate kāle mahayānasaddharmasya ciramavasthānārtham |
body.translated_text: Therein, for the cutting off of doubt of those who wonder 'How does this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> bring about the unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage?' For the generation of conviction in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> among <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose continuums are not yet ripened, by making known the abundance of merit. For the entry of those whose continuums are ripened into profound meanings. For the non-regression of those who, though assailed by wrong practice, exert themselves in taking up and retaining [the teaching], through their desire for abundant merit. For the generation of supreme joy in those who have been favored and whose aspirations are purified, through showing them the <s>Dharma</s> they have [themselves] realized. And for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in the future age.

body.text: samāsatastu sandigdhānāṃ samyak samprakāśanāya, puṇyābhikāṅkṣaṇām aparikvabodhisattvānāṃ samyagavatāraṇāya, vipratipattivihatānāṃ sampraharṣaṇāya, śuddhādhyāśayānāṃ pramodāya ca | tatra sthātavyam chandapraṇidhānābhyām | pratipattavyam yogasamāpattyā | cittaṃ pragrahītavyam vikṣepanigraheṇa | tatra (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 109

children.text: ) chandastāvadabhilāṣaḥ | praṇidhānaṃ tu abhilaṣitārthe 'bhisaṃskāralakṣaṇena yaccintanam | yogasamāpattiḥ khalvavitarkasamādhiḥ | vikṣepanigrahastāvat samādhito vikṣiptaṃ cittaṃ vikṣepebhyo nivārya tatraiva viniyojanam | prathamena prayogamārgaḥ, dvitīyena pariniṣpattimārgaḥ, tṛtīyena tvavipraṇāśamārgaḥ parideśitaḥ |
children.translated_text: aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) is longing. Vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) is the contemplation characterized by the mental formation (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>) toward the desired object. Meditative attainment (<s>yogasamāpatti</s>) is the concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) free from discursive thought (<s>avitarka</s>). Restraint of distraction is: having withdrawn the mind that has become distracted from concentration from the distractions, [one] reapplies it right there [in concentration]. By the first [the path of] preparation (<s>prayogamārga</s>) is indicated; by the second, the path of accomplishment (<s>pariniṣpattimārga</s>); by the third, the path of non-loss (<s>avipraṇāśamārga</s>) is taught.

body.translated_text: In brief: for the proper illumination of those in doubt; for the proper entry of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who desire merit and whose continuums are not yet ripened; for the encouragement of those harmed by wrong practice; and for the delight of those whose aspirations are pure. Therein, one should abide through aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>); one should practice through meditative attainment (<s>yogasamāpatti</s>); and the mind should be uplifted through the restraint of distraction. Therein,

body.text: sthāne pṛcchato bhagavān āryasubhūtaye sādhukāramadāt | śṛṇu ityavahitaśrotrābhyāṃ śrotuṃ pravartasva | sādhu ityaviparītapratipattyā udgrahītum | suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru samyaktayā udgrahītumudyukto bhava ityarthaḥ | tadapi avāṅmukha-aśuci-sacchidrabhāṇḍānāmiva śrotṛjanānāṃ yathākramaṃ trividhadoṣaparihārārthamidamudīritamiti | bhāṣiṣye iti tebhya eva samprakāśayiṣyāmi, nānyebhya iti | anyathā avāṅmukha-aśuci-sacchidrabhāṇḍeṣu ambuvṛṣṭiriva (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 110

children.text: ) dharmavṛṣṭirapīyaṃ nirarthakaiva syādityarthaḥ | athavā ahaṃ tu kevalaṃ deśayiṣyāmi tvameva tāvad yatnataḥ pratipadyasvetyarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Otherwise, like rain falling on inverted, impure, and leaky vessels, this shower of <s>Dharma</s> too would be fruitless — that is the meaning. Or alternatively: I shall merely teach; it is for you to practice diligently — that is the meaning.

body.translated_text: To the one asking appropriately, the Blessed One gave approval (<s>sādhukāra</s>) to the noble <s>Subhūti</s>. 'Listen' (<s>śṛṇu</s>) means: engage in hearing with attentive ears. 'Good' (<s>sādhu</s>) means: take it up with correct, non-distorted understanding. 'And attend well in your mind' (<s>suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru</s>) means: be diligent to take it up correctly — that is the meaning. This was uttered for the purpose of removing the three defects of listeners, which are respectively like inverted, impure, and leaky vessels (<s>bhāṇḍa</s>). 'I shall speak' (<s>bhāṣiṣye</s>) means: I shall illuminate [the teaching] for these very ones, not for others.

body.text: bodhisattvayāneti bodhisattvānāṃ yānam, yena bodhisattvā niryānti | tacca daśabhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ daśabhiśca bhūmibhiḥ parigṛhyate | tatra samprasthānaṃ tāvat praṇidhiprasthānacittābhyāṃ sampravartanam | etadviśeṣaṇaṃ tu śrāvakādibodhipratiṣedhārtham, bodhisaṃprasthitena ityetāvaducyamāne bodhīnāṃ tritvādanyasyā api bodheravagamaḥ syāditi | pratyaśrauṣīt ityabhyupagamādityarthaṃ | uktāḥ pratipattilakṣaṇapadārthādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Bodhisattvayāna</s>' means the vehicle (<s>yāna</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> go forth (<s>niryānti</s>). And that is comprised of the ten <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections) and the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages). Therein, 'setting forth' (<s>samprasthāna</s>) is the setting in motion through the aspiration-mind and the setting-forth-mind (<s>praṇidhiprasthānacittābhyām</s>). The qualifier [<s>bodhisattva</s>-] is for the purpose of excluding the awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others; for if only 'one who has set forth toward awakening' were said, since there are three [types of] awakening, it might be understood as referring to another awakening as well. 'Assented' (<s>pratyaśrauṣīt</s>) means 'agreed' — that is the meaning. The meanings of the characteristic of practice and related topics have been stated.

body.text: pratipattisthānam :
body.translated_text: The ground of practice (<s>pratipattisthāna</s>):

body.text:
sāmprataṃ tatsthānānyabhidhīyante | tatsthānāni tāvat samāsato 'ṣṭādaśaprakārāṇi; tadyathā-
1. cittotpādaḥ
2. pāramitāyogaḥ
3. rūpakāyāptikāmatā
4. dharmakāyāptikāmatā
5. bhāvanāviśeṣalābhe 'nabhimānaḥ
6. buddhotpādārāgatā
7. kṣetraviśuddhipraṇidhānam
8. sattvaparipākaḥ

children.text:
9. bāhyaśāstreṣu vyapagatarāgatā
10. sattvabhājanalokayoḥ piṇḍagrāhaviśīrṇatāyogaḥ
11. tathāgatapūjāsatkāraḥ
12. kāyacittapariśrāntau vīryavaimukhyānārambhalāsatkāravirahitatā | kāyacittapariśrāntau vīryārambhotovinivṛttiḥ, na ārambha ityanārambhaḥ | aho, ārabdhavīryo 'yamiti pareṇa jñāyamāne sati śraddhāmāgamya lābhasatkārādhyavasitatvam | tasmād bodhisattva etebhyaḥ sarvebhyo vimucya prajahyāt |
13. duḥkhādhivāsanam
14. dhyānāsvādaviratiḥ
15. abhisamayakāle 'hamitivikalpaviyogaḥ
16. avavādaparyeṣaṇam
17. abhisamayaḥ
18. buddhabhūmiparyeṣaṇaṃ ca |
children.translated_text:
9. Freedom from attachment to non-Buddhist scriptures.
10. The practice of dissolving the aggregate-apprehension of beings and the vessel-world.
11. Worship and veneration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
12. Absence of weariness, aversion to effort, indolence, and lack of honor when body and mind are exhausted. When body and mind are exhausted, there is no cessation of the undertaking of effort; <s>anārambha</s> means "no undertaking." When another perceives "Ah, this one has exerted effort," and comes to have faith, there is no settling into gain and honor. Therefore the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abandon and relinquish all of these.
13. Endurance of suffering.
14. Non-cessation of the relishing of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
15. At the time of realization, separation from the conceptual construction of "I."
16. Seeking instruction.
17. Realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>).
18. And seeking the <s>Buddha</s>-ground.

body.translated_text:
Now those grounds are described. Those grounds are, in brief, of eighteen kinds; namely:
1. Generation of the [awakening] mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>)
2. Engagement in the perfections (<s>pāramitāyoga</s>)
3. Desire for attaining the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>)
4. Desire for attaining the <s>Dharma</s>-body (<s>dharmakāya</s>)
5. Non-conceit regarding the attainment of special meditative cultivation
6. Reverence for the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>
7. Aspiration for the purification of [<s>Buddha</s>-]fields (<s>kṣetra</s>)
8. Maturation of sentient beings (<s>sattvaparipāka</s>)

body.text: etāni tāvadaṣṭādaśavidhāni sthānāni, yatra bodhisattvena sthātavyaṃ pratipattavyaṃ cittaṃ ca pragrahītavyamiti | etaiḥ sthānairbhūmitrayaṃ saṃgṛhyate, tadyathā- ṣoḍaśabhiḥ sthānairadhimukticaryābhūmiḥ, abhisamayasthānenaikena śuddhādhyāśayabhūmiḥ, buddhabhūmiparyeṣaṇena ca buddhabhūmiḥ saṃgṛhyate | sarvasattvaparinirvāpaṇacittamutpādya pāramitāyogī tāvat tathāgatasya rūpakāya-dharmakāyaprāptau chandamutpādayati | tataḥ ā abhimānam antimam ahaṃ-vikalpaṃ yāvadabhisamayastāntarāyebhyaścittaṃ viprakarṣate | tataścābhisamayārthamavavādaṃ paryeṣate, tadanantaramabhijānāti, tadūrdhvaṃ buddhabhūmiṃ paryeṣate | ayameva teṣāṃ kramaḥ |
body.translated_text: These are the eighteen stations where a <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide, should practice, and should take hold of the mind. By these stations, three grounds are encompassed, namely: by sixteen stations, the ground of practice through aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>); by the single station of realization, the ground of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>); and by the seeking of the <s>Buddha</s>-ground, the <s>Buddha</s>-ground is encompassed. Having generated the mind for the complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings, the practitioner of the <s>pāramitās</s> first generates desire for the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body) and <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body). Then, up to the final conceit, the last "I"-construction before realization, he draws the mind away from obstacles. Thereafter, for the sake of realization, he seeks instruction; immediately after that, he realizes; above that, he seeks the <s>Buddha</s>-ground. This is the order of these [stations].

body.text: 1. cittotpāda-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 1. The station of the generation of mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>):

body.text: tatra bodhicittamadhikṛtya yāvantaḥ sattvāḥ ityāha | yāvat iti parimāṇam | kiṃ tatra parimāṇam? sattvasaṃgraheṇa ityuktam 'sattvadhātustu (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 112]

children.text: ) aparimitaḥ, athāpi sattvaḥ sattva iti yastatsvabhāvaḥ taditaravyāvṛttaśabdādhyāropitārthasabhāgarūpeṇa khyātaḥ sa eva sattvena saṃgṛhyate | tena dṛśyavikalpyayokatvenābhisaṃkṣipya tadrūpeṇādhyavasitatvād rūpādiskandhaviśeṣairupādīyante | ataste āyuṣmāniva pratīyante |
children.translated_text: "The <s>sattvadhātu</s> (realm of beings) is immeasurable." Furthermore, that which is a being—called "being"—whose nature is such, appearing in the form of a meaning that is similar [to a real entity] through the superimposition of words that exclude what is other, is what is encompassed by "being." Therefore, by compressing [reality] through the capacity of the visible and the conceptualizable, and by determining it in that form, [beings] are appropriated through the specific <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) such as form and the rest. Hence they appear as if possessing life.

body.translated_text: There, regarding <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), he says "as many beings as there are." "As many" indicates quantity. What is the quantity there? It is said "by way of the collection of beings":

body.text: evaṃ sāmānyato nirūpya viśeṣato darśayitumāha- aṇḍajāḥ ityādi | viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ tāvat tribhiḥ prabhedairabhihitam | yonibhedenāṇḍajādayaścattvāraḥ | sthānabhedena tu rūpiṇāmarupiṇāṃ ca pṛthaksthānatvāt | kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāstāvad rūpiṇaḥ, arupāvacarāstu arupiṇaḥ | nimittodgrahaṇabhedena saṃjñinaḥ ityādayaḥ | bṛhatphalasyaikadeśaṃ bhavāgrajāṃścaṃ sattvān vihāya sarve sattvāḥ saṃjñinaḥ | bṛhatphalasyaikadeśastāvad asaṃjñīnaḥ | ayamapi nimittodgrahaṇabhedātmaka eva, tadabhāvabhedenopalakṣitatvāt | bhavāgrajāstāvad naiva saṃjñino nāsaṃjñino vā | prabhedo 'yaṃ mandamedhasāmanugrahāyaiva kṛtaḥ, anyāvadhyānaparihārārthaṃ tāvannaiva prapañcitaḥ | 'sarve dharmāḥ niḥsattvāḥ'; ityanena saha vacanasyāsyāvirodhaḥ pradarśitaḥ | atra sattvadhāturiti sāṃvṛte satye sattvadhātustaṃ darśayituṃ yāvān ityādyāha | prajñapyamānaḥ iti pañcaskandhaviśeṣātmakatvena prajñāyata iti, na tu tairthikāḥ prajñaptyā prajñapayantītyarthaḥ | anenāpavādāntastāvat parihṛtaḥ, prajñaptāvapavādābhāvāt | yasmin apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇadhātau sāsravopadhirnāśiṣyate, sa tathocyate | śrāvakāṇāṃ parinirvāṇaṃ tāvad nātra nirvāṇadhātu; tasya hīnatvāt | praṇītaphale saṃvidyamāne kṛpālūnāṃ hīnaphalārthitā na khalu yuktimatī | saṃvidyamāne 'pi praṇītaphale prāptumaśakyatvādevaṃ prārthyata iti cet? tvanmatānusāraṃ tāvad trividhagotratvādagotratvācca sarvaiḥ hīnaphalamapi prāptuṃ naiva śakyate |
body.translated_text: Having thus examined [beings] in general, to show [them] in particular, he says "egg-born" and so forth. The specific characteristic has been stated through three divisions: by division of birth, there are four types such as egg-born and the rest; by division of abode, form-possessing and formless beings have separate places—beings of the desire realm and form realm are form-possessing, while beings of the formless realm are formless; by the division of grasping at signs, [there are] "those with perception" and so forth. Excluding one portion of [the heaven of] <s>Bṛhatphala</s> and the beings at the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), all beings are percipient. One portion of <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, however, consists of non-percipient beings. This too is essentially a division of grasping at signs, since it is characterized by the absence of that [grasping]. Those at the summit of existence, however, are neither percipient nor non-percipient. This division is made solely for the benefit of those of dull intellect; it is not elaborated for the purpose of eliminating other faults. "All <s>dharmas</s> are without a self"—the non-contradiction of this statement with that [teaching] has been shown. Here, "realm of beings" (<s>sattvadhātu</s>): to show the realm of beings in conventional truth, he says "as many as" and so forth. "Being designated" (<s>prajñapyamāna</s>) means that [a being] is cognized through the specific nature of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); the meaning is not that the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) designate through [mere] designation. By this, the extreme of nihilism (<s>apavāda</s>) is first avoided, since there is no nihilism regarding designation. That <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm (<s>nirvāṇadhātu</s>), which is the <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa), where the substratum with <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) does not remain, is so called. The <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) is not the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm meant here, because of its inferior nature. When a superior fruit exists, it is surely not reasonable for the compassionate ones to desire an inferior fruit. If [one objects] that "even though the superior fruit exists, because it cannot be attained, it is thus sought"—then, following your own doctrine, because of the three types of <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage) and the absence of <s>gotra</s>, it is not possible for all [beings] to attain even the inferior fruit.

body.text: atha bodhisattvagotraṃ tāvattathāvidhaṃ yadvaśatayā mahākaruṇāvegābhibhūtena (mayā) kathamidaṃ śakyamiti, saṃvidyamāneṣvapareṣu parārthakāriṣu buddhabodhisattveṣu nirarthakena mayātra praṇidhānena kimiti vicārān santyajya parapratyayatāṃ ca dūrīkṛtya mahākaruṇārdraḥ jājvalyamānena duḥkhāgninā pīḍyamānaṃ jagad vilokya ahameva tārayiṣyāmīti cintayamānaḥ praṇidadhāti | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Now, as for the <s>bodhisattva</s>-lineage, it is of such a nature that, overwhelmed by the force of great compassion, [one thinks] "How can I accomplish this?" Knowing that there exist other <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> who act for the benefit of others, [one thinks] "What purpose would my vow serve here since it would be pointless?" But abandoning such deliberation, setting aside dependence on others, softened by great compassion, beholding the world tormented by the blazing fire of suffering, thinking "I myself shall save [them]," he makes the vow. As it has been said:

children.translated_text: "Having abandoned the calculation that "it is difficult, most difficult,"
And [seeing] that the afflicted world has been taken up—by you yourself."

body.text: iti | yadyapyevam, tathāpi priyaputrasya nṛpatvāya praṇidhānamiva satyapyaprāpye praṇītaphale kathanna praṇidhānamiti | kimarthaṃ hīnameva prārthyate | ata evāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇam evātra anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhāturyujyate | tatra sāsravopadheḥ śeṣatvābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Although this is so, nevertheless, just as in the case of a vow for the kingship of a dear son, even though the superior fruit is unattainable, how could there not be a vow? Why should only the inferior [fruit] be sought? For this very reason, <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s> (non-abiding nirvāṇa) alone is appropriate here as the <s>anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātu</s> (nirvāṇa-realm without residual substratum), since therein there is no remainder of the substratum with defilements.

body.text: nirvāpayitavyāḥ ityetāvanmātraṃ kasmānnoktam? prathamādidhyānānāṃ vyāvṛttyarthamiti | tāni tāvadadhobhūmikleśābhāvād nirvāṇaparyāyeṇoktāni bhagavatā | sopadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau iti kasmānnoktamiti cet? duḥkhopadhiśeṣasyāprahīṇatvāttatra | sarvasattvanirvāpaṇāśayastu bodhisattvānāṃ tribhirhetubhirdraṣṭavyaḥ, tadyathā-
body.translated_text: Why was it not said merely "they should be led to <s>nirvāṇa</s>"? For the purpose of distinguishing from the first and other <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations). For those [meditations] are spoken of by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) as synonyms of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, due to the absence of the afflictions of the lower grounds. If asked why it was not said "in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm with residual substratum"—because the substratum of suffering has not been abandoned therein. The <s>bodhisattvas</s>' intention to lead all beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s> should be understood through three causes, namely:

body.text:
1. akṣaṇotpannebhyaḥ kālāntarāvasthānam, akṣaṇāvasthā tāvadupalakṣaṇamiti | naitāvanmātram | tasyāmavasthitau parinirvāṇaṃ naiva sambhāvyate |
2. aparipakvānāṃ paripācanam |
3. paripakvānāṃ vimokṣaṇaṃ ca |
body.translated_text:
1. For those born in unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>), providing abode at another time; unfavorable condition is merely illustrative, not the only [case]. For beings in that state, <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is not at all possible.
2. The ripening of the unripened.
3. And the liberation of the ripened.

body.text: tasmānnāśaktārthitā (teṣām) | nikhilasattvānāṃ parinirvāpaṇāśayena anena ādāryaṃ tāvad bodhicittasyādarśitam | chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ kathaṃ sthātavyaṃ- (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 114]

children.text: ) tadapyatrāveditam | kathaṃ yogasamāpattyā pratipattavyamiti taddeśayitumāha evam ityādi | saṃvṛtau sarvasattvānāṃ parinirvāpaṇe 'pi yathā paramārthato na ko 'pi sattvaḥ bodhisattvenopalabhyate, tasyāabhāvādityevaṃ yogamāpattyā pratyavekṣaṇīyam | vyutthito bhūtvā na paramārthataḥ ko 'pi sattvo mayā parinirvāpitaḥ iti yaścittotpādastena gambhīratvaṃ paramārthabodhicittatvañca darśitaṃ bhavati, pūrveṇa tu saṃvṛtiriti | tena vikṣepanigraheṇa kathamatra cittaṃ pragrahītavyamityādarśayitumāha- tatkasya hetoḥ? sacet iti yadītyarthaḥ |
children.translated_text: That too is indicated here. To teach how one should practice through <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment), he says "thus" and so forth. Even though in conventional [truth] all beings are to be led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, since in ultimate [truth] no being whatsoever is apprehended by the <s>bodhisattva</s>—because of the non-existence of that [being]—thus it should be contemplated through <s>yogasamāpatti</s>. The generation of mind [that occurs] upon emerging [from meditation], [thinking] "not a single being has been led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> by me in ultimate truth"—by this, the profundity and the nature of ultimate <s>bodhicitta</s> have been shown; while the former [shows] the conventional [truth]. Therefore, to show how the mind should be taken hold of here through the restraint of distraction, he says "For what reason? If..." meaning "if indeed."

body.translated_text: Therefore, [the <s>bodhisattvas</s>'] aspiration is not for the unattainable. By the intention of the complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings, the nobility of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) has been shown. How one should abide through aspiration and resolve—

body.text: atha yaḥ pudgalādisaṃjñayā pravartate kiṃ sa bodhisattva iti vaktavyaḥ? sattva ityuktau punaḥ kasya hetoḥ iti praśnenetarābhirapi (saṃjñābhiḥ) na vaktavyaḥ ityāha | asyāyamabhiprāyaḥ- kumatibhistāvat pañcaskandhātiriktaḥ antarvyāpāravāṃścaturṇāṃ bhogānāṃ bhoktā ekaḥ puruṣa iti parikalpyate sattvaḥ, jīva ityādiśabdaiśca vyavahriyate | ye cānirvacanīyatvena pudgalamicchanti tairapi tasya skandhasvabhāvavilakṣaṇatvenābhyugatatvāt tadbalenārthāntara evābhyupeyate | na kadāpi padārtho 'nirvacanīyaḥ sambhavati, sarvasyāpyanirvacanīyatvaprasaṅgāt | tatsādhakapraṇābhāvād bādhakasadbhāvācca taddraṣṭā bodhisattvo viparītābhiniveśena viparyasta eva bhavati | yaḥ khalu viparyastaḥ sa kathaṃ paramārthabodhisattvaḥ?
body.translated_text: Now, should one who operates with the concept of <s>pudgala</s> (person) and the like be called a <s>bodhisattva</s>? Since "being" has been said, and then the question "for what reason?"—[the answer is that] one should not be called [a <s>bodhisattva</s>] through the other concepts [of <s>pudgala</s>, etc.] as well. The purport of this is: by those of wrong understanding, a being (<s>sattva</s>) is imagined as a single person (<s>puruṣa</s>), a self separate from the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), having inner agency, enjoying the four [types of] enjoyments; and it is referred to by words such as "soul" (<s>jīva</s>) and the like. And those who accept the <s>pudgala</s> as inexpressible—since even by them it is accepted as having a nature different from that of the <s>skandhas</s>, by that force a different entity is accepted. A real entity (<s>padārtha</s>) that is "inexpressible" is never possible, since everything would absurdly become inexpressible. Because there is no valid cognition that establishes that [pudgala], and because there are refutations [of it], a <s>bodhisattva</s> who perceives that [<s>pudgala</s>] would be perverted through attachment to what is false. And how could one who is perverted be an ultimate <s>bodhisattva</s>?

body.text: anye punarāhuḥ- asti tāvadātmasādhakaṃ pramāṇamiti | tathā hi-bandha-mokṣa-mārga-hetuphalasambandhasmṛtipratyabhijñādīnāmekādhikaraṇakatve tāvat prasiddhe nairātmyavādināṃ yuṣmākaṃ mate tu yastadādhāra ekaḥ prasiddhaḥ sa nāsti kaściditi kastāvadādhāraḥ? vijñānakṣaṇānāṃ pratikṣāṇaṃ pṛthaktvāt | baddho (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 115]

children.text: ) devadattaḥ muktaścānyo yajñadatta iti naiva vyavasthā, na cānyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati anyena kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalamityatiprasaṅgaḥ | kṛtavipraṇāśo 'kṛtābhyāgamaśca prasajyete | tathā hi- kartṛtvena prajñapto yo hi vijñānakṣaṇaḥ, tasya phalenānabhisambandhāt kṛtavipraṇāśākhyo doṣaḥ | akartuścaiva tasya phalena yogādakṛtābhyāgamo doṣaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: <s>Devadatta</s> is liberated while another, <s>Yajñadatta</s>, [is not] — no such distinction [would be possible], and the absurd consequence arises that one person would experience the fruit of action performed by another. The faults of <s>kṛtavipraṇāśa</s> (loss of what was done) and <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s> (receiving what was not done) would follow. For the moment of consciousness (<s>vijñānakṣaṇa</s>) designated as the agent has no connection with the fruit — this is the fault called <s>kṛtavipraṇāśa</s>. And the fault of <s>akṛtābhyāgama</s> would arise because the fruit is connected with that [moment] which is not the agent.

body.translated_text: Others, however, say: "There does exist a valid cognition that establishes the self." For example: since it is well-known that bondage, liberation, path, cause-and-effect relation, memory, recognition, and the like have a single basis, in the view of you who advocate <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), that one well-known [entity] which is their single basis does not exist—then what is the basis? Since the moments of consciousness are each distinct at every moment, the one who is bound

body.text: smṛtyādikaṃ a bhinnādhikaraṇakamiti na loke pratītam | atha kathamiti cet? ekādhikaraṇakameva | devadattasya cittānubhavaḥ yajñadattacittena na smaryate vā pratyabhijñāyate vā | yenānubhūyate tenaiva smaryate pratyabhijñāyate veti prasiddham | phalataścaika eva puruṣaḥ sarvāvasthāsvanugantā bhavati | prayogaḥ- yau bandhamokṣau tāvekādhikaraṇakau, yathā- devadattasyaiva śṛṅkhalābandhanaṃ mokṣaśca | vivādāspadībhūtau bandhamokṣāvapi bandhamokṣāveveti bandhamokṣāveveti svabhāvahetuḥ | tathaiva kartrāderapyekādhikaraṇatvasādhane prayogāḥ kalpayitavyā iti |
body.translated_text: Memory and so forth are not established in the world as having different substrates (<s>bhinnādhikaraṇa</s>). Then how? They have a single substrate (<s>ekādhikaraṇa</s>). The mental experience of <s>Devadatta</s> is not remembered or recognized by the consciousness of <s>Yajñadatta</s>. It is well known that what is experienced by one is remembered and recognized by that same one. From this result, a single person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is the one who persists through all states. The argument: bondage and liberation have a single substrate, just as <s>Devadatta</s> alone has both shackling and liberation. The bondage and liberation that are the objects of dispute are indeed bondage and liberation — this is a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential reason). Similarly, arguments should be constructed to prove that the agent and so forth also have a single substrate.

body.text: tatra yadi svatantrasyaikasya paramārthasato nityasya puruṣasyādhikaraṇatvaṃ sādhyate, tadā tathāvidhena puruṣeṇa saha kvāpi hetoḥ sambandhāsiddheranaikāntikatvam, sarveṣāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvāt, devadattādeḥ nityatvaikatasvabhāvāsiddheḥ dṛṣṭāntasyāpi sādhyavikalatvam | ata eva viruddho hetuḥ tadviparyavyāptatvāt |
body.translated_text: If the single-substrate-ness of a permanent, ultimately real, independent self (<s>puruṣa</s>) is being proved, then the reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), since the connection of the reason with such a self is unestablished anywhere — for all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>). And the example too is lacking the property to be proved, since the permanent, unitary nature of <s>Devadatta</s> and the like is unestablished. Therefore the reason is actually contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), since it is pervaded by the opposite [of the thesis].

body.text: atha ekādhikaraṇatvamātraṃ sādhyate, tadā siddhasādhanam | ekasantānapravṛttatvena tena bandhanādīnāmekādhikaraṇatvamiṣyata eva |
body.translated_text: If mere single-substrate-ness is being proved, then it is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). For it is accepted that bondage and the like have a single substrate by virtue of operating within a single continuum (<s>santāna</s>).

body.text: api ca, yadā yatra santāne 'vidyādikaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvenāvicchinnaṃ nirantaraṃ pravartate, tadā sa baddhaḥ ityucaryate, sa eva punaḥ śrutamayādikrameṇāryamārgotpādād avidyādinirodhenāśrayaparāvṛttau muktaḥ ityupacaryate | ubhāvapi tau bandhamokṣau nityaikaparamārthavastuviṣayakau natarāṃ siddhau | laukikabandhamokṣayorapi tathātvāt |
body.translated_text: Moreover, when in a particular continuum (<s>santāna</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and the rest operate continuously without interruption through cause and effect, then it is figuratively said 'he is bound' (<s>baddha</s>). When that same [continuum], through the sequence of learning-based [wisdom] and the rest, by the arising of the Noble Path (<s>āryamārga</s>) and the cessation of ignorance and so forth, [undergoes] the transformation of its basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), it is figuratively said 'he is liberated' (<s>mukta</s>). Neither of these two — bondage and liberation — is at all established with respect to a permanent, unitary, ultimately real entity. For even worldly bondage and liberation are of that [figurative] nature.

body.text: yasmin santāne śubhoo vā aśubho vā cittānubhavaḥ samutpadyate, tasminneva kālāntare santatiparipākamāgamya mastuluṅgalākṣādirasāvasiktasantatiparipāka iva sukha-duḥkha-smṛtyādiphalodayo dṛṣṭāḥ, tasmācchubhādīnāmekādhikaraṇatvaṃ tāvat prasiddham | naiva khalu kaścidekaḥ kartā bhoktā smartā vā | sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ vyavahārasya prajñaptervā kāryakāraṇabhāvamātreṇa prabhāvitatvāt | na cātiprasaṅgaḥ, niyatasāmarthyavato bījāderiva kāraṇaśakteḥ pratiniyatatvāt | tataśca yeṣu kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ pratiniyataḥ teṣu naiva kaścid eko 'nugataḥ bhinnāvasthaśca paridṛśyate | iha sattvahetostathātve sati kimanenātmanā parikalpitena | ātmopacārasya yā khalu kartrādyavasthā, sā tāvad hetuḥ, yā khalu bhoktrādyavasthā, sā phalamityevaṃvidho hi kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'vaśyamabhyupetavya iti | anyathā tayorubhayorapyavasthayoranupapannatve parasparokārakatvābhāve vā ākāśamiva kathaṃ tāvat tāvat sidhyet bhoktrādiḥ | śaktipratiniyamo 'pyabhyupagantavya eva | itthaṃ pratiniyatātmanā sambandhena sukhādīnāṃ sambhavaḥ na tu sarvatra | ataḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 117

children.text: ) kāryakāraṇabhāvena dṛśyamānāni kuśalādīnyeva kartā, bhoktā ca syāt, kimanenādṛṣṭasvabhāvena ātmanā parikalpitena |
children.translated_text: wholesome and unwholesome [deeds] and the like, observed through causal relations, are themselves the agent and experiencer — what need is there of this imagined self (<s>ātman</s>) whose nature is unseen?

body.translated_text: In whatever continuum (<s>santāna</s>) a wholesome or unwholesome mental experience arises, in that very [continuum], at a later time, through the maturation of the series — like the maturation of a series watered with the juice of <s>mastuluṅga</s> (citron) and <s>lākṣā</s> (lac) — the arising of fruits such as pleasure, suffering, memory, and so forth is observed. Therefore, the single-substrate-ness of wholesome [deeds] and the like is well established. There is certainly no single agent, experiencer, or rememberer. For all these conventional usages and designations (<s>prajñapti</s>) arise merely through causal relations (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>). Nor is there the absurd consequence [of confusion], because the causal power is restricted, just as seeds and the like have determinate capacities. And thus, among those things where causal relations are determinate, no single persisting entity of different states is perceived. Here, when the causes of [what is called] a being are of such a nature, what need is there of this imagined self (<s>ātman</s>)? The state of agency, which is the figurative designation of self, is indeed the cause; the state of being an experiencer is the fruit — such a causal relation must necessarily be accepted. Otherwise, if both those states are untenable or if they lack mutual efficacy, how could the experiencer and the like be established at all, [being as inert] as space? And the restriction of causal power must also be accepted. Thus, through a determinate intrinsic connection, the arising of pleasure and the like is possible — not everywhere. Therefore,

body.text: atha nānumānena ātmā siddhaḥ syāt, tathāpi pratyaviṣayatvād ahaṃbuddheḥ pratyakṣata evātmā sidhyatīti cet? tadapi tāvanna yujyate, bhrāntatvāt savikalpatvād asiddhatvācca pratyakṣeṇa tatrāhaṃbuddheriti | ahaṃbuddhau pratīyamānatve yathā khalu pratyakṣa eko nityo vibhuścātmā svasiddhāntairukalpyate tathā naivopalabhyata ityavaśyameva draṣṭavyam | anyathā ahaṃbuddheryadi pratyakṣatvaṃ syāt tadā vivādamāneṣu tāvannaiva pravarteta ātmaviṣaye kaścana vivādaḥ, savikalpāyā ahaṃbuddherniścayātmakatvāt, niścayena ca viṣayīkṛte adhyāropābhāvācca |
body.translated_text: If the self (<s>ātman</s>) is not established by inference, still, since it is not the object of perception, 'the self is established by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) itself through the I-cognition (<s>ahaṃbuddhi</s>)' — if this is objected? That too is untenable, because the I-cognition is erroneous, conceptual (<s>savikalpa</s>), and unestablished as perception. It must be recognized that what is imagined in one's own doctrines — that a single, permanent, all-pervading self is perceived through the I-cognition — is simply not apprehended [in that way]. Otherwise, if the I-cognition were truly perceptual, there would be no dispute at all regarding the self, since the I-cognition, being conceptual, is of the nature of certainty, and where there is certainty about an object, there is no superimposition (<s>adhyāropa</s>).

body.text: evamevānyo 'nyeṣvapyevañcātīyeṣu sambhavād vipralambhaḥ | anādikālābhyāsavaśāt pratinīyateṣu rūpādiskandheṣu ekatvamadhyāropya paraṃ vyāvarttīyatumahamiti pratītiḥ, tasyāṃ pratītau teṣāmeva rūpādīnāṃ pratibhāsamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: Similarly, just as deception occurs in other cases of similar [mis]identification, through the force of beginningless habitual impressions (<s>anādikālābhyāsavaśāt</s>), the cognition 'I' arises by superimposing unity upon the particular aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) such as form and so forth. For in that cognition, it is those very form-aggregates and the rest that appear.

body.text: kāye cāyamātmagrahaḥ, kathaṃ tarhi mama deha iti bhedamātragrahaṇamiti cet? taccātmālambane 'pi tulyam | yadi cātmani ayamātmagrahaḥ, kathaṃ tarhi mama ātmā iti cintyate | atha vastuto 'bhinne 'pi bhedāntaraparihāreṇa tanmātrajijñāsāyāṃ śilāputrakasya śarīravad bhedopacāreṇa grahaṇānnāsti virodha iti cet? dehālambane 'pi caitat samānam |
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] this self-apprehension (<s>ātmagraha</s>) is in the body — then how is there the apprehension of a distinction [expressed as] 'my body'? That is equally [problematic] even when [the self-apprehension is taken as] having the self as its object. For if the self-apprehension is in the self, then how does one think 'my self'? If [one responds:] even though there is no real distinction, when one wishes to know just that [self] to the exclusion of any other distinction — like [saying] 'the body of the stone-statue' — there is no contradiction because the apprehension is through a figurative distinction? The same applies equally to the apprehension [in respect of] the body.

body.text: ātmā khalu viṣayaḥ punaḥ kramotpattyā virudhyata iti paścāt vakṣyate | na kevalamātmagraha ātmā apitu tadviṣayo rūpādirātmāstītyapi vaktuṃ na śakyate, tadavilakṣaṇatvāttasya | krameṇopalabhyamānatvānna te ekasvabhāvāḥ, na ca svatantrāḥ | ata evoktam-
body.translated_text: The self (<s>ātman</s>) as an object is contradicted by sequential arising — this will be stated later. Not only is self-apprehension not the self, but even the object of that [apprehension] — form and the rest — cannot be said to be the self, because it is not different in character from that [apprehension]. Being apprehended sequentially, they are not of a single nature, nor are they independent. Therefore it is said:

body.text:
na cātmadṛṣṭiḥ svayamātmalakṣaṇā
na cāpi duḥsaṃsthitatā vilakṣaṇā |
body.translated_text: Self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) is not itself of the character of self, nor is that ill-established [view] of a different character.

body.text: nāmavyavahāsya tu abhīṣṭatvānnātra kaścidapi vivādaḥ | ata eva nāsti kiñcidātmaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇam | nāsti pratyakṣamanumānaṃ ca vyatiricya pramāṇamityanyatra vicāritam |
body.translated_text: Since conventional naming is accepted [as useful], there is no dispute here at all. Therefore, there is no valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that establishes the self. That there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> other than perception and inference has been examined elsewhere.

body.text: bādhakapramāṇaṃ tāvannirākriyate- yadyevamātmā skandhebhyo 'bhinnastadā skandhavat kṣāṇikaḥ syād athavā skandhāḥ khalvātmavannityāḥ syuḥ, tadabhinnatvāt, skandhavadanekatvaprasaṅgo 'pi durnivāraḥ syāt | ataḥ skandheṣveva ātmeti prajñapyate, na tāvannāmni vivādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now the invalidating argument (<s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s>) is set forth: If the self (<s>ātman</s>) is thus non-different from the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), then it would be momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) like the aggregates; or the aggregates would be permanent like the self — since it is non-different from them. The absurd consequence of multiplicity, like the aggregates, would also be unavoidable. Therefore, the self is merely designated (<s>prajñapyate</s>) upon the aggregates — there is no dispute about the name.

body.text: atha skandhebhyo bhinna ātmā iṣyate tadā sukhādināsambaddhatve na sidhyet tasya bhoktṛtvādikam | tatra prayogaḥ- yo nāsti sukhaduḥkhādibhiḥ sambaddhaḥ sa nāsti kartā vā bhoktā vā, muktaḥ saṃsārī vāpi na yujyate, yathā vandhyāputraḥ | ātmāpi tathārthakriyādibhirna kathañcanāpi sambadha iti vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ | na cāyamasiddho hetuḥ, tathā hi- sukhādinā hi sambandhe sati ādhārādheyalakṣaṇo vā saṃyogalakṣaṇo vā kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇo veti pakṣatrayam |
body.translated_text: If the self (<s>ātman</s>) is held to be different from the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), then, being unconnected with pleasure and the like, its agency, experiencer-ship, and so forth would not be established. The argument: that which has no connection with pleasure, suffering, and the like is not an agent, experiencer, nor can it be said to be liberated or a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrant) — like the son of a barren woman. The self too is in no way connected with efficacious action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) and the rest — this is inference from the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). Nor is this an unestablished reason (<s>asiddha hetu</s>). For if there is connection with pleasure and the like, there are [only] three possibilities: it is characterized as container and contained (<s>ādhārādheyalakṣaṇa</s>), or as contact (<s>saṃyogalakṣaṇa</s>), or as cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ, akiñcitkaratvāt | tathā hi- adhaḥprasarpaṇadharmiṇāṃ jalādīnāmadhogamanapratibandhakatvena vyavasthāpyate tāvadādhāraḥ | sukhādīnāmamūrtatvānna sambhavati (teṣām) adhogamanamiti kathamiva ātmana ādhāratvamiti | sthityāpi nādhāraḥ, sthiteḥ sthāturabhinnatvāt, tasyaiva kārakatvamiti? tadapi tāvanniṣidhyate | sthiteḥ pṛthakatve sati sā naiva tāvatsthāturupakārikā arthāntarabhūtatvāttasyāḥ | nāstyeva tasyāṃ sthāturutpādasāmarthyam, asāmarthasya sarvatraivābhivyaktatvāt | svayaṃ bhaṅgātmanaḥ tāvannāsti kaścana sthāpakaḥ, anavasthitatvāttasya, anyathā tena bhaṅga eva tasya syānna tāvadavasthānam | avipariṇāmātmani tāvat sthāpakena kiṃ kriyate, sthīrātmanā svabhāvena svayamavasthitatvāt |
body.translated_text: The first alternative is not [tenable], because it serves no purpose. For a container (<s>ādhāra</s>) is established as that which prevents the downward falling of things whose nature is to flow downward, such as water. Since pleasure and the like, being immaterial (<s>amūrta</s>), cannot fall downward, how could the self be their container? [If one says] the container is for the purpose of stability (<s>sthiti</s>) — a container is not [needed] for stability, since stability is non-different from what is stable; [if one says] that very [stable entity] is the agent [of its own stability] — that too is denied. If stability is separate, then it is of no benefit to the stable thing, being a different entity. There is simply no capacity in [stability] to produce the stable thing, since [that] incapacity would be manifest everywhere. For something whose nature is to perish, there is no agent of stability, since it is not enduring — otherwise that [agent] would cause its very destruction, not its abiding. And for something whose nature is unchanging, what would a stabilizer do, since it abides by itself through its own stable nature?

body.text: ata evākiñcitkaratvena saṃyogasambandho 'pi tāvannaiva yujyate, atiprasaṅgāt | evaṃ hi sati sarvasya sarvasaṃyogahetutvam | evaṃ ca naivopapadyate tāvad bhinnārthena bhinnārthasya saṃyogaḥ, sarvasya svayamavasthitatvāt lauhaśalākāvat | api ca, saṃyogabalena yadi ātmā sukhī vā duḥkhī vā bhavet, tadā saṃyogaikatvameva syāt, aviśiṣṭatvena pratiniyatātmabhiḥ sukhādibhirnaiva syāt sambandhaḥ | tata evātmanā sahaikatve sukhādinā naiva syāt kaścit sukhī vā duḥkhī vā | adarśane 'pi balenābhyupagate niścaye tenaiva niścitaḥ syāttadā kiṃ tāvat saṃyogaparikalpanayā, sarvasāmarthyavirahitatvāttasya | sambandhibhedena bhinnāyāmapi prajñaptau paramārthataḥ bhāvānāmabhinnasvabhāve sati kathaṃ svabhāvabhedāśritaḥ pṛthagarthakriyābhedaḥ syāditi kumatiparikalpita evāyaṃ khalu sambandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: For this very reason, conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) as a relation is also not tenable, since [the self] is devoid of any causal efficacy — this would lead to over-extension. For in that case, everything would be the cause of conjunction with everything. And thus, conjunction of one entity with a distinct entity is not at all established, since everything would have conjunction with everything.

body.text: na cāpi kāryakāraṇasambandhaḥ | krameṇa vedyamānatvāt sukhādinām | avikale hetau sati na yujyate tāvat kādācitkakāryasambhavaḥ, aviśiṣṭatvāt | parairanādheyātiśayo 'pratibaddhasāmarthyo vā khalvātmā kathaṃ sahakārikākāraṇamapekṣyakrameṇotpādayet, na hi sahakāriṇi tadapekṣā | duḥkhotpādahetutvād yadi baddhastadā sarvathā baddhatvānnaiva muktaḥ syāt, tatsvabhāvāparityāgāt, parityāge vā kathaṃ nityaḥ syāt | aduḥkhāvasthotpādahetutvād yadi muktastadā vimukta eva bhavenna kadācidapi baddhaḥ syāttadā kathaṃ tāvat kalpyeta ādheyanibandhanaṃ bandhamokṣatvamiti |
body.translated_text: Nor is there a cause-and-effect relation [between the self and pleasure, etc.]. Because pleasure and so on are cognized successively. When the cause is complete, the occasional occurrence of the effect is not tenable, since [the conditions] would be indistinguishable. The self, whose capacity is either not augmentable by others or not dependent [on conditions],

body.text: yadi caitanyādilakṣaṇatvenotpādasāmarthyena vā kartā syāttadā kartā eva sadā bhavet katha tāvad bhoktā? atha sukhādyutpādahetutvena yadi bhoktā syāttadā bhoktaiva bhavet kathaṃ tāvat kartā? kiñca kāpilaparikalpitasya (atmanaḥ) (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_120

children.text: ) sukhādibhirākāśavannirvikāratvena naiva khalu yujyate bhoktṛtvam, atiprasaṅgāt | sati vā vikāre nityatāhāniḥ | na khalu hetumātratayā kartā vā bhoktā vā, atiprasaṅgāt | tathaiva smṛtyādiṣvapi nāśrayitvamupayujyata iti yojyam |
