children.translated_text: since [the self] is unalterable like space with regard to pleasure and so on, the status of being an experiencer is certainly not tenable — because of over-extension. Or if there is alteration, then permanence is lost. And not merely by being a cause is one an agent or an experiencer — because of over-extension. Likewise, with regard to memory and other [mental functions], the substratum [i.e., the self]...

body.translated_text: If [the self] were an agent by virtue of its nature as consciousness, etc., or by the capacity to produce, then it would always be an agent — how then could it be an experiencer? And if it were an experiencer by virtue of being the cause of the production of pleasure and so on, then it would always be an experiencer — how then could it be an agent? Moreover,

body.text: tasmānnairātmyavādinyeva pakṣe bandhomokṣādivyavasthā yuktimatī | kāryakāraṇavaiśiṣṭayamātreṇa tasyā vyavasthāyā prabhāvitatvāt | sa ca kāryakāraṇabhāvastāvadanityeṣveva sambhavati, na khalu nityeṣu | teṣu nāsti kasyacidapi kāryasya krameṇotpādasāmarthyam, yathoktaṃ prāk | na cāpi yugapad, tathāvidhaphalotpādasamarthasvabhāvānugame phalotpādābhāvastāvanna yujyate prāgvat | ananugame ca prāksvabhāvatāhāniḥ | kramayaugapadyābhyāṃ vyatirikto nāstyeva kaścidākārāntaraḥ, yaḥ syādarthakriyāyāṃ prabhuviṣṇuḥ, parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvāttayoḥ | ata eva yāvantaḥ paraparikalpitā ākāśādayo 'kṣaṇikābhāvāste sarve arthakriyāsāmarthyahitatvād abhāvavyavahāraviṣayā ucyante paramavicakṣaṇairbauddhairiti | śaśaviṣāṇādāvapi abhāvavyavahāraprajñaptiḥ arthakriyāyāṃ sāmarthyābhāvamātranibandhanaiva, eatadbalenārthakriyāsamarthaviṣayikā khalu bhāvavyahāraprajñaptiḥ, parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvād bhāvābhāvayoḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is only in the position of the <s>nairātmyavādin</s> (proponent of non-self) that the establishment of bondage, liberation, and so forth is reasonable — because that establishment is effected merely through the specific differentiation of cause and effect. And that cause-and-effect relation is possible only among impermanent things, certainly not among permanent ones.

body.text: evaṃvidhe sarvasāmarthyaśūnye śaśaviṣāṇādyaviśeṣe 'pi 'bhāvaḥ'; iti nāma vyavahāre sati nāsti nāmni vivādaḥ | tathāpi arthakriyārthino hi prekṣāvantaḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_121

children.text: ) tathāvidhānupalambhasvabhāve vandhyāputrādyaviśeṣe ca bhāvavyavahāro na yujyata ityāhuḥ | ata eva nāsiddho hetuḥ | na cānaikāntikaḥ, ākāśādiṣvapi kartṛtvaprasaṅgāt | sapakṣe sattvānna ca viruddhaḥ | tasmādātmano lakṣaṇāntarābhāvād bandhyāputrasadṛśa eva | vinaśvaratve sati skandhāntargatā eva pudgalāḥ prasajyeran, sarvasaṃskṛtānāṃ skandhasaṃgṛhītatvāt | athāvinaśvaratve tāvat skandhāntargatadharmavisadṛśatvādarthāntarā eva te bhaveyuriti doṣo 'yamuktapūrva eva | ato nāsti kaścidanirvacanīyo bhāva iti | ataḥ 'sarve dharmā nirātmānaḥ'; iti bhagavataḥ siṃhanādaḥ samastatairthikakuñjaravṛndānāṃ bhīkaraḥ, anavamardanīyatvāt | alamativistareṇa |
children.translated_text: say that the conventional designation of 'entity' is not tenable for that which has the nature of being unapprehended, and which is no different from the son of a barren woman, etc. For this very reason, the reason [in the argument] is not unestablished. Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because agency would absurdly follow for space and so on as well. Since it exists in the positive instances (<s>sapakṣa</s>), it is not contradictory.

body.translated_text: In the case of such [an entity] that is devoid of all causal capacity and no different from a hare's horn, etc. — if there is a conventional usage of the name 'entity' (<s>bhāva</s>), there is no dispute about the name. Even so, the discerning, who are intent upon causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>),

body.text: 2. pāramitāyoga-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 2. The section on the practice of the perfections (<s>pāramitāyoga</s>):

body.text: pāramitāyogamadhikṛtyāha- api tu khalu punaḥ ityādi | etacca padadvayaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣasvabhāvātmakaṃ draṣṭavyam | dānaṃ dātavyaṃ na tuvastupratiṣṭhitena bodhisattvenetyarthaḥ | dānam ityanena trividhadānamadhikṛtya ṣaṭ pāramitā darśitāḥ na tu dānamātram | tatrāmiṣadānena dānapāramitā nirdiṣṭā, abhayadānena tāvad śīla-kṣāntipāramite, dharmadānena tu vīrya-dhyāna-prajñāpāramitāḥ | vīryābhāve dharmādāna-pravacanayoḥ parikhinnatvānna dharmaṃ deśayet | dhyānābhāve śraddhātirekakarmābhilaṣatayā saṃkliṣṭā bhaved deśanā | prajñāyāścābhāve sa tad viparītatayā dharmaṃ deśayet | tasmāt trayābhāve na sidhyati dharmadānam | vīryaṃ sarvatragamityapare |
body.translated_text: Regarding the practice of the perfections, he says 'But moreover...' and so on. These two terms should be understood as having the nature of the general and the specific. The meaning is: giving (<s>dāna</s>) should be practiced, but not by a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is established in [real] entities. By [the word] 'giving,' the three kinds of giving...

body.text: dānaṃ dātavyam ityanena ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu chanda-praṇidhānābhyāṃ kathaṃ sthātavyamiti nirdiṣṭam | na vastupratiṣṭhitena ityādinātra yogasamāpattyā (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_122

children.text: ) kathaṃ pratipattavyamityāveditam | evaṃ hi bodhisattvena dānaṃ dātavyam ityādinā vikṣepaṃ nigṛhya kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyamityetannirdiṣṭam | tatra na vastupratiṣṭhiteneti prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogasya yāthāvattvaṃ tāvannirdiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: it is made known how one should practice. For thus, by [the statement] 'giving should be practiced by a <s>bodhisattva</s>,' having restrained distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), it is indicated how the mind should be uplifted. Therein, 'not established in entities' [indicates] the practice of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom).

body.translated_text: By [the statement] 'giving should be practiced,' it is indicated how one should abide among the six perfections (<s>pāramitās</s>) through aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). By 'not established in entities' and so on, here through meditative attainment (<s>yogasamāpatti</s>),

body.text: tatra deya-dāyaka-pratigrāhakādivastuṣu yattattvato 'bhiniveśanaṃ tat pratiṣṭhānam | yadi bodhisattvaḥ vastunyabhiniviśya pāramitāyāṃ yuñjīta, mithyāyogobhavet, paramārthataḥ kasyacidapyabhiniveśyavastunaḥ sarvathābhāvena viparītābhiniveśāt, tassādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvabhāvataśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'establishment' (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) refers to the grasping in reality at objects such as the gift, the giver, the recipient, and so on. If a <s>bodhisattva</s>, grasping at entities, were to engage in the perfection, it would be a wrong practice (<s>mithyāyoga</s>), because ultimately there is no entity to be grasped.

body.text: tathā hi- paraiḥ paramārthataḥ iṣṭā vijñānavyatiriktā arthāstāvānna pratyakṣasiddhāḥ, arthāntareṇa jñānena grahaṇāyogāt | arthe sati sākāreṇa nirākāreṇa anyākāreṇa vā jñānena grahaṇamiti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ | tatra tāvanna sākāreṇa citravarṇādidarśanakāle ekajñānābhinnatvādākāraṇāmapyekatvaṃ prasajyeta, athavā ākārabhinnatvādākāravajjñānasyāpyanekātmakatvaṃ prasajyeta |
body.translated_text: For thus: The external objects accepted by others as ultimately real and distinct from consciousness — they are not established by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), because apprehension by a cognition that is different from the object is not tenable. Given that an object exists, there are three positions: apprehension by a cognition with form (<s>sākāra</s>), without form (<s>nirākāra</s>), or with a different form.

body.text: anekatvaṃ tāvanna yujyata eva, ekaikaparamāṇugrāhyajñānānubhavābhāvānna sidhyati tāvajjñānasyaikatvam, tadasiddhāvanekatvamapi khalvasiddham, ekaikasahaṃtisvarūpatvād anekasya | citrākāravyavasthāpanāyai anekajñānotpādaparikalpanayāpi jñānasya viṣayaṃ vyāpya sthitatvād grāhakajñānānāmutpādo 'pi na sambhavati, amūrttatvājjñānānām |
body.translated_text: Plurality is certainly not tenable — since the experience of a cognition apprehending each individual atom is not established, the unity of cognition is not established, and without that being established, plurality is also not established, since the many have the nature of each individual unit. The establishment of a variegated form...

body.text: anyacca, sārūpyaṃ tāvadekadeśena bhavet sarvātmanā vā | tatra na tāvat sarvātmanā- arthajjñānasyāpi jaḍasvabhāvaprasaṅgāt | na caikadeśena- ekasya tāvanniravayavatvād | vyāvṛttibhedenāṃśopacāre 'pi vastvādisārupyadharmāṇāṃ sarvatra (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_123

children.text: ) vidyamānatvāt sarveṇa sarvamavagamyeta | atha tadutpannaṃ tatsārūpyaṃ cetyetaddvayena vedayatīti arthasārupyasya samanastarapratyayasyāpi grāhakatvaprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: since [similarity] is present [everywhere], everything would be cognized by everything. If one says that [cognition] arises from that [object] and possesses similarity with that — then by this pair, [cognition] apprehends [the object]; [but in that case] there would be the absurd consequence that even a simultaneous condition possessing similarity with the object would be an apprehender.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, similarity (<s>sārūpya</s>) would be either partial or complete. In the first case, not complete — because cognition would absurdly become of an inert nature like the object. Nor partial — because a single [entity] has no parts. Even if parts are posited through differentiation of exclusions (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>),

body.text: satyapi sārūpye paramārthataḥ bāhyārtho na pratyakṣasiddhaḥ, nīlākārātmano jñānasya svasaṃviditatvāt | yato hi pratyakṣaiva nīlādivijñaptirnāparā | yattad vijñānaṃ tadevārthagrāhakamiti cet? bhavatu nāma prajñaptitaḥ, na tu paramārthatastad vedanam, ātmākārasya svasaṃviditatvāt, atyantaparokṣatvādarthānāṃ kathaṃ tadākāraṃ jñānaṃ bhavediti | svākārādhānena tāvadutpādako heturnaiva niyamena sidhyati, vyabhicārāt |
body.translated_text: Even granting similarity, ultimately the external object is not established by direct perception, because cognition whose nature is the form of blue is self-cognized. For direct perception itself is the awareness (<s>vijñapti</s>) of blue and so forth, and nothing else. If [one objects:] 'That very consciousness is what apprehends the object' — let it be so nominally, but ultimately that is not [real] awareness, because the self-form is self-cognized, and because [the external object] is utterly beyond [direct] experience.

body.text: paramāṇavaḥ khalu naiva sthūlapratītiviṣayaḥ, sūkṣmatvātteṣām | na ca saṃhitāḥ, tebhyo 'narthāntaratvāt vikalpaviṣayāṇām asattvācca | saṃhatārthāntaratve pṛthak pratibhāsaḥ syāt | āvṛtānāvṛtayośca virodhānnaiva tāvad yujyata ekatvam | anekatve saṃghātasya paramāṇureva sa syānna tvarthāntaraḥ |
body.translated_text: Atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>) are certainly never the object of gross perception, because of their subtlety. Nor are they in aggregation [as something distinct], because the aggregation would not be something different from them, and because objects of conceptual construction are unreal. If the aggregation were something different, each [atom] would appear separately. And due to the contradiction between being covered and uncovered, unity is certainly not tenable. In the case of plurality, the aggregate would be just atoms and nothing different.

body.text: na ca tāvannirākārapakṣaḥ- nīlādiṣvakiñcitkaratvāttasya | bhāvamātreṇa vedane sati sarvaiḥ sarvavedanaprasaṅgaḥ, aviśiṣṭatvāt sarvasya | ato nīlasaṃvedanamidam, na pītamiti vyavasthā na syāt, vyavasthāyāḥ kasyāpi hetuviśeṣasyābhāvāt | viśeṣasya kasyacidabhyupagame sa eva tāvat sākāratvābhyupagamaḥ | pratītisvabhāvamātre tāvad viśeṣābhāvājjñānātmani nākārātiriktaṃ bhedakamanyat syāt |
body.translated_text: Nor is the 'formless cognition' thesis [tenable] — because it would be ineffective with regard to blue and so forth. If awareness occurred through mere existence [without form], then everything would be aware of everything, because of the indistinguishability of all [bare existence]. Thus the determination 'this is the awareness of blue, not yellow' would not be possible, because there would be no distinguishing cause for such determination. If some distinguishing feature were accepted, that itself would be the acceptance of cognition having form (<s>sākāratva</s>).

body.text: naivānyākārapakṣaḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | evaṃ hi sati rūpaviṣayakamākāravijñānaṃ tāvat parīkṣāmarhati, tathā hi- na tāvat pratyakṣato 'rthaḥ sidhyati, nānumānādapi | apratyakṣasyārthasya jñānasya ca kenāpi hetunā sambandhāsiddheḥ | phalajñānād bhinnasya kāraṇamātratvānumāne neṣṭasiddhiḥ, itarasya samanantarapratyayasya vidyamānatvāt | itarat pramāṇaṃ nāsti, ato tāvannaiva sidhyati bāhyo 'rthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Nor is the 'other-form' thesis [tenable], due to overextension. For in that case, cognition having form regarding visible objects would first deserve examination. For the object is not established by direct perception, nor by inference either — since the connection between an object that is not directly perceived and cognition cannot be established by any reason. Inference of mere causality for [an object] different from the resultant cognition does not yield the desired proof, and [the inference of] the other [i.e., similarity]

body.text: na tāvat paramārthataḥ jñānasvabhāvatā pratyakṣeṇa sidhyati, addhaitasvabhāvatāyā asaṃviditatvāt, anyathā na ko 'pi tattvadraṣṭā syāt | nānumānenāpi evaṃvidhenākāreṇa kasyāpi hetoḥ sambandhasyāsiddheḥ |
body.translated_text: is not established ultimately by direct perception — the nature of cognition as non-dual is not cognized; otherwise everyone would be a perceiver of reality. Nor by inference either, because the connection of any reason with a form of this kind is not established.

body.text: nanvevaṃ kathaṃ saṃkleśavyavadāne syātāmiti cet? na, tvanmate tābhyāṃ saha tasya kasyacidapi sambandhasyāsiddhatvāt | tayoḥ paramārthataḥ kvacidapi vastuni (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_124

children.text: ) sambandhāsiddheḥ | na tāvat tadutpattilakṣaṇasambandhaḥ, sarvathā parokṣatvāttasya | parokṣeṇa saha sambandhastu na kenāpyarvāgdarśinā grahītuṃ śakyate | avidyādīnāmavicāraramaṇīyatve 'pi saṃkleśamūlatve nāsti virodhaḥ, avidyādau vicāreṇa tṛṣṇānivṛttau vyavadānam, tato vipakṣabhūtalakṣaṇam avicāraikaramaṇīyamupapadyate, tadā paramārthato vastvabhāvena kathaṃ tayorapyabhāvaprasaṅgaḥ | ye etayorekāntena nirhetukatvamabhyupagacchanti, teṣvevāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ, na tu saṃvṛtitaḥ pratītyasamutpādavādiṣu |
children.translated_text: is not established ultimately. The connection characterized by origination from that [object] is certainly not [established], because it is utterly beyond experience. And no one with limited vision can grasp a connection with what is beyond experience. Even though ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and the like are charming when unexamined, there is no contradiction in their being the root of affliction; when through examination of ignorance and the like there is cessation of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), there is purification — hence the characteristic of being opposed [to affliction] is non-examination

body.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'But then how would affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) be possible?' — No, because in your own position the connection of either of those with anything whatsoever is not established. The connection with anything whatsoever

body.text: ata eva paramārthataḥ bhāvasvabhāvasādhakaṃ kiñcidapi pramāṇaṃ nāsti, astyeva ca bādhakam | ityevaṃ tāvat- yadekānekasvabhāvavigataṃ tat paramārthato niḥsvabhāvam, gaganāravindavat | parairiṣṭāḥ sarve jñānajñeyātmakāḥ bhāvākārāḥ, ekānekasvabhāvaśūnyā ityato vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ, ekānekābhyāṃ vyāptatvāt svabhāvasya | dvayametat tatra nāsti | evaṃ tāvad rūpādyāyatanānāṃ bāhyavastūnāṃ naikatvam, āvṛtyanāvṛtyorviruddharmayostatropalabdhe | api ca, viruddhadharmasaṃsarge 'pyekatve viśvamapyekadravyaṃ syāt | tato yugapadutpattivināśau syātām |
body.translated_text: Therefore, there is no valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) whatsoever that establishes the essential nature of entities ultimately; rather, there is indeed a refuting [cognition]. Thus then — whatever is devoid of the nature of unity or plurality is ultimately without inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), like a sky-flower. All forms of entities — whether cognition or cognizable — as accepted by others, are empty of the nature of unity or plurality; hence the non-apprehension of the pervader [applies], since they are pervaded by either unity or plurality.

body.text: nānekatvamapi, tathā hi- anekasmin vibhajyamāne sati vibhaktāḥ paramāṇava eva syuḥ tataśca paurvāparyāvasthānaṃ na syānniravayavatvāt paramāṇūnām, cittacaitasikavat | tato diśaṃ vyāpya avasthitā na pratibhāseran | ata eva digbhāgabhedo 'bhyupagantavya eva | sati cābhyupagame kathaṃ nāma bhavedekatvam | ataḥ siddha eva tāvadekānekasvabhāvavirahatvaṃ bāhyārthānām |
body.translated_text: Nor is plurality [established] either. For when a plurality is divided, the divided [parts] would be just atoms. And then there could be no spatial arrangement, because atoms are partless — like mental events (<s>citta-caitasika</s>). Therefore they would not appear as occupying directions. Hence a distinction of directional parts must be accepted. But if it is accepted, how could there be unity?

body.text: nīlādipratibhāsino jñānasyāpi naikasvabhāvatvam, citrākāragrahitayāvabhāsyamānatvāt, bhinnasantānavarttyanekavijñānakṣaṇavat | yathāsaṃkhyam anekavijñānāni yugapat pravartanta ityapi vaktuṃ na yujyate niravayavānāmamūrtānāṃ khalu paurvāparyāvasthiterayuktatvāt | tathāvasthānābhāve na tathāvabhāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Even cognition that manifests blue and the like does not have a unitary nature, because it appears as apprehending variegated forms — like multiple momentary cognitions occurring in different mental continua. It is also not tenable to say that multiple cognitions arise simultaneously in a one-to-one correspondence, because for partless, immaterial [cognitions] spatial arrangement is untenable. Without such arrangement, there would be no such appearance.

body.text: atha syāt- vijñānaṃ tvekameva, mithyākārāṇāṃ tatrāvabhāsyamānatvānna nānātvadoṣa iti cet? sati caivaṃ kathaṃ te tatra bhāseran mṛṣāḥ | avabhāsa iti prakāśātmaka ucyate | tasya jñānagatadharmatve sati mithyākārāṇāṃ śaśaviṣāṇādivadatyantābhyāvaḥ syāditi kathamavabhāseranniti |
body.translated_text: Now if one were to say: 'Consciousness is indeed one; since false forms appear within it, there is no defect of plurality' — if so, how would those false [forms] appear within it? 'Appearance' is said to be of the nature of luminosity. If that is a property belonging to cognition, then false forms would be utterly absent like the horn of a hare — so how would they appear?

body.text: tataḥ prakāśātmakākārebhyaḥ mṛṣātvenābhyupetebhyaḥ kastāvadanyaḥ jñānasvabhāvaḥ sadbhūtaste 'vaśiṣyate, prakāśātmalakṣaṇatvād vijñānasya | nīlādayo 'pi prakāśātmakāḥ svabhāvenāvabhāsyamānatvāt | nīlādīnāṃ svasvabhāvād bhinnaṃ yadanyat prakāśarūpamiti sadbhūtaṃ kimapi nāti, anyavyavacchedāpekṣayā viśeṣe prāyaśo vyavahārāt |
body.translated_text: Then what other nature of cognition that is real would remain apart from the forms that are of the nature of luminosity yet accepted as false — since consciousness is defined by the character of luminosity? Blue and the like are also of the nature of luminosity, since they appear by their own nature. There is nothing real that is a form of luminosity different from the own-nature of blue and the like — [any such distinction being] merely a specific characterization relative to the exclusion of other [things].

body.text: viśeṣāṇāṃ mithyātve sarveṣāṃ mithyātvamativispaṣṭaṃ syāt | nirākārasya (mithyākārarasya) satyākārātmani (sākārātmani) jñāne kathaṃ niyamenāabhāsaḥ syāt, tayostāvat tādātmyalakṣaṇo vā tadutpattilakṣaṇo vā sambandha eva nāsti | sambandhābhāve na khalu yujyate 'vabhāsanam, atiprasaṅgāt | ata eva nāsti tāvadasiddho hetuḥ | bhāvānāmanyākārābhāvānnāpyaikāntikaḥ | na cāpi viruddha, sapakṣe sattvāt | ata eva yathā yathārthāścityante viśīryante tathā tathā | tathā coktam-
body.translated_text: If the particular forms are false, then the falsity of all [cognition] would be abundantly clear. How could a formless [cognition] have a necessary appearance in cognition whose nature is the real form? For between those two there is simply no connection — neither identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) nor origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>). Without a connection, appearance is certainly not tenable, due to overextension. Therefore there is no [such cognition].

children.translated_text: Just as in the examination of the essential nature of things there is no real nature,
so too, neither unity nor plurality of nature exists for them.

body.text: api cāryalaṅkāvatāre bhagavatoktam :
body.translated_text: Moreover, in the noble <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s> [<s>Sūtra</s>], the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

children.translated_text: Just as a form in a mirror, free from unity and otherness,

children.text: dṛśyate na ca tannāsti tathā cotpādalakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: is seen yet does not [truly] exist — such is the character of origination.
When examined by the intellect, [their] own-nature is not ascertained;
therefore they are taught as inexpressible and without own-nature.

body.text: tathā cāryamādhirājasūtre 'pi
body.translated_text: And likewise in the noble <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> also:

children.text: yathaiva ārdraṃ kadalīyaskandhaṃ sārārthikaḥ puruṣu vipāṭayet |
children.translated_text: Just as a man seeking the pith would split open a moist plantain stalk —

children.text: bahirvā adhyātma na sāramasti tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: neither externally nor internally is there pith: thus know all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) to be.

body.text: tasmāt sarvabhāvānāṃ māyāvadavicāraramaṇīyatvādanabhiniveśena dānaṃ dātavyam, na tu vastupratiṣṭhitena ityayamartho 'tra yuktisaṅgataḥ | evaṃ dānādiṣu yathā yogastathā ādarśitaḥ, nānyatra |
body.translated_text: Therefore, since all entities are charming when unexamined, like an illusion, giving (<s>dāna</s>) should be practiced without attachment, not by one who is established in [the reality of] things — this is the meaning that is here consistent with reasoning. Thus the proper manner regarding giving and the other [perfections] has been shown, and not otherwise.

body.text: yadi paramārthata kasyacidapi vastuno bhāvābhāvād vastupratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ na dātavyam, tadā avastvabhiniveśena tu dānasya kathaiva kā, ata eva na (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_127

children.text: ) kvacipratiṣṭhitena ityuktam | bodhisattvenābhāvavikalpo 'pi prahātavyaḥ, bhāvagrāhābhāve sati tasyāpyabhāvāt | saṃvṛtau tāvad deyadāyakādayo bhavantyeva | tato vastuno 'bhāve 'pi tāvadabhiniveśo na yujyata evetyabhiprāyaḥ | na rūpapratiṣṭhitena ityādinā bodhisattvena na kvacitpratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyamityeva vistareṇābhihitam |
children.translated_text: 'not established in anything' — so it is said. The <s>bodhisattva</s> should also abandon the conceptual construction of non-existence, because in the absence of grasping at existence, that [non-existence grasping] too ceases. In conventional [truth], the gift, the giver, and so on certainly exist. Therefore, even when things are [ultimately] non-existent, attachment is not tenable — this is the intent. By [the statement] 'not established in form' and so forth, [it is meant that] giving should be practiced by the <s>bodhisattva</s> not established in anything.

body.translated_text: If, because no thing whatsoever exists or does not exist ultimately, giving should not be practiced by one established in things — then what occasion could there even be for giving with attachment to non-entity? Therefore

body.text: dharmaḥ ityanena śabdena dharmāyatanaṃ parigṛhyate, āyatanena prapañcaḥ abhivyajyate, ataścakṣurādīni ādhyātmikāyatanāni nocyante | anutpādādayo vikalpā api na karaṇīyā iti nidarśanārtha subhūte, yathā ityādyuktam | nimittaṃ tu vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgaṃ vānutpādādi, tasyodgrahaṇaṃ saṃjñā | tatra nirvikalpantu apratiṣṭhitam | ata eva na kvacit pratiṣṭhitena iti nirdiṣṭam | athavā samagreṇaitena gāmbhīryamasya vyapadiṣṭam, adhyāropāvādāntau pratiṣiddhau ceti |
body.translated_text: By the word "dharma," the dharmāyatana (mental-object sense-base) is encompassed; through the sense-base, conceptual proliferation (prapañca) is manifested; therefore the internal sense-bases such as the eye and others are not mentioned. Conceptual constructions such as non-arising and the like should also not be made—to illustrate this, he says "<s>Subhūti</s>, just as..." and so forth. A sign (nimitta) is either the particular characteristic of an entity or an indication such as non-arising and the like; grasping at that [sign] is <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception/concept). Non-conceptual [awareness], however, is non-established [in anything]. For this very reason, "not established in anything" has been stated. Alternatively, by all of this together, the profundity of this [teaching] has been indicated, and the two extremes of <s>adhyāropa</s> (superimposition) and <s>apavāda</s> (nihilism) have been negated.

body.text: asmin darśane upalambhakānāṃ jñānapuṇyasambhārapāripūroyogyatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, evaṃ pūjānugrahakāmyayā yad dīyate, tenātitarāṃ samprasādo janyate, na tu deya-dāyaka-pratigrāhakānupalambhe pratiṣṭhitatvena, evaṃ hyabhāvaḥ, deyādyanupalabdhatvād viṣayasyābhāvācca | prathamapakṣe kenāpi kasyacidapi deyasyābhāvāt puṇyābhāvaḥ prasajyate, (dvitīyapakṣe tāvat) bodhisattvaiḥ yo hi sattvārthaṃ śrama āsthitaḥ, so 'pi vyarthaḥ syāt sattvābhāvāt | ata eva nābhāvamātram |
body.translated_text: In this view, the capacity for fulfilling the accumulations of wisdom and merit by those who grasp at [real] apprehension is negated. Thus, what is given out of desire for worship and benefit generates even greater faith—but not through being established in the non-apprehension of the gift, the giver, and the recipient, for in that case there would be non-existence, since the gift and the like are unapprehended and the object is non-existent. In the first position, since no one has anything to give to anyone, the absence of merit would absurdly follow; in the second position, the effort that <s>bodhisattvas</s> have undertaken for the sake of beings would also be pointless, since beings do not exist. For this very reason, [the teaching is] not mere non-existence.

body.text: bhagavatā deyādivastūnāṃ dṛṣṭatvāt, na ca viṣayasyāpyabhāvaḥ | anyathā kathaṃ bhagavatārthijanebhyaḥ putrādayaḥ pradattā iti sarvāṇyetāni codyāni manasi nidhāya tatkasya hetoḥ? iti pṛcchāyāṃ yaḥ subhūte, bodhisattvaḥ ityādinā visarjitam |
body.translated_text: Because the <s>Bhagavān</s> has seen the entities such as the gift and the like; nor is there non-existence of the object [either]. Otherwise, how could the <s>Bhagavān</s> have given sons and the like to those who sought them? Holding all these objections in mind, when the question "For what reason?" is asked, it is answered with "<s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>..." and so forth.

body.text: ayamabhiprāyaḥ- samyagdṛṭivihitāni dānādīni suviśuddhatayā viśiṣṭeṣṭaphalāni abhinirvartayanti, na viparītatayā samudbhūtāni, mithyādṛṣṭipravartitaśīlāṅgādivat | deyādivastūni yathoktanyāyena kathañcidapyasattvāt mithyopalabdhānyeva, marīcikāsu udakopalambhavat | tasmāt tadudbhūtaḥ sarvapāramitāidhistāvad ātmātmīyaviparyasodgatasodgatadānādivadaviśuddhahetoḥ sambhūtatvāt kṣīṇabalaḥ, deyādyupalakṣaṇaprāptānupalambhastu bhūrtārthagocaratvādaviparyastaḥ, maricikāyāmudakānupalabdhivat | tasmādupacitahetusambhūtadānādīni bṛhatphalāni, puṣṭabījābhinirvṛttāṅkurādivat | ata eva anupalambhapratiṣṭhitāni dānādīni samyagdṛṣṭisambhūtānīti vipaścitsu prasādātiśayaṃ janayanti, nānyeṣu |
body.translated_text: The purport is this: giving and the like, performed with right view, being supremely pure, produce superior desired fruits, not those arising from a contrary [view], like the limbs of morality and the like impelled by wrong view. The entities such as the gift and the like, being in no way existent according to the stated reasoning, are merely falsely apprehended, like the apprehension of water in a mirage. Therefore, all the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) arising from that [false apprehension] are of diminished power, having arisen from an impure cause like giving and the like arising from the perversion of self and "mine"—while non-apprehension that reaches the designation of the gift and the like has a real object and is non-perverted, like the non-apprehension of water in a mirage. Therefore, giving and the like arising from accumulated causes produce great fruit, like sprouts and the like arising from nourished seeds. For this very reason, giving and the like established in non-apprehension, having arisen from right view, generate an extraordinary faith in the wise, but not in others.

body.text: tataśca dānādiṣvapravṛttatayā puṇyābhāvo deyādīnāṃ caikāntābhāvo neṣyate, saṃvṛtisattvābhyupagamāt | asamāhitāvasthāyāṃ māyāvadupalambhānna sarvatrānupalambhaḥ | tadā cādhimuktitaḥ prādurbhāvādevānupalambho vyavasthāpyate | samāhitāvasthāyām upalambhasyātyantābhāvamātram, tadā dānādiṣu pravṛttirnābhyupeyate prayogāvasthāyāṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 129]

children.text: ) vyutthitāvasthāyāṃ vā kriyayopālambho na yujyate | ato mahāphalatvāya pāramitāyogasyaidāryamabhidhīyate | saṃvṛtau kāryakāraṇabhāvasyopadarśanād apavādānto 'pi niṣidhyate |
children.translated_text: Or in the post-meditative state, the fault [of grasping] through action is not applicable. Therefore, for the sake of great fruit, the nobility of the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) is declared. Since the cause-and-effect relationship is shown in conventional [truth], the extreme of nihilism (<s>apavāda</s>) is also negated.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, absence of merit due to non-engagement in giving and the like, and absolute non-existence of the gift and the like, are not accepted, because of the acceptance of beings in conventional [truth]. In the non-concentrated state, since there is apprehension like an illusion, non-apprehension does not [apply] everywhere. At that time, non-apprehension is established precisely through the arising of conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>). In the concentrated state, there is merely the absolute absence of apprehension; at that time, engagement in giving and the like is not accepted. In the preparatory state

body.text: 3. rūpakāyāptikāmatā-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 3. The station of desire for attaining the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body):

body.text: tridhā puṇyamākāśasamaṃ bhavati- sarvatragodārākṣayatvaiḥ | laukikalokottarapuṇyaprasavanāt sarvatragatvam, laukikaṃ tāvat puṇyamasamāhitāvasthāyāṃ prasūyate, lokottaraṃ tu samāhitāvasthāyāmeva | viśiṣṭa-viśiṣṭataragamanādudāratvam | yāvatsaṃsāramaparyādānādakṣayatvam | tadabhāvānna rūpapratiṣṭhitena dānaṃ dātavyamiti bodhisattvaḥ tathāgatarūpakāyāptikāmanayā dānādiṣu kathaṃ pravarteteti cediti codyamāśaṅkaya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādinā rūpakāyāptikāmatā sthānaṃ nirdiṣṭam | arthato 'tra rūpakāye tathāgatatvābhimānalakṣaṇo vipakṣo 'pākriyate | lakṣaṇasampadā iti nimittamātrābhidhānena tathāgatasya nikhilo rūpakāyaḥ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanairalaṅkṛtaḥ paridīpitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Merit becomes equal to space in three ways: through being all-pervading, vast, and inexhaustible. All-pervasiveness is through the production of worldly and supramundane merit: worldly merit arises in the non-concentrated state, while supramundane [merit] arises only in the concentrated state. Vastness is through going to progressively more distinguished [states]. Inexhaustibility is through not being depleted as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> [continues]. Because of the absence of that [fruit if giving is established in form], "giving should not be given by one established in form"—to the objection "If the <s>bodhisattva</s>, out of desire to attain the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s>, engages in giving and the like, how then [should he proceed]?" anticipating this objection, by "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?" and so forth, the station of desire for attaining the <s>rūpakāya</s> is indicated. In meaning, the opponent characterized by the conceit of <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood regarding the <s>rūpakāya</s> is refuted here. By "the perfection of marks" (<s>lakṣaṇasampad</s>), through the designation of mere signs, the entire <s>rūpakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, adorned with marks and minor marks, is illuminated.

body.text: tatra lakṣaṇāni tāvat cakrāṅkahastapādatādīni dvātriṃśat padabāhulyabhiyā nollikhyante, sūtreṣu yathoktānī tathaivāvadheyāni | sthānasthottaptapūrṇatvena niṣpattiḥ | (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 130]

children.text: ) aśītiranuvyañcanāni tāmravarṇanakhādīni, yathāsūtraṃ jñātavyāni | tāni lakṣanādīnyapi māyānirmitabuddhalakṣaṇavanmithyaiva | ata eva tathāvidhe rūpakāye chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti nirdeśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), such as copper-colored nails and the like, should be known as [stated] in the <s>sūtras</s>. Those marks and the like are merely false, like the marks of a magically created <s>Buddha</s>. For this very reason, the instruction is that one should abide in such a <s>rūpakāya</s> through aspiration and resolve.

body.translated_text: Among these, the marks are the thirty-two, such as the wheel-marked hands and feet, and the like—they are not written out for fear of excessive length of text, but should be understood just as stated in the <s>sūtras</s>. Their accomplishment is through being established, risen, fully heated, and complete.

body.text: athemāni lakṣaṇāni paramāṇusañcayasvabhāvāni vā tadārabdhāvayavirūpāṇi vā bhaveyuriti? na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣa, paramāṇūnāṃ pūrvameva nirastatvāt | nāpi dvitīyaḥ, asati cārambhake tadārabdhāvayavino 'pyabhāvāt, pūrvoktāvaraṇādiviruddharmopalambhācca | taduddiṣṭenābhihito 'bhiprāyaḥ | etad vicintya subhūtirāha no hīdam iti vyaktīkṛtam |
body.translated_text: Now, would these marks be of the nature of aggregations of atoms, or would they be composite forms composed of those [atoms]? The first position is not [tenable], since atoms have already been refuted. Nor is the second, since if the component [atoms] do not exist, the composite composed of those [components] also does not exist, and because contradictory properties such as the aforementioned obstructions are apprehended. The purport indicated by that has been stated. Reflecting on this, <s>Subhūti</s> says "No indeed"—thus making [the answer] explicit.

body.text: yadi lakṣaṇāni mṛṣā bhaveyustarhi kathaṃ bhagavatā tattatsūtreṣu lakṣaṇāni samupadiṣṭānīti cintayan tatkasya hetoḥ iti pṛṣṭvaivaṃ saivālakṣaṇasampad ityāha | sā lakṣaṇasampat tāvannoktā paramārthataḥ | māyānirmitabuddhavadityanena mṛṣāsvabhāvatvamātramuktamityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: If the marks were false, then how were the marks taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the various <s>sūtras</s>?—thinking thus and having asked "For what reason?", he says "That very non-mark perfection..." The mark-perfection has not been stated as [existing] ultimately. By [the analogy of] "like a magically created <s>Buddha</s>," only the nature of being false has been stated—that is the meaning.

body.text: āryasubhūtinoktamevārtha paripūrayituṃ bhagavatā yāvat ityādyāha | yāvallakṣaṇasampad iti paramārthato yāvallakṣanasampatsvabhiniveśaḥ, tāvanmithyābhiniveśa evetyarthaḥ, yathoktameva pūrvam | yāvallakṣaṇasampad iti tadvīparītatayā abhihitetyavagantavyam | etena yogasamāpattyā kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti taddeśitam | kathamantadvayaṃ parivarjya cittaṃ pragrahītavyamiti tannirdiṣṭam | evam iti māyānirmitabuddhavallakṣaṇatastathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | anenāpavādānto nirākriyate, saṃvṛtau bhagavato rūpakāyaspāpratyākhyānāt | alakṣaṇaṃ tāvat paramārthe draṣṭavyam, kasyāpi lakṣaṇasyāsiddhatvāt | anena tāvat samāropānto nirākriyate | tathāgatasya rūpakāyāvāptaye praṇidhānaistvaudāryamuktam | tadanupalambhatayā ca gāmbhīryam | rūpakāyāptikāmatāsthānaṃ tāvaduktam |
body.translated_text: To complete the meaning stated by the noble <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says "as much as" and so forth. "As much as the perfection of marks" means: ultimately, as much as there is attachment to the perfection of marks, that much is merely false attachment—that is the meaning, just as stated before. "As much as the perfection of marks" should be understood as stated in the opposite sense [i.e., the non-mark perfection is the true perfection]. By this, how one should practice through <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) has been taught. How the mind should be taken hold of while avoiding both extremes has been indicated. "Thus" [means]: the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be seen from [the perspective of] marks as being like a magically created <s>Buddha</s>. By this, the extreme of nihilism is refuted, since the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s> in conventional [truth] is not denied. Ultimately, however, non-mark should be seen, since no mark whatsoever is established. By this, the extreme of superimposition is refuted. The nobility [of the bodhisattva path] is expressed through vows for attaining the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s>. And through its non-apprehension, the profundity [is expressed]. The station of desire for attaining the <s>rūpakāya</s> has thus been stated.

body.text: 4. dharmakāyāptikāmatāsthānam : (a) pravacanadharmakāyaḥ
body.translated_text: 4. The station of desire for attaining the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body): (a) The <s>pravacanadharmakāya</s> (doctrinal truth body)

body.text: dvividhaḥ khalu dharmakāyaḥ- pravacanadharmakāyaḥ, adhigamadharmakāyaśca | adhigamadharmakāyo 'pi dvividhaḥ-jñānahetukaḥ puṇyahetukaśca | tatrānāgate puruṣeṣu pañcakaṣāyāṇāmādhikyādevaṃvidhadharmaratnasya atyantagambhīrodāraphalatvāt pravacanadharmakāye 'nāptatvāśaṅkayā asti iti pṛṣṭavān | asti iti padaṃ tu kecit sattvāḥ ye imeṣvevaṃrūpeṣu sūtrāntapadeṣu bhāṣyamāṇeṣu bhūtasaṃjñāmutpādayiṣyanti ityarthapadena yojyam | paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyām ityatra śatānāṃ pañcakaṃ pañcaśatī, bhagavatāṃ śāsanaṃ pañcaśatavarṣāṇi sthāsyatīti prasiddheḥ | ata eva paścimeti viśeṣaṇaṃ vihitam | tasmin kāle pañcakaṣāyāṇāmadhimātratā bhavati |
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmakāya</s> is indeed twofold: the <s>pravacanadharmakāya</s> (doctrinal truth body) and the <s>adhigamadharmakāya</s> (realization truth body). The realization truth body is also twofold: that caused by wisdom and that caused by merit. There, among people in the future, because of the predominance of the five corruptions (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>), because this jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> produces an extremely profound and vast fruit, due to the suspicion that the <s>pravacanadharmakāya</s> might not be attained, he asked "Does [it exist]?" The word "does exist" should be connected with the meaning-passage: "There will be some beings who, when such <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourse) passages are being spoken, will generate a perception of truth." "In the last five hundred" means: a group of five hundreds is <s>pañcaśatī</s>; since it is well known that the teaching of the <s>Bhagavāns</s> will last five hundred years, for that reason the qualifier "last" is applied. At that time, the five corruptions are at their maximum intensity.

body.text: saddharmavipralopastāvad adhimukti-vācana-svādhyāya-upadeśa-ākhyāna-śravaṇa-cintādīnāṃ hāniḥ | evaṃ iti gambhīrodārārthaḥ | sūtrāntapadeṣu iti sūtrāntadeśanāvācaḥ, tābhirarthasya pratipādyamānatvāt jñāpyamānatvācca | anena nimittamātrābhidhānena samastapravacanadharmakāyastāvat paridīpyate | athavā sūtrāntapadeṣu ityabhidhiyamānārthakeṣu | asmin kathane 'evam'; ityanena tāvad gambhīraudārye yojanīye | bhāṣyamāṇeṣu iti prathamatayā abhidhiyamāneṣu | dvītīyatayā (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 132]

children.text: ) arthapratipādakeṣvityarthaḥ | arthato 'viparyayastasaṃjñaivātra bhūtasaṃjñetyabhidhīyate na tu śabdābhiniveśamātram 'ayaṃ bhūtaḥ'; iti saṃjñā | anena tāvadarthasiddhau abhūtasaṃjñā nirākriyate |
children.translated_text: ) [the words] 'in those that convey the meaning' — this is the sense. The non-distortion of the meaning is what is here called <s>bhūtasaṃjñā</s> (true conception), not the mere verbal attachment [thinking] 'this is true' — that is [not true] <s>saṃjñā</s> (conception). By this, for the establishment of the meaning, <s>abhūtasaṃjñā</s> (false conception) is first refuted.

body.translated_text: The deterioration of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharmavipralopa</s>) is the decline of faith, recitation, self-study, instruction, exposition, hearing, reflection, and the like. "Thus" refers to the profound and vast meaning. "In the <s>sūtrānta</s> passages" means: the words of the <s>sūtrānta</s> teaching; since the meaning is being conveyed and made known through those [words]. By this designation of mere signs, the entire <s>pravacanadharmakāya</s> is illuminated. Alternatively, "in the <s>sūtrānta</s> passages" means: in those whose meaning is being expressed. In this discourse, "thus" should be connected with profundity and vastness. "Being spoken" means: being expounded in the first [manner]. In the second [manner],

body.text: sarvatrāpratihatajñānena tān bhāvinaḥ (sattvān) pratyakṣavad dṛṣṭavā bhagavān sūbhūtisaśayaṃ parihartuṃ bhaviṣyanti ityāha | mahāsattvāḥ iti teṣāṃ bodhisattvaguṇānāṃ sampradarśanārthamuktam | te 'pi yathā pratipannāḥ, yādṛśena ca hetunā sampratipannāḥ, yāddṛśena kalyāṇamitreṇa parigṛhītāḥ, yathā vā bhūtasaṃjñayā saṃjñitāstān bhagavān paridīpitaṃvān | śīlavantaḥ guṇavantaḥ prajñāvantaśca ityanena tu kramaśo 'dhiśīlādhicittādhiprajñāśceti śikṣātrayapratiprattisamanvitāḥ nirdiṣṭāḥ | śīlaprajñayośca pṛthaguktatvād guṇastāvadatra dhyānajo grāhyaḥ, gobalīvardanyāyeneti |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having seen those future [beings] as if directly perceived through his knowledge unobstructed everywhere, in order to remove the doubt of <s>Subhūti</s>, says 'there will be.' '<s>Mahāsattvas</s>' (great beings) is said for the purpose of displaying the qualities of those <s>bodhisattvas</s>. How they have practiced, by what kind of cause they have practiced well, by what kind of spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) they have been embraced, and how they have conceived with <s>bhūtasaṃjñā</s> (true conception) — all this the <s>Bhagavān</s> has illuminated. 'Endowed with morality, endowed with qualities, endowed with wisdom' — by this, they are taught as being endowed with the practice of the three trainings: <s>adhiśīla</s> (higher morality), <s>adhicitta</s> (higher mind), and <s>adhiprajñā</s> (higher wisdom), in that order. Since morality and wisdom are mentioned separately, the 'quality' here should be understood as that born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), by the principle of the ox and the bull.

body.text: kleśavati paścimakāle tu kathaṃ tathāvidhaśīlādiguṇavanto bhaviṣyantīti cintayitvā sūbhūte ityādyāha | paryupāsitāḥ iti cīvara-piṇḍapātādibhiḥ paryūpāsitāḥ, chatradhvajapatākādibhiśca pūjitā bhaviṣyanti | avaropitakuśalamūlāḥ tāvadavavādamanuśāsanīṃ ca śirasādāya śīlādiguṇasampadbhyaḥ prayatnavanto draṣṭavyāḥ | teṣāṃ tato 'pi bahutaraṃ puṇyamabhidhātuṃ anekabuddhaśatasahasraḥ ityuktam | (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_133

children.text: ) anena teṣāṃ hetusiddhiḥ saṃdarśitā | jñātāste tathāgatena iti nāmānyāśayāśca | dṛṣṭāste tathāgatena iti kāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: By this, the establishment of the cause for those [<s>bodhisattvas</s>] has been shown. 'They are known by the <s>Tathāgata</s>' [means he knows] their names and dispositions. 'They are seen by the <s>Tathāgata</s>' [means he sees] their physical forms.

body.translated_text: Reflecting 'how could beings endowed with such qualities of morality and the like exist in the last age beset with afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>)?', he says '<s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth. '<s>Paryupāsitāḥ</s>' means they will have attended [<s>Buddhas</s>] with robes, alms-food, and the like, and will have worshipped them with parasols, banners, flags, and the like. Those who have planted roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) should be understood as those who, having received admonition and instruction upon their heads, are diligent in the accomplishments of morality and other qualities. To express that their merit is even more abundant than that, 'many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>' is stated.

body.text: anena tāvat kalyāṇamitraparigṛhītā ioti darśitam | tacca samprasthitānāṃ protsāhanārtham, viprasthitānāṃ hrīsañjananārthamāha | anyathā sarveṣāṃ jñānāt jñānāt sarvajño bhagavāniti deśanayā ko viśeṣo darśito bhavet, athavā tatteṣāṃ bhavyatvaṃ yat tatpramukhaṃ kṛtvā deśanā pravartitetyavagantavyam | bhavyā jñātā iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | atasteṣāmaśeṣaṃ puṇyaskandhasaṅgrahaṃ darśayituṃ sarve te sattvāḥ ityāha | prasaviṣyanti iti puṇyotpādakālaḥ, pratigrahīṣyanti iti nirodhakāle tadvāsanāḥ parigrahīṣyanti |
body.translated_text: By this, it has been shown that [they are] embraced by a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). And that is said for the purpose of encouraging those who have set forth [on the path] and for the purpose of generating shame in those who have strayed. Otherwise, since the <s>Bhagavān</s> is omniscient through knowing all, what distinction would be shown by the teaching 'he knows'? Alternatively, it should be understood that the teaching was set forth with their capacity as the principal [consideration]. 'Those capable are known' — this completes the sentence. Therefore, to show the entirety of their accumulation of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>), he says 'all those beings.' 'Will produce' indicates the time of generating merit; 'will receive' indicates that at the time of cessation they will receive the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) thereof.

body.text: ebhiḥ sarvairabhūtasaṃjñāṃ nirākṛtya bhūtasaṃgyotpādane chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamityādarśitaṃ tathā sthānasyāsyaudāryamapi paridīpitam | tatkasya hetoḥ? te anekabuddhaśatasahasraparyupāsitāḥ kathaṃ jñāsyanta iti jñāpakahetau paripṛṣṭe 'tra teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām ityādyāha | anena tavat yogasamāpattau kathaṃ pratittavyamityetat prakāśitam, gambhīratā cāpyabhihitā |
body.translated_text: By all of these, having refuted <s>abhūtasaṃjñā</s> (false conception), it has been shown that one should abide through desire (<s>chanda</s>) and aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) in generating <s>bhūtasaṃjñā</s> (true conception), and the nobility of this station has also been illuminated. 'For what reason?' — when the question is asked regarding the cause by which it will be known how they have attended many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, he says 'of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>' and so forth. By this, how one should practice in <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) has been made clear, and the profundity has also been stated.

body.text: ahamityātmagrahaṇam ātmasaṃjñā sā | mameti grahaṇaṃ sattvasaṃjñā, tasyaivātmana ā sthitiṃ parigrahaḥ jīvasaṃjñā, punaḥ punaḥ gatiṣu gamanādānaṃ pudgalasaṃjñā | yadi nāsti ātmādisaṃjñā tarhi kiṃ śrāvakādivad asti rūpādidharmasaṃjñā? iti cintāyāṃ na dharmasaṃjñā ityuktam | paramārthataḥ kasyacidapi dharmasyābhāvādityabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The grasping of 'I' is the apprehension of self — that is <s>ātmasaṃjñā</s> (self-conception). The grasping of 'mine' is <s>sattvasaṃjñā</s> (being-conception); the clinging to that very self as enduring is <s>jīvasaṃjñā</s> (life-conception); the taking on of going again and again through the destinies of existence is <s>pudgalasaṃjñā</s> (person-conception). If there is no <s>ātmasaṃjñā</s> (self-conception) and the like, then does there exist a <s>dharmasaṃjñā</s> (dharma-conception) regarding form and the like, as with <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and others? — to this reflection, 'there is no <s>dharmasaṃjñā</s>' is stated. The intent is: because ultimately no <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) whatsoever exists.

body.text: atha kim ucchedavādināmiva abhāvasaṃjñā? iti cintāyāṃ evaṃ nādharmasaṃjñā pravartate ityuktam | saṃvṛtau avicāraramaṇīyatayā dharmāṇāṃ sadbhāvāt saṃvṛtipathasthitebhyastāvad adharmasaṃjñā naiva yuktimatī, na tu paramārthajñānasthitebhyaḥ | tanniṣedhānna kaścid dharma upalabhyate yatrādharmasaṃjñā pravarteta, dharmāgrahaṇe tadabhāvāt | viṣayābhāvaniṣedhastu na kutrāpi sambhavati, tadyathā satye 'pi vijñaptimātre vijñaptimātrateyamiti vikalpayan na vijñaptimātratāyāṃ sthitaḥ, evameva satye 'pyadharme 'dharmabodhasya tatrāvasthānāsambhavāt sarvaṃ samānam |
body.translated_text: Then is there a conception of non-existence (<s>abhāvasaṃjñā</s>), as with the nihilists? — to this reflection, 'thus no <s>adharmasaṃjñā</s> (non-dharma conception) operates' is stated. Because in <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional truth), <s>dharmas</s> exist as charming when unexamined, for those established on the path of conventional [truth], <s>adharmasaṃjñā</s> is certainly not reasonable — but not for those established in <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate) knowledge. By the negation of that, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is apprehended in which <s>adharmasaṃjñā</s> would operate, because in the non-apprehension of <s>dharma</s>, that [non-dharma conception] is absent. The negation of the non-existence of the object is not possible anywhere — just as, even when consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>) is true, one who conceptualizes 'this is consciousness-only' is not established in consciousness-only; in exactly the same way, even when <s>adharma</s> (non-dharma) is true, since establishment in the cognition of <s>adharma</s> there is impossible, all [cases] are alike.

body.text: yadyātmādīnāmasattvaṃ tadā tatra tatsaṃjñāyā apravṛtau satyāṃ 'ātmaiva rūpamidam'; ityādikaṃ nāmamātramiti nāmābhiniveśasaṃjñā teṣāṃ bhavediti matvā saṃjñāpi ityuktam | nāmnastāvad rūpaskandhāntarbhūtatvād rūpādivad mithyātvameva, viprayuktamapi prajñaptimātramiti | tasmāt saṃjñāpi mithyābhiniveśa evetyabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: If self and the like are non-existent, then when the conception of those does not operate, [one might think] 'self is just this form' — such a conception would be mere name-clinging (<s>nāmābhiniveśasaṃjñā</s>), [thinking it] to be merely a name. Having considered this, 'even the conception' is stated. Since name is included within the aggregate of form (<s>rūpaskandha</s>), it is false just like form and the like; even as a dissociated [entity], it is mere designation (<s>prajñaptimātra</s>). Therefore, the intent is that even the conception is nothing but false clinging (<s>mithyābhiniveśa</s>).

body.text: yadyevaṃ tarhi tasyāmavasthāyāṃ sarvasaṃjñāvigamād mṛta-nirodhasamāpannapudgalavad yogino 'bhāva eva syāditi nāpi..... nāaṃjñā pravartate ityuktam | yena te yogino bhavanti, tacca yogijñānaṃ tathyasaṃvṛtisvabhāvamiti | vyutthāne śuddhalaukikajñānamudbhavatīti, anyathā ahetukameva tad bhavet | yad yogijñānaṃ saṃvṛtisvabhāvaṃ tat kenāvagamyata iti cet? tenaiva hetunā | yathā pratyātmavedyatayā pudgalanairātmāvabodhena ātmasthitaṃ pudgalanairātmyamadhigamyate, atrāpi tattulyam | jñānaṃ saṃvittiśca na saṃvṛtau nābhyupagamyete | yoginā svalakṣaṇapratyabhimukhīkaraṇāt tatrasthaṃ nairātmyaṃ nopalabhyate, tadānīmatītādestāvadasaṃnihitatvādanantatvācca |
body.translated_text: If so, then in that state, through the departure of all conceptions, the <s>yogin</s> would simply be non-existent, like a dead person or one who has entered the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) — [to counter this,] 'nor does... conception operate' is stated. That by which those <s>yogins</s> exist is <s>yogijñāna</s> (yogic cognition), and that is of the nature of authentic conventional truth (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>). Upon emergence [from meditation], pure mundane knowledge arises; otherwise, it would be entirely without cause. If one asks: by what is it known that <s>yogijñāna</s> is of conventional nature? — by that very reason. Just as through the self-experienced cognition of <s>pudgalanairātmya</s> (non-self of persons), the <s>pudgalanairātmya</s> established in the self is realized, here too it is the same. Knowledge and awareness (<s>saṃvitti</s>) are not denied in conventional [truth]. Because the <s>yogin</s> directly faces the particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) established therein is not apprehended, since at that time past and other [moments] are not present and because of their infinity.

body.text: katha tarhi? niḥsvabhāvatāvicāreṇa tadgocarībhūtānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sāmānyena nairātmasaṅgrahāt yā khalu vyavasthā saiva yugapadulambhanam | teṣāṃ tajjñānamapi paramārthato 'viṣaya eva, (tathāpi) satyasvapnajñānavadavisaṃvādakatvena prāmāṇyaṃ vyavasthāpyate | sāmānyena tatra tadātmabhāvo 'pi saṃgṛhyate, na tatra pṛthak tadālambakatvam | tasmāt sati nairātmyadvayāvabodhe teṣāmanekaśatasahasrabuddhānāṃ paryupāsanaṃ pratīyate | buddhānāmaparyupāsanayā tāvanna sambhavati tadavabodhaḥ tairthikavat | sa tu saṃsāre na ucito bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ | anayā yogasamāpattyā kathaṃ pratipattavyaṃ kīdṛśyā ca bhūtasaṃjñayā tat saṃjñātavyamiti saṃdarśitaṃ tadgāmbhīryamityapi ca paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: How then? Through the investigation of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>), by the general inclusion of all <s>dharmas</s> that have become the objects [of that investigation] under <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self), that very determination is the simultaneous apprehension. The knowledge of those [<s>dharmas</s>] too is ultimately without object; [nevertheless], like knowledge in a true dream, its validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is established through being non-deceiving. In general, the self-nature of that [knowledge] too is included therein — there is no separate objectification of it there. Therefore, when the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self [of persons and dharmas]) is realized, the attendance upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> by those [<s>bodhisattvas</s>] is understood. Without attending upon <s>Buddhas</s>, that realization is impossible, as with the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). But that [realization] is not appropriate in <s>saṃsāra</s> [without such attendance] — this is the intent. By this <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment), how one should practice, and with what kind of <s>bhūtasaṃjñā</s> (true conception) one should conceive — this has been demonstrated, and the profundity thereof has also been illuminated.

body.text: ātmādīnāmasattve teṣāmātmādisaṃjñāyā abhāvāt padasamudāyādibhiḥ ātmatva sūktaṃ duraktaṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ dharmādharmasaṃjñaṃ kiṃ teṣu niyamena na pravartate? naivam, yadi bodhisattvānā na bhavet tatra saṃjñā, (tarhi) ayuktayupapannatīrthakaradharmān parityajya bhagavaddeśiteṣu dharmeṣu tadadhigamāya kathaṃ chanda utpādanīya ityāśaṅkāyāṃ tatkasya hetoḥ? iti tatsamādhānāya sacet subhūte ityāha |
body.translated_text: When self and the like are non-existent, since the conception of self and the like regarding them is absent, does the well-spoken and poorly-spoken characteristic expressed through combinations of words and the like — the conception of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — necessarily not operate regarding them? It is not so. If the <s>bodhisattvas</s> had no conception regarding those [<s>dharmas</s>], then having abandoned the unreasonable doctrines of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), how would desire be generated for realizing the <s>dharmas</s> taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s>? — to this objection, 'for what reason?', in order to resolve that, he says 'if, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth.

body.text: ayamabhiprāyaḥ- ekānekasvabhāvavicāreṇa yathā rūpādilakṣaṇadharmā na saṃvidyante, tathā deśanādharmā api | yatra dharmasaṃjñā tatrātmādisaṃjñā api niścayena naiva prahīṇā, dharmanimittagrahaṇamūlatvāt tasyāḥ | dharmanimittagrāhakamanasikārasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_136

children.text: ) tasyā eva manasikārarūpatvāt maitrīprabhṛtiṣu tattvamanasikārāsadbhāve nātmadṛṣṭiḥ parihīyate | ata eva ekameva yānam, tacca mahāyānamityuktam |
children.translated_text: is itself of the nature of that very mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>); therefore, in the absence of true mental attention (<s>tattvamanasikāra</s>) in [practices such as] <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the like, the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) is not abandoned. For this very reason, there is only one vehicle, and that is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) — so it is stated.

body.translated_text: The intent is this: just as through the investigation of the nature of being one or many, <s>dharmas</s> characterized by form and the like are not found [to exist], so too the <s>dharmas</s> of the teaching [are not found]. Where there is <s>dharmasaṃjñā</s> (dharma-conception), there <s>ātmasaṃjñā</s> (self-conception) and the like are certainly not abandoned, because that [self-conception] has its root in the grasping of the sign of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmanimittagrahaṇa</s>). The mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>) that grasps the sign of <s>dharma</s>

body.text: api ca, bodhisattvānāṃ sā dharmasaṃjñā yadyavaśyamanutpannadarśanamārgaḥ syāt tathā sati tena kathamātmādisaṃjñā prahīṇā syāt? darśanamārgapraheyatvāttasyāḥ | ataḥ sarvametat parīkṣya sa eva teṣāmātmagrāho bhavet ityuktam | tasya taddhetutvāt tadanuśayāprahīṇatvāccetyabhiprāyaḥ | anyathā tayorbhinnākāratvāt kathaṃ dharmasaṃjñaiva ātmagrāhaḥ syāditi | dharmāstāvadatra yuktyupapannāgamalakṣaṇā eveṣṭāḥ tadviparītā adharmāḥ | evaṃ sati tattatsūtreṣu kathaṃ bhagavatā bodhisattvebhyaḥ saddharmaḥ parigrāhayiṣyate? evamanucintya tatkasya hetoḥ? iti paripapraccha | tadarthaṃ subhūte ityādyāha | nodgrahītavyaḥ vitathamārgeṇa viparītābhiniveśakṣaṇena nodgrahītavyaḥ, satya iti nābhiniviṣṭavyamiti vākyārthaḥ | abhipretasiddhyarthaṃ kolopamadeśitasya lakṣaṇasya na grahaṇaniṣedha ityabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' notion of <s>dharma</s> necessarily means the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) has not arisen, then how could the notion of self (<s>ātman</s>) and so on be abandoned? Because that [notion of self] is to be abandoned on the path of seeing. Therefore, having examined all this, that very [understanding] is their self...

body.text: tasmāt ityādinā sa evārthaḥ padāntarai prayuktaḥ, yato hi sarvo dharmo 'dharmaśca satya ityabhiniveśasya viparītābhiniveśatvād, yuktyopapanno ya āgamasamūhaḥ saṃsārārṇavottaraṇāya proktaḥ kolopamaḥ sa (yadā) pāraṃ gatvā niṣprayojanatvāt parityājyo bhavati, kimu (tadā) te 'yuktayopapannāstairthikānāmivādharmāḥ | saprayojanamapi tadālambanaṃ mayā nānujñātamityevamuktavān tathāgataḥ | anyathā dharmādharmādikaṃ yadi satyasvabhāvaṃ syāt tadā paramārthaviṣayatvāt tadabhiniveśasya saṃsārapāragateṣvapi yuktisahaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_137

children.text: ) syāditi, kimiti tathāgataḥ tanniṣedhatīti? iti tu saṃgrahārthaḥ | tathā āryaratnakaraṇḍasūtre 'pi bhagavatā uktam-
children.translated_text: ...would it be so — why then does the <s>Tathāgata</s> negate that? This [question] is for the purpose of summarization. Likewise, in the <s>Āryaratnakaraṇḍasūtra</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has also said:

body.translated_text: By 'therefore' and so on, that same meaning is expressed with different words. Since every conviction that '<s>dharma</s>' and '<s>adharma</s>' are real is an inverted conviction, the collection of scripture that is established by reasoning and proclaimed for crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> is like a raft...

body.text: "bhadanta subhūte kolopamaṃ dharmaparyāyajānadbhirdharmā eva prahātavyāḥ, prāgevādharmā iti | yo hi dharmaḥ prahīyate, so 'pi nādharmaḥ iti |"
body.translated_text: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, by those who know that the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> is like a raft, even <s>dharmas</s> (wholesome states) should be abandoned — how much more so <s>adharmas</s> (unwholesome states)! For the <s>dharma</s> that is abandoned — even that is not <s>adharma</s>.'

body.text: yaḥ sūtrādidharmaparyāyaḥ sa kolopama ucyate | dharmā eva ityetad upalakṣaṇam | tena rūpādayo mārgalakṣaṇāśca dharmāḥ saṃgṛhyante | adharmā ityapi upalakṣaṇamātram, tena prasiddhaviruddhāḥ adharmalakṣaṇāḥ paraparikalpitā ātmādayaśca upadiṣṭāste 'pi saṃgṛhyante | athavā dharmādharmābhidheyābhidhānāt na sarvasaṃgrahe doṣaḥ | anena tāvad vikṣepaṃ nīgṛhya kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyamityetad darśitam |
body.translated_text: The teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> such as sūtras and so forth is said to be like a raft. 'Even <s>dharmas</s>' is merely an indication; by that, <s>dharmas</s> characterized by form (<s>rūpa</s>) and so on and the characteristics of the path are included. '<s>Adharmas</s>' is also merely an indication; by that, the well-known opposite characteristics...

body.text: ba
body.translated_text: B

body.text:
adhigamadharmakāyasthānam : [1] jñānahetudharmakāyaḥ
nanu dharmādayaḥ sarve paramārthato mithyāsvabhāvāḥ, tadā abhisambuddho bhūtvā 'bhagavatā sarve dharmā deśitāḥ'; iti tadapi mṛṣaiva syāt, ata eva bodhisattvaiḥ tathāgatajñānahetumadhigamadharmakāyaṃ prāptuṃ chando na janayitavyaḥ, ityetad vicārya jñānahetudharmakāyāvāptaye chandotpādanāya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityaktam |
body.translated_text:
The section on the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) of realization: [1] The <s>dharmakāya</s> as cause of knowledge.
Now, if all <s>dharmas</s> and so on are of a false nature ultimately, then [the statement] 'having become fully enlightened, the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught all <s>dharmas</s>' — that too would be merely false; therefore...

body.text: anenārthataḥ paramārthastu anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti abhisambuddha ityetayoḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_138

children.text: ) grahaṇamapi vipakṣatayā paridīpitam, tathyasaṃvṛtisvabhāvaṃ tu tathāgatasya jñānahetuṃ jñānadharmakāyaṃ prāptuṃ chandaḥ praṇidhānaṃ ca pradarśite | anuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ ityupalakṣaṇamātraparidīpanena śrāvaka-pratyekabuddhādīnāṃ pratipattibhedena bhinnaḥ jñānahetuko 'dhigamakāyastāvannirdiśyate | śrāvakādīnāmapi guṇā bodhisattvenāvagantavyā eva, anyathā kathaṃ tāvat sarvajñapadalābhaḥ |
children.translated_text: has been illuminated as being on the side of the opponent. But [regarding] the nature of authentic conventional truth (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>), the aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) to attain the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s cause of knowledge, the <s>jñānadharmakāya</s> (knowledge truth-body), have been demonstrated. 'Unsurpassed perfect awakening' is merely an indication...

body.translated_text: By this, in terms of meaning, the ultimate — 'unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)' — and 'fully enlightened' (<s>abhisambuddha</s>), the grasping of both of these

body.text: saṃvṛtisvabhāvastvevam- sambodhiḥ samboddhavyaṃ deśanā deśitavyamityādayaḥ sarve paryāyāḥ | bhagavatā kaṃ paramārthābhiprāyamabhilakṣya sarvaṃ mithyaivetyuktam, taduktābhiprāyaṃ saṃgṛhya āryasubhūtisthaviraḥ yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi ityetadavocat | yathāhamājānāmityabhiprāyavivaraṇam | kasmānnābhisambuddhaḥ, dharmadeśanā ca na sta iti cintāyāṃ tatkasya hetoḥ? iti | agrāhyaḥ iti paramārthastāvannirvikalpajñānagocaro 'pi na bhavatīti uktapūrvam | anabhilāpyaḥ śabdāviṣayatvāditi | sarve śabdagocarāstāvat samāropitasāmānyamātrātmakāḥ, sāmānyasya cābhāvarūpatvāt | imau dvau (śabdau) abhisambuddhābhāvasya dharmadeśanābhāvasya ca yathākramaṃ hetutayābhihitau |
body.translated_text: But the conventional nature is thus: 'awakening,' 'what is to be awakened to,' 'teaching,' 'what is to be taught' — all these are synonymous expressions. What ultimate intent did the <s>Bhagavān</s> have in view when he said 'everything is merely false'? Comprehending the intent of what was said, the noble <s>Subhūti</s>...

body.text: nanu syuḥ sarve bhāvā agrāhyāḥ anabhilāpyāḥ, tathāpi svalakṣaṇadhāraṇāt paramārthataḥ dharmasvabhāvatāsthitā evetyāśaṅkāyāṃ na sa dharmaḥ ityāha | sarvabhāvānāṃ paramārthataḥ svabhāvena parinirvṛttatvānna sambhavati svalakṣaṇadhārakatvam | yadyevaṃ tarhi bhagavatā abhāvo 'bhisambuddho draṣṭavya iti vicārya nādharmaḥ ityuktam | sa tu prasajyapratiṣedhasvabhāvaḥ anena tāvat yogasamāpattiṃ nirdiśya adhyāropo 'pavādāntaśca nirastau | tatkasya hetoḥ? ityupapattiḥ pṛcchyate, tadarthaṃ asaṃskṛtaprabhāvitāḥ ityāha | asaṃskṛtatvaṃ tāvad dharmāṇāṃ paramārthasvabhāvaḥ, tacca yuktyā vicāryamāṇamanutpattilakṣaṇameva paryavasyati, yathā pūrvaṃ vicāritam |
body.translated_text: Now, if all entities are ungraspable and inexpressible, nevertheless — [objection:] because they bear their own characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), they are ultimately established in the nature of <s>dharma</s>. In response to this doubt, he says 'that is not a <s>dharma</s>.' Because all entities are ultimately extinguished by their own nature (<s>parinirvṛtta</s>)...

body.text: uktaṃ bhagavatā dharmasaṃgītau-
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said in the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti</s>:

body.text: 'yo ānanda, dharmo 'nutpannaḥ, aniruddhaḥ, asthitaḥ avikṛtastaducyate āryasatyamiti'; | idamānanda, abhisandhāya tathāgatena asaṃskṛtaprabhāvitā āryaśrāvakā iti deśitam, yathā pūrvamuktam |
body.translated_text: '<s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>dharma</s> which is unoriginated, unceased, non-abiding, and unaltered — that is called noble truth.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, with this intention in mind, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has taught that the noble disciples (<s>āryaśrāvakas</s>) are empowered by the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)' — as stated before.

body.text: ayañca 'utpādād vā tathāgatānām, anutpādād vā tathāgatānām, nityaṃ tathaiva sattvānnirvikāratvāccāsaṃskṛtaḥ, tadadhigamādāryapudgalāḥ tatprabhāvitā bhavanti, dharmatattvādhigamena prabhāvitatvādāryaṇām | anyeṣu tattvasadbhāvo naiva tāvad yujyate, tacca (tattvaṃ) asaṃskṛtamapi na (syāt) prasajyapratiṣedhasvabhāvābhāvāt, bhāvasvabhāvasvāttasya | āryaiḥ nānyavidho bhāvasvabhāvo 'vabudhyate, tadbhinnasvabhāvasyaivādhigamāt | bhāvagrahaṇābhāvena tadabhāvarūpatve sati bhāvagrāha eva tāvat prasajyate | ata eva āryasandhinirmocanasūtre uktam- 'na tattvasya bhāvāditaro 'rthaḥ'; iti |
body.translated_text: And this [passage]: 'Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, [reality] always remains just so — because of being unchangeable, it is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). Through its realization, noble persons become empowered by it; because the noble ones are empowered through the realization of the true nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatattvādhigama</s>).'

body.text: ataḥ yathoktadoṣa āpadyate | tattu (tattvaṃ) paramārthato nāsti bhāvasvabhāvaḥ, asiddhaiva bhāvasvabhāvatā kasyāpi | bhāvasvabhāvateva tadapi (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_140

children.text: ) saṃskṛtaṃ prasajyeta | ataḥ abhāvarūpatvena dharmeṣu sattvādatattvameva svabhāvena tat | sarveṣāmapi tajjñānaprasaṅgaḥ, bhāvasvabhāvavat | saṃkleśahetuprasaṅgo 'pi durnirvāraḥ syāt | ata eva teṣu āryasandhinirmocanādiṣu- 'na tattvasya bhāvāditaro 'rthaḥ'; ityuktam | ata eva na dharmo nādharmaḥ ityuvāca | anena bhāvābhāvasadasadādīnāṃ niṣedharūpaṃ deśitam | api cānena vikṣepanigraho 'pi nirdiṣṭaḥ | etatsarvaiḥ sthānasyāsya gambhīratvamapi saṃdarśitam |
children.translated_text: would absurdly be conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Therefore, since the true nature (<s>tattva</s>) exists among <s>dharmas</s> in the form of non-entity, that very [nature] is by nature the non-true. There would be the absurd consequence of everyone having that knowledge, just as with the nature of entities. The absurd consequence of [reality] being a cause of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) would also be unavoidable. For this very reason, among those [<s>dharmas</s>], the noble ones...

body.translated_text: Therefore the stated fault follows. But that [truth] — ultimately, the nature of entities does not exist; the nature of entities is completely unestablished for anything whatsoever. That nature of entities itself also

body.text: (2) puṇyahetukadharmakāyaḥ
body.translated_text: (2) The <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) whose cause is merit.

body.text: yadi bhagavato 'bhisambodhirvā dharmadeśanā vā nāsti kaściod dharmaḥ, kathaṃ tarhi bodhisattvena puṇyahetudharmakāyaṃ prāptukāmena saddharmaparigrahe 'nupravartitavyamiti vicintya puṇyahetudharmakayakāmatācchandotpādanāya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityuktam | tatra saptaratnāni tāvat svarṇa-raupya-vaiḍūrya-aśmagarbha-musāragalva-lohitamuktā-sphaṭikāḥ āryasaddharmapuṇdarīke uktāni | 'caturdīpādānāṃ sahasraṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 141

children.text: ) sāhasro lokadhātuḥ | tatsahasaṃ dvisāhasraḥ | tatsahasraṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ'; | tato nidānam iti ratnadānānāṃ nidānāt tataḥ puṇyodbhavaḥ, tadahetoḥ sambhavatītyarthaḥ | sarvāṇi kuśalacittāni, tadutpannā vāsanāḥ puṇyāni | teṣāṃ rāśiḥ skandha iti | phalabāhulyāt tadbāhulyam | bahu iti viśeṣaṇam | bahu bahu iti dviruktyā bāhulyādhikyam |
children.translated_text: is a first-order thousand world-system (<s>sāhasra lokadhātu</s>); a thousand of those is a second-order thousand (<s>dvisāhasra</s>); a thousand of those is a third-order great thousand world-system (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>).' 'Arising from that' (<s>tato nidānam</s>) means the arising of merit from the cause of giving jewels — 'it arises from that cause' is the meaning. All wholesome mental states (<s>kuśalacittāni</s>), and the habitual impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) born from them, are merits (<s>puṇya</s>). Their aggregate is the 'heap' (<s>skandha</s>). The abundance [of merit] is due to the abundance of its fruit. 'Much' (<s>bahu</s>) is the qualifier. By the repetition 'much, much,' the great excess of abundance [is indicated].

body.translated_text: If neither the <s>Bhagavān's</s> perfect awakening (abhisaṃbodhi) nor his teaching of the Dharma constitutes any [real] dharma, then how should a Bodhisattva who wishes to attain the Dharmakāya (truth-body) — whose cause is merit — engage in embracing the true Dharma? Reflecting thus, to arouse the aspiration born from the desire for the Dharmakāya whose cause is merit, it is said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' The seven jewels are: gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald), <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), <s>lohitamuktā</s> (red pearl), and crystal — as stated in the <s>Āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>. 'A thousand of the four-continent [world-systems]

body.text: yadi paramārthataḥ sarve (dharmāḥ) anutpannāḥ, kathaṃ tato nidāna puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyāt? ityāśaṅkya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityuktvā svayamabhiprāyaṃ viditvā askandhaḥ ityabhihitavān | paramārthata iti śeṣaḥ | prajñaptisattvāt skandhānāṃ na puṇyaskandho bhāvarūpeṇa sambhavati | puṇyamapi vāsanāsvarūpamavasthāviśeṣe upacaryate | bhāvānāṃ sthiratvena abhisaṃskāreṇa apravṛttatvāt cittamapi prajñaptisanmātrameva | ekānekasvabhāvena pratisvaṃ parīkṣāyāṃ mithyaiva tāvat svabhāvaḥ | ata eva na puṇyaskandhaḥ paramārthato vidyate |
body.translated_text: If ultimately all dharmas are unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>), how could one produce a heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>) arising from that? Anticipating this objection, having said 'What is the reason?' and knowing his own intention, he stated 'non-heap' (<s>askandha</s>). 'Ultimately' (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>) is the implied qualifier. Because the aggregates exist only as designations (<s>prajñaptisattva</s>), the merit-heap does not exist in the form of a real entity (<s>bhāvarūpa</s>). Merit too, being of the nature of habitual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), is figuratively applied to a particular state. Because entities do not function through stable, permanent construction (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>), even the mind is merely a designational existent (<s>prajñaptisanmātra</s>). When examined individually in terms of unity or multiplicity, its intrinsic nature is simply false. Therefore, the merit-heap does not exist ultimately.

body.text: anena yogasamāpattiḥ paridīpitā, adhyāropāntaśca niṣiddhaḥ | vidyanta eva puṇyaskandhāḥ saṃvṛtau | ata eva puṇyaskandhastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ ityuktam | yadyevaṃ na syāt, paramārthataḥ sa puṇyaskandho bhavet (tadā) paramārthasya śabdāgocaratvāt na bhavet tadabhidhānam | abhāṣitamityevaṃ vacanaṃ nirarthakamiti cet? yato bhāṣitāstasmāt saṃvṛtāvevetyavagantavyam | anenāpavādāntasya niṣedho nirdiṣṭaḥ | evamāryasubhūtinā antadvayaparihāraḥ kṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, meditative attainment (<s>yogasamāpatti</s>) is illuminated, and the extreme of superimposition (<s>adhyāropānta</s>) is negated. Merit-heaps do exist conventionally (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). Therefore it is said: 'the merit-heap was spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' If it were not so — if the merit-heap existed ultimately — then, because ultimate reality is beyond the scope of words, there could be no such designation. If [one objects:] 'the statement that it was not spoken would be meaningless' — since it was spoken, it should be understood as [existing] only conventionally. By this, the negation of the extreme of deprecation (<s>apavādānta</s>) is indicated. Thus, by the Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, the avoidance of both extremes (<s>antadvayaparihāra</s>) is accomplished.

body.text: tadanantaraṃ pārṣadā udāradharmaśravaṇabhavyāḥ, tena ca bahutaraṃ puṇyamiti āvedituṃ bhagavatā yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyuktam | anena tathāgatānāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 142

children.text: ) puṇyahetukādhigamakāyasya pravacanakāyato nirjātatvāt tataścatuṣpādikāyāmapi gāthāyāṃ deśyamānāyāṃ (yadā) tādṛśaṃ puṇyāyatanaṃ bhavet (tadā) tathāgatānāṃ puṇyahetukadharmakāyasya tu kathaiva keti nirdiśyate | nāyaṃ padārthaḥ, (tathāpi) sāmarthyalabhyo 'yamartha ityadoṣaḥ | etena paramārthataḥ dharmadeśanāyāḥ abhisambuddhasya cāpyasattve saṃvṛtau tāvat puṇyakāyadeśanāyāḥ sattvāt bodhisattvaiḥ puṇyamadhigāntuṃ pravartayitavyamevetyabhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: merit-caused realization-body (<s>adhigamakāya</s>) arises from the teaching-body (<s>pravacanakāya</s>); therefore, when even a four-line verse (<s>catuṣpādikā gāthā</s>) is taught, [if] such a field of merit (<s>puṇyāyatana</s>) exists, then how much more so for the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> whose cause is merit — thus it is indicated. This is not [stated as] a word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>); [nevertheless,] since this meaning is obtainable through implication (<s>sāmarthyalabhya</s>), there is no fault. By this, the intention is that, although the Dharma-teaching and the awakened one do not truly exist ultimately, since conventionally the merit-body-teaching does exist, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should indeed exert themselves to accumulate merit.

body.translated_text: After that, since the assembly was fit to hear the exalted Dharma, and to make known that there is even greater merit, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said 'And again, <s>Subhūti</s>,' etc. By this, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>'

body.text: anena tāvad viśiṣṭapuṇyapratipādanena audāryamasya paridīpitam, tadutpādāya ca chandapraṇidhāne nirdiṣṭe | ṣaṭpādikāyā gāthāyāḥ sattve 'pi catuṣpādikā iti viśeṣīkṛtā | gāthā iti yatra na yatio, 'pāda'; śabdena catuḥpādaṃ gāthāparimāṇaṃ parigṛhyate | udgṛhya iti svādhyāyaṃ vidhāya | deśayet iti padāni | samprakāśayet ityarthaḥ | asaṃkhyeyam iti saṃbahulam | aprameyam iti pramaviṣayātītatvāt | anena cārthataḥ puṇyānuttivipakṣastāvannirākṛtaḥ | puṇyamityupalakṣaṇamātrametena tathāgatasya samastaḥ punyasambhāro nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this demonstration of distinguished merit, the magnificence of this [teaching] is illuminated, and aspiration and resolve (<s>chanda</s> and <s>praṇidhāna</s>) for producing that [merit] are indicated. Even though the verse has six lines, it is specified as 'four-lined' (<s>catuṣpādikā</s>). 'Verse' (<s>gāthā</s>) means wherever [there is meter]; by the word 'line' (<s>pāda</s>), the standard measure of four lines per verse is encompassed. 'Having memorized' (<s>udgṛhya</s>) means having undertaken study (<s>svādhyāya</s>). 'Would teach' (<s>deśayet</s>) means the words; 'would illuminate' (<s>samprakāśayet</s>) is the meaning. 'Incalculable' (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>) means very many. 'Immeasurable' (<s>aprameya</s>) because it transcends the scope of measurement. By this, the opponent of [the view that] merit has no arising is factually refuted. 'Merit' (<s>puṇya</s>) is merely indicative; by this, the entire merit-accumulation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is indicated.

body.text: kimiti śraddheyamātramuta yuktito 'vagamyamiti manasi kṛtvā tatkasya hetoḥ? iti pṛcchāyām ato nirjātā hi subhūte, tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ iti yuktivacanamabhihitavān | evaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 143

children.text: ) bahutaraṃ puṇyam iti tacca bṛhatphalatvāttat bahutaraṃ puṇyam, na tu svarūpatasyasya kāyābhāvāt | ratnanirjātaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ tu mahāparibhogādi gauṇasāaṃsārikaṃ phalaṃ prāpayati | prajñāparigṛhītatve sati dānādīnāṃ mahābodhiphalamadhigamyate, na tu prādeśikānām | dharmadānena tāvadakṣayāpratimatathāgatapadaprāpteḥ tanmahattvaṃ kimiti na prasaktam? yathā dharmeṇānugraho na tathā ratnaiḥ pareṣāmanugrahaḥ | tathā hi parebhyaḥ samprakāśitena kramaśo 'nena dharmeṇa kṣiprameva buddhatvapadaṃ labhyate, na tu ratnaiḥ | ata eva parebhyaḥ parānugrāhakatvād ratnadānād dharmadānaṃ viśiṣṭamityābhisandhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'greater merit' (<s>bahutaraṃ puṇyam</s>) — that is greater merit because of its great fruit, not in its own form, since [the merit-heap] has no [real] body. The merit arising from jewels yields secondary saṃsāric fruits such as great enjoyment and so forth. When giving (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest are embraced by wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the fruit of great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) is attained — but not from partial [merits]. Since through the gift of Dharma, the incomparable, inexhaustible state of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is attained, why should its greatness not be established? The benefit to others through Dharma is not [equaled] by the benefit through jewels. For by this Dharma, illuminated to others, the state of Buddhahood is swiftly attained in succession — but not through jewels. Therefore, because it benefits others more than others [are benefited by jewels], the gift of Dharma is superior to the gift of jewels — this is the intended meaning.

body.translated_text: Thinking 'Is this merely to be accepted on faith, or is it to be understood through reasoning?' — in response to the question 'What is the reason?', he uttered the rational statement: 'For from this, <s>Subhūti</s>, the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly awakened ones, has arisen.' Thus,

body.text: ato nirjātāḥ iti saṃsādhyate | daśacaritāni niḥśritya pāramparyeṇa prāpyanta ityarthaḥ | tāni tāvad daśa caritāni- lekhanaṃ pūjanaṃ dānaṃ vācanaṃ śravaṇam udgrahaṇam samprakāśanaṃ svādhyāyaḥ cintanaṃ bhāvanā ceti | ato nirjātāśca buddhā bhagavantaḥ iti saṃvṛtau etānyāśritya buddhāḥ prajñaptā iti (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 144

children.text: ) vākyaśeṣaḥ paramārthatastu bodhiḥ buddhaśca bhinnau na staḥ | anena tāvat puṇyasya paramavaiśiṣṭayaparidīpanena tadutpādayituṃ chanda-praṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti deśitam |
children.translated_text: the remainder of the sentence: but ultimately, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) and <s>Buddha</s> are not different. By this illumination of the supreme distinction of merit, it is taught that one should abide in aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and resolve (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) to produce that [merit].
