body.translated_text: 'Arisen from this' (<s>ato nirjātāḥ</s>) is thus established. The meaning is: depending on the ten practices (<s>daśacarita</s>), [the Buddhas] are attained in succession. Those ten practices are: (1) writing (<s>lekhana</s>), (2) worship (<s>pūjana</s>), (3) giving (<s>dāna</s>), (4) reciting (<s>vācana</s>), (5) hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), (6) memorizing (<s>udgrahaṇa</s>), (7) explaining (<s>samprakāśana</s>), (8) self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), (9) reflection (<s>cintana</s>), and (10) meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). 'And from this have arisen the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones' — conventionally, depending on these [practices], the <s>Buddhas</s> are designated. Thus,

body.text: yadi paramārthataḥ sarvadharmānutpāda eva tadā sarve buddhadharmā apyanutpannā eva bhaveyuḥ tatkatham ato nirjātā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti? na buddhānāṃ bodherbhinnatvamiti vicārya tatkasya heto? iti paripṛcchā, etadarthamatra buddhadharmāḥ ityuktam | buddhaprajñaptihetukā anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhilakṣaṇā dharmā eva hi buddhadharmāḥ | tasmānnaiva kevalaṃ bodhibhinnāḥ paramārthataḥ buddhāḥ, apitu prajñaptihetutvād ato nirjātā buddhaḥ ityuktamityabhiprāyaḥ | te 'pi paramārthato 'nutpannatvād abuddhadharmā iti, saṃvṛtimāśritya tathāgatānāmanusamyaksaṃbodhistu ato nirjātā ityādinā tathāgatena bhāṣitā, na tu paramārthata iti | ata eva tattaditarapakṣebhyaḥ buddhadharmā iti paramārthato naiva vaktuṃ śakyate | pratyātmavedanīyatvenānabhilāpyāsta ityabhiprāyaḥ | anena yogasamāpattiḥ vikṣepanigrahaḥ gāmbhīryañca deśitāni |
body.translated_text: If ultimately all dharmas are indeed unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>), then all Buddha-dharmas too would be unborn — then how can 'the unsurpassed perfect awakening has arisen from this'? Reflecting that <s>Buddhas</s> are not different from <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), the question 'What is the reason?' is asked. For this purpose, 'Buddha-dharmas' (<s>buddhadharmāḥ</s>) is stated here. The dharmas characterized as unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>), which are the causes for the designation of 'Buddha,' are indeed the Buddha-dharmas. Therefore, not only are the <s>Buddhas</s> ultimately non-different from bodhi, but rather, because they are causes for designation, 'the Buddhas have arisen from this' is said — this is the intention. Since even those [Buddha-dharmas] are ultimately unborn, they are 'non-Buddha-dharmas'; conventionally, the <s>Tathāgatas'</s> unsurpassed perfect awakening has been spoken of by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as 'arisen from this,' but not ultimately. Therefore, from any of those alternative positions, 'Buddha-dharmas' cannot be ultimately stated. The intention is that they are inexpressible (<s>anabhilāpya</s>), being objects of personal realization (<s>pratyātmavedanīya</s>). By this, meditative attainment (<s>yogasamāpatti</s>), restraint of distraction (<s>vikṣepanigraha</s>), and profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>) are taught.

body.text: atra kecidāhuḥ kathaṃ tridhā bhinno 'yaṃ dharmakāyaḥ | atha dharmakāyaprāptiḥ dharmakāyahetoścānurūpatayā puṇyasvabhāvaḥ, prajñaptyā ca pravacanasvabhāvo dharmakāya iti ced? tathā sati rūpakāyo 'pi tatprāpteranurūpahetutvāt tatprāpakahetutvācca dharmakāyaḥ syāditi | (ataḥ) tanna satyam, bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ dharmakāyastu pariśuddhajñānasvabhāvastathā yā ca tasya sāmānyadharmatā,. tasyāṃ vyavasthāpyate | nāstyasyāyaṃ vipākabhedaḥ, na cātra pravacanapuṇyayorupacāreṇa dharmaḥ iti deśanāpi | kimiva tarhīti cet? vastumātraṃ dharma iti deśanā | dharmā ityādi svayamevaṃ khyātatvāt | svasāmānyalakṣaṇadhāraṇād dharmā iti yat vyākhyātaṃ tat sarvadharmasādhāraṇamiti na rūpakāyastathāgatatvena nirdiṣṭaḥ, ajñāpakatvāt | prajñaptita ityucyamāne 'pi na rūpakāyo dharmakāyatvena prasakto bhavati, puṇyahetvanurūpatvāt (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 145
of that. As it is said:

body.translated_text: Here some say: how is this <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) divided threefold? If the attainment of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> and its cause, being of corresponding nature, are of the nature of merit, and by designation the teaching (<s>pravacana</s>) is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — if so, then the form-body (<s>Rūpakāya</s>) too, being a corresponding cause for its attainment and a cause that leads to its attainment, would be the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. [Therefore] that is not correct. The <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> is of the nature of completely purified knowledge (<s>pariśuddhajñāna</s>), and it is established in its general characteristic (<s>sāmānyadharmatā</s>). There is no division of karmic fruition (<s>vipākabheda</s>) for it, nor is there a teaching here in which 'dharma' is applied figuratively to teaching and merit. What then? The teaching is that dharma simply means 'thing' (<s>vastumātra</s>). 'Dharmas' and so forth — [the term is] self-evident. The explanation that [things are called] 'dharmas' because they bear their own and general characteristics is common to all dharmas; therefore the form-body (<s>Rūpakāya</s>) is not designated as the <s>Tathāgata</s>-nature, because it does not make known [the truth]. Even when 'designated' (<s>prajñaptita</s>) is said, the form-body is not established as the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, because it is of the nature of a merit-based cause.

children.text: buddhānāṃ rūpikāyo hi puṇyaṃ sambhṛtya jāyate |
children.translated_text: 'The form-body (<s>Rūpikāya</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s> is born from having accumulated merit;
the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), in brief, is born from the accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñānasambhāra</s>), O king.'

body.text: tasmājjñānasambhārasyaiva tatprāptyupāyatvānna rūpakāyena sa gṛhyate, prajñaptihetvabhāvānnocyate rūpakāyo 'dharmakāyaḥ'; iti | pravacanakāyastu samyagjñānasya phalamiti | sambhāralakṣaṇapuṇyanicayasyāpi tatprāptihetutvāt prajñaptyā dharmakāya ityucyamāno 'pi yujyata eveti alamadhikena | anyat kucodyaṃ yuktamayuktaṃ veti vicakṣaṇairviveciyiṣyata iti matvā padabāhulyabhiyā na likhyate | dharmakāyāptichandasthānamuktam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, since it is the accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñānasambhāra</s>) alone that serves as the means for attaining that [dharmakāya], it is not grasped through the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>); because there is no cause for designation, the form-body is not called the <s>dharmakāya</s>. The body of sacred teaching (<s>pravacanakāya</s>) is the fruit of correct knowledge. The heap of merit characterized by accumulation...

body.text:
itaḥ paraṃ dvādaśavipakṣāṇāṃ pratipakṣāṇi dvādaśasthānāni yathākramaṃ veditavyāni | ime tāvad dvādaśa vipakṣāḥ-
1. abhimānaḥ
2. abhimānābhāve 'pi alpaśrutatvam
3. bāhuśrutye 'pihīnālambanamanasikārabhāvanā
4. hīnālambanamanasikārabhāvanāyā abhāve 'pi sattvopekṣā
5. tadupekṣāyā abhāve 'pi bāhyaśāstreṣu sānurāgā pravṛttiḥ
6. tathā pravṛttyabhāve 'pi bhāvanimittābhibhavopāyeṣvakauśalam
7. tatra upāyakauśale 'pi puṇyasambhārāsañcayaḥ
8. puṇyasambhārasañcaye 'pi lābhasatkārakausīdyaiḥ piṇḍāsvādanam
9. tathāsvādanābhāve 'pi duḥkhākṣāntiḥ
10. duḥkhādhivāsanāyāmapi jñānasambhārāsañcayaḥ
11. jñānasambhārasañcaye 'pi ātmaparigrahaḥ
12. ātmagrahābhāve 'pi avavādāyogaḥ
body.translated_text:
Hereafter, the antidotes to the twelve adverse factors should be understood in order through twelve sections. These are the twelve adverse factors:
1. Conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>)
2. Even in the absence of conceit, being of little learning
3. Even with great learning, mental engagement with inferior objects...

body.text: 5. bhāvanāviśeṣalābhe 'nabhimānasthānam :
body.translated_text: 5. The section on non-conceit upon attaining distinction in cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>):

body.text: tatra bhagavatā dharmapudgalayorvistareṇa nairātmye deśite 'pi anādikālīnadṛḍhātmābhiniveśasañcayabalena yadi kaścidevaṃ manyeta- yasya sattvādisaṃjñā pravartate, na sa bodhisattva iti? evaṃ tarhi yaduktaṃ bhagavatā 'tasmin kāle 'haṃ vīradatto nāma nṛpo 'bhavam,'; yuṣmabhyaṃ mayā dharmo deśayiṣyate ityādi kathaṃ syāt | (ataḥ) sattvasaṃjñādivirahasya naivamabhiprāya iti vighnabhūtābhimānavisaṃyogārthaṃ pañcamasthānamadhikṛtyāha- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādi |
body.translated_text: Therein, even though the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught the selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of both <s>dharmas</s> and persons (<s>pudgala</s>) extensively, if someone, through the force of the accumulation of firm grasping at self cultivated since beginningless time, were to think: 'One who has the notion of beings and so on is not a <s>bodhisattva</s>' — then, [in response to this:]

body.text: asyāyamatra sāmānyato 'rthaḥ- ye mama mṛduśrāvakāḥ srotaāpannatvādiṣu dharmanairātmyānadhigamād aprāptarasānubhavāḥ, teṣāmapi ahantvena mamatvena cābhiniveśo na bhavati, kiṃ khalu punaḥ ubhayanairātmyādhigamena prahīṇaniravaśeṣāvaraṇānāmiti | tasmin kāle 'ham..... ityādi yattallokena saha vyavahāraprajñaptyarthaṃ parasantānavyavacchedamātrajñāpanārthaṃ vā, senāvanādivyavahāravat, na tvekatva- (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_147

children.text: ) śāśvatatvābhiniveśatayā | tattvajñānasthitaiḥ na śakyate tāvallokena saha vyavahartum | tasmādabhimānasthānavisaṃyogārthaṃ tvayāpi nātmanyabhiniveṣṭavyamiti samādāpayati |
children.translated_text: ...because of grasping at eternalism. Those established in the knowledge of reality cannot engage in worldly conventions with ordinary people. Therefore, in order to separate [you] from the ground of conceit, he instructs: 'You too should not grasp at self.'

body.translated_text: The general meaning here is this: Those who are my gentle <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), stream-enterers and so on, who have not yet experienced the taste of realization because of not having realized the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> — even they do not grasp at selfhood (<s>ahaṃtva</s>) and mine-ness (<s>mamatva</s>). How much more then those who have realized the selflessness of both [persons and dharmas]!

body.text: tatra srotaḥ nirvāṇamahānagaraprāpakadarśanamārgalakṣaṇam, āpannaḥ prāptaḥ, darśanapraheyasamastakleśaprahāyakaḥ srota āpanna iti, tasya ca kartari karmaṇi kriyāyāṃ cābhiniveśaprahāṇena idampratyayatādhigamānnairātmyādhigamo darśitaḥ | mayā iti kartaryabhiniveśaḥ | phalam iti karmaṇyabhiniveśaḥ | prāptaḥ iti kriyāyāmabhiniveśaḥ | ityanena tāvadarthataḥ mayā prāptamiti vipakṣatvena paridītyate | na srotaāpannasyaivaṃ bhavati mayā prāptam ityanena apalakṣaṇamātrapradarśanena sarveṣāmabhimānānāṃ praheyatvaṃ pradarśaye | tatra chandaḥ praṇidhānañcāpi nirdiśyata iti | āryasubhūtirapi bhagavato 'bhiprāyaṃ nirdiśan paramārthasthāpannārthaṃ tatra yogasamāpattiṃ ca grahītuṃ na hi sa bhagavan kañcid (dharmaṃ) āpannaḥ ityāha | kathamiti na rūpamāpannaḥ ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: Therein, the 'stream' (<s>srotas</s>) has the character of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) that leads to the great city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Entered' (<s>āpanna</s>) means attained. A 'stream-enterer' (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) is one who has abandoned all afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) to be abandoned on the path of seeing. Through the abandonment of grasping at agent, object, and action, conditioned arising (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>)...

body.text: anena tāvat paramārthata phaladvaividhyasyāprāpyatvamapi nirdiśyate, tathā hi-phalabhūtaṃ prāpyasvabhāvaṃ kiñcit syāt (tarhi) saṃskṛtamasaṃskṛtaṃ vā syāt | tatra tāvadanutpannamevāsaṃkṛtam, abhāvarūpatvād śaśaviṣāṇamiva tanna yujyate (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_148

children.text: ) prāptum, aprāptyavasthāviśiṣṭatvāt | saṃskṛtaṃ tāvat kṣaṇikam, utpādasamanantaraṃ vināśitvāt, sthiterabhāvāt kenāpi kathamapi tanna prāptuṃ śakyate | yasmin santāne nairātmyamārgalakṣaṇahetusannihitatayā kleśamutpādātyantaviruddhāśrayalakṣaṇaṃ phalamutpadyata iti phalaṃ prāptyata ityevamucyate, na tu paramārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: ...to be attained, because of being no different from the state of non-attainment. As for the conditioned, it is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), because it perishes immediately upon arising, and because there is no abiding; it cannot be attained by anyone in any way. In whichever mental continuum (<s>santāna</s>) the cause characterized by the path of selflessness is present...

body.translated_text: By this, ultimately, the unattainability of the twofold fruit is also indicated. For thus: If there were something of the nature of attainable fruit, it would be either conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) or unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). Among those, the unconditioned is unoriginated, of the nature of non-entity...

body.text: api ca, prāpyaprāpakabhāvaḥ khalu bhinnakālikaḥ samakāliko vā syāt | tatra na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ dvayorapi sthitatvāt, bhinnakālikastu ekasmin pratyāsanne 'parasya cāsaṃnihite sati (bhavati), tatkathaṃ dvayoḥ sthitiriti | na ca samakālāvasthitayorubhayoḥ parasparopakārakatvam, asati copakāre prāpyaprāpakabhāvo naivopayujyate, atiprasaṅgatvāt |
body.translated_text: Moreover, the relationship of attainable and attainer would be either sequential in time or simultaneous. In the first case — neither [works], because both [must] exist; but in the sequential case, when one is proximate the other is absent, so how [could there be a relationship]?

body.text: anyo 'nyasaṃyogenotpādalakṣaṇenāpi prāpyaprāpakabhāvasya samakālikatvaṃ na yujyate, tathā hi- ye 'mūrtabhāvāḥ, te naiva saṃyujyante, kvacidapyanavasthānātteṣām | na syāt prāpyaprāpakabhāve samakālatvamātramapi teṣām, atiprasaṅgāt | na cāpyekasya hetutvam, ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇatvāt, idaṃ prāpyamidañca prāpakamiti niścayo na bhavatī | ye tāvanmūrtāḥ, teṣāṃ sarvātmanā saṃyoge sati ekatvaṃ prasajyate, ekadeśena (saṃyoge tu) sāvayavatvaṃ prasajyate | nairantaryeṇāvasthāne 'pi na bhavituṃ śaknoti ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇatvāt | aviśeṣānna niścayaḥ | ataḥ kalpanāsamāropita evāyam | anena tāvat sarvaḥ karmakartrādivyavahāraḥ spaṣṭamavaboddhavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The simultaneous relation of attainable and attainer through mutual conjunction — characterized by origination — is also not tenable. For thus: Those entities which are formless (<s>amūrta</s>) are never conjoined, because they have no location anywhere. There would be no simultaneity in the relationship of attainable and attainer...

body.text: dharmāḥ iti dharmāyatanam, anenāsaṃskṛtamapi saṃgṛhyate, dharmāyatanasya saptadravyātmakatvāt, śeṣeṇa rūpādinā ca dharmāyatanaikadeśena ca saṃskṛtā nirdiśyante | upalakṣaṇamidam ataścakṣurādikaṃ grahītavyam | evaṃ yataḥ paramārthataḥ sa kañcit (dharmaṃ) nāpannaḥ, mayā prāptamityapi na manyate, tasmāt sanmārgasthitatvāt srotaāpanna ityucyate |
body.translated_text: '<s>Dharmas</s>' means the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (the mental-object sense-field); by this, even the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) is included, because the <s>dharmāyatana</s> consists of seven substances. By the remainder — form (<s>rūpa</s>) and so on, together with a portion of the <s>dharmāyatana</s> — the conditioned [entities] are indicated. This is merely an indication; by this, the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) and other [sense faculties] should also be understood...

body.text: yadi mayā prāptamityabhiniveśastadā kathaṃ nocyeta srota āpanna iti vicintya saced bhagavan ityādyāha | mayā iti yasyāhamityabhiniveśaḥ syāttasya nāstyātmadṛṣṭiprahāṇam, yaścāprahīṇātmadṛṣṭiḥ sa anutpannāryamārgaḥ, yaścānutpannāryamārgaḥ, sa pṛthagjana iti kathaṃ syāt srota-āpanna ityabhisandhiḥ | evaṃ hi 'mayā iti yo 'yamabhiniveśaḥ, sa ātmadṛṣṭisamudayaḥ | anena cittapragraho nirdiṣṭaḥ | anena tāvat sakalena sthānasyāsya gāmbhīryamabhihitam |
body.translated_text: If there were grasping at 'I have attained,' then how could one not be called a 'stream-enterer'? Reflecting thus, he says 'If, <s>Bhagavān</s>...' and so on. The one who would grasp 'I' — for such a one there is no abandonment of the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>); and one who has not abandoned the view of self, [being] unarisen...

body.text: amumevārthaṃ dṛṣṭāntāntare prapañcya nirdeṣṭuṃ sakṛdāgāminaḥ ityādyāha | atrāpi padārthābhisandhyādīni pūrvavad yojyāni | prahīṇabhāvanāhetaṣaḍvidhakāmāvacarakleśa evāryasakṛdāgāmī, sakṛdāgāmitvāt kāmadhātau | prahīṇabhāvanāheyasakalakāmāvacarakleśa evānāgāmītyucyate, punaranāgāmitvāt (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_150

children.text: ) kāmadhātau | yadā samastatraidhātukāvacarakleśamalānāṃ prahāṇaṃ jāyate, tadā sa sakalalokapujyatvād arhannityucyate | na hi sa kaścid dharmo yo 'rhannāma prahīṇatathāvidhakleśāvaraṇajñānasantatau upacaritatvāt, santateśca prajñaptau sattvānna sa kaścana paramārthataḥ, samāropita evāsāvityabhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: ...in the desire realm. When the abandonment of all affliction-stains pervading the three realms arises, then one is called an <s>Arhat</s> because of being worthy of worship by the entire world. For there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever called '<s>Arhat</s>' that arises in the mental continuum in which such affliction-obscurations (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and knowledge [obscurations] have been abandoned.

body.translated_text: In order to elaborate and explain this very meaning with another example, he says 'the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>)' and so on. Here too, the intent of the terms and so on should be construed as before. The noble once-returner (<s>āryasakṛdāgāmin</s>) is one who has abandoned the six types of afflictions of the desire-realm that are to be abandoned through cultivation. Because of being a once-returner, [there is one more return to] the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>).

body.text: sāmpratam āryasubhūtiḥ 'ahaṃ'; padaprayojyamātmānamadhikṛtya viśiṣṭatvena araṇāvihārīti sādhāraṇaguṇatvena arhanniti ca 'ahamasmi'; ityanenoktvā cittapragrahamātraṃ darśayituṃ aham ityādyavocat | araṇā iti samādhiviśeṣaḥ, atra cobhatobhāgavimuktatvamarhattvamālambya taditareṣu raṇā notpādyanta iti vicintya yogaḥ samāpadyate | tato vyutthāya tamālambya taditareṣu nopajāyante raṇāḥ | yastayā araṇayā viharaṇaśīlaḥ sa evamucyate | sugamo 'yaṃ vibhaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now the noble <s>Subhūti</s>, using the word 'I' to refer to himself as the one addressed, spoke of himself as distinguished by being an <s>araṇāvihārin</s> (dweller in peaceful meditation) — a quality shared [with others] — and as an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one), saying 'I am.' Having said this, in order to show [the state of] mere mental composure, he spoke the words beginning with 'I' and so forth. '<s>Araṇā</s>' refers to a particular type of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption); and here, relying on [his status as] one liberated on both sides (<s>ubhatobhāgavimukta</s>) and as an <s>arhat</s>, conflicts (<s>raṇā</s>) do not arise with respect to others.

body.text: na māṃ vyākariṣyat iti tadā aprahīṇatvādātmadṛṣṭermayā srota-āpattiphalamapi durlabham, kiṃ khalu punaḥ ubhatobhāgavimuktenārhatā prāpyamaraṇāvihāritvamityabhisandhiḥ | kathamaraṇāyāṃ vihartavyamiti cintāyāṃ na kvacid viharati ityavocat | prāptaṃ mayā kiñcat saṃkṛtamaṃskṛtaṃ vetyevamabhiniveśena yo 'sthitaḥ, sa evāraṇāvihārīti dvirabhidhānam, nāpara ityarthaḥ | adhunā ahamasmi bhagavaṃstathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena araṇāvihāriṇāmagryo nirdiṣṭaḥ | ahamasmi bhagavan arhan vītarāgaḥ iti nātmābhiniveśena, atha kathamiti cet? vyavahāramātrābhiniveśatayā, etacca prāgeva mayā proktam |
body.translated_text: [The <s>Bhagavān</s>] would not have declared me [an <s>arhat</s>] — for at that time, since the view of self had not been abandoned by me, even the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) would have been difficult to attain, let alone the state of being an <s>araṇāvihārin</s> that is achieved by an <s>arhat</s> liberated on both sides — this is the intended meaning. When [asked] how one should dwell in <s>araṇā</s> (peaceful meditation), he said 'one does not dwell anywhere' — [meaning] one who thinks with attachment 'I have attained something conditioned or created' would have that [very attachment as an obstacle].

body.text: 6. buddhotpādārāgatā-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 6. The topic of devotion to the arising of <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>buddhotpādārāgatā-sthāna</s>):

body.text: nanvasati kasmiṃścidapi prāpye prāpake vā paramārthataḥ, bodhisattvabhūtena bhagavatā kathaṃ tathāgatadīpaṅkarasyāntikād dharma udgṛhītaḥ? atha nodgṛhīta iti ced? tadāsmābhirdharmamudgrahītukāmaiḥ kathamārādhanīstathāgatotpāda iti ye parikalpayanti teṣāmalpaśrutatvapratibandhāpākaraṇārtha ṣaṣṭhaṃ sthānamadhikṛtyāha- asti sa kaścid dharmo yastathāgatena dīpaṅkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasyāntikādudgṛhītaḥ? iti | subhūtirapi prāgevābhiprāyaṃ viditvā no hīdam ityavocat | nāsti paramārthataḥ kasyacidapi dharmasya prāpyaprāpakatvena udgrahaṇaṃ nāma, yathoktaṃ pūrvam | 'sarve dharmāḥ prakṛtyā śāntāḥ'; (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_152

children.text: ) tathāpi tathāgatānubhāvena nānāpadasamudāyādīnāṃ jñānāvabhāsotpādamatre udgṛhītaḥ ityupacaryate, ataḥ śrutaparyeṣaṇaṃ saphalam |
children.translated_text: [is stated]. Even so, through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it is figuratively said that [the <s>Dharma</s>] was 'received' merely in the sense that from the assemblage of various words and so forth, the appearance of knowledge was produced. Therefore, the pursuit of learning is fruitful.

body.translated_text: If there is nothing whatsoever to be attained or any attainer ultimately, then how did the <s>Bhagavān</s>, when he was a <s>bodhisattva</s>, receive the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>? If [one says] he did not receive it, then how should we, who wish to receive the <s>Dharma</s>, regard the arising of a <s>Tathāgata</s> as something to be honored? — for those who imagine thus, in order to remove the obstacle of their limited learning, the sixth topic

body.text: anenārthataḥ 'bodhisattvena śrutaparyeṣaṇakāle buddhotpāda ārādhanīyastadanantaraṃ buddhadharmā udgṛhītavyāḥ'; ityabhiniveśo vipakṣatvena nirdiṣṭaḥ | tatprahāṇe chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamityapi nirdiṣṭam | asti sa kaścid dharmo dīpaṅkarasyāntikādudgṛhītaḥ? iti diṅmātrābhidhānena udgṛhītadharmasya sarvanimittaṃ vinivartate | 'nāsti sa kaścid dharma udgṛhītaḥ'; ityanena paramārthataḥ dharmāṇāmagrāhyatvaṃ vyavasthāpya tatra yogasamāpattiḥ vikṣepanigrahaśca nirdiṣṭau | sthānasyāsya gāmbhīryamapi paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: By this, the intended meaning is: 'During the time of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s pursuit of learning, the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> should be honored, and subsequently the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> should be received.' The attachment [to this process] is indicated as being on the side of the adversary (that which is to be abandoned). For its abandonment, one should abide in aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and resolution (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) — this too is indicated. The question 'Was any <s>dharma</s> received from <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>?' — by this mere indication, the <s>dharma</s> that was received

body.text: 7. kṣetraviśuddhipraṇidhāna-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 7. The topic of the vow for field-purification (<s>kṣetraviśuddhipraṇidhāna-sthāna</s>):

body.text: yadi paramārthataḥ karmakartrādayo na syustadā kathaṃ bodhisattvā buddhakṣetrapariśodhanārthaṃ praṇidadhatīti tarkayatāṃ teṣāṃ hīnālambanamanasikārabhāvanāvibandhasaṃyogārthaṃ saptamasthānamadhikṛtyāha- yaḥ kaścid bodhisattvaḥ iti | vitatham iti mṛṣā | yadyevaṃ (tarhi) bhagavān bodhisattvānāṃ tattatkṣetrapariśuddhisampadaṃ kathamuktavāniti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? iti pṛcchāyaṃ kṣetravyūhāḥ ityādi samādhānamabhihitam | bahūni kṣetrāṇi tu kṣetravyūhāḥ | avyūhāste iti paramāṇubhirābdho 'vayavibhūto vā nāsti kaścid vyūhaḥ paramārthata ityavyūhā eva te, tathāpi svapnopalabdhakṣetravyūhavad avicāraramaṇīyamātra saṃvṛtisattvamuktaṃ tenocyante kṣetravyūhāḥ iti | anyathā (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_153

children.text: ) paramārthasvabhāvastvanābhilāpyatāyānabhilāpya ityabhiprāyaḥ | uktañcāpratiṣṭhitatvaṃ prāgeva | evāṃ muṣitasmṛtikānāmupakārāya upasaṃhāropayena smārayituṃ tasmād ityādyāha | evam iti yathoktena vidhinā, kasyacidapi vastunaḥ siddherabhāvāt tatra 'apratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam'; ityarthaḥ | śeṣaṃ tu pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: The ultimate nature, however, is inexpressible because of inexpressibility — this is the intent. And non-establishment has already been stated previously. Thus, in order to remind those whose mindfulness has been impaired, by way of summary, he says the words beginning with 'therefore.' 'Thus' means in the manner stated. Since no thing whatsoever is established, the meaning is: 'one should generate a mind that is not established in anything.' The remainder

body.translated_text: If ultimately action, agent, and the rest do not exist, then how do <s>bodhisattvas</s> make vows for the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields? — for those who reason thus, in order to effect disengagement from the impediment of cultivating mental attention based on inferior objects, the seventh topic is addressed by saying: 'Whoever is a <s>bodhisattva</s>...' '<s>Vitatham</s>' means false. If so, [then how did] the <s>Bhagavān</s> [speak of] such and such [field-arrays] for the <s>bodhisattvas</s>?

body.text: tatra vitathaṃ vadet ityanenārthataḥ paramārthataḥ mayā kṣetravyūho niṣpādyata ityabhiniveśo vipakṣatvena paridīpitaḥ | 'kṣetravyūhāḥ'; iti nimittamātrābhidhānena samastahīnālambanabhāvanāvisaṃyogo nirdiṣṭaḥ | hīnālambanamanasikārabhāvanāṃ prati chandaḥ praṇidhānamapi [na karttavyamityapi] nirdiṣṭam | avyūhāste tathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ ityanena paramārthavyavasthāpanena yogasamāpattau pravṛttiḥ gambhīratā ca nirdiśyete | tenocyante kṣetravyūhāḥ ityanenāpavādāntaṃ parihṛtya vikṣepanigraho nirdiṣṭaḥ, sthānasyāsya audāryaṃ ca paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: is clear. Therein, by [the statement] 'he would speak falsely,' the intended meaning is: the attachment [thinking] 'the field-array is accomplished by me ultimately' is indicated as being on the side of the adversary. By the mere indication '<s>kṣetravyūhāḥ</s>' (field-arrays), disengagement from the entire cultivation of mental attention based on inferior objects is indicated. It is also indicated that aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) toward the cultivation of mental attention based on inferior objects [should not be made].

body.text: 8. sattvaparipāka-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 8. The topic of the maturation of sentient beings (<s>sattvaparipāka-sthāna</s>):

body.text: skandhebhyaḥ pṛthaktvenāsattve 'pi kiṃ nābhinnā eva sattvāḥ? anyathā sattvaparipākārthaṃ kathaṃ bodhisattvāḥ pravarteran? iti yo vicāraḥ, tasmāt sattvopekṣālakṣaṇavighnabhūtād visaṃyogārtham aṣṭamasthānamadhikṛtya tadyathāpi nāma ityuktam | puruṣaḥ ityasurendro rāhuriti | tasyātmabhāvastu kāmadhātau sumeruparimāṇaḥ | tasya mahattve 'pi vyarthaiva tanmahattā | kimarthaṃ deśitaṃ bhagavatetyabhiprāyaṃ vaktukāmanayā tatkasya hetoḥ? ityāpṛṣṭam | tameva abhiprāyaṃ vaktumāha- na bhāvaḥ iti | paramārthataḥ ekānekasvabhāvena viyogāt (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_154

children.text: ) niḥsvabhāvatā eva | svapnadṛṣṭa iva sa ātmabhāvaḥ saṃvṛtitaḥ proktastathāgatena, na tu paramārthataḥ |
children.translated_text: [and its nature] is precisely the absence of inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>). That physical form is said by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be like [one] seen in a dream — conventionally, not ultimately.

body.translated_text: Even though [sentient beings] do not exist separately from the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), are sentient beings not simply identical [with them]? If otherwise, how would <s>bodhisattvas</s> engage in the maturation of sentient beings? — [for those who engage in] such inquiry, in order to effect disengagement from the obstacle characterized by indifference toward sentient beings, the eighth topic is addressed by saying: 'Just as, for example...' '<s>Puruṣa</s>' (person) [means] <s>Asurendra</s> (lord of <s>Asuras</s>) <s>Rāhu</s>. His physical form, however, is in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>)

body.text: tenocyate ātmabhāvaḥ ityatropapattimāha | evamayaṃ saṃvṛtireva, tasmāttathocyate, anyathā paramārthataḥ kasyacidapi dharmasyāsiddhatvāt tathā nocyetetyabhiprāyaḥ | abhāvaṃ tāvad bhāvatvenābhyupagacchatāṃ teṣāṃ jaiminyādīnāṃ pratiṣedhārtham na sa bhāvaḥ ityāha | abhāvasya tu bhāvavyatirekeṇa sthitalakṣaṇatvāt kathaṃ tadviparītasvabhāvo na syāt?'; tenocyate ātmabhāvaḥ'; | anyathā patamārthataḥ kasyacidapyātmabhāvasyāsiddheḥ kimityātmabhāva ihocyate, tato 'yamabhāvatvena deśitaḥ sumerumātraparimāṇo 'pi ya ātmabhāvo yadā niḥsvabhāvatvāt paramārthato nāsti, tadā kathaṃ parātmabhāvaḥ sasvabhāvaḥ sātmako vā bhavet?
body.translated_text: He states the reason why it is called 'physical form' (<s>ātmabhāva</s>): Thus, this is merely conventional reality (<s>saṃvṛti</s>); therefore it is so called. Otherwise, since nothing whatsoever is established ultimately, it would not be so called — this is the intent. In order to refute those such as <s>Jaimini</s> and others who accept non-existence as a [kind of] entity, he says: 'That is not an entity.' But [the question of] non-existence's standing as distinct from entity

body.text: atrārthataḥ sattvaparipākāyodyamaratānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ sattvābhiniveśaḥ paramārthataḥ vipakṣatvena pradarśitaḥ tatprahāṇāya chandaḥ praṇidhānaṃ ca nirdiṣṭe | 'puruṣaḥ'; ityupalakṣaṇamātrābhidhānena aṇḍajādīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ pṛthagātmabhāvānāṃ parigrahaṇamuktam | na bhāvaḥ sa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ ityanena tāvat paramārthaṃ vyasthāpya yogasamāpattisthānaṃ gambhīratvaṃ ca paridīpite | na sa bhāvaḥ ityanena tu vikṣepanigraho nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here the intended meaning is: for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who delight in effort for the maturation of sentient beings, attachment to sentient beings is shown to be ultimately on the side of the adversary. For its abandonment, aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) are indicated. By the mere illustrative term '<s>puruṣa</s>' (person), the inclusion of all distinct physical forms of those born from eggs and the rest is stated. By [the statement] 'That entity is not spoken of as an entity by the <s>Tathāgata</s>,'

body.text: 9. bāhyaśāstreṣu vyapagatarāgatā-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 9. The topic of detachment from external treatises (<s>bāhyaśāstreṣu vyapagatarāgatā-sthāna</s>):

body.text: sampratyasya dharmaparyāyasya mahārthatvapratipādanena bāhyaśāstreṣvabhiniviṣṭānāṃ tatrānunayavikṣepaparihārārthaṃ navamasthānamadhikṛtya- tatkiṃ manyase sūbhūte ityāha | (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_155

children.text: ) anena tāvat caturbhiḥ prakārairasya dharmaparyāyasya vaiśiṣṭyaṃ paridīpyatepuṇyaparigrahaḥ, devādibhiḥ satkāraḥ, duskarakṛtyavidhānam, tathāgatāditulyatākaraṇam | tatra puṇyaparigrahastu yadāha tato nidānaṃ bahupuṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyāt iti | devādibhiḥ satkārastu yadāha sa pṛthivīpradeśaḥ caityabhūtyabhūto bhaved iti | duṣkarakṛtyavidhānaṃ tu yadāha parameṇa te āścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti iti | tathāgatāditulyatākaraṇaṃ tu yadāha tasmiṃśca pṛthivīpradeśe śāstā viharatyanyatarānyataro vā vijñagurusthānīyaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: ) By this, the excellence of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) is illuminated in four ways: the gathering of merit, the worship by gods and others, the undertaking of difficult deeds, and the making [of the practitioner] equal to <s>Tathāgatas</s> and the like. There, the gathering of merit is what is stated as 'from that basis, one would produce a great accumulation of merit.' The worship by gods and others is what is stated as 'that spot of earth would become a shrine (<s>caityabhūta</s>).' The undertaking of difficult deeds is what is stated as 'they will be endowed with the supreme wonder.' The making [of the practitioner] equal to <s>Tathāgatas</s> and the like is what is stated as 'in that spot of earth, the Teacher dwells, or one or another [person] worthy of the status of a wise teacher.'

body.translated_text: Now, in order to establish the great significance of this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, and to remove the distraction caused by attraction toward external treatises for those who are attached to them, the ninth topic is addressed by saying: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?'

body.text: tatra ratnadānasya puṇyābhidhānaṃ viśeṣadvayena viśiṣṭaṃ paridīpitam- vastuviśeṣaḥ kṣetraviśeṣaśca | vastuviśeṣo 'pi tāvat udāraḥ praṇītaśceti |- (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_156

children.text: ) tatraudāryaṃ tu vastubhedasaṃbāhulyam, yadāha tāvato lokadhātūn iti | praṇītastu loke dūrlabhatvena khyātaḥ yadāha saptaratnaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā iti | kṣetraṃ svaparārthasampadyogena viśiṣṭam | tatra parārthasampattāvat heyopādeyārthānāṃ parebhyo 'viparyayeṇa samprakāśanam, āha tathāgatebhyaḥ iti | yathā vastutathatā tathā bhāṣitatvāt niruktyā tathā ukta iti kathyate |
children.translated_text: There, magnificence is the abundance of varieties of substance, as stated 'as many world-realms.' Excellence is that which is renowned in the world as rare, as stated 'having filled [them] with the seven precious substances.' The field is distinguished by the conjunction of accomplishing one's own and others' aims. There, regarding the accomplishment of others' aims: the non-distorted exposition to others of the meanings to be abandoned and adopted — he says 'from the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.' Because reality (<s>vastutathatā</s>) is spoken just as it is, by etymology it is said to be 'thus spoken' (<s>tathā ukta</s>).

body.translated_text: There, the declaration of merit for the gift of jewels has been illuminated as distinguished by two distinctions: distinction of substance and distinction of field. The distinction of substance is further twofold: magnificent and excellent —

body.text: svārthasampattu jñāna-prahāṇasampadbhedena dvividhā | tatra arhadbhyaḥ ityanena prahāṇasampad darśitā, hatakleśāritvād niruktyā 'arhan'; ityucyate | samyaksambuddhebhyaḥ ityanena tāvajjñānasampaduktā | tasmāt padatrayasyokteḥ sāphalyamiti sāmānyena saṅgrahārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of one's own aim is twofold, by the division of the accomplishment of knowledge and the accomplishment of abandonment. There, 'from the <s>Arhats</s>' — by this, the accomplishment of abandonment has been shown, since by etymology <s>arhan</s> is so called because of having slain the enemy of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). 'From the <s>samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> (perfectly awakened ones)' — by this, the accomplishment of knowledge has been stated. Therefore, the fruitfulness of stating the three terms is for the purpose of general inclusion.

body.text: ārocayāmi itīcchā dyotitā bhavati | ārocayāmi prativedayāmi avabodhayāmi prajñāmutpādayāmītyarthaḥ | tatra pūrvaṃ tāvat parasya phalam athavā aparaṃ tu pūrvasya vyākhyānam | deśayet iti śabdaṃ samprakāśayet iti chandam adhimuktimutpādayedityarthaḥ | saṃkhyayā paricchettumaśakyatvād asaṃkhyeyam iti | pramāpayitumaśakyatvād dṛṣtāntābhāvād vā aprameyam iti |
body.translated_text: 'I declare' — [the word] indicates his wish. 'I declare, I announce, I make known, I generate wisdom' — this is the meaning. There, the first [expression] is the fruit for the other [person], or alternatively the latter is the explanation of the former. 'Would teach' means 'would make the words clear,' meaning 'would generate desire and conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>).' Because it cannot be delimited by number, [it is called] 'innumerable' (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>). Because it cannot be measured, or because there is no example [sufficient to illustrate it], [it is called] 'immeasurable' (<s>aprameya</s>).

body.text: bhāṣyeta iti ātmanā granthasvādhyāyaḥ, samprakāśyeta iti parebhyaḥ samyak padārthadeśānā, athavā 'bhāṣyeta'; iti padam 'samprakāśyeta'; ityartham | caityabhūtyabhūtaḥ iti vandanīyaḥ, caitya eva caityabhūtaḥ vaśībhūta itivat, yadaivaṃ pudgalanairātmyagāthāmātropadeśenāpi caityabhūtyabhūto jāyate kiṃ khalu punaḥ nairātmyadvayopadeśena ityabhiprāyaḥ | udgṛhya iti padam, dhārayiṣyanti ityavismaraṇam, vācayiṣyanti iti pustakagatam paryavāpsyanti iti artham |
body.translated_text: 'Would be recited' means one's own study of the text (<s>svādhyāya</s>); 'would be elucidated' means the proper exposition of the meaning of the words to others. Alternatively, the word 'would be recited' has the meaning of 'would be elucidated.' '<s>Caityabhūtyabhūta</s>' means 'worthy of veneration'; a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) itself is <s>caityabhūta</s>, like [the expression] '<s>vaśībhūta</s>' (one who has become controlled). If even through the mere teaching of a verse on <s>pudgalanairātmya</s> (non-self of persons) [a place] becomes a shrine, how much more so through the teaching of the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) — this is the intent. The word '<s>udgṛhya</s>' [means 'having taken up']; '<s>dhārayiṣyanti</s>' means not forgetting; '<s>vācayiṣyanti</s>' refers to that which is written in a book; '<s>paryavāpsyanti</s>' means [grasping] the meaning.

body.text: anena tāvad śrutamayaprajñayā dhāraṇaṃ darśitam, cintāmayyā bhāvanāmayyā prajñayā codgṛhītatvād yoniśaśca (manasi kariṣyanti) ityāha | aviparītatayārthamavabodhayiṣyantīti vākyaśeṣaḥ | kvacid dhārayiṣyanti ityekameva padam, tatra dhāraṇaṃ tu padārthayordraṣṭavyam | parameṇa āścaryeṇa iti tu evaṃvidhagambhīrodāradharmasyādhigatatvāt |
body.translated_text: By this, retention through <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of hearing) has been shown; and because it has been taken up through <s>cintāmayī</s> (wisdom born of reflection) and <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of meditation), he says 'and will attend to it with proper mental engagement (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>).' 'They will understand the meaning without distortion' — this completes the sentence. In some [readings], '<s>dhārayiṣyanti</s>' is a single word only; there, retention should be understood in terms of both the words and the meanings. 'With supreme wonder' — because of having realized such a profound and magnificent <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: śāstā ........ sthānīyaḥ iti dharmabhāṇakaḥ, śāstṛkṛtyakaraṇāt, sa eva sākṣād dharamāṇabuddha iveti vākyaśeṣaḥ | guru iti mañjughoṣādyanyataraḥ kaścit tatkāryasādhanāya dharmabhāṇakaḥ sthānīyarūpeṇa draṣṭavyaḥ | kutracit anyatarānyataro iti padadvayam | tacca ye kecana gurusadṛśāḥ (teṣāṃ) sarveṣāṃ paryāyaḥ | atastatra sthānīyaḥ iti nirdiṣṭaḥ | ebhiḥ sarvaiḥ sthānasyāsyaudāryaṃ nirūpitam | arthataśca saddharmaparigrahamutsṛjya bāhyaśāstrānurāgo vipakṣatvena paridīpitaḥ, tasminnanurāgaṃ parityajya dharmaṃ pratipattuṃ chandaḥ praṇidhānaṃ ca darśite | ito dharmaparyāyād ityupalakṣaṇamātraparikīrtanena bāhyaśāstreṣvanurāgaṃ parivarjya sarvasaddharmān prati yatna āstheya iti paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: 'The Teacher... worthy of the status [of teacher]' — [this refers to] the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (Dharma reciter), because he performs the function of the Teacher; he is as if the <s>Buddha</s> himself presently living — this completes the sentence. '<s>Guru</s>' means any one such as <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> or another; a <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> for accomplishing that [teaching] function should be regarded in the role of a representative. In some [readings], '<s>anyatarānyatara</s>' is two words. And that is an expression encompassing all those who are like a <s>guru</s>. Therefore 'worthy of the status [of teacher]' has been stated. By all of these, the nobility of this station has been established. And in meaning, having shown that abandoning the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) and pursuing external treatises (<s>bāhyaśāstra</s>) is the adversary, it has been illuminated that one should abandon attachment to those [external treatises] and that desire (<s>chanda</s>) and aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for practicing the <s>Dharma</s> have been demonstrated. The mention 'from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>' is merely illustrative; [the intent is] that having abandoned attachment to external treatises, effort should be applied toward all true <s>Dharma</s> teachings.

body.text: acintyasāmarthyanvitatvādayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ nāmamātraśravaṇenāpi parānupakarotīti sattvānāṃ puṇyotpādakathanāya āryasubhūtiḥ ko nāma ayam iti pṛṣṭavān |- (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_158

children.text: ) kathaṃ cainaṃ dhārayāmi ityanena asyodgrahaṇenāpyaprameyapuṇyaṃ bhavatīti paridīpyate |
children.translated_text: By 'how shall I retain it?', it is illuminated that even by taking up this [discourse], immeasurable merit arises.

body.translated_text: Because this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) is pervaded by inconceivable power, even by merely hearing the name it benefits others — to express the generation of merit for beings, the noble <s>Subhūti</s> asked 'what is the name of this [discourse]?'

body.text: prajñāpāramitā nāma iti yasyā tannāma tattathā ucyate | iyaṃ prajñāpi, pāramadhigamya paricchedayatītyapi pāramiteti, prajñā ca sā pāramitā ceti samāsaḥ | athavā prajñāyāḥ pāraṃ prajñāpāram, anayā tadadhigamya paricchidyate 'tastathocyate | sā cārthataḥ sarvavidhaprajñāsu uttamā tāthāgatī prajñā nānyadā prajñayā pāraṃ parimāpayituṃ śakyam | athavā prajñyāpāram itā gatā ityevārthaḥ | sā ca yathoktā prajñaiva, na tvanyat tatpāragamanāsambhavāt | anena dānapāramitādayo 'pyuktā bhavantīti | tadabhidhānenāyaṃ dharmaparyāyo 'pi tathoktaḥ, yathā sītāharaṇādikāvyayojanā | tasyāśca bhagavatāḥ pratyātmavedyatvenāsādhāraṇatvāt paramārthataścānutpannatvāt sā śabdenābhidhātuṃ na śakyata ityāśayena vitarkya tatkasya hetoḥ? itio pṛṣṭavān | yaiva subhūte, prajñāpāramitā tathāgatena bhāṣitā sā ityudatarat |
body.translated_text: 'Named <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — that whose name is such is so called. This is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and also, because it determines [things] having reached the far shore (<s>pāra</s>), it is <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection); <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that is <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) — such is the compound. Alternatively, the far shore of wisdom is <s>prajñāpāra</s>; because through this [wisdom] one determines [things] having reached that [far shore], it is so called. And that, in meaning, is the supreme among all types of wisdom — the wisdom of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; the far shore of wisdom cannot be measured by any other wisdom. Alternatively, '<s>prajñāyāḥ pāram itā</s>' means 'gone to the far shore of wisdom' — this is the meaning. And that is precisely the wisdom as described, not something else, because going to that far shore is impossible [for anything else]. By this, the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) and the others are also included. By the designation of that [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>], this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> is also so called, like the arrangement of a poem about the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>. And because that [wisdom] of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is uncommon due to being self-experienced, and because it is ultimately unoriginated, it cannot be designated by words — with this intent, pondering [this], he asked 'for what reason?' [The <s>Bhagavān</s>] answered: 'That which, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that...'

body.text: paramārthataḥ pratyātmavedyatvenāsādhāraṇatvāt paramārthataśca sarvadharmāṇām atyantānutpannatvāt ca sā na śabdenābhidheyā, tathāpi vikalpapratibimbaḥ- (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_159

children.text: ) svasvarūpabahirbhūta ivāropyate | sa vikalpo 'pi prakṛtyā bhrāntaḥ, atastena samāropita ākāro 'pi mithyaiva | tasmāt vikalpapratibimbabhūtā yā prajñāpāramitā tathāgatena deśitā, sā śabdena vyutpādyamānā apāramitaiva, na tu tathāgatasya prajñā, satyasaṃvṛtyā jñeyasya pāraṅgatatvāttasyāḥ, anyathā kathaṃ bhagavān sarvajñaḥ syāditi | tato bhrāntapratīteḥ sa vikalpapratibimbo naiva bhedenāvagamyate, ato jñānasvabhāvatvena saiva paramārthaprajñā tathāgatena bhāṣitā ityucyate | tasmāt tathāvidhadeśanāyāṃ naiva virodha ityabhiprāyaḥ | athavā yā tāthāgatī prajñā pratītirūpatvena tathāgatena bhāṣitā saiva paramārthato na vidyate, paramārthato 'pāraṅgatatvāttasyāḥ | eva iti śabdastu apāramitā ityetadanantaraṃ draṣṭavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: it is superimposed as if external to its own essential nature. That conceptual construction too is by nature erroneous; therefore the aspect superimposed by it is also merely false. Therefore, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that is a reflection of conceptual construction, as taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, when being conveyed through words, is indeed a non-perfection (<s>apāramitā</s>), not the wisdom of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [itself], because that [wisdom] has gone beyond the knowable in authentic conventional truth (<s>satyasaṃvṛti</s>) — otherwise, how could the <s>Bhagavān</s> be omniscient? Therefore, since that reflection of conceptual construction is not apprehended as different [from the ultimate], by virtue of being of the nature of knowledge (<s>jñānasvabhāva</s>), it is said that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has spoken that very [reflection] as the ultimate <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom). Therefore, there is no contradiction in such teaching — this is the intent. Alternatively, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s wisdom, which was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as having the form of conventional understanding (<s>pratītirūpa</s>), that very [wisdom] does not exist ultimately, because ultimately it has not gone beyond (<s>apāraṅgata</s>). The word 'eva' (indeed/only) should be seen as following after '<s>apāramitā</s>' (non-perfection).

body.translated_text: Ultimately, because of being uncommon due to being self-experienced (<s>pratyātmavedya</s>), and because ultimately all <s>dharmas</s> are absolutely unoriginated, it cannot be designated by words. Nevertheless, [it is] a reflection of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpapratibimba</s>) —

body.text: anena paramārthatvaṃ pratipādya tatra yogasamāpattyā kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti nirdiṣṭam | yathā prajñāpāramitā vikalpapratibimbātmikaiva bāhyatvena samāropya bhagavatā bhāṣitā, tathaiva sarve dharmā api nānyathā tathāgatena kathitā iti deśanārthamāha- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte iti | paramārthataḥ sarvadharmāṇāmasiddhatvāt, siddheṣvapi svalakṣaṇasyāsādhāraṇatvena saṅketena prajñapayitumaśakyatvāt, sāmānyalakṣaṇameva tāvat prajñapyamānatvāt, svasāmānyalakṣaṇe vyatiricya aparasyābhidheyasyābhāvāt parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvāttayoḥ, ata eva ca paramārthataḥ 'nāsti kaścid dharmo yastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ'; iti vijñāya sthaviraḥ subhūtiḥ no hīdaṃ bhagavan, nāsti sa kaścid dharmo yastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ ityavocat | anena vikṣepanigrahaḥ gāmbhīryaṃ ca nirdiṣṭe bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: Having thus established the ultimate nature, how one should practice through <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) has been taught. Just as the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, being of the nature of a mere reflection of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpapratibimba</s>), was spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s> by superimposing it as external, in exactly the same way all <s>dharmas</s> too were spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in no other way — to convey the meaning of the teaching, he says 'what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' Because ultimately all <s>dharmas</s> are unestablished; because even among established [<s>dharmas</s>], the particular characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) cannot be designated through convention due to being uncommon; because only the general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) is what is designated; because apart from the particular and general characteristics there is no other designatum; and because those two [characteristics] exist through mutual exclusion — for this very reason, having understood that ultimately 'there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>,' the elder <s>Subhūti</s> declared: 'No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' By this, the restraint of distraction (<s>vikṣepanigraha</s>) and the profundity have been taught.

body.text: 10. sattvabhājanalokayoḥ piṇḍagrāhaviśīrṇatāyoga-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 10. The station of the disintegration of gross apprehension (<s>piṇḍagrāha</s>) regarding the world of beings (<s>sattvāloka</s>) and the world of environment (<s>bhājanāloka</s>):

body.text: evaṃ sarvadharmeṣu nairātmyaṃ vistareṇa darśitam, tathāpi ye tāvad ādikarmikāḥ kathaṃ sarvadharmeṣu nairātmyaṃ bhāvayitavyamiti cintayanti, bhāvanimittamabhiobhavitumanupāyakauśalavisaṃyogārthaṃ daśamasthānadhikṛtyāha- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādi | atra dvividhena upāyena ekānekasvabhāvaviyogādhigamāt sarvadharmanairātmyaṃ bhāvayitavyamiti darśyate | tatra dvividha upāyastāvat tanūkaraṇopāyaḥ nirābhāsakaraṇopāyaśca | tatra yāvat pṛthivīrajo bhavet ityanena ekasvabhāvaviyogādhigamāt tanūkaraṇopāyo nirdiśyate | na yujyate hyasya lokadhātorekatvam, āvṛttānāvṛttādivispaṣṭalakṣaṇayuktatvād | anekatvanirākaraṇāya tāvat paramāṇornirākaraṇamabhyupetavyam | ata eva paramāṇuvibhāvanāyāṃ sattyāmekatvaṃ prahīyata eveti | bodhisattvaistāvat prāyeṇa parīttālambanamanasikārābhāvāt trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātvālambanārthaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasre ityāha | anena tāvadaudāryaṃ paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: Thus, the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> has been shown at length. Nevertheless, for those beginners who think "How should the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> be cultivated?" and for the purpose of separating them from lack of skill in means when overcoming the sign of cultivation, he speaks regarding the tenth station: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?" and so forth. Here it is shown that the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> should be cultivated through two methods, namely the realization of separation from one-nature and many-nature. The twofold method is: the method of attenuation and the method of eliminating appearance. By "as much earth-dust as there would be," the method of attenuation through realization of separation from one-nature is indicated. For the oneness of this world-system is not tenable, since it possesses clearly distinct characteristics such as covered and uncovered [areas]. For the refutation of multiplicity, the refutation of the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) must be accepted. For this very reason, when the analysis of atoms is accomplished, oneness is indeed abandoned. Since <s>bodhisattvas</s> generally lack mental attention directed at limited objects, he says "three-thousand-great-thousand" for the purpose of taking the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system as the object. By this, the vastness [of the practice] has been illuminated.

body.text: te ca paramāṇavo 'pi yadi digbhāgabhedena bhinnatvādasiddhā eva syuḥ, (tarhiṃ) kathaṃ tad bahu rajaḥ? iti pravādināmāśayamabhilakṣya kasya (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 161]

children.text: ) hetoḥ? ityapṛcchat | yattad pṛthivīrajaḥ iti tadudatarat | bahu tat pṛthivīrajo 'pi yaḥ paramāṇusvabhāva uktastadekatvagrahaṇaniṣedhāt tadaraja eva | māyānirmitasvabhāvatvānnāsti paramāṇuḥ paramārthataḥ, buddhyopacaritarūpatvāt | idaṃ tāvadekatvagrahaṇopāyamātram, na tu paramārtham, tenocyate pṛthivīraja iti | tad yuktaṃ saṃvṛtau sattvāt, anyathā paramārthastasyāsattvād anabhilāpyatvācca svalakṣaṇaṃ nābhilapyata ityevamabhiprāyaḥ | udbhāvanāsaṃvṛtyāpi tasya deśanaṃ na yujyate, tadīyānyatarātmasvabhāvasya apratibhāsamānatvāt | anena tāvad anekasvabhāvaviyogādhigamopāyo nirābhāsakaraṇatvenopadarśyate | evañcāntaśaḥ paramāṇūnāmapi yuktyā pratyekaṃ parikṣyamāṇānāṃ pratītāveva sattvāt pratīyate lokadhātūnāṃ cānekasvaviyuktatvam, tataśca (teṣāṃ) niḥsvabhāvatvamavagamyate |
children.translated_text: asked "For what reason?" "That which is earth-dust"—he answered that. "That much earth-dust" also, that which has been said to be of the nature of atoms, since the grasping of its oneness is negated, that is indeed non-dust. Because of being of the nature of a magical creation, the atom does not exist ultimately, since it is a form superimposed by the mind. This is merely a method for [refuting] the grasping of oneness, not the ultimate [truth]; therefore it is called "earth-dust." That is fitting since it exists in conventional [truth]; otherwise, since it does not exist ultimately and since it is inexpressible, its own characteristic cannot be expressed—such is the purport. Even through the convention of analysis, its teaching is not proper, because neither of its possible natures [one or many] appears. By this, the method of realization of separation from many-nature is demonstrated as the elimination of appearance. And thus, when even atoms, being examined individually by reasoning, exist only in dependence, the separation of world-systems from many-nature is understood, and from that their essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) is comprehended.

body.translated_text: If those atoms too, being divided by the division of directional parts, would indeed be unestablished, then how could "that be much dust?"—discerning the intent of the proponents, [<s>Subhūti</s>]

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhājanalokasya ekānekasvabhāvaviyogena niḥsvabhāvatvamṝ evamabhidhāya sattvalokasyāpyabhidhānārtha yo 'sau lokadhātuḥ ityāha | atra lokadhātunā sattvaloko 'bhipretaḥ, itarasya pūrvamevoktatvāt | adhātuḥ saḥ iti ekānekasvabhāvarahitaḥ sa ityabhiprāyaḥ | evaṃ yo hi rūpaskandhaḥ sa bhājanalokatvenābhihitaḥ, śeṣāścatvāraḥ skandhāstu yathaikānekasvabhāvena viyuktāstathā pūrvaṃ vivecitā eva | evaṃ sati paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatvāt sarve dharmā māyopamā dṛśyante yogibhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the essencelessness of the vessel-world through separation from one-and-many nature, in order to state [the same] for the sentient-being world as well, he says "that which is a world-system." Here, by "world-system," the sentient-being world is intended, since the other [vessel-world] has already been stated. "That is non-realm" means: it is devoid of one-and-many nature—such is the purport. Thus, the form-aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>) has been stated as the vessel-world, while the remaining four <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) have already been analyzed as separated from one-and-many nature, as previously discussed. This being so, since all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately essenceless, they are seen by <s>yogins</s> as being like an illusion.

body.text: anena gāmbhīryamapi tāvaduktam | arthataḥ paramārthe sattvabhājanalokīyabhāvābhiniveśo vipakṣatvena paridīpitaḥ | tatprahāṇārthaṃ ca chandaḥ praṇidhānaṃ ca nirdiṣṭe | trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau iti nimittamātrābhidhānena sarvabhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvabhāvanā sandarśitā | arajastat iti adhātuḥ ityābhyāṃ paramārthavyavasthāpanayā yogasamāpattyā kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti tat paridīpitam | tenocyate lokadhātuḥ ityanenāpavādāntaṃ parihṛtya vikṣepanigraho nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, the profundity too has been stated. In meaning, the grasping at the ultimate existence of the sentient-being and vessel-worlds has been illuminated as being on the side of the opponent. Aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and resolve (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for the purpose of abandoning that [grasping] have been indicated. By the expression "three-thousand-great-thousand world-system," through the designation of mere signs, the cultivation of the essencelessness of all entities has been demonstrated. By "that is non-dust" and "that is non-realm," through the establishment of the ultimate meaning, how one should practice through <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) has been illuminated. By "therefore it is called world-system," having avoided the extreme of nihilism (<s>apavāda</s>), the restraint of distraction has been indicated.

body.text: 11. tathāgatapūjāsatkāra-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 11. The station of worship and veneration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>:

body.text: samprati ye bodhisattvāḥ puṇyasambhārapratipattaye 'tyantamupakāritvād bhagavantaṃ pūjayeyusteṣāṃ tasya (bhagavataḥ) avināśikāyo na pūrayati puṇyasambhāram, samyaṅmanasikārāpravṛttatvāt | tasmāt teṣāṃ sambhārāsañcayato viyogārthaṃ ekādaśasthānamadhikṛtyāha- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādi | sāmānyato 'trāyaṃ saṅgrahārthaḥ, tathāgatapūjāsatkāreṣu lakṣaṇasampadā tathāgato na draṣṭavyaḥ, atha kathamiti cet? paramārthadharmatāyāmityucyate |
body.translated_text: Now, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who, for the practice of the accumulation of merit, would worship the <s>Bhagavān</s> as being supremely beneficial—their [concept of] the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s imperishable body does not fulfill the accumulation of merit, because of the non-engagement of right mental attention. Therefore, for the purpose of separating them from failure to accumulate [merit], he speaks regarding the eleventh station: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?" and so forth. The general purport here is: in the worship and veneration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of marks. If [one asks] "Then how?"—it is said: "Through the ultimate <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature)."

body.text: iha avaśiṣṭavyākhyānaṃ tu rūpakāyāptikāmatāsthānānurūpam | na cātra punaruktirapyāśaṅkanīyā | pūrvaṃ rūpakāyāptikāmatāprasaṅge tu tadvyudāso darśitaḥ, adhunā tathāgatapūjāsatkāraprasaṅge darśitatvād bhinna eva (rūpakāyaḥ) | atrārthataḥ rūpakāye tathāgatābhiniveśaṃ vipakṣatvena nirdiśya tatprahānārthaṃ chandaḥ praṇidhānaṃ cāpi pradarśite | lakṣaṇāni ityupalakṣaṇamātroktyā sakalo rūpakāyaḥ paridīpitaḥ | alakṣaṇāni iti paramārthavyavasthānam | tena ityādinā vikṣepanigraho nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the remaining explanation follows the pattern of the station of desire for attaining the <s>rūpakāya</s>. Nor should repetition be suspected here. Previously, in the context of the desire for attaining the <s>rūpakāya</s>, its removal was shown; now, since it is shown in the context of worship and veneration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>rūpakāya</s> is indeed distinct [in this context]. Here, in meaning, the attachment to [seeing] the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the <s>rūpakāya</s> is indicated as being on the side of the opponent. Aspiration and resolve for the purpose of abandoning that are also demonstrated. By the expression "marks" alone, as a mere indication, the entire <s>rūpakāya</s> is illuminated. "Non-marks" is the establishment of the ultimate. By "therefore" and so forth, the restraint of distraction is indicated.

body.text: 12. kāyacittapariśrāntau viryamyukhyānārambhalābha-satkāravirahitatā :
body.translated_text: 12. Freedom from aversion to effort, laziness, and lack of attachment to gain and honor when body and mind are exhausted:

body.text: evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nairātmyāvagamopāye nirdiṣṭe 'pi kāyajīviteṣvāsajya ye lābhasatkārādhyasitāḥ kausīdyalābhasatkārapiṇḍapātānuraktā teṣāṃ tatrānuraktivisaṃyogārthaṃ dvādaśasthānamadhikṛtyāha- yaśca khalu punaḥ sūbhūte, strī vā puruṣo vā ityādi |
body.translated_text: Even though the method for comprehending the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> has thus been indicated, for those who, being attached to body and life, are settled in gain and honor, fond of laziness, and attached to gain, honor, and alms—for the purpose of separating them from such attachment, he speaks regarding the twelfth station: "And moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, whether a woman or a man..." and so forth.

body.text: anena cāsāre 'nekaśatasahasraduḥkhaikasthānatucchātmabhāve tasmin snihyan etāvacchariraparityāgenāpi yatpuṇyaṃ na prāptam, tadantarāyakaratvāttasmin kāyajīvite nirapekṣacittatayā sarvātmanāsmin (dharmaparyāye) yogaḥ karaṇīya iti paridipitam | anenārthataḥ kausīdyādayo vipakṣatvena darśitāḥ | tatprahāṇāya saddharmasamādānāya ca chandaḥ praṇidhānañcāpi nirdiṣṭe | ito dharmaparyāyāt ityupalakṣaṇamātroktyā samastamahāyānaśravaṇādīni ābadhyante | bahutaraṃ puṇyam ityanena ādāryamuktam |
body.translated_text: By this, it is illuminated that: in this insubstantial, valueless [body] which is the single locus of hundreds of thousands of sufferings—even through the sacrifice of so much body-life, the merit that is not obtained [merely through bodily sacrifice]—since that [attachment to body] is an obstacle, one should, with a mind indifferent to body and life, engage in <s>yoga</s> with one's entire being in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. By this, in meaning, laziness and the like are shown as being on the side of the opponent. Aspiration and resolve for abandoning those and for undertaking the true <s>Dharma</s> have been indicated. By the expression "from this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse" alone, as a mere indication, all hearing and the like of the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> are encompassed. By "greater merit," the nobility [of this practice] is stated.

body.text: dharmavegena iti dharmaśraddhābalenetyarthaḥ | āryasubhūtiḥ aśrūṇi prāmuñcat tadapi bhagavato 'dhiṣṭhānenānyeṣu kusīdeṣu janeṣu adbhutamahāyānadharmasyābhidhānena paramaśraddhotpādārthe draṣṭavyam | tasmād hastena aśrūṇi pramṛjya bhagavantametadavocat āścaryaṃ bhagavan, yāvadayaṃ dharmaparyāyastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ ityāha | yāvad iti kāritraviśeṣaḥ | yāvatā prakāreṇa deśānārhāstān bodhisattvānupadiśantviti vākyārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: "By the force of <s>Dharma</s>" means: by the power of faith in the <s>Dharma</s>. The noble <s>Subhūti</s> shed tears; this too should be seen as [occurring] through the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), for the purpose of generating supreme faith in other lazy people through the proclamation of this wondrous <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, wiping his tears with his hand, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the extent to which this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>." "The extent" indicates a special quality of the teaching. The meaning of the sentence is: to the extent that it is worthy of being taught, may [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] instruct those <s>bodhisattvas</s> [accordingly].

body.text: kasmādityākāṅkṣāyāṃ yato me jñānamutpannam ityakathayat | yataḥ ityāryasatyagocarajñānotpādamārabhya etatparyantaṃ dharmaparyāyasya paramapuṇyaphalasya yathoktā deśanā śrāvaka-pratyekabuddhanāmagocarā naivaṃ śrutapūrvetyarthaḥ | etena (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 164]

children.text: ) daurlabhyaṃ proktam | evaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ puṇyaṃ śrutvā yeṣāṃ vīryamārabhya pravṛttānāmasmin dharme yathārutasaṃjñā bhavati teṣāṃ taddoṣaparijihīrṣayā parameṇāścaryeṇa ityavocat | vipulapuṇyānyutpādayato 'dhamapuruṣasya tādṛgduṣkaraśraddhādhimuktito 'tyantagambhīrapudgala-dharmanairatmyādhimuktiśca mameva pudgalanairātmyamātraśuddhajñānena, parameṇa te āścaryeṇaṃ samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | bhūtasaṃjñām ityaviparītārthasaṃjñām, na tu śabdābhiniveśenedaṃ bhūtatvamiti saṃjñā | evamatra paramārthabhipretya sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatvaṃ nirdiṣṭam, na tu saṃvṛtim, niḥsvabhāvatāyā abhāvāttatra | tasmānna darśanadinā virodha ityabhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: By this, the rarity [of this Dharma] has been declared. Having heard such distinguished merit, for those who, having begun with effort in this <s>Dharma</s>, have a literal notion [of it], in order to remove that fault, he said "with supreme wonder." For the one of lowly character who produces vast merits—from such difficult faith and conviction, [there arises] the conviction in the supremely profound selflessness of both persons and <s>dharmas</s>; while my own knowledge is purified only with regard to the selflessness of persons [alone]. "They will be endowed with supreme wonder." "Perception of truth" means perception of non-inverted meaning, not the perception that "this is truth" through grasping at words. Thus, in this [passage], the ultimate has been intended in stating the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, not the conventional, since essencelessness does not apply there. Therefore there is no contradiction with seeing and the like—such is the purport.

body.translated_text: When [the question] "Why?" was anticipated, he said "Because knowledge has arisen in me." "Because" [means]: from the arising of knowledge regarding the domain of the Noble Truths up to this point, the teaching of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of supremely meritorious fruit as described—the meaning is that [<s>Subhūti</s>] had never before heard [such a teaching] even within the scope of the name of <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha).

body.text: nanu bhūtasaṃjñāyāṃ satyāṃ, saṃjñāyā api sattvaṃ paramārthataḥ syāt, asatsu ca saṃjñeyeṣu saṃjñāyā apyabhāvaḥ prasajyeta, tasmāt kathaṃ paramārthataḥ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatvaṃ sidhyedityupālambhaṃ vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityavocat | yā caiṣā bhagavan, bhūtasaṃjñā ityuadatarat | saṃjñānāma na kācana, ekānekasvabhāvena viyogāt, paramārthataḥ sā asaṃjñaiva | ata eva nocyate bhūtasaṃjñeyaṃ bhūtasaṃjñātveneti darśitam, yato hyavicāraramaṇīyamātrataḥ vidyate tasmāt tāṃ tathāgato bhāṣate bhūtasaṃjñā, anyathā sarvathābhāvānna bhāṣeta | tataḥ paramārthavyavasthāyāṃ kathaṃ yogasamāpattyā pratipattavyam, kathaṃ ca vikṣepo nigrahītavya ityubhayaṃ darśitaṃ gāmbhīryañcāpi nigaditam, adhyāropāpavādāntāvapi parihṛtau |
body.translated_text: Now, if the notion of [real] entities exists, then the notion too would ultimately be real; and in the absence of the objects of notion, the absence of the notion itself would follow. Therefore, how could the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> be established ultimately? — Anticipating this objection...

body.text: teṣu kusīdeṣvevāścaryotpādanārtham na mama bhagavan, āścaryaṃ yadahamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣyamāṇamavakalpayāmi, adhimucye, ye 'pi te bhagavan, sattvā bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani paścime kāle paścime (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_165

children.text: ) samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ ye imaṃ bhagavan, dharmaparyāyam udgrahīṣyanti, dhārayiṣyanti, paryavāpsyanti, te paramāścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti ityāha |
children.translated_text: ...time, in the last five hundred [years], who will take up, hold, and master this discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s> — they will be endowed with the most extraordinary wonder,' he says.

body.translated_text: For the purpose of arousing wonder in those very indolent ones: 'It is not a wonder for me, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that I comprehend and have faith in this discourse on <s>Dharma</s> as it is being spoken. But those beings, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who will exist in the future time, in the last period, in the last...

body.text: atrāyaṃ sāmānyena samāsārthaḥ- anāgate saddharmavipralopakāle ye bodhisattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, na te pudgalādibhirgṛhītā bhaviṣyanti, mayyapyevaṃ sambhāvanāyāṃ saddharmotthānakāle 'pi yuṣmākametādṛśapratipattyabhāve idamatyantaṃ lajjāsthānaṃ tat syādityucyate | tatra 'aham'; iti padgalanairātmyaṃ bodhyate, imaṃ ityanena pudgaladharmanairātmyaṃ prakāśyate, bhāṣyamāṇam iti tu sākṣāt prākāśyamānaṃ bhagavatā, avakalpayāmi iti prasādākāraḥ prasannatā saṃdarśyate, adhimucye iti sampratyayaśca, te sattvāḥ ityanena bhagavan, anāgate kalpe bhāvinaḥ | atrodgrahīṣyantītyādīni yāni padāni tāni pūrvamevoktāni |
body.translated_text: Here, the general meaning in brief is this: In the future, at the time of the decline of the true <s>Dharma</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who will uphold this discourse on <s>Dharma</s> will not be grasped by [notions of] person (<s>pudgala</s>) and so on. Given that even for me, at the time of the arising of the true <s>Dharma</s>, such an estimation [is remarkable]...

body.text: taccaivaṃ nirucyate- pudgalanairātmyamātramavaganturmama bhagavataḥ sakāśāt sākṣāt śravaṇabalena yaddhi nairātmyadvayapratipādake 'smin dharme prasādasampratyayamātraṃ jātaṃ tannaivāścaryam | ye bhagavan (teṣu) kalpeṣu asmin [dharme] dhāraṇādikrameṇa īdṛśaṃ dharmaparyāyamadhigamya paryavāpsyanti te paramāścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | bhagavan, (teṣu) kalpeṣu bahulatayā mahāyānaviprakṛṣṭā bhavanti, teṣu (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_166
The intent is: the arising of faith [in them] is exceedingly rare.

body.translated_text: And this is explained thus: For me, who has comprehended merely the selflessness of persons, through the power of hearing directly from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the mere arising of faith and trust in this <s>Dharma</s> that establishes the twofold selflessness is indeed not a wonder. Those, <s>Bhagavān</s>, [who will do so in the future]...

body.text: etena kausīdyaṃ prahāya saddharmagrahaṇādau chandena praṇidhānena ca sthātavyamityādarśitam | na kevalaṃ teṣu āgamayoga evāpitu (teṣu) pratipattisampadamapi darśayitum api tu khalu punarbhagavan ityavocat | ātmā ityādivacanam, tūpalakṣaṇam, atasteṣāṃ dharmasaṃjñā (api) na pravartiṣyate, dvayornairātmyayoryugapadadhigamāt |
body.translated_text: By this, it is shown that having abandoned laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), one should abide in the taking up of the true <s>Dharma</s> and so on through aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). Not only does he show the scriptural method (<s>āgamayoga</s>) in their case, but also to demonstrate the excellence of practice (<s>pratipattisampad</s>), he says 'But moreover, <s>Bhagavān</s>...' and so on.

body.text: yadyanātmādikaṃ sat tadā saṃjñāpi tatra niyamena pravartayediti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? iti pṛṣṭvā ātmasaṃjñā ityudatārīt | yathātmetyādyuktastathā ayamahamityayātmasaṃjñā yā sarvajanaprasiddhā, tasyā api parikṣākṣamatvādakiñcanatve sati ātmādyanubhavābhāvādasatyāḥ kā kathā | anena tāvad yogasamāpattiḥ nirdiṣṭā |
body.translated_text: Thinking 'If self and so on were real, then the notion would necessarily operate with regard to them,' he asks 'Why is that?' and then raises [the topic of] the notion of self (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>). Just as 'self' and so on have been explained, this notion of self — 'I am this' — which is well known to all people, that...

body.text:
nanu cāsattve satyātmādestadviparyayeṇa nātmasaṃjñā pravartiṣyata iti kuta ityābhyantarotthitaṃ praśnaṃ vicārya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityavocat | sarvasaṃjñāpagatā hi buddhā bhagavantaḥ ityudatarat | atrāyamarthaḥ- samastabhāvānāṃ yathāvattattvādhigamena 'buddhā bhagavantaḥ'; ityucyate | paramārthataḥ kasyāpi saṃjñeyasyābhāvāt, na kutrāpi te saṃjñā pravartate, anyathā viparyāsaḥ syāt | bodhisattvāstu buddhānunuśikṣāmanuvartante, anyathā kathaṃ tatpadaṃ prāpnuyuḥ, tasmāt buddhairbhagavadbhiryathā sarvasaṃjñāpagatatvaṃ śikṣitaṃ tathā bodhisattvairapi śikṣitavyam | tasmād ye bodhisattvāstasyāmanuśikṣante teṣāmātmādisaṃjñā niyamato na pravartate |
(

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_167

children.text: ) evametat iti vineyānāṃ niścayāpādanārthaṃ svayamabhyupagamya bhagavatā dviruktam | itaḥ pūrvamanārabdhavīryānadhikṛtyābhihitam | samprati pudgalā dharmagāmbhīryaṃ śrutvā trasyanti | ataḥ prathamataramanārabdhavīryāṇāṃ teṣām anārabdhavīryatvāpanayanārthaṃ ye sattvāḥ ityādyāha | santrāse sati nārabhante vīryam, śrāvakayāne 'smin bhagavatā dharmamātramidaṃ pudgalāsattvamityuktam, mahāyāne tu tadapi dharmamātraṃ mithyeti deśitam, tasmād anādikālīnasahajātmadṛṣṭisamprayuktāntaḥkaraṇā abhāvitātmānaḥ pudgalanairātmyaṃ śrutvā nāstyahamiti trasiṣyanti | tanniṣedhāryaṃ no trasiṣyanti iti deśitam | ye dharmamātre 'bhiniviṣṭāste dharmanairātmyadeśanāśravaṇakāle santrasiṣyanti, yad dharmamātraṃ tasyāpyasattve 'aho ! na mayā bhāvyam'; iti matvā daśadigavalokanenāpi śaraṇābhāvāt santrāse tadapākaraṇāya na santrasiṣyanti ityuddiṣṭam | cintākāle ubhayābhāvayogasyāśakyatvāt santrasiṣyanti 'kathamasmābhirnairātmyadvayamadhigantavyam'; ityādimasantrāsāpasāraṇārthaṃ na santrāsamāpatsyante ityuktam |
children.translated_text: 'It is so, it is so' — in order to produce certainty in those to be trained, the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, having accepted [this], stated it twice. What was said previously pertained to those who had not yet initiated their effort. Now, persons, hearing the profundity of <s>dharma</s>, become frightened. Therefore, first...

body.translated_text: Now, since if self and so on are non-existent, the notion of self would not operate by virtue of their opposite — to examine this internally arising question, he says 'Why is that?' He answered: 'For the Buddhas, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are free from all notions.' Here...

body.text: anye tāvannairātmyadvayānavabodhād yo hi trāso mṛdu-madhyādhimātrātmakaḥ sa ebhistribhiḥ padaiḥ yathākramamudīrita ityevaṃ manyante, apare tu trividhastrāsaḥ śravaṇa-manana-bhāvanākāle bhavatītyabhyupagacchanti | samprati lābhasatkāreṣu vītarāgatvāt 'te paramāścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyantīti |'; śrotukāmānāṃ hitāya svayaṃ pūrvaṃ praśnamuthyāpya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityavocat | paramapāramiteyaṃ ityuktam | prajñāpāramiteyaṃ bodherāsānnahetuḥ | asyā abhāvena dānādipāramitānāmabhāvāt sarvapāramitāsu śreṣṭhā | na kevalaṃ mayaiveyaṃ paramā paramā proktā, (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_168

children.text: ) api tu sarvabuddhairapīyaṃ parametyukteti darśanārthaṃ yāṃ ca paramapāramitāṃ iti nigaditam |
children.translated_text: But to show that this [perfection] is asserted as supreme by all Buddhas as well, it is said 'and that supreme perfection (<s>paramapāramitā</s>).'

body.translated_text: Some hold that the three levels of fright — mild, medium, and intense — which arise due to non-comprehension of the twofold selflessness, are expressed respectively by these three terms. Others hold that the three types of fright occur at the time of hearing, reflection, and meditation (<s>śravaṇa</s>, <s>manana</s>, <s>bhāvanā</s>)...

body.text: anena 'ekabuiddhena deśitamapi aviparītārthatvena gṛhyate sarvabuddhaikābhipretatve khalu kimucyatām'; ityevaṃ dīpitam | (yadi) asmābhiḥ sarvaiḥ paramā saṃsādhitā syāt, kathaṃ na (vayaṃ) parameṇāścaryeṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyāmaḥ? anena paramatvadarśanena hriyaḥ dvitīyaṃ sthānaṃ nirdiśyate, tathā hi- dharmo 'yaṃ (etāvān) śreṣṭhastathāpi tvaṃ yallābhasatkārādhyavasitaḥ pramādena sthitastadatīva lajjājanakamityucyate | anena cittapragrahaḥ sandarśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, it is illuminated: 'Even though taught by a single <s>Buddha</s>, it is grasped as having a non-erroneous meaning, being the unanimous intent of all Buddhas — what more need be said?' If this supreme [perfection] has been accomplished by all of us [Buddhas], how could we not be endowed with supreme wonder...

body.text: 13. duḥkhādhivāsana-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 13. The section on endurance of suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsana</s>):

body.text: evaṃ hrīsthāne deśite 'pi ye duḥkhe 'kṣāntyā vīryātiśayamārabdhuṃ notsahante, teṣāṃ duḥkhākṣāntervyapagamārthaṃ trayodaśasthānamadhikṛtyāha apia tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādi | kimatra kṣāntiḥ? kena lakṣaṇena sā kṣāntirjñāyate? tasyāḥ ya ākāraḥ, yathā vākāraḥ, yaścākṣānteḥ pratipakṣaḥ so 'nena sthānena darśyate | kīdṛśī kṣāntiriti cet? sarvadharmānupalambhasvabhāvaḥ, ataḥ yā tathāgatasya kṣāntipāramitā saiva apāramitā ityuktam | paramārthataḥ kā kṣāntiḥ, yena kṣāntiḥ, yatra kṣāntiḥ, yaśca kṣamyaḥ, yā ca kṣāntiḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāmanupalambhāt (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_169

children.text: ) saiva apāramitā | evaṃ paramārthato 'nutpannatvāt nāsti tatra pāraṃ gatetyabhisandhiḥ | anena tasyāḥ kṣānteḥ svabhāvenānutpannatvaṃ gāmbhīryaṃ cāpi darśitam |
children.translated_text: That itself is a non-<s>pāramitā</s> (non-perfection). Thus, because it is ultimately unoriginated, there is no 'gone to the other shore' — this is the intended meaning. By this, the unoriginated nature of that patience by its own essence, as well as its profundity, is shown.

body.translated_text: Even though the topic of moral shame has been taught, for those who, through inability to endure suffering, cannot muster the supreme effort of vigor, in order to remove their lack of patience with suffering, the thirteenth topic is addressed by saying: 'Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth. What here is patience (<s>kṣānti</s>)? By what characteristic is that patience known? Its nature, the manner of its nature, and the antidote to impatience — these are shown by this topic.

body.text: evaṃ sarvadharmānupalambhamanasikāreṇa kutaḥ bodhisattvānāṃ kṣāntiriti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? iti jñāpakahetau pṛṣṭe yadā subhūte ityādyattaramāha | aṅgāni hastapādādīni, pratyaṅgāni aṅgulyādīni | nāpi me kācitsaṃjñā iti paradehasaṃjñā, śastrasaṃjñā, chedasaṃjñā, parasaṃjñā, kṣāntisaṃjñādayaśca | anena sarvadharmānupalambho 'bhihitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, contemplating through the mental attention of non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>: 'From where does patience arise for <s>bodhisattvas</s>?' — when the indicative reason is asked with 'For what reason?', the answer is given beginning with 'When, <s>Subhūti</s>...' '<s>Aṅga</s>' (limbs) means hands, feet, and the like; '<s>pratyaṅga</s>' (minor limbs) means fingers and the like. 'Nor was there any perception for me' — [this means] perception of another's body, perception of a weapon, perception of cutting, perception of the other person, perception of patience, and so forth.

body.text: nanu asatyāñca kasyāñcit saṃjñāyāṃ mūrcchāvasthāvad cittābhāvo bhaviṣyatīti cet? tatra nāpi asaṃjñā vā babhūva ityāha | tasmin kāle sarvadharmanairātmyāvabodhakaṃ yogijñānaṃ tathyasaṃvṛtisvabhāvabhipretam | tacca kathamiti cittagataṃ praśnaṃ vikalpya svayaṃ tatkasya hetoḥ? ityuktvā sacet sūbhūte ityudatarat | vyāpādasaṃjñāpi asyāyamabhiprāyaḥ- yatra ātmasaṃjñā, tatra nūnaṃ tanmatreṇātmasneho jāyate | evamātmasnehasamprayoge 'vaśyaṃ sva-paravikalpau jāyete | tenaivaṃ ya ātmopakāritvenopādattāsteṣvātmīyatvaṃ parikalpyate, itareṣu ca paratvaṃ kalpyate | ata evātmānurūpā pravṛtiḥ | tatrātmani ātmīyeṣu ca pravṛttau anurāgaḥ, tadviparīteṣu ca dveṣaḥ | tābhyāṃ sambaddhaḥ samasto doṣarāśiḥ sambhavati | ata evoktam :
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'But in the absence of any perception whatsoever, there would be an absence of mind, as in the state of unconsciousness' — to this he says: 'Nor was there non-perception.' The <s>yogin</s>'s knowledge that comprehends the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> at that time is intended [to be] of the nature of correct conventional [truth]. And [to explain] how this is so, anticipating the mental question, he himself says 'For what reason?' and [then:] 'If, <s>Subhūti</s>...'

children.translated_text: When there is [the notion of] self, there is the perception of other due to the distinction of self and other; grasping and aversion [arise];

children.text: anayoḥ sampratibaddhāḥ sarve doṣāḥ prajāyante || iti ||
children.translated_text: bound by these two, all faults are produced.

body.text: yatra vyāpādādidoṣaustatra kathaṃ kṣāntivādīti prasetsyati, yena kṣāntibalena kaliṅgarājā eva sattvaḥ narakaṃ gamiṣyatītyabhipretam | anena kṛtāpakāre 'pi (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_170

children.text: ) sati nirvikāratayā niyataṃ vyāpādādisambhavābhāvatayā ātmādisaṃjñāvyapagamahetutayā ca īdṛśyāḥ kṣānterjñānamādarśitam |
children.translated_text: because of being free from agitation, because of the definite absence of the arising of malice and the like, and because of being a cause for the removal of perceptions such as self and the like — the knowledge of such patience is shown.

body.translated_text: Where faults such as malice and the like exist, how could one be called a 'practitioner of patience'? — [meaning] that it is through the power of patience [alone] that even a being [such as] the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s> would [otherwise] go to hell. This is the intent. By this, even when harm has been done,

body.text: anenaiva ca trividhāḥ kṣāntayo 'pi tāvannirdiśyante | atra kaliṅgarājā ityanena apakāramarṣaṇakṣāntiḥ paridīpitā, aṅga-pratyaṅga ityanena duḥkhādhivāsanakṣāntiḥ me tasmin samaye ityādinā ca dharmanidhyānakṣāntiḥ | anena dharmapudgalavikalpayorvipakṣatayā nirdeśena vineyāstatprahāṇe yathoktakṣāntyutpāde samyaggrahaṇe cāvataranti | tadevam, vineyajanāḥ 'yadā bhagavāneva bodhyarthamevaṃvidhāṃ parāṃ kṣāntiṃ bhāvitavān, tatkathamasmābhirna bhāvanīyā, duṣkarakarmaṇyananuṣṭhite durlabhapadaṃ nādhigamyate'; iti vicārayanti | tataste vineyāstasyāṃ praotsāhyante | aṅga-pratyaṅgeti nimittamātrābhidhānena sarvaduḥkhādhivāsanakṣāntiḥ samudīrītā |
body.translated_text: And by this very [passage], the three types of patience are also indicated.
