Here, by 'the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s>,' the patience of enduring harm (<s>apakāramarṣaṇakṣānti</s>) is illustrated; by 'limbs and minor limbs,' the patience of enduring suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsanakṣānti</s>); and by 'at that time for me' and so forth, the patience of contemplating the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>). By the indication that conceptual constructions regarding <s>dharmas</s> and persons are on the side of the adversary, [it is shown that] those to be trained should [strive for] the arising of patience as described, through the abandonment of those [constructions].

body.text: samprati yadākārā sā kṣāntiḥ, tathā darśayitum- abhijānāmyahaṃ subhūte ityāha | tadapi kaliṅgarājā me aṅgapratyaṅgamāṃsānyacchetsīt ityetatprasaṅgaprāptam, sākṣānnoktam | sā ca kṣāntiḥ dvividhā dīpitānirantaraparāpakāraduḥkhaviṣayikā parāpakārāsahyaduḥkhaviṣayikā ca | tatra nirantaraduḥkhaviṣayastu yat pañcajātiśatāni iti | etena asyaudāryam abhihitam | asahyaduḥkhaviṣayastu yat aṅga-pratyaṅgānīti kathitam |
body.translated_text: Now, in order to show the nature of that patience, he says: 'I remember, <s>Subhūti</s>...' And this — that the king of <s>Kaliṅga</s> cut the flesh from my limbs and minor limbs — is brought up by context, not stated directly. That patience is shown in two aspects: that which pertains to the suffering of continuous harm from others, and that which pertains to the suffering of others' unbearable harm. Regarding the continuous suffering aspect,

body.text: trividhaṃ (hi) duḥkhaṃ tāvad asahyaṃ vastu, tadyathā- saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ sattvapratikūlapravṛttiduḥkhaṃ paribhogavaikalyaduḥkhaṃ ca | tatra prathamasyāsahyavastunaḥ pratipakṣatvena tasmāttarhi ityuktam | samastenānena asahyaprahāṇāt bodhau chandena (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_171

children.text: ) praṇidhānena ca sthātavyamiti darśitam | bodhicittotpāde sati na kenāpi saṃsāraduḥkhena spṛṣṭo bhaviṣyatītyabhiprāyaḥ | bodhicittotpāde 'pi ātmābhiniviṣṭatayā trividhaduḥkhasaṃjñābhiḥ santrasya kadācit punarnotpādaḥ syādataḥ sarvasaṃjñā vivarjayitvā ityāha | sarvasaṃjñāścātra ātmādisaṃjñāḥ trividhaduḥkhasaṃjñāśca | rūpādyabhiniveśena śrāvakādivat saṃsāraṃ parikalpya tadduḥkhasantaptāḥ na kadācidapi bodhicittamutpādayanti, ataḥ na rūpapratiṣṭhitam ityādyūktam |
children.translated_text: By all this together, it is shown that one should abide in aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for awakening through the abandonment of the unbearable. The intent is that when the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) has arisen, one will not be touched by any suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And [further,] even after the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, because of attachment to self, one might be frightened by the three types of suffering-perception and might sometimes not generate [<s>bodhicitta</s>] again — therefore he says: 'Having abandoned all perceptions.' And 'all perceptions' here [means] perceptions of self and the like, together with the three types of

body.translated_text: there are three types of unbearable suffering, namely: the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the suffering of beings' adverse conduct, and the suffering of deprivation of enjoyments. As the antidote to the first type of unbearable [suffering], the words 'therefore, then' are spoken.

body.text: rūpādiṣu satābhiniveśo hi tatra pratiṣṭhita iti pūrvavadatrāpyuktaḥ, na cātrapunaruktirapi | anena asahyavastunaḥ pratipakṣo 'bhihitaḥ | pūrveṇa tu pāramitāyāṃ yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | atra vineyaiḥ nādharmapratiṣṭhitam iti śeṣaḥ | anena tāvadabhāve 'bhiniveśaḥ pratiṣidhyate | na kvacit pratiṣṭhitam ityanena rūpādiṣu nāmamātrasattābhiniveśaḥ pratiṣidhyate, yogasamāpattiścodīritā bhavati |
body.translated_text: suffering[-perception]. Attachment to the real existence of forms and the like is called 'established therein,' as stated previously; and there is no repetition here either. By this, the antidote to the unbearable [suffering] is stated. By the former, however, [it is shown that] effort should be made in the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection). Here, by those to be trained, [the implicit meaning is:] 'not established in non-<s>dharma</s>' — this is the remainder. By this, attachment to non-existence is prohibited. By 'not established in anything,'

body.text: kiṃ rūpādīnāṃ satāṃ tatsattvasya prahāṇārtham, yaduta asatāṃ vitathābhiniveśasya prahāṇārthaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate? iti cittotthitaṃ praśnaṃ vitarkya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityapṛcchat | uttarārthamāha- yatpratiṣṭhitaṃ tadevāpratiṣṭhitam iti | atrāyamarthaḥ- anādikālastaccitaṃ rūpādiṣu bhāvābhiniveśabalena rūpādau pratiṣṭhitam, yaḥ khalu satyābhiniveśaḥ, sa tasya rūpādivastuno 'bhāvāt paramārthato na pratiṣṭhitaḥ | tasmādeva ityanenopasaṃhāreṇātra dvitīye pakṣe pratisṭhitatvameva darśitaṃ bhavati | dānaśabdenātrāpi pūrvavat ṣaṭ pāramitā evābhipretāḥ |
body.translated_text: is the negation made for the purpose of abandoning the reality of forms and the like that exist, or for the purpose of abandoning the false attachment to [forms and the like that] do not exist? — anticipating this mental question, he asked: 'For what reason?' For the purpose of answering, he says: 'What is established — that itself is non-established.' The meaning here is: the mind, from beginningless time, through the force of attachment to the existence of forms and the like,

body.text: dvitīyāsahyavastuna pratipakṣatvena api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | samastenānena bodhisattvā yeṣāmarthāyātiduṣkarapāramitāyogamārabdhumutsahante, te 'pi sattvā yadi paramārthato na syuḥ, sattvasaṃjñāpi paramārthato na syāt, kathaṃ te tathāvidheṣu mithyāpravṛtteṣu sattveṣu khinnā bhaveyuḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_172

children.text: ) ityādarśitam | tatra sattvaṃ saṃjñāṃ ca pratiṣidhya nairātmyadvayamudīritam | sarvasattvānāmarthāya ityanenātraudārya darśitam | avaśiṣṭena sakalena gāmbhīryaṃ sandarśitam |
children.translated_text: This is shown. Therein, by negating both 'sentient being' and 'perception,' the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmyadvaya</s>) is expressed. By 'for the sake of all sentient beings,' the magnanimity (<s>audārya</s>) [of the teaching] is shown. By the entire remainder, the profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>) is shown.

body.translated_text: As the antidote to the second type of unbearable [suffering], he says: 'Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth. By all this together, [the following is shown:] the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — those for whose sake they undertake the practice of the extremely difficult <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) — even those sentient beings, if they do not exist ultimately, and even the perception of sentient beings does not exist ultimately, how could they become weary of those sentient beings who are falsely engaged?

body.text: evaṃ tāvad yuktyā kṣāntiryujyata iti nirdiśya sāmprataṃ tathāgate sampratyayo 'pi yujyata iti nirūpayan bhūtavādī ityādyāha | prathamam uddeśaḥ, śeṣaḥ vidheyam | athavā satyacatuṣṭayamuddeśaḥ, kramaśaḥ abhisambadhyate | athavā bhūtavādī iti sādhyam, tathāgataḥ iti jñāpakanirdeśaḥ | yathānye buddhā bhagavantaḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇāni prahīṇavantastathaiva tathāgato 'pyayaṃ gataḥ prāptaḥ, tena tathāgataḥ | tasmādaviparyastatvena bhūtavādīti, viparītadeśanāyāśca hetorāvaraṇasyābhāvaḥ sidhyati hetvanupalabdheḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, having indicated through reasoning that patience is justified, now establishing that conviction in the <s>Tathāgata</s> is also justified, he says: 'One who speaks truth...' and so forth. First is the heading (<s>uddeśa</s>); the rest is the subject matter. Alternatively, the four [kinds of] truth are the heading, which are connected in sequence. Or, 'one who speaks truth' is what is to be proved, and '<s>Tathāgata</s>' is the indicative designation — just as other <s>Buddhas</s>

body.text: tathāgata evāyamiti kathaṃ sidhyatītyāha- satyavādī iti | 'satyam'; caturāryasatyalakṣaṇam, tasya yo vādī, sa tathāgata iti nirdhāryate | atyantaparokṣārthastu sarvathā samyak kathayituṃ na śakyate, yathoktam-
body.translated_text: How is it established that 'he is indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s>'? He says: 'truth-speaker' (<s>satyavādī</s>). 'Truth' (<s>satya</s>) has the character of the four noble truths; he who speaks of it — that one is ascertained to be the <s>Tathāgata</s>. However, the meaning that is extremely remote cannot be correctly stated in every respect; that which...

body.text: parokṣopeyataddhetostadākhyānaṃ hi duṣkaram |
body.translated_text: For it is difficult to explain that which is remote [from direct experience], its cause, and its designation.

body.text: ayaṃ satyavādī satyaṃ kena rūpeṇa jānātityāha- tathāvādī iti | sa vastutattvamaviparītatayā yathāvad vadatīti tathāvādī | sa heyopādeyatattvaṃ sopāyaṃ yathāsthitaṃ tathaiva bhāṣate 'taḥ sa kathaṃ na satyavādī syāditi | evaṃbhūte 'pi taddeśitāni catvāri satyāni kiṃ tathaiva pratiṣṭhitānīti? ityata āha- na vitathavādī iti | yato 'viparītapramāṇopapannāni, na pramāṇabādhitāni uktānyataḥ satyānītyarthaḥ etena samagreṇa kāryakāraṇena bhagavataḥ prāmāṇyaṃ sādhitam | ata evoktam-
body.translated_text: In what form does this truth-speaker know the truth? He says: 'thus-speaker' (<s>tathāvādī</s>). He speaks the true nature of things (<s>vastu-tattva</s>) correctly, without error — therefore [he is called] a thus-speaker. He speaks of the true nature of what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted, together with the means, just as it is — how then could he not be truthful?

body.text: tāyāt tattvasthirāśeṣaviśeṣajñānasādhanam |
body.translated_text: [The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s speech] is the means for the firm and complete special knowledge of reality.

body.text: ekasyāpi bhāvasvabhāvasya paramārthato 'siddhatvād ekamapi satyaṃ tāvad duḥsādhyam, kimiti satyacatuṣṭayamiti catuḥsatyābhidhānācca bhūtavādīti |
body.translated_text: Since not even the nature of a single entity is established ultimately, even a single truth is difficult to establish — why then speak of a fourfold truth? Because he enunciates the four truths, he is called a 'speaker of what is real' (<s>bhūtavādī</s>).

body.text: evaṃ bhagavatā 'māyopamāḥ pañcaskandhāḥ'; ityukte sati kathaṃ teṣāṃ duḥkhasatyasvabhāvatvam, duḥkhasyāpi paramārthato 'nṛtatvāt tatsamudayanirodhayopyasattvameva, atyantābhāvabhūte śaśaśrṛṅgādau tāvattau (samudaya-nirodhau) na sambhavataḥ | nirodhasya tvabhāvāt tatprāpako mārgo 'pi naiva paramārthataḥ, gamyābhāve naiva gamako 'pi | tathoktam- 'bodhiṃ pratiṣṭhāya ekasyāpi satyasya siddhirna dṛṣṭā, kimiti caturṇām?'; iti deśanāvat |
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said 'The five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) are like illusions,' how can they have the nature of the truth of suffering — since suffering too is ultimately unreal? And the origin and cessation of that [suffering] are also equally non-existent. In the case of what is absolutely non-existent, like a hare's horn...

body.text: etat pravicintya ye bhūtavādini śabdaśo 'bhiniviṣṭāsteṣāmadhyāropāntaparihārārtham api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | na tatra satyam iti paramārthataḥ kasyacidapi svabhāvasyāsiddheḥ | na mṛṣā ityatra satyavyavacchedena (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_174

children.text: ) sthitatvāt tadvyavacchedyatvābhāvād yena mṛṣāatvaṃ bhavet tanmṛṣā | atha vā na satyam iti yathā māyopamā mṛṣā jñānarūpāḥ | avicāraramaṇīyamātratayā sthitatvād na mṛṣā iti | anena tāvad antadvayapratiṣedhena madhyamā pratipad eva nirdiśyate | śrāvakāṇāmātmābhiniveśasya prahāṇārthaṃ pudgalanairātmyāṃśamātreṇa catvāryāryasatyāni deśitāni, na tu sarvebhya ityavirodhaḥ |
children.translated_text: because of being established [conventionally], there is no object to be excluded by which it would be false — that [which has such an excluded object] is false. Or alternatively, 'not true' means [all things are] like illusions, false, of the nature of knowledge. 'Not false' because they are established as merely delightful without analysis (<s>avicāraramaṇīya</s>). By this, the rejection of both extremes...

body.translated_text: Having reflected upon this, for the purpose of removing the superimposition of those who are literally attached to [the epithet] 'speaker of what is real,' he says 'But moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so on. 'There is no truth therein' — because ultimately no intrinsic nature whatsoever is established. 'Nor is it false' —

body.text: kāyādikamupalabhya tadarthako dānaṃ dadāti, anupalabhya atadarthako vā, tayoḥ ko viśeṣa iti yaccintanaṃ tat tṛtīyasyāsahyavastunaḥ pratipakṣatvenāha tadyathāpi nāma ityādi | yaḥ kāya-bhava-bhogātmakavastuṣu sukhamātratvenābhiniviśya (satyatvenaivābhiniviśya) tadarthikastatra patitvā dānaṃ dadāti, sa andhakārapraviṣṭapuruṣasadṛśaḥ, satorapi cakṣuṣoḥ vastvarthānupalambhena heyopādeyārthānabhijñatayā viparyastārtheṣu samastaduḥkhasthāneṣu patito bhavati | tataḥ bodhisattvā mahāsukhabhogāt pracyutā bhaviṣyanti | tadviyogena śrāvakādivat duḥkhasantaptatayā bodhervyāvṛtā bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: One gives a gift after apprehending body and so on, for the sake of that [body], or one gives without apprehending, not for the sake of that — what is the difference between these two? To address this, as the antidote to the third unbearable object, he says 'Just as, for example...' and so on. The three things — body, existence, and enjoyments —

body.text: yo vastvapatioto dānaṃ dadāti, kāyādivastvanupalabhya tadanarthī bhūtvā dānaṃ dadāti tattu yathāpi nāma cakṣuṣmān puruṣaḥ nānāvidhāni rūpāṇi paśyet dṛṣṭvā ca heyasya hānam upādeyasya copādānamiva | (atha) tadapi asatyaruṇodaye kadācinna dṛśyata iti? sūrye 'bhyudgate ityāha | sūrye 'bhyudgate 'pi andhakārapūrṇeṣu gṛhādiṣu na paśyatīti matvāha prabhātāyām iti | (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_175
The word 'dawned' (<s>prabhāta</s>) is said for the purpose of illuminating [the removal of] darkness; therefore the meaning is: 'in the direction free from darkness.'

body.translated_text: One who gives a gift without being attached to things, having not apprehended things such as body and so on, having become unconcerned with them, gives the gift — that is just as a man with eyes would see various forms, and having seen them, would abandon what is to be abandoned and adopt what is to be adopted.

body.text: tatsāmagrye 'pi yo 'ndhaḥ, sa kadācidapi na paśyatītyāśaṅkāyāṃ cakṣuṣmān ityāha | evamavastupatito bodhisattvo draṣṭavyaḥ, saḥ avidyātāmisraprabodhena jñānasūryābhyudgamena ca nānāvidhāni jñeyāni yathāvat sampaśyati, viparyastavastūni samastaduḥkhasthānāni heyaduḥkhāni cāpi mṛṣātvāt parivarjayati, samastasukhasthānasyānurasamyaksambodhilakṣaṇasyopādeyasyottamapadasyāpi kāmanayā tatra pravartate |
body.translated_text: If there is an objection that 'even with all the conditions [present], one who is blind never sees' — to this he says 'one with eyes' (<s>cakṣuṣmān</s>). Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is not attached to things should be understood: through the awakening from the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and through the rising of the sun of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), [he sees] the various objects of knowledge just as they are.

body.text: tasmād bodhisattvā mahābhogasampadanuprāpya anuttarasukhena kāyaṃ sthirīkṛtya bodheravinivṛttā bhavantītyabhiprāyaḥ, ata eva avinivṛtā iti | pūrvaṃ tvālambanamātreṇa tasmin sthitirādarśitā, atra tu ālambanapūrvakaṃ tasminnanurāgalakṣaṇe patanam | tasmādatra patita ityuktam, pūrvaṃ tu pratiṣṭhita ityuktam | anena sakalena cittapragrahaḥ paridīpitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having attained the wealth of great enjoyments and having stabilized the body with unsurpassed happiness, become non-regressing from awakening — this is the intent. Hence [the term] 'non-regressing' (<s>avinivṛtta</s>). Previously, abiding in that [giving] was shown merely through its object; but here, [abiding] together with the object...

body.text: 14. dhyānasāsvādavirati-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 14. The section on desisting from savoring <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption):

body.text: anena prakāreṇa kṣāntipravṛtā api ye dhyānasamāsvādayantastatraivāsaktā jñānasambhārapāripūraye hetubhūtaṃ mahāyānadharmamanārabdhāsteṣāṃ jñānasambhāraviyogaparihārārthaṃ caturdaśasthānamadhikṛtya api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | sthānenānena dhyānarasāsvādāpagamāya pañcabhiḥ prakāraiḥ saddharmaṃ prati vīryārthaṃ guṇaviśeṣaḥ paridīpitaḥ, (yathā)- 1. tathāgatānubhāvaḥ, 2. viśiṣṭapuṇyasañcayaḥ, 3. dharmatatsādhanayoḥ praśaṃsanam, 4. devādibhiḥ satkāraḥ, 5. pāpapariśodhanaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: By this method, even those who have engaged in patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) but who savor meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>) and become attached there, and who have not undertaken the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s> which is the cause for the completion of the accumulation of knowledge — for the purpose of removing their separation from the accumulation of knowledge, taking up the fourteenth section, he says 'But moreover...' and so on.

body.text: tatra tathāgatānubhāvastu jñātāste tathāgatena ityādi yadāha | udgrahīṣyanti ityādipadānāṃ vyākhyānaṃ pūrvavadeva | bhagavān hi sarvaṃ vijānātīti sarvajñaḥ draṣṭā ca | tatra kiṃ mahad āścaryaṃ teṣvityanveṣaṇāyāṃ puṇyasañcayavaiśiṣṭyamādarśayitumāha sarve te sattvāḥ iti | aprameyapuṇyaskandhānāṃ prasavanād jñātāste bhāgyavanta iti vākyaśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is [shown by]: 'they are known by the <s>Tathāgata</s>' and so on. The explanation of the terms 'will take up' and so on is as before. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> knows everything — hence [he is] omniscient and a seer. What great wonder is there in those [beings being known by him]?

body.text: kiṃ ca tāvat puṇyaskandhasya vaiśiṣṭyam, yena (saḥ puṇyaskandhaḥ) aparimito bhavatīti vicintya viśiṣṭapuṇyasaṃgrahaṃ darśayan paśca khalu punaḥ subhūte ! strī vā puruṣo vā ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: Moreover, what is the special quality of the heap of merit, by which that heap of merit becomes immeasurable? — reflecting thus, showing the collection of distinguished merit, he says 'Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, if a woman or a man...' and so on.

body.text: sūrya-prabhā-pṛthvījalādyavasthāviśeṣaḥ pūrvāhṇaḥ | evambhūteṣvavasthāviśeṣeṣveva kālaḥ iti prajñapyate, na tu viśiṣṭatvena parikalpita iveti darśayituṃ kālaśabdastatsāmānyādhikaraṇyena viśeṣyate | anyathaikātmyād ayaṃ pūrvāhṇa ityādibhedā na syuḥ | viśeṣaṇāntarairbhede 'bhyupagate sa eva viśeṣaḥ sūryādyavasthānāṃ viśeṣaḥ pūrvāhṇādivyavahāraprajñaptīnāṃ ca hetuḥ syāt, akiñcitkaratve kimadṛṣṭasāmārthyena kālena prajñaptenetyabhiprāyaḥ | na ca sa mandatīvrabuddhayādiliṅgavānapi yujyate, mandādibuddhīnāṃ taddhetutaḥ samudbhave kramoṇotpattivirodhād, etacca pūrvaṃ darśitameva | bādhakapramāṇasyāpi prāgevātmadūṣaṇaprasaṅge darśitatvāt kimadhikena |
body.translated_text: The particular state of the sun's rays, earth, water, and so on constitutes the forenoon (<s>pūrvāhṇa</s>). Time is designated precisely in terms of such particular states — to show that it is not conceived as [an entity] with [its own] distinguishing quality, the word 'time' (<s>kāla</s>) is qualified by its general substrate. And...

body.text: sāmānyajanaiḥ saṅketavaśenotpannastathāvidhaḥ praṇināmavasthāviśeṣaḥ kālaḥ iti vyavahāre prajñapyate, na tu śabdārthasambandhaprajñaptivaśeneti darśayituṃ samaye iti śabdena viśeṣyate | kasyacidekasyāpyakathanena yathoktadeśanābhiprāyasya pratipādanābhāvāt padatrayamuktam | saṅketaviṣayatvena prajñāpakaṃ śabdamāropya samānādhikaraṇyaṃ kṝtam | dhyānarasāsvādavirāgāyātredamuktam | pūrvaṃ deyasya evaṃvidhasya ca kālasyānirdeśānnaiva tāvat punaruktidoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Such a particular state of living beings, arisen through convention by ordinary people, is designated in usage as 'time' (<s>kāla</s>) — to show that it is not [established] through the force of designating the connection of word and meaning, it is qualified by the word 'occasion' (<s>samaya</s>). Of a single [entity]...

body.text: ayameva tato nidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyād aprameyamasaṃkhyeyam ityanena audāryaṃ paridīpyate | saṃkhyā-dravyakāla-viśeṣairviśiṣṭaṃ dānodbhūtaṃ puṇyamabhibhūyate | evaṃ tāvat gaṅgānadībālukāsamāna iti saṃkhyāviśeṣaṃ darśayati | ātmabhāvaḥ iti duravagāho dravyaviśeṣaḥ | kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi iti kālaviśeṣaḥ | sā ca kalpakoṭiḥ niyutā, sāpi śatasahasreti padena yuktā |
body.translated_text: "From that cause he would produce a greater, immeasurable, incalculable heap of merit"—by this, the vastness is illuminated. Merit produced from giving, distinguished by number, substance, and time, is surpassed. Thus, "equal to the sands of the river Ganges" shows the distinction of number. "Physical existence" (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) is the distinction of substance, difficult to comprehend. "Hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of aeons" (<s>kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi</s>) is the distinction of time. And that <s>kalpakoṭi</s> is [multiplied by] <s>niyuta</s>, and that too is joined with the word "hundred-thousand."

body.text: etat kathaṃ jñātavyam? iti dharmastutivaiśiṣṭyaṃ darśayitum api tu khalu subhūte ityādyāha | acintyo 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ atyantagambhīraḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nisvabhāvatālakṣaṇaḥ tathāgataiḥ pratyātmavedanīyaḥ, śrāvakādibhiraparaiścāpi (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 178]

children.text: ) cintayitumaśakyo hyatra nirdiṣṭaḥ | atulyaḥ iti anyatra evaṃvidhasya adarśanāt, etattulyasya viśiṣṭasya vābhāvāt, tulyasya adhikasya vābhāvena acintyahetuto 'cintyameva phalaṃ sambhavatītyuktam | kathaṃ atulya iti cintāyāmāha śreṣṭhayānasamprasthitānām iti | atiśayena pāraṃ gatastu śreṣṭha iti | śrāvakādīnām ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ ityuktam | agrayānam ityagrāṇāṃ yānaṃ vā agraṃ cedaṃ yānamiti vā padavigrahaḥ | ye tatra samprasthitāste tathocyante | evameva śreṣṭhayānasamprasthitanāmityapi tassamānameva | tau tāvat paryāyau | paryāyadeśanābhiprāyastu vineyajanopakāraḥ, yena katipaye bhavyā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: It is indicated as incapable of being thought about. "Incomparable" (<s>atulya</s>) means: because such [a teaching] is not seen elsewhere; because of the absence of anything equal to or superior to it; because of the absence of anything equal or superior, it has been stated that from an inconceivable cause, only an inconceivable fruit is possible. When [one asks] "How is it incomparable?", in response he says "for those who have set out in the Supreme Vehicle" (<s>śreṣṭhayānasamprasthitānām</s>). "Supreme" (<s>śreṣṭha</s>) means: having gone to the other shore in an eminent way. "This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is for the <s>śrāvakas</s> and others"—this has been stated. "Foremost vehicle" (<s>agrayāna</s>): the word-analysis is either "the vehicle of the foremost ones" or "this vehicle which is the foremost." Those who have set out in that are so called. Likewise, "those who have set out in the supreme vehicle" is equivalent. These are two synonyms. The purpose of the synonymous teaching is the benefit of those to be trained, whereby some become receptive.

body.translated_text: "How is this to be known?"—to show the special excellence of the praise of the <s>Dharma</s>, he says "But moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>" and so forth. "This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is inconceivable"—it is supremely profound, having the character of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, to be personally realized by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; and by <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and others as well

body.text: itarayānānyapekṣya śreṣṭha iti kecit | samastakleśajñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhayā vā śreṣṭha athavā agramiti paramam | pratyekabuddhayānamapi śrāvakayānāpekṣayā paramiti vicāraṇāyāmāha- śreṣṭhayānasamprasthitānām iti | atyantaṃ praśastagamanāt śreṣṭha ityuktam | śrāvakādyenekayānebhyo 'tiśayena praśasyatvādatra śreṣṭhaḥ iti śabda prayuktaḥ | tacca mahāyānamityeva | śrāvakādināmabhavyatvād dharmadeśaneyaṃ bodhisattvebhya evoktā | tena siddho 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyo 'tulya iti | tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ ityanyeṣāmagocaratvāt | dharmaparyāyo 'yam ityādibhiḥ yathoktārthān prasādhya upasaṃhṛtya ca tatpratipattuṃ viśeṣastutiḥ sandarśitā |
body.translated_text: Some say "supreme" in relation to the other vehicles. Or "supreme" through the purification of all affliction-obscurations and knowledge-obscurations; or "foremost" means the highest. When examining whether the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle is also "highest" in relation to the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, he says "for those who have set out in the Supreme Vehicle." "Supreme" is said because of going forth in the most praiseworthy manner. The word "supreme" is employed here because of being more praiseworthy than the many vehicles of the <s>śrāvakas</s> and others. And that is indeed the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). Since the <s>śrāvakas</s> and others are not receptive, this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is stated for <s>bodhisattvas</s> alone. By that, it is established that this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is "incomparable." "Spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>"—because it is beyond the scope of others. By "This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse" and so forth, having established the stated meanings and having summarized them, a special praise for practicing them has been demonstrated.

body.text: yato hi dharmaparyāyo 'yamacintyo 'prameyaśca tasmād vipāko 'pyasyācintya eva | tataḥ ye imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti ityādi tu siddhamevetyarthaḥ | aprameyam ityuddeśaḥ, śeṣastānnirdeśaḥ | tatra acintyam iti cintāviṣayātikrāntatvena ananumeyatvāt | atulyam ityapratisamam | amāpyam iti sarvasattvaprayoge 'pi māpayitumaśakyatvāt | aparimāṇam iti (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 179]

children.text: ) mahadbhirdeśādibhirapyaparimāpyatvād ākāśatopyadhikam | athavā sarvāṇyapīmāni paryāyāntargatāni | sarve te subhūte, sattvāḥ samāṃśena bodhiṃ dhārayiṣyanti iti bodhibhārodvahanam aṃśodvahanasadṛśam | anena tāvat sakalena dhyānasukhāsvādaṃ parityajya jñānasambhārapāripūrihetau dharmaparigrahaṇādau chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti darśitam |
children.translated_text: Because it cannot be limited even by great measures of place and the like—it exceeds even space. Alternatively, all of these are included within other synonyms. "All those beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, will bear awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) as an equal share"—the bearing of the burden of <s>bodhi</s> is similar to the bearing of a share. By all of this, it has been shown that, having abandoned the relishing of the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), one should abide through aspiration and resolve in the cause of fulfilling the accumulation of knowledge, namely the grasping of the <s>Dharma</s> and the like.

body.translated_text: Since this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is inconceivable and immeasurable, its fruit (<s>vipāka</s>) is also indeed inconceivable. Therefore, "those who will uphold this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse" and so forth—the meaning is that this is already established. "Immeasurable" is the heading; the rest is its elaboration. Among these, "inconceivable" (<s>acintya</s>) means: because it transcends the domain of thought and cannot be inferred. "Incomparable" (<s>atulya</s>) means without equal. "Immeasurable" (<s>amāpya</s>) means: because it cannot be measured even by the effort of all beings. "Unlimited" (<s>aparimāṇa</s>) means:

body.text: kasmāt khalu śreṣṭhayānasamprasthitebhyo bhagavatā bhāṣito na tvanyebhyaḥ, kiṃ khalu bhagavatyapi rāgo dveṣaśca iti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityāha, ataḥ subhūte hīnādhimuktikaiḥ ityudatarat | anena khalu bhagavati sarvasattveṣu ekasutavad vātsalyamiti nāsti rāgo dveṣo vā | tathāpi ye yadā bhavyā bhavanti tadā tebhyo deśayanti, na tvanyebhyaḥ | anyathā upāyānabhijñatvānnaiva bhaved bhagavān sarvajñaḥ ityevaṃ darśyate | hīnādhimuktikairiti śrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ | ātmādidṛṣṭikaiḥ iti tairthikaiḥ | nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate iti nāsti tadarthamavakāśa iti |
body.translated_text: Why was this spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to those who have set out in the Supreme Vehicle and not to others? Could it be that the <s>Bhagavān</s> also has desire and hatred?—thinking thus, he says "For what reason?" Therefore, "<s>Subhūti</s>, by those of inferior conviction"—he answered. By this, indeed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has affection toward all beings equally like an only son—there is no desire or hatred. Nevertheless, when certain [beings] become receptive at certain times, then [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] teaches to them, but not to others. Otherwise, due to lack of skill in means, the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not be omniscient—thus it is shown. "By those of inferior conviction" means: by the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. "By those who hold to the view of self and the like" means: by the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). "This situation does not exist" means: there is no opportunity for that purpose.

body.text: yacchrāvakaiḥ pratyekabuddhaiścāpi śrotuṃ na śakyate tatkathaṃ śakyate pṛthagjanaiḥ śrotum? yattairna śrotuṃ śakyaṃ tat kathaṃ śakyata udgrahītuṃ vā paryavāptuṃ vā | atastadasambhavamityarthaḥ | anena tāvad yogasamāpattāvavātāryate |
body.translated_text: If it cannot be heard even by <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, how could it be heard by ordinary persons? That which cannot be heard by them—how could it be grasped or fully comprehended? Therefore, its impossibility [for them] is the meaning. By this, one is led into <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment).

body.text: yadyevaṃ kathaṃ tāvadāryasubhūtinā dharmaparyāyo 'yaṃ śrotuṃ śakyata iti ced? bhagavato 'dhiṣṭhāneneti nāsti doṣaḥ | sarvapradeśeṣu yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe sūtramidaṃ bhāṣyate sa evaikaḥ pṛthivīpradeśo 'nuśaṃsanīya iti pratipādayan devadisatkāravaiśiṣṭyaṃ darśayitum api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyavocat |
body.translated_text: If so, then how was it possible for the noble <s>Subhūti</s> to hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse? [Answer:] Through the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>—therefore there is no fault. In all places, in whichever place on earth this <s>sūtra</s> is spoken, that very place on earth is to be praised—in order to demonstrate this and to show the special excellence of veneration by gods and others, he said "But moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>" and so forth.

body.text: pūrvaṃ tāvad bāhyaśāstrābhiṣvaṅgaparivarjanārthamuktam, samprati dhyānarasāsvādavarjanārthamiti nāsti punaruktatā, samastasaṃgṛhītārthābhidhāne 'pi bhinnaprasaṅgābhidhānānnāsti punaruktateti jñātavyam | pūjanīyaḥ iti chatradhvajapatākādibhiḥ, vandanīyaḥ iti namaskaraṇīyaḥ, pradakṣiṇīyaḥ pradakṣiṇāyogyaḥ, ata eva pūjanīyatvādidharmairyuktāvād caityaḥ |
body.translated_text: Previously, [this station] was stated for the purpose of abandoning attachment to external treatises; now it is for the purpose of abandoning the relishing of the taste of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)—therefore there is no repetition. Even when the meaning is stated comprehensively, since the contexts are different, it should be known that there is no repetition. "To be worshipped" (<s>pūjanīya</s>) means: with parasols, banners, flags, and the like. "To be honored" (<s>vandanīya</s>) means: to be saluted. "Worthy of circumambulation" (<s>pradakṣiṇīya</s>) means: fit for circumambulation. For this very reason, because it possesses the qualities of being worthy of worship and the like, it is a <s>caitya</s> (sacred monument).

body.text: nanu īdṛśeṣu dharmaparyāyeṣu abhyudyatānāmapi kathaṃ kecit paribhūtā dṛśyanta iti cintāyāṃ pāpapariśodhanaviśeṣadeśanāya ye subhūte, kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā ityādyāha | paribhūtā bhaviṣyanti iti paribhāṣaṇabhaṇḍanādibhirvyāpannā bhaviṣyanti, suparibhūtāśca bhaviṣyanti iti vadhabandhanādibhiḥ pīḍitā bhaviṣyanti |
body.translated_text: Now, even among those who are engaged in such <s>Dharma</s>-discourses, how is it that some are seen to be reviled?—in order to teach the special purification of evil [karma], he says "Those, <s>Subhūti</s>, sons of good family or daughters of good family" and so forth. "They will be reviled" (<s>paribhūtā bhaviṣyanti</s>) means: they will be afflicted by blame, quarrel, and the like. "They will be greatly reviled" (<s>suparibhūtā</s>) means: they will be tormented by killing, imprisonment, and the like.

body.text: evamete mahātmānaḥ kathaṃ paribhūtā bhaviṣyantīti vicintyāha tatkasya hetoḥ? iti | teṣāṃ sattvānām ityādyudatarat | paurvajanmikāni iti pūrvajanmani kṛtāni | dṛṣṭa eva dharme iti pratyutpannajīvite | buddhabodhiṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 181]

children.text: ) cānuprāpsyanti iti pāpāni pariśodhya kālāntare bhāvanāniratā na ciraṃ anuttarasamyaksabodhimabhisambuddhya buddhā bhaviṣyantīti vākyārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The meaning of the sentence is: having purified their sins and at a later time being devoted to cultivation, before long they will become <s>Buddhas</s>, having realized the unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.translated_text: Reflecting "How will these great beings be reviled?" he says "For what reason?" "Of those beings" and so forth—he answered. "Of previous births" (<s>paurvajanmika</s>) means: done in previous lives. "In this very life" (<s>dṛṣṭa eva dharme</s>) means: in the present lifetime. "They will attain <s>Buddha</s>-awakening"—

body.text: tato nidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaskandhaṃ prasunuyādaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam iti yadāha tatra kena prakāreṇa aprameyākhyeyāvabodhaḥ syāt? ityatra abhijānāmyahaṃ subhūte ityādyāha | atra prabhāveṇa bahutareṇa cāprameyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ ca paridīpitam | tatrābhijānāmi subhūte atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ asaṃkhyeyataraiḥ ityādinā prabhāvaḥ paridīpataḥ | ayaṃ tāvat puṇyaskandhasyaiva prabhāvaḥ | etāvatā praśastaro viśiṣṭataraḥ (pūrvakaḥ) puṇyaskandho 'pyabhibhūyate | dīpaṅkarataḥ yāvat asaṃkhyeyakalpam | asaṃkhyeyakalpastāvad gaṇanātītatvāt, dīpaṅkarasya pareṇa paratareṇa caturaśītibuddhakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhūvan, ye mayārāgitāḥ iti pratipattyarcayā ārādhitāḥ | na virāgitāḥ ityantarāle 'pi tadabhinirhārasya anutsṛṣṭatvāt | yacca iti kartṛviśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: When he says "from that cause he would produce a greater, immeasurable, incalculable heap of merit"—in what manner would the comprehension of the immeasurable and inexpressible be? To this, he says "I recall, <s>Subhūti</s>" and so forth. Here, through the power [of the illustration], that which is greater, immeasurable, and incalculable has been illuminated. Among these, "I recall, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the past time, in incalculable aeons, even more incalculable" and so forth—by this, the power is illuminated. This, however, is the power of the merit-heap alone. By this much, even the more praiseworthy and more distinguished previous merit-heap is surpassed. From <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> throughout the incalculable aeons: the incalculable aeons [are so designated] because they transcend counting. Beyond and further beyond <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, there were eighty-four billions of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, "who were honored by me"—that is, pleased through the worship of practice. "They were not displeased"—because even in between, the accomplishment of that [practice] was not abandoned. "And that which"—indicates the distinction of the agent.

body.text: tato 'yamarthaḥ yaśca ārāgaṇādikaḥ (puṇyaskandhaḥ), yaśca udgrahaṇādiśraddhādipuṇyaskandhastadutpāditaśca vāsanātmakaḥ skandhaḥ, anayoḥ (puṇyaskandhayoḥ) pūrvapuṇyaskandhaḥ uttarapuṇyaskandhasyāsya śatatamīmapi kalāṃ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 182]

children.text: ) nopaiti iti | etāvato 'lpīyastvaṃ darśayituṃ sahasratamīmapi ityāha | saṃkhyā iti tulyeṣveva yujyate, yathā himavatā (tulya) vindhya ityucyate, na tu sarṣapaḥ | kalām ityaṃśaḥ, sa ca samānajātīya eva, yathā sumeroḥ kalā parvataśikharameva, na tu tṛṇaśikharaḥ | gaṇanām ityapi tulyeṣvev, yathā sumerurapi giriḥ, himavānapi giriḥ, na tu sarṣapaḥ | upamām ityapi sadṛśeṣveva, yathā gosadṛśo gavaya ityucyute, na tu makṣikā | laghurapi parikarmavaśena tasya (mahataḥ) kṛtyaṃ karoti, yathā niśite kṛte sati dātramapyasikṛtyaṃ karotīti matvā upaniṣadam ityāha | tāḍanapīḍanādivistāropāyena tīkṣṇīkṛte 'pyatilaghutayā na kṣamata ityarthaḥ | ata eva aupamyamapi ityāha | tasyopamābhāvamapi na kṣamate |
children.translated_text: does not approach [it]. To show that even this much is [only] a fraction, he says 'even a thousandth part' and so forth. 'Number' (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) is appropriate only between comparable things, just as one says 'the <s>Vindhya</s> [is comparable to] the <s>Himavat</s>,' not a mustard seed. 'Fraction' (<s>kalā</s>) means a part, and that too is only of the same class — just as a fraction of <s>Sumeru</s> is a mountain peak, not a blade of grass. 'Reckoning' (<s>gaṇanā</s>) too [applies] only between comparable things — just as <s>Sumeru</s> too is a mountain, and <s>Himavat</s> too is a mountain, but not a mustard seed. 'Comparison' (<s>upamā</s>) too [applies] only between similar things — just as one says a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is similar to a cow, but not a fly. Thinking that even a light thing, through the force of refinement, can perform the function of a great thing — just as a sickle, when sharpened, can perform the function of a sword — he says 'approximation' (<s>upaniṣad</s>). The meaning is: even when sharpened to a fine point through the method of extensive beating and pressing, due to its extreme lightness, it is not able [to compare]. Therefore he also says 'even a simile' (<s>aupamya</s>) — it does not admit even a simile of that.

body.translated_text: Therefore the meaning is: the merit-heap that consisted of honoring and the like, and the merit-heap born of the faith of grasping and the like, together with the latent-impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) aggregate produced thereby—of these two merit-heaps, the former merit-heap does not equal even a hundredth part of this latter merit-heap,

body.text: sarvajñavacanādevaitajjñātavyam, evaṃvidheṣu indriyaviṣayātīteṣu viṣayeṣu sarvajñavacanasyaiva prāmāṇyāt | api ca pariśuddhe kāle sarvasattvānāmapi pariśuddhatvānnāścaryām, apariśuddhe tāvat kāle ye sattvā kṣaṇamātramaśyapariśuddhā bhavanti, tadāścaryam | evaṃ prabhāvamukhena tāvadaprameyatvaṃ pradarśitam |
body.translated_text: This should be known from the word of the omniscient one (<s>sarvajña</s>), since in matters that transcend the scope of the senses, only the word of the omniscient one has authority. Moreover, at a time of purity, the purity of all beings is not surprising; but at a time of impurity, when beings become pure even for a single moment — that is truly wondrous. Thus, through the door of [demonstrating its] power, the immeasurability [of merit] has been shown.

body.text: kathamasaṃkhyeyaṃ saṃkhyayeti vicāraṇāyāṃ sacetpunaḥ subhūte...... tasmin samaye ityādyāha | tena bahulaṃ paridīpitam | tatpuṇyagaṇanayāpi viṣādamanuprāpya (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 183

children.text: ) vyāmugdhacittāntarviśeṣe unmādamanuprāpnuyuḥ | tataḥ udbhūtenonmādena cittavikṣepaṃ vā gaccheyuḥ | anena gāmbhīryamaudāryaṃ copadiṣṭim |
children.translated_text: through the mental disturbance caused by bewilderment, [beings] would attain madness. Then, from the arisen madness, they would undergo mental distraction. By this, the profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>) and the magnificence (<s>audārya</s>) are taught.

body.translated_text: When the inquiry arises 'How can the incalculable be calculated?', he says 'If, moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>... at that time' and so forth. By that, much has been illuminated. Even by counting that merit,

body.text: evamasnād dharmaparyāyāt saṃkhyāprabhāvapratisaṃyuktamevaṃvidhaṃ phalaṃ kathaṃ jñāyata iti? api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | phalaṃ punaḥ hetvanurūpameva bhavati | laghiṣṭhe 'pi nyagrodhavṛkṣabīje 'tiśayasārasampannatvād bṛhacchākhāpallvavṛkṣabhūtaṃ phalaṃ nopadṛśyate | dharmaparyāyo 'pyayam alpaparivarto 'pyatyantagambhīraḥ, acityadharmadeśanād acintyaḥ | ato 'smādacintyād hetupratyayayānurūpamacintyaṃ phalaṃ bhavati, hetupratyayaprabhāvastāvat sarvajñagocaratvād acintyaḥ | vipākaśabdo 'tra phalārthaḥ, tena niṣyandādiphalāni saṃgṛhyante | etena sarveṇa cittapragraho darśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: How is it known that such a fruit, connected with enumeration and power, arises from this Dharma-discourse? [In response,] he says 'But moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth. The fruit is always in accordance with the cause. Even in a very small banyan seed, because it possesses surpassing vital essence, [its] fruit is seen to become a great tree with vast branches and leaves. This Dharma-discourse too, though of few chapters, is exceedingly profound; because its teaching of the Dharma is inconceivable, it is inconceivable. Therefore, from this inconceivable [cause], the fruit is inconceivable, in accordance with the cause and conditions; the power of cause and conditions is inconceivable because it is within the scope of the omniscient one alone. The word 'maturation' (<s>vipāka</s>) here means fruit; by it, outflow-fruits (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) and other fruits are also encompassed. By all of this, the taking hold of the mind (<s>cittapragraha</s>) has been shown.

body.text: 15. abhisamayakāle 'hamitivikalpaviyoga-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 15. The station of freedom from the conceptualization of 'I' at the time of realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>):

body.text: evaṃ nirākṛte 'pi dhyānasāsvāde pratyāsanne 'bhisamayakāleṃ yaiḥ bodhisattvaiḥ ātmavaiśiṣṭyamavalokya 'ahaṃ samyaksambodhimārgapratipannaḥ, sarve mayā sattvāḥ parinirvāpayitavyāḥ'; iti manyamānaistaistasmin ātmagrāhavikale 'bhisamayākāle kathaṃ sthātavyam, kathaṃ pratipattavyam, kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyam? ityetad darśayituṃ pañcadaśasthāmadhikṛtyāha- sūbhūti....... avocat- kathaṃ bhagavan, bodhisattvayānasamprasthitena sthātavyam iti | sthātavyamityādideśanātrayaṃ tu (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 184

children.text: ) prāgevoktaṃ bhagavatā | nāsti subhūte, sa kaścid dharmo yo bodhisattvayānasamprasthito nāma ityavaśiṣṭenātra ātmagrāhavisaṃyogaḥ kriyate | śeṣāṇāṃ (padānāṃ) vyākhyā tu pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: have already been spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. By what remains — 'There is no such dharma, <s>Subhūti</s>, called one who has set out in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle' — the severance from self-grasping (<s>ātmagrāhavisaṃyoga</s>) is accomplished here. The explanation of the remaining words follows the previous pattern.

body.translated_text: Thus, even when the relish of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) has been rejected, at the time of approaching realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>), for those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who, beholding their own excellence, think 'I am one who has entered the path of perfect awakening; all beings are to be led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> by me' — for them, at that time of realization when there is the fault of self-grasping (<s>ātmagrāha</s>), how should one abide, how should one practice, how should one take hold of the mind? To show this, regarding the fifteenth station, he says: '<s>Subhūti</s>... said: How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should one who has set out in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle abide?' The three [aspects of] instruction — 'how to abide' and so forth —

body.text: yathedaṃ pudgaladharmanairātmyaṃ prāgeva bhagavatā prakāśitaṃ tathokte sati bodhisattveṣu punaḥ abhisamayakāle kathamātmagrāhaḥ sambhaved? tannirākaraṇāyoktamapi kiṃ punarucyate? athaivamapi deśanāyāṃ saṃmuhyet prāguktasyānavasthānaṃ ca syāditi? tathā deśite 'pi anādikālātyantadṛḍhībhūtātmābhiniveśavaśatayā keṣāñcit sammohasyānivṛtteḥ deśito 'pyarthaḥ punarupadiśyate | punardeśanākāle pāriṣadyānāṃ sammohanivṛttenārnavasthā syāt | bhagavatā kṛtasyopadeśasya phalaṃ tāvat sammohavinivṛttireva vineyajanānāmiti na niṣphalam | ata eva sammohanirvṛtau satyāṃ phalābhāvena punaḥ pravṛttyabhāvāt prakṛtamevedam |
body.translated_text: Since the selflessness of persons and dharmas (<s>pudgaladharmanairātmya</s>) has already been made clear by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, when that has been stated, how could self-grasping arise again in <s>bodhisattvas</s> at the time of realization? Why is what has already been stated for its removal being said again? If even with such teaching one might be confused, and the earlier statement might not remain stable — [the answer is:] even when thus taught, because of the tenacity of self-attachment (<s>ātmābhiniveśa</s>), which has become exceedingly firm from beginningless time, the confusion of some has not ceased; therefore, the meaning that has been taught is taught again. At the time of re-teaching, through the cessation of confusion in the audience, there will be no infinite regress. The fruit of the instruction given by the <s>Bhagavān</s> is precisely the cessation of confusion in those beings to be trained — hence it is not fruitless. Therefore, when the confusion has ceased and there is no [further] fruit, there is no [further] engagement — this itself is precisely [the resolution of] the matter at hand.

body.text: 16. avavādaparyeṣaṇasthānam :
body.translated_text: 16. The station of seeking instruction (<s>avavādaparyeṣaṇa</s>):

body.text: yadi bodhisattvayānasamprasthito nāma na syāt sa kaścid dharmaḥ (tarhi) kathaṃ bhagavān dīpaṅkarasya śāsturantikādavavādaṃ prāpya anuttarāṃ samyaksambomabhisambuddhaḥ? atha na syād (saḥ) abhisambuddhaḥ (tarhi) abhisamayakāṅkṣiṇāvavādo na paryeṣṭavya iti ye manyante, teṣāmavavādaviyogavisaṃyogāya ṣoḍaśasyāmadhikṛtya tatkiṃ manse subhūte ityādyāha | pūrvaṃ dharmakāyāptikāmatāvasare dharmagrāhaniṣedha uktaḥ, idānīmabhisamayakāle abhisambuddhasya tasya niṣedhaḥ kriyate 'to na punaruktatā | nāsti paramārthataḥ sa kaścidapi jñānajñeyātmako dharmaḥ, yathā pūrvaṃ vicāritam | tadbalena avicāraramaṇīyamātratayā śrutamayyādiprajñopādakameṇa bhagavataḥ- (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s> 185
self-arisen omniscient knowledge (<s>svayambhūsarvajñajñāna</s>) arises in the form of conventional truth (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>) as graspable.

body.translated_text: If there is no such dharma called 'one who has set out in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle,' then how did the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having received instruction from the Teacher <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>, attain unsurpassed perfect awakening? And if he were not thus awakened, then those who desire realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) should not seek instruction — for those who think thus, for the purpose of separating them from the conceptualization of disconnection from instruction (<s>avavādaviyogavikalpa</s>), regarding the sixteenth station, he says 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so forth. Previously, the negation of grasping at dharmas (<s>dharmagrāha</s>) was stated in the context of the desire to attain the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; now, the negation is made of that which is realized (<s>abhisambuddha</s>) at the time of realization — hence there is no repetition. There is no dharma, ultimately, of the nature of knowledge or knowable — as was previously examined. By that power, through merely learning-based and other [types of] wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that is attractive only to the unexamined [mind], the <s>Bhagavān's</s>

body.text: nanu tadapi bhagavato dīpaṅkarasyānubhāvamātramiti ced? evaṃ satyapi anurūpameva, tathāpi tasmin sarvabuddhānāṃ sādhāraṇānubhāvāḥ, na kevalaṃ bhagavato dīpaṅkarasyaiva | yadi na syādabhisambuddhaḥ (kaścit tarhi) kathaṃ tena samyaksaṃbodhau bhagavān vyākṛta iti vicārya sacet punaḥ sūbhūte ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] but that too is merely the empowerment (<s>anubhāva</s>) of the Blessed <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>? Even if that is so, it is still in accord [with our position]; nevertheless, all <s>Buddhas</s> share those common empowerments — not the Blessed <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> alone. If [one asks:] if no one is awakened, how was the <s>Bhagavān</s> predicted by him for perfect awakening? — reflecting thus, he says 'If, moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth.

body.text: ayamabhiprāyaḥ- yadi bhagavataḥ pratyātmavedyo dharmaḥ paramārthato tathābhūto bhavart tadā syādabhisambuddhaḥ, athavā 'mayā punaḥ dharmo 'bhisambuddhaḥ'; ityahaṅkāraḥ samudbhavet tadā syād 'abhisambuddhaḥ'; ityevaṃ viparītābhiniveśāt tathāgatasya vyākaraṇaṃ na bhavet | yato hi tadā 'mayābhisambuddhaḥ'; iti na bhavati, na ca dharmodiṣvapyabhiniveśaḥ bhavati | tata evāham aviparītasamyagjñānamārgasthitau vyākṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the intention: if the <s>Bhagavān's</s> personally realized dharma (<s>pratyātmavedya</s>) were ultimately of such a [fixed] nature, then there would be 'one who is awakened'; or if the I-conceit (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) 'I have realized the dharma' were to arise, then there would be 'one who is awakened' — through such inverted attachment, the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) by the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not occur. Since at that time the thought 'I have realized' does not arise, and since there is no attachment even to dharmas and the like, therefore I was predicted as being established on the non-inverted path of right knowledge (<s>aviparītasamyagjñānamārga</s>).

body.text: nāsti sa kaścid dharmo 'bhisambuddhaḥ ityanena arthato dīpaṅkarasyāntikād avavādagrāhavikalpaṃ vipakṣatvena darśayitvā tadvikalpaprahāṇāya chandaḥ praṇidhānaṃ cāpi deśitam | dīpaṅkaretyupalakṣaṇamātreṇābhihitena sarve dharmodgrahaṇavikalpā nirvatante | nāstī ityanena tasya gambhīratvamuktam, samyaksambodhaye avavādaparyeṣaṇavidhānena tāvadasyodāratvaṃ coktam, śrāvakapratyekabuddhāvavādād atyantaviśiṣṭatvāt |
body.translated_text: By 'there is no such dharma that was realized,' having shown the conceptualization of grasping at instruction from <s>Dīpaṅkara</s> (<s>avavādagrāhavikalpa</s>) as being on the side of the adversary (<s>vipakṣa</s>), aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and resolve (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for the abandonment of that conceptualization are also taught. By '<s>Dīpaṅkara</s>' being stated as mere indication, all conceptualizations of grasping at Dharma are brought to cessation. By 'there is no [such dharma],' its profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>) is stated; through the prescription of seeking instruction for perfect awakening, its magnificence (<s>audārya</s>) is also stated — because it is exceedingly distinguished from the instructions of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas).

body.text: yadi tathāgatena samyaksambuddhena na syāt sa kaścid dharmo yo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau abhisambuddhaḥ, tadā kathaṃ tathāgatatvaṃ bhavet? tadyathā pūrvabuddhā abhisambodhiṃ gatāḥ, tathaivātrāpi gatatvādabhisambuddhastathāgata ucyata iti cet? abhisambuddha ityākhyasya kasyacid dharmasyābhāvāt tatkathaṃ bhavediti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ iti pṛṣṭhavān | tathāgata iti subhūte ityādi codatarat | tathatā iti dharmāṇāmaviparītasvabhāva ucyate, sa candiśāntādisvabhāvaḥ, sarvadharmasādhāraṇatvāt sā bhūtaḥ iti vacanena viśeṣitā, bhutastu yathārthatvena tathāgatajñānamabhidhīyate | tasyāstathatāyā yā paramārthato 'nupannadharmatā sa tathāgata ityucyate | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: If the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the perfectly awakened one, has no such dharma that has been realized in unsurpassed perfect awakening, then how can <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood exist? [If one says:] just as previous <s>Buddhas</s> have gone to awakening, so too has this one — therefore he is called '<s>Tathāgata</s>' (the one who has thus gone), i.e., the one who is awakened? Since there is no dharma whatsoever called 'realized' — how could that be? Reflecting thus, he asked 'For what reason?' [In response,] '<s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth is stated. <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness) is said to be the non-inverted nature of dharmas, and that is of the nature of peace and so forth; because it is common to all dharmas, it is qualified by the word '<s>bhūta</s>' (real), and '<s>bhūta</s>' means 'in accordance with reality' — it designates the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. That <s>tathatā</s>, whose ultimate nature is unoriginated (<s>anutpannadharmatā</s>) — that is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>. As it is said:

body.text: anutpādadharmaḥ satataṃ tathāgataḥ | iti |
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is constantly of the nature of non-arising (<s>anutpādadharma</s>).'

body.text: paramārthato dharmatāpi dharmiṇo netarā, ataḥ paramārthataḥ sarvadharmāṇāmanutpādo dharmatā | sarvadharmādhigamasvabhāvo 'vicāraramaṇīyaḥ paramārthato 'nutpannaḥ tathyasaṃvṛtau parikalpyamānaḥ sajjñānaviśiṣṭaḥ 'tathāgataḥ'; ucyata iti vākyārthaḥ | tasya ca paramārthato 'nutpannatvānnāsti kaścid grāhyo grāhako vā | tasmānnāsti kaścid dharmo 'pyabhisambuddhaḥ (nāma) paramārthataḥ | tathyasaṃvṛtimāśrītya tena viśiṣṭajñānena yathā abhisambuddhaḥ tathā gata ityevamabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Ultimately, even the nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) is not other than the <s>dharma</s>-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). Therefore, ultimately, the non-origination of all <s>dharmas</s> is [their] true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>). The essential nature of the realization of all <s>dharmas</s>, charming when unexamined, ultimately unoriginated, yet conventionally conceived, distinguished by genuine knowledge — that is called '<s>Tathāgata</s>': this is the meaning of the statement. And because of his ultimate non-origination, there is no grasping whatsoever.

body.text: paramārthāśrayeṇābhisambuddha iti kasmāttathā nocyate? iti cintāyāṃ yaḥ kaścit subhūte ityādyāha | tatkasya hetoḥ? iti na satyam ityanena yogjam | śeṣastu sugamānna vyākhyāyate | evaṃ tarhi 'saṃvṛtitaḥ tathāgatena abhisambuddhaḥ'; iti vyavasthaiva kathaṃ vyavasthāpyata iti vicārya yaśca dharmaḥ ityuktam | yaḥ iti rūpādilakṣaṇadharmaḥ, tatra na satyam itiḥ māyāvatpratibhāsamānānāṃ vicāryamāṇānāmatyantaśūnyatvenānutpannatvāt śaśaśrṛṅgavad atyantābhāvaḥ | na mṛṣā avicāraramaṇīyasvabhāvena māyāvatpratibhāsamānāt | athavā nāpi satyam, na kasyāpi dharmasya paramārthataḥ siddheḥ | na mṛṣā, na ca vicāragocaraḥ kaścit satyaḥ siddhaḥ, sarvadharmāṇāmanutpādāt |
body.translated_text: Thinking: 'Why is it not said that [something was] fully awakened to based on the ultimate?' — he says: 'Whoever, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth. 'For what reason?' — this is appropriate in connection with 'it is not true.' The rest, being easy to understand, is not commented upon. 'If so, then how is the determination that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened conventionally to be established?' — reflecting thus, he speaks the words: 'And whatever <s>dharma</s>...'

body.text: anenādhyāropāpavādāntau nirākṛtya madhyamamārgaṃ ca vyavasthāpya yogasamāpattau pravarttyate | tasmāt ityevaṃ paramārthataḥ sarvadharmāṇāmanutpādāt na satyaṃ na ca mṛṣā | tathāgato 'pi pariśuddhyānutpādadharmayā prabhāvitaḥ, anutpādadharmatāyāḥ sādhāraṇatvāt, (tathā hi)-
body.translated_text: By this, having refuted both superimposition (<s>adhyāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>), and having established the middle path (<s>madhyamamārga</s>), one is set in motion in yogic concentration. Therefore, since ultimately all <s>dharmas</s> are unoriginated, [the <s>Dharma</s>] is neither true nor false. The <s>Tathāgata</s> too is pervaded by the purity of the nature of non-origination, because the nature of non-origination is shared [by all <s>dharmas</s>]. Thus indeed:

body.text: anutpādadharmaḥ satataṃ tathāgataḥ

children.translated_text: and all <s>dharmas</s> are similar to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One).
But those of childish understanding, grasping at signs,
engage in the world with regard to <s>dharmas</s> that do not [truly] exist.

body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is perpetually of the nature of non-origination;

body.text: ityādi | sarvadharmā buddhadharmāḥ iti tathāgato bhāṣate | yadyanutpannā evāmī dharmāstat kathaṃ sarvadharmāḥ ityucyanta iti pravicintya sarvadharmā iti subhūte ityādyāha | ayamatrārthaḥ- paramārthatastathā vidyante, na tu vyavahāraprajñaptitaḥ | asantastāvat paramārthato rūpādidharmāḥ, kintvaparamārthaṃ khalvavicāritamāśritya yasmāt svasāmānyalakṣaṇagrahaṇaṃ tasmāt sarvadharmāḥ ityucyante, na tu paramārthataḥ, tatra sthitānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dṛśyamānatve 'pyabhāvāt | anena tāvad vikṣepanigrahaḥ sandarśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: And so forth. The <s>Tathāgata</s> declares: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.' Reflecting: 'If indeed these <s>dharmas</s> are unoriginated, then how are they called "all <s>dharmas</s>"?' — he says: 'All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth. The meaning here is: they exist thus ultimately, but not from the standpoint of conventional designation. Forms and other <s>dharmas</s>, being non-existent ultimately, yet being not non-ultimate

body.text: 17. abhisamaya-sthānam :
body.translated_text: 17. The topic of realization (<s>abhisamaya-sthāna</s>):

body.text: yadi na syāt sa kaścid dharmo bhagavatābhisambuddhaḥ kathaṃ (tarhi) bodhisattvā upādattamavavādaṃ sammukhīkṛtya dharmapudgalanairātmyamadhigaccheyuḥ? iti vicintyābhisamayapratipādanārthaḥ tadyathāpi nāma ityādyāha | ayamabhisamayastāvat jñānaprāptinirabhimānitābhyāṃ saṃdarśyate | kathaṃ jñānaprātyeti cet? dvividhaṃ jñānamāśritya, gotrasamparigrahajñānaṃ samatājñānañca | tatra yajjñānaprāptyā tathāgatagotre samutpadya buddhagotre niyato jāyate tad gotrasamparigrahajñānam | tadutpādena upetakāyo bhavati | upeta ityātmanā parigṛhītaḥ, kāyastu tathāgatakāyaḥ | yena so 'dhigataḥ, sa upetakāyaḥ | kathaṃ jñāyate tajjñānaprāptirityāha- mahākāyaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: If there were no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that was fully awakened to by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, then how would <s>bodhisattvas</s>, taking up the instruction presented directly, realize the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons? — reflecting thus, in order to establish realization, he says: 'Just as, for example...' and so forth. This realization is shown through knowledge-attainment and freedom from conceit. How is knowledge-attainment [shown]?

body.text: anena pudgaladharmanairātmyasamatājñānaṃ samavāpya abhisamayaḥ sampradarśyata ityato gotrajñānamabhidhīyate | tena samatājñānena pudgaladharmanairātmyadhigamya sarve (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_189

children.text: ) sattvā ātmani (ātmavat) saṅgṛhītā bhavanti | tasmāt samastasattvakāyānāmātmani saṅgraheṇa sa mahākāya iti | nāpyapārthako 'yaṃ śabdaḥ, evaṃ sarvasattvānāmātma- saṅgraheṇa sa kāya ityucyate | teṣāṃ saṃbahulve 'pi na mahākāyaśabdārthatvam | anena sthānasyāsya audāryaṃ samudīritam |
children.translated_text: sentient beings are included within the self (as the self). Therefore, through the inclusion of the entirety of sentient beings within the self, he [is called] '<s>mahākāya</s>' (great body). Nor is this word meaningless — thus, through the self-inclusion of all sentient beings, it is called 'body' (<s>kāya</s>). Even though they are numerous, [the word] '<s>mahākāya</s>' does not [merely] mean 'great body' [in the literal sense]. By this, the magnanimity of this topic is expressed.

body.translated_text: By this, realization is demonstrated by attaining the knowledge of the equality of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s>; therefore, <s>gotra</s> (lineage) knowledge is stated. Through that knowledge of equality, having realized the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s>, all

body.text: ayamabhiprāyaḥ- bodhisattvānāmabhisamayo 'pyayaṃ tathyasaṃvṛtimāśritya viśiṣṭajñānotpādamātreṇa prabhāvito bhavati | paramārthato na kiñcinnirūpakaṃ nirūpyaṃ veti darśayitum, āryasubhūtiḥ- bhagavaṃstathāgatena puruṣo bhavedupetakāyaḥ ityādyāha | anenārthatastāvadupetakāya-mahākāyābhiniveśastu vipakṣatvena nirdiṣṭaḥ | (ataḥ) tatprahāṇāya chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti darśitam | upetakāyo mahākāya iti nimittamātrābhidhānena bodhiasattvānāṃ sarvadharmeṣvabhiniveśo nivartate | paramārthe 'pi tāvad vyavasthāpya yogasamāpattau cāvatāryate | gambhīryamapyuktam, samāropānto 'pi nirākṛtaḥ | pūrveṇa tāvadapavādāntaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The intent is this: even this realization of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, based on correct conventional [truth], is accomplished merely through the arising of distinguished knowledge. In order to show that ultimately there is nothing to be analyzed or that is analyzed, the noble <s>Subhūti</s> says: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, would a person be one endowed with a body by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' and so forth. By this, the intended meaning is that attachment to '<s>upetakāya</s>' (endowed body) and '<s>mahākāya</s>' (great body) is on the side of the adversary.

body.text: yadi tathāgatena sa eva kāyo syāt noktaḥ syāt tadā prāptābhisamayo bodhisattvaṃ 'evaṃ mayā bodhisattvābhisamayaḥ samprāptaḥ sāmpratamahaṃ sattvān parinirvāpayiṣyāmi'; ityetat kathaṃ sañcitayetyanyadīyaṃ sadvikalpaṃ samudīkṣya nirabhimānitayābhisamayaṃ darśayituṃ yo bodhisattvaṃ ityādyāha | anena ya evaṃ vadet- ahaṃ sattvān parinirvāpayiṣyāmīti 'ahaṃ ya evaṃ vadet- ahaṃ sattvān parinirvāpayiṣyāmīti'; ahaṃ bodhiasattvo 'smi (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_190

children.text: ) ityabhimānī sa tathyato na bodhisattvaḥ iti darśyate | tatkasya hetoḥ? ityatra jñāpakahetuḥ paripṛṣṭaḥ | dharmaḥ iti tu rupādiasvabhāvo vā pudgalādisvabhāvo va | yuktito vicāraṇāyāṃ tasya dharmasyādṛsṭatvād āryasubhūtirapyāha no hīdam iti | tasyā yukteḥ sarvatra sādhāraṇatvād bhagavān nairātmyadvayāvatāraṇārthaṃ tasmād ityāha | nisattvāḥ ityādi tāvadupalakṣaṇam, niḥsvabhāvā api draṣṭavyāḥ | anena vikṣepanigraho nirdiṣṭaḥ | ukto 'bhisamayaḥ |
children.translated_text: has such conceit — it is shown that he is not truly a <s>bodhisattva</s>. 'For what reason?' — here the indicative reason is asked. '<s>Dharma</s>' means either the nature of forms and the like, or the nature of persons and the like. Since that <s>dharma</s> is not perceived upon examination through reasoning, the noble <s>Subhūti</s> also says: 'No, indeed not.' Because that reasoning is universally applicable, the <s>Bhagavān</s> [teaches] the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmyadvaya</s>).

body.translated_text: If that very body were [established by] the <s>Tathāgata</s> and not [merely] designated, then a <s>bodhisattva</s> who had attained realization [might think]: 'Thus have I attained the realization of a <s>bodhisattva</s>; now I shall lead sentient beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' Looking toward such dualistic conceptualization of others, in order to show realization through freedom from conceit, he says: 'Whoever is a <s>bodhisattva</s>...' and so forth. By this, whoever

body.text:
ata ūrdhvaṃ buddhabhūme paryeṣaṇam | tadapi buddhasya saptabhiḥ sampadbhiḥ saṃgṛhyate | sapta sampadaśca-
1. kṣetrapariśuddhisampad
2. anuttaradṛṣṭipariśuddhisampad
3. anuttarajñānapariśuddhisampad
4. prāptapuṇyaskandhādhipatyasampad
5. kāyasampad
6. vāk-sampad
7. cittasampacca |
body.translated_text:
From here onward is the investigation of the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. This too is comprised within the seven excellences (<s>sampad</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>. The seven excellences are:
1. Excellence of field-purification (<s>kṣetrapariśuddhisampad</s>)
2. Excellence of purification of the supreme view (<s>anuttaradṛṣṭipariśuddhisampad</s>)
3. Excellence of purification of supreme knowledge (<s>anuttarajñānapariśuddhisampad</s>)
4. Excellence of mastery over the attained heap of merit (<s>prāptapuṇyaskandhādhipatyasampad</s>)
5. Excellence of body (<s>kāyasampad</s>)
6. Excellence of speech (<s>vāksampad</s>)
7. Excellence of mind (<s>cittasampad</s>)

body.text: 1. kṣetra pariśiddhisampad :
body.translated_text: 1. Excellence of field-purification (<s>kṣetrapariśuddhisampad</s>):

body.text: tatra yadi na syāt kaścid bodhisattvo nāma dharmaḥ, (tarhi) kastāvad buddhakṣetraṃ pariniṣpādayituṃ yatnaṃ kuryāt? ityāśaṅkāṃ nirākartuṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhisampadamadhikṛtya- yaḥ subhūte bodhisattvaḥ ityādyāha | so 'pi tathaiva vaktavyaḥ ityabhimānitvānnocyate sa bodhisattva ityarthaḥ | (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_191

children.text: ) pudgaladharmanairātmyayoranadhigame 'pyadhigatamityabhimānāt | evamahasmītyabhimānānna tasya pudgalanairāatmyāvagamaḥ, na ca dharmanairātmyāvabodhaḥ, asatsu kṣetravyuheṣvapi tatrābhimānāt | anena kṣetravyūheṣu māyopamatvādhimuktyā bodhisattvena kathaṃ sthātavyamityetad darśitam |
children.translated_text: Because of the conceit 'I have realized' even without [actual] realization of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, because of the conceit 'I am such,' there is for him neither understanding of the selflessness of persons nor comprehension of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, [and there is] conceit even regarding field-arrays that do not [truly] exist. By this, it is shown how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide — through the conviction that field-arrays are like an illusion.

body.translated_text: Therein, if there were no such <s>dharma</s> as a <s>bodhisattva</s>, then who would make the effort to accomplish a <s>Buddha</s>-field? — in order to remove this doubt, addressing the excellence of <s>Buddha</s>-field purification, he says: 'Whoever, <s>Subhūti</s>, is a <s>bodhisattva</s>...' and so forth. Because one who would say it in that very way [i.e., with conceit] is not called a <s>bodhisattva</s> — this is the meaning.

body.text: yadi paramārthato na syuste kṣetravyūhāḥ (tadā) bhagavatā kathamuktā iti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityāha | pūrvavadasya vyākhyānam | na ceyaṃ punaruktiḥ | pūrvaṃ tāvadadhimukticaryābhūmisthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bodhisattvakṣetrapariśuddhau praṇidhānāvasthāyāṃ bodhisattvavikalpasya niṣedhārtham (uktāḥ), samprati buddhekṣetrapariśuddhipariniṣpattaye ye bodhisattvā evaṃvidhenābhiniveśena pravartante, yeṣāṃ caivaṃvidho vikalpaḥ, tannirākaraṇārthamuktam | na cānavasthāprasaṅga, tadaivaṃvidhasya kasyaciditaravikalpasyāsambhavāt |
body.translated_text: If those buddha-field adornments (<s>kṣetravyūha</s>) do not exist ultimately, then how were they spoken of by the <s>Bhagavān</s>? — Reflecting thus, he says 'Why is that?' The explanation is as before. And this is not a repetition. Previously, for <s>bodhisattvas</s> abiding on the stages of the practice of conviction (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>)...

body.text: aneneha bodhisattvena kathaṃ pratipattavyaṃ tad vyapadiṣṭam | kīdṛśo bodhisattvo nāmetyatra yaḥ subhūte bodhisattvaḥ ityādyāha | nirātmāno dharmāḥ iti dviruktayā dvividhena nairātmyena sarvadharmāṇāṃ nairātmyaṃ darśyate | bodhisattvo bodhisattvaḥ iti dviruktyā tadeva dvividhaṃ nairātmyajñānaṃ darśyate | athavā ekastāvad bodhisattvaḥ āvṛttaḥ, bodhisattva ityākhyāta ityuttarastu (kathanasya) prakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: By this, how the <s>bodhisattva</s> should practice here is indicated. As to what kind [of being] is called a <s>bodhisattva</s>, he says 'That <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so on. 'Selfless are the <s>dharmas</s>' — by the double statement, the essencelessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> through the twofold [selflessness]...

body.text: tena kiṃ darśayiṣyata iti ced? kena niṣpādyante yadi pudgalādigrāhakābhāvaḥ, kṣetravyūhāḥ iti dharmagrāhakasyāpyabhāvaḥ, ubhayabhāvādhigamena bodhisattva ityākhyāta iti nirdiṣṭam | anena cittapragraho deśitaḥ | ebhiḥ sarvaiḥ sthānai gāmbhīryaṃ darśitam | tatra māyāvadbuddhakṣetrapariniṣpādanādhimuktayā bodhisattvānāṃ pravṛttipradarśanenaudāryamuktam |
body.translated_text: If asked 'What will he demonstrate by that?' — 'By whom are they accomplished, if there is no grasper of persons?' [answers:] 'buddha-field adornments' [shows] the absence of a grasper of <s>dharmas</s> as well. Through the realization of both [absences], one is designated as a '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' By this, the uplift of the mind (<s>cittapragraha</s>)...

body.text: 2. anuttaradṛṣṭipariśuddhisampad :
body.translated_text: 2. The excellence of the purification of unsurpassed view (<s>anuttaradṛṣṭipariśuddhi</s>):

body.text: yadi nāsti bodhisattvo nāmaḥ kaścid dharmaḥ, tadā tathāgataḥ pariśuddhadarśanena pariśuddhajñānena ca yukta eva na bhavet, tasya bodhisattvādutpannātvāt, tasyābhāve sa kathaṃ bhavatumarhati, ahetukatve nityasattvādidoṣāḥ, tasmād yasyāṃ saṃnipatitatāyāṃ pariṣadhevaṃ vikalpo bhavet, tasyāḥ kṛte pariśuddhaṃ darśanaṃ jñānañcetyanuttaradvayamadhikṛtya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | pūrvataḥ bhagavato 'bhiprāyaṃ gṛhītvā āryasubhūtirapyāhasaṃvidyate iti |
body.translated_text: If there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever called '<s>bodhisattva</s>,' then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would not be endowed with purified vision and purified knowledge, since he arises from the <s>bodhisattva</s> [stage]. In its absence, how could he come to be? Because of the absence of a cause...

body.text: anena paramārthataḥ bodhisattvo nāma sa kaścid dharmo na bhavati, tathāpi saṃvṛtau puṇyajñānasambhāraṃ paripūrya pariśuddhaṃjñānadarśanābhyāṃ yastathāgato bhavati, (tena) avicāramaṇīyaskandhamātrasya bodhisattvasyāstitvaṃ bhavantyeva | anyathā saṃvṛtāvapi yadi sa na bhavet tadā kastathāgato bhavedityevaṃ tāvat darśitam | tatra saṃvidyate tathāgatasya prajñācakṣuḥ ityeva tāvannocyate, (api tu) viśiṣṭaṃ viśuddhadarśanamabhidhātuṃ cakṣuṣo vidyāmānatvaṃ darśitam |
body.translated_text: By this [it is shown that]: ultimately there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever called '<s>bodhisattva</s>'; nevertheless, conventionally, having completed the accumulation of merit and knowledge (<s>puṇyajñānasambhāra</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> who arises through purified knowledge and vision — [thereby] the mere aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) that are delightful without analysis (<s>avicāramaṇīya</s>)...

body.text: samāsataścaturvidhaṃ bhavati cakṣuḥ- rūpagrāhakam, paramārthasatyagrāhakam, saṃvṛtisatyagrāhakam, sarvākārajñeyagrāhakaṃ ca | rūpagrāhakamapi dvividham- karmaphalaṃ bhāvanāphalañceti | pañcavidhaṃ cakṣuḥ kramaśaḥ- tatra sthūlaviṣayatvāt prathamaṃ rūpagrāhakaṃ kathitam, paramārthavaśena saṃvṛtijñānaṃ pariśuddhadhyatītyataḥ pūrvaṃ paramārthasatyagrāhakaṃ paścācca saṃvṛtisatyagrāhakamabhihitamiti saṅgacchate kramanirdeśaḥ | pudgaladharmanairātmyayoḥ saṃvidyate prajñācakṣuḥ, saṃvṛtau dharmamātrameva tāvadavabhāsate, na tu pudgala iti pudgalaśūnye dharmamātre dharmacakṣuḥ, sarvajñeyānāṃ sarvākārajñānaṃ tāvad buddhacakṣurityucyate, anenedānīṃ sākṣātkṛtya viharaṇāt | tathyasaṃvṛtau pañcacakṣuṣāṃ deśanayoktaṃ viśuddhadarśanam |
body.translated_text: In brief, the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) is of four kinds: that which apprehends form, that which apprehends ultimate truth, that which apprehends conventional truth, and that which apprehends all aspects of the knowable. That which apprehends form is also of two kinds: the fruit of action (<s>karma</s>) and the fruit of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Thus the eye is of five kinds.

body.text: 3. anuttarajñānapariśuddhisampad :
body.translated_text: 3. The excellence of the purification of unsurpassed knowledge (<s>anuttarajñānapariśuddhi</s>):

body.text: viśuddhajñānābhidhānārtham- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | traikālikāḥ cittacaitasāstāvaccittasantatiḥ | tataḥ traikālyaviṣayatvena tadviṣayāvabodho jñānamityucyate, na tu darśanam | tadapi sarāgacittavītarāgacittetyādinānāvidhasaṃkleśavyavadānabhāvena veditavyam |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of expressing purified knowledge, he says 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so on. The mental states (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) of the three times constitute the mental continuum (<s>cittasantati</s>). Because its object encompasses the three times, the cognition of that object is called knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), but not [mere] vision (<s>darśana</s>). That [knowledge] too, with or without attachment...

body.text: tāvanto lokadhātavaḥ ityupalakṣaṇam, anantalokadhātvantarnihitasattvānāṃ cittadhārāyāḥ parijñānāt | tathāhi- saṃvṛtau tathāgatasya māṃsacakṣurādīni bhavanti, atastanniṣpādanārthaṃ bodhisattvena chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyam | anena tāvad vacanena sampaddvayaṃ paridīpitam |
body.translated_text: 'So many world-realms' is merely an indication — because of the complete knowledge of the stream of mind (<s>cittadhārā</s>) of beings contained within infinite world-realms. For thus: conventionally, the <s>Tathāgata</s> possesses the fleshly eye (<s>māṃsacakṣus</s>) and so on; therefore, for the purpose of accomplishing those, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should, through aspiration...

body.text: māṃsacakṣurādīnyapi ekānekasvabhāvābhyāṃ vicāraṇāyāmanupalabdhānyeva | na hyarthāntarajñānena grahaṇaṃ yujyate, yathā pūrvaṃ vicāritam, evaṃ sati kathaṃ prajñāsyete tathāgatasya māṃsacakṣurādividyamānatā cittadhārā ceti cittāśayaṃ viditvā tatkasya hetoḥ? ityāha | bodhisattvena kathamanayordvayorviśuddhayoryogasamāpattyā pratipattavyam? ityetadabhidhātuṃ cittadhārā cittadhārā ityādyāha | paramārthataḥ adhārā iti | svabhāvato 'sattve 'pi saṃvṛtimadhikṛtyāha- tenocyate cittadhāreti iti | anyathā paramārthataḥ sarvavāggocarātītatvānna vaktuṃ śakṣyata ityabhiprāyaḥ | cittadhāretyupalakṣaṇam | māṃsacakṣurādīnyapi cakṣuḥsvabhāvarahitānyeva uktānīti kathanaṃ prakṛtaṃ sākṣānnoktam |
body.translated_text: Even the fleshly eye and so on, when examined in terms of singular or plural nature, are simply unapprehended. For apprehension by a cognition of something different is not tenable, as was analyzed previously. This being so, how are the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s fleshly eye and so on to be designated as existing?

body.text: atra kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyamiti tadabhidhātumāha tatkasya hetoḥ? iti | adhāretyanena saha yojanīyam | atītādīnāṃ cittānāṃ paramārthato 'nutpannatvād anupalambhaḥ | sattve 'pi grahaṇānupapattyā nānupalambhaḥ | tathā sati acittadhārādeśanamapi na bhavet, na cānupalambhamātreṇa bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ syāt | yathā traikālikacittasya paramārthato 'bhāvastathā pūrvamuktaṃ vakṣyate ca | cittoktirūpalakṣaṇam, tato 'tītādimāṃsacakṣurādīnyapyanupalabdhānyeva | atra adhārā ityādibhiḥ padairgāmbhīryamuktam, śeṣairaudāryam |
body.translated_text: To state how the mind should be uplifted here, he says 'Why is that?' This should be construed together with [the word] 'because.' The minds of the past and so on are unapprehended because they are ultimately unoriginated. Even if they existed, because apprehension would still be untenable, [they are] not...

body.text: 4. prāptapuṇyaskandhādhipatyasampad :
body.translated_text: 4. The excellence of the mastery over the heap of merit that has been attained (<s>prāptapuṇyaskandhādhipatya</s>):

body.text: yadi nāsti traikālikaṃ cittaṃ tadā puṇyaskandho 'pi na syāt, cittāśritatvāttasya | tataḥ tathāgatasya puṇyaskandhādhipatyasampadaṃ sampādayituṃ kathaṃ bodhisattvo yatnaṃ kūryāditi vicintya puṇyaskandhādhipatyasampadamadhikṛtya- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | anena kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā yo 'ntaśo ratnādikaṃ bāhyavastu tyajati, so 'pi (yadi) mahāpuṇyaskandhena yukto bhavati (tadā) kathaṃ na tathāgatasya asaṃkhyeyāprameyakalpeṣu duṣkarānekaśatānyabhyasyataḥ puṇyaskandhādhipatyaṃ syādityevaṃ deśitam |
body.translated_text: If the mind of the three times does not exist, then the heap of merit (<s>puṇyaskandha</s>) also would not exist, since it depends upon the mind. Then, reflecting on how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should make effort to accomplish the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s excellence of mastery over the heap of merit, [he discusses] the heap of merit...

body.text: ata eva paramārthato 'satyapi puṇyaskandhe saṃvṛtau sattvād bodhisattvena tatra vaśībhāvaṃ niṣpādayituṃ chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamityādarśitam | anenaudāryamapyuktam | kathaṃ na paramārthataḥ puṇyaskandhasattvaṃ vyavasthāpyata iti vicintya 'bodhisattvenātra kathaṃ pratipattavyam, kathañca cittaṃ pragrahītavyam,'; ityubhayaṃ sandarśiyituṃ sacet subhūte ityādyāha | sacet iti 'yadi'; ityarthaḥ | na tathāgato 'bhāṣiṣyat iti paramārthato 'bhidhānaṃ nācariṣyat | anirdeśe 'pi tathā khyāyata ityabhiprāyaḥ | yathā paramārthataḥ puṇyaskandhasyābhāvastathā prāgvarṇitaḥ | anena tathāgatasya puṇyaskandhādhipatyasampadaṃ pariniṣpādayituṃ prasthitena bodhisattvena paramārthatastadanupalambhena yogasamāpattyā pratipattavyam | paramārthatastadālambanābhiniveśaparihāreṇa (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_196
the mind should be taken hold of — thus both [matters] have been taught, and the profundity has also been stated.

body.translated_text: For this very reason, it has been shown that ultimately, even though the <s>puṇyaskandha</s> (accumulation of merit) exists in conventional [truth], the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide through desire (<s>chanda</s>) and aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) in bringing about mastery over it. By this, the nobility [of the teaching] has also been stated. Reflecting 'how is the non-existence of the <s>puṇyaskandha</s> ultimately established?', in order to demonstrate both [matters] — 'how should the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice here, and how should the mind be taken hold of?' — he says 'if, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth. 'If' means 'supposing that.' 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> would not have spoken' means he would not have engaged in designation ultimately. The intent is that even without [explicit] designation, it is so renowned. How the <s>puṇyaskandha</s> is ultimately non-existent has been described previously. By this, it is taught that the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has set forth to bring about the mastery over the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s accumulation of merit should practice through <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) with the ultimate non-apprehension of that. Ultimately, by abandoning the clinging to that as an object,

body.text: 5. kāyasampad : (a) rūpakāyasampad
body.translated_text: 5. The perfection of the [<s>Tathāgata</s>'s] body (<s>kāyasampad</s>): (a) The perfection of the form body (<s>rūpakāyasampad</s>)

body.text: yadi puṇyaskandho naiva syāt tadā tathāgatānāṃ dvividhā kāyalakṣaṇasampad-anuvyañjanakāyasampad, lakṣaṇakāyasampacca yānuttarapuṇyenābhinirvartayitumiṣyate, sā naiva syāt, kāraṇābhāvāt | tasmāt tathāgatasya dvividhāṃ kāyasampadaṃ pariniṣpādayituṃ kathaṃ bodhisattvairyatno 'nuṣṭheya iti vicintayadbhyastathāgatasya rūpakāyasampadamadhikṛtya- tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: If the <s>puṇyaskandha</s> (accumulation of merit) did not exist at all, then the twofold perfection of the body-marks of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — the perfection of the body of minor marks (<s>anuvyañjanakāyasampad</s>) and the perfection of the body of major marks (<s>lakṣaṇakāyasampad</s>) — which is desired to be brought about by unsurpassed merit, would not exist at all, due to the absence of a cause. Therefore, for those who are reflecting 'how should <s>bodhisattvas</s> make effort to bring about the twofold perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body?', concerning the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body), he says 'what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so forth.

body.text: rūpakāyaḥ ityanuvyañjanakāyarūpeṇa draṣṭavyaḥ | lakṣaṇakāyaḥ paścād vakṣyate gobalivardanyāyena | tato 'yamatrāryasubhūterāśayaḥ- yathā paramārthato 'skandha eva puṇyaskandhastathā rūpakāyo 'pyunutpanna eva | ataḥ paramārthataḥ na rūpakāyapariniṣpattyā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ ityucyate | saṃvṛtau māyānirmitabuddhavad vidyata eva rūpakāyaḥ, tata upapanna eva (tasya) puṇyaskandhādudbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Rūpakāya</s>' (form body) should be understood here in terms of the body of minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>). The body of major marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) will be discussed later, by the principle of the ox and the bull. Then this is the intent of the noble <s>Subhūti</s>: just as the <s>puṇyaskandha</s> is ultimately not an aggregate at all, so too the <s>rūpakāya</s> is utterly unoriginated. Therefore, ultimately the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of the <s>rūpakāya</s> — so it is said. In conventional [truth], however, the <s>rūpakāya</s> does exist, like a magically created <s>Buddha</s>; therefore its arising from the <s>puṇyaskandha</s> is indeed established.

body.text: tasmād bodhisattvena māyānirmitabuddhasya tathāvidharūpādhimuktayā tatpratipattaye chanda-praṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti deśitam | nāpyatra punaruktitā | pūrvamadhimukticaryābhūmau rūpakāyāptikāmatākāle tathāgatapūjāsatkārakāle ca tathāvidho 'bhiniveśaḥ parivarjitaḥ, samprati śuddhādhyāśayabhūmau tathāgatarūpakāyasampadaṃ (
