children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_197

children.text: ) pariniṣpādayituṃ samprasthitasya bodhisattvasya rūpe 'bhiniveśo bhavatīti yāsāṃ prasiddhistāsāṃ pariṣadāṃ durvikalpo nirākṛta ityuktatvāt |
children.translated_text: has clinging to form — the false conceptualization of those well-known assemblies [who think so] has been refuted, as has been stated.

body.translated_text: Therefore, it is taught that the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide through desire (<s>chanda</s>) and aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for attaining [the <s>rūpakāya</s>] through such a conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) in the form of a magically created <s>Buddha</s>. Nor is there any repetition here. Previously, at the stage of conviction-conduct (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), at the time of desire for attaining the <s>rūpakāya</s> and at the time of worship and veneration of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, such clinging was rejected. Now, at the stage of pure superior resolve (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has set forth to bring about the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s>

body.text: evaṃ tarhi tathāgatānāṃ rūpakāyaḥ kasmād deśita iti vicintya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityapṛcchat | na rūpakāyapariniṣpattyā tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ ityanena yojanīyam | nāsau tāvat sidhyati, avapavirūpeṇa paramāṇusañcayarūpeṇa vā rūpasyāsiddhatvād, yathā vicāritaṃ prāk | anena bodhisattvena kathaṃ pratipattavyam, tannirdiṣṭam | tena iti ityaṃ saṃvṛtau bhāvaḥ, na tu śaśaviṣāṇavat sarvathābhāvaḥ | anena cāpavādāntaṃ parihṛtya kathaṃ cittaṃ pragrahītavyam, (iti) etannirdiṣṭam | anena sarvasthānena gāmbhīryaṃ pradarśitam | saṃvṛtau tathāgatasya rūpakāyasampadaṃ niṣpādayituṃ bodhisattvaiḥ karaṇīyānāṃ yatnānāṃ nidarśanena ādāryamapi dīpitam |
body.translated_text: Then, reflecting 'if so, why was the <s>rūpakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> taught?', he asked 'for what reason?' This should be connected with 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of the <s>rūpakāya</s>.' That [<s>rūpakāya</s>] is not established either as a composite form or as an aggregation of atoms, since form is unestablished, as was analyzed previously. By this, how the <s>bodhisattva</s> should practice has been taught. 'By that' — this is existence in conventional [truth], but not absolute non-existence like a hare's horn. By this, having avoided the extreme of nihilism (<s>apavādānta</s>), how the mind should be taken hold of has been taught. By this entire section, the profundity has been demonstrated. Through the illustration of the efforts to be undertaken by <s>bodhisattvas</s> in conventional [truth] to bring about the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>rūpakāya</s>, the nobility [of the teaching] has also been illuminated.

body.text: (ba) lakṣaṇakāyasampad :
body.translated_text: (b) The perfection of the body of marks (<s>lakṣaṇakāyasampad</s>):

body.text: lakṣaṇakāyasampadamadhikṛtya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityadyāha | atra pūrvavat sarvamabhihiatam |
body.translated_text: Concerning the perfection of the body of marks (<s>lakṣaṇakāyasampad</s>), he says 'what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so forth. Here, everything has been stated as before.

body.text: 6. vākasampad :
body.translated_text: 6. The perfection of speech (<s>vāksampad</s>):

body.text: yadi rūpakāyapariniṣpattyāa na tathāgato draṣṭavya iti cet, tadā deśanāpi bhagavatā naiva bhavet, rūpakāyena saṃgṛhītvāt tasyāḥ? ato (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_198

children.text: ) bodhisattavaistathāgatasya vāksampadaṃ niṣpādayituṃ kathaṃ yatnaḥ karttavya iti vicintayadbhyo vāksampadamadhikṛtya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | paramārthato vācya-vācaka-vacanānāmabhāvāt na tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati mayā dharmo deśita iti | anyathā viparyayānna bhavet sarvajñaḥ | yathā vācakāḥ ātmādayaḥ, vācyā bāhyādhyātmikā bhāvāḥ, vacanāni karaṇarūpāṇi śabdasvabhāvābhāvātmakāni vā tathā vistareṇa prāgevoktāni | sarve bhāvāḥ śūnyatvavyāptāḥ prāgeva pratipāditāḥ | saṃvṛtau vācya-vācaka-vacanānām avicāraramaṇīyatvena vyavahāramātra eva (te) bhavanti, na tu paramārthe |
children.translated_text: for those who are reflecting 'how should <s>bodhisattvas</s> make effort to bring about the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s speech?', concerning the perfection of speech (<s>vāksampad</s>), he says 'what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so forth. Because ultimately the expressible (<s>vācya</s>), the expressor (<s>vācaka</s>), and the expression (<s>vacana</s>) do not exist, the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not think thus: 'I have taught the <s>Dharma</s>.' Otherwise, through being the contrary, he would not be omniscient. Just as the expressors — self and the like — [are unestablished], [and] the expressible — the external and internal entities — [are unestablished], [and] the expressions — which are of the nature of instruments and are constituted by the non-existence of the nature of sound — have been extensively stated before. All entities are pervaded by emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), as has been established previously. In conventional [truth], the expressible, the expressor, and the expression exist merely as convention due to being charming when unexamined — but not ultimately.

body.translated_text: If the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen through the perfection of the <s>rūpakāya</s>, then neither would the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching exist, since it is encompassed by the <s>rūpakāya</s>. Therefore,

body.text: yadi vastutattvasyaivamabhidhāne 'pi vyāmohena kicit paramārthatastrayāṇāṃ (teṣāṃ) parāmārthasattvaṃ kalpayeyastadā 'kiṃ nu syāt'; iti vicintya yaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | abhyācakṣīta ityabhyālapet | kathaṃ tadabhūtamālapituṃ śakyata iti vicāraṇāyāmāha asatodgṛhītena iti | viparītābhiniveśato vitathagrahaṇāt tadabhūtamityarthaḥ | anena tathāgatasya vāksampadi pravṛttena bodhisattvena pratiśrutkādivajjñātvā pravartitavyamiti, bodhisattvena kathaṃ sthātavyamiti deśitam |
body.translated_text: If, despite the reality of things having been thus declared, someone through delusion were to construct the ultimate existence of those three [expressible, expressor, expression], then — reflecting 'would that be so?' — he says 'whoever, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth. 'Would claim' means 'would assert.' When the investigation is made as to how that which is untrue can be asserted, he says 'by grasping what is non-existent.' Because of perverted clinging, because of false apprehension, that is untrue — this is the meaning. By this, it is taught that the <s>bodhisattva</s> engaged in [bringing about] the perfection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s speech should proceed knowing [it to be] like an echo and the like — and how the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide has been taught.

body.text: yadi vacanāditrayamasat (tadā) pudgaladharmanairātmyadeśakena bhagavatā nānāpadavākyātmikeyaṃ dharmadeśanā kathaṃ prasidhyati? tasyāṃ satyāṃ tadabhidheyo vācyo 'pi syādeva, yaśca taddeśako vācakaḥ, so 'pi bhavedeva | tadbalena trīṇyapi (vācya-vācaka-vacanāni) bhaveyuriti cintāyāṃ tatkasya hetoḥ? iti pṛṣṭam | atra dharmadeśanā ityudatarat |
body.translated_text: If the triad of expression and the like is non-existent, [then] how does this <s>dharmadeśanā</s> (Dharma-teaching) — consisting of various words and sentences — which was taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> who expounds the non-self of persons and <s>dharmas</s> (<s>pudgaladharmanairātmya</s>), come to be established? If that [teaching] exists, then its expressible content (<s>vācya</s>) would also have to exist, and the one who teaches it, the expressor (<s>vācaka</s>), would also have to exist. By the force of that, all three — the expressible, the expressor, and the expression — would exist. When this reflection arises, 'for what reason?' is asked. Here, '<s>dharmadeśanā</s>' (Dharma-teaching) is the answer.

body.text: ayamabhiprāyaḥ- paramārthataḥ dharmadeśanāyāṃ satyāṃ (sā) svalakṣaṇasvabhāvā vā syāt sāmānyalakṣanasvabhāvā vā | tatra na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ, sarvaṃ pāramārthikaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ tāvat pūrvameva vistareṇa nirākṛtam | na ca dbitīyo 'pi (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_199

children.text: ) asati svalakṣaṇe ādhārasyābhāvena kasyacidapyasattvāt | sāmānyadravyatvābhyupagame svalakṣaṇa eva saṅgṛhītaṃ syāditi tanniṣedhena tasyāpi niṣedha eva | anyavyāvṛttyā sāmānyalakṣaṇamadhyāropitasvabhāvamiti parikalpite sati dharmadeśanāyā nairarthakyatvena siddhasādhanam |
children.translated_text: because in the absence of particular characteristics, due to the non-existence of a substrate, nothing whatsoever exists. If the existence of a general substance (<s>sāmānyadravya</s>) were accepted, it would be included in the particular characteristics themselves; therefore, by the negation of those [particular characteristics], that [general substance] too is negated. If [one supposes that] through exclusion of others (<s>anyavyāvṛtti</s>), the general characteristic is of a superimposed nature — then since the <s>dharmadeśanā</s> would become purposeless, [the argument] proves what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

body.translated_text: The intent is this: if the <s>dharmadeśanā</s> (Dharma-teaching) were to exist ultimately, it would either be of the nature of particular characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) or of the nature of general characteristics (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>). The first position is not [tenable], since all ultimate particular characteristics have already been extensively refuted previously. Nor is the second,

body.text: tasyāḥ (śabdātmikāyā deśanāyāḥ) paramārthataḥ svalakṣaṇasattve 'pi na yujyate tayā dharmadeśanā | sphoṭādiśabdasya nityasvabhāvasya paraiḥ padatvena parikalpitasya kramākramābhyāmarthakriyākāritvaṃ tāvad virudhyate, sarvasāamarthyāpagatatvāccaitanyādiṣu kutrāpi khalu naiva yujyate, akiñcitkaratvena kathaṃ tad bhavet padam? anityasyāpi tāvat svalakṣaṇasva na yujyate padatvam, saṅketakāle dṛṣṭasya vyavahārakāle 'nanvayāt | na hi yujyate anyasya saṅketo 'nyasya ca vyavahāraḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | ata eva svalakṣaṇamapyabhidhātuṃ na yujyate, ananvayāt | sāmānyapadārthe 'bhidheyatvenābhyupagate sati abhidheyasvabhāvatvena tasya svalakṣaṇasvarūpatvānna hi pradeśāntaragamanam |
body.translated_text: Even if the particular characteristic of that [teaching], being of the nature of words, were to exist ultimately, the <s>dharmadeśanā</s> (Dharma-teaching) through that is still not possible. For the <s>sphoṭa</s> (meaning-bearing phoneme) and other [conceptions of] sound, which are of an eternal nature and conceived by others as having the status of words — their capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), whether successive or simultaneous, is contradicted, since they are devoid of all capacity. Indeed, in [entities such as] consciousness and the like, [such eternal sound] is in no way appropriate anywhere. Since it accomplishes nothing, how could that be a word? Even for that which is impermanent, the status of wordhood is not appropriate for its particular characteristic, because what was perceived at the time of convention is not continuous with [what exists at] the time of ordinary usage. For it is not appropriate that the convention pertains to one [thing] and the usage to another, due to overextension. For this very reason, the particular characteristic too cannot be expressed, due to non-continuity. If a general word-meaning were accepted as the expressible, then since that would be of the nature of particular characteristics by being the nature of the expressible, there would be no going to another [referent].

body.text: ekatvaṃ tu deśakālādibhinnāsvanekavyaktiṣvanugatamapi na yujyate tathā hi- (atha) ekasyāṃ vyaktau sarvātmanā vyāptaṃ syāt tadā yena ekatvena parikalpitaḥ sa svabhāvastena anyatrādhigatetaravyaktibhiḥ sambaddhaḥ taditarasvabhāvastatra na bhavediti, ekatvahāniprasaṅgāt | (atha) ekadeśena vyāptaṃ syāt tadā sāvayatvāgrahaṇadoṣaḥ | evaṃ yāvatyo bhinnavyaktayastāsāmekadeśena vyāptivyavasthayā tāvatīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ syāttadā ekavyaktigrahaṇaṃ tāvadekadeśagrahaṇena yuktaṃ bhavet, bhinnavyaktiṣu deśakālaparimāṇādibhinnāsu tāsvekavyaktigrahaṇaṃ tāvadekadeśagrahaṇād yugapudgrahaṇābhāva eva | tasmād vācya-vācakatvaṃ tāvadaśyāropeṇaiva yujyate, na tattvataḥ | ata evoktaṃ bhagavatānyatra-
body.translated_text: Oneness, however, even though it pervades many instances that are distinct in place, time, and the like, is not tenable. For thus: if it were completely pervaded in a single instance, then the nature imagined as oneness, being connected with other instances apprehended elsewhere, would not be the nature of those others—and the absurd consequence of the loss of oneness would follow. If it were pervaded only in part, then there would be the fault of grasping [the universal] as having parts. Thus, as many distinct instances as there are, by establishing pervasion in one part of each, there would be the grasping of that many [parts]; then the grasping of a single instance would be justified only through the grasping of one part, but in distinct instances that differ in place, time, measure, and the like, the grasping of even a single instance through the grasping of one part would simply be the absence of simultaneous grasping. Therefore, the relationship of signifier and signified (<s>vācya-vācakatva</s>) is justified only through superimposition (<s>adhyāropa</s>), not in reality. For this very reason, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said elsewhere:

body.text: yena yena hi nāmnā vai yo yo dharmo 'bhilapyate |

children.text: na sa saṃvidyate tatra dharmāṇāṃ sā hi dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: That [<s>dharma</s>] is not found therein—for such is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of <s>dharmas</s>."

body.translated_text: "By whatever name whatsoever any <s>dharma</s> is expressed,

body.text: vacanaṃ mithyā, vācya-vācyakānāṃ yā deśanā taddvārā āgatā, sāpi spaṣṭaiva | ubhayorabhāvo bhagavatā pṛthakatvena noktaḥ | anena bodhisattvena kathaṃ pratipattavyam, kathañca cittaṃ pragrahītavyamityetad darśitam | etena sarveṇa gāmbhīryaṃ darśitam |
body.translated_text: Speech is false; the teaching that has come through the medium of the signified and the signifier—that too is clearly [false]. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has not stated the non-existence of both separately. By this, how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should practice and how the mind should be taken hold of has been shown. By all of this, profundity has been demonstrated.

body.text:
7. saptadhā cittasampadaḥ-
1. smṛtyupasthānam
2. abhisambodhiḥ
3. mahādharmārthaprajñaptiḥ
4. mahāvavādārthaprajñaptiḥ
5. dharmakāyaparigrahaṇam
6. saṃsāre nirvāṇe cāpratiṣṭhānam
7. prasthiti-pāriśuddhiḥ |
body.translated_text:
7. The sevenfold excellences of the mind (<s>cittasampad</s>):
1. Establishing mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)
2. Full awakening (<s>abhisambodhi</s>)
3. Designation of the great <s>Dharma</s>-meaning (<s>mahādharmārthaprajñapti</s>)
4. Designation of the great instruction-meaning (<s>mahāvavādārthaprajñapti</s>)
5. Grasping of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (<s>dharmakāyaparigrahaṇa</s>)
6. Non-establishment in <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>
7. Purification of the setting-forth (<s>prasthitipāriśuddhi</s>)

body.text: 1. smṛtyupasthānam :
body.translated_text: 1. Establishing mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>):

body.text: tatredānīmevaṃ gambhīradharmo 'yamanāgate kāle ghanībhūte kudṛṣṭijāle kathaṃ saphalo bhaviṣyatīti nābhiśraddhadhanti parivārāḥ | ya evaṃ cintayanti teṣāmaviśrambhaṃ nivārayitum āryasubhūtiścittasampatsu smṛtyupasthānamadhikṛtya bhagavan ityādyāha | bhagavatāpyanāgate 'dhvani śīlavanto guṇavantaśca bhaviṣyantīti kiṃ noktapūrvam | samprati teṣāṃ sattve 'sattve vā ekāntenānabhiniveśaṃ deśayitum asti iti noktam, antadvayaniṣedhārthaṃ te subhūte ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: Now, the attendants do not have faith that this profound <s>Dharma</s>, in a future time when the thicket of wrong views has become dense, will be fruitful. For those who think thus, in order to remove their lack of confidence, the noble <s>Subhūti</s>, addressing the establishing of mindfulness among the excellences of mind, says "<s>Bhagavān</s>" and so forth. Has the <s>Bhagavān</s> not already stated that in the future there will be those who are virtuous and endowed with qualities? Now, in order to teach that one should have no one-sided attachment regarding their existence or non-existence, he does not say "they exist," but rather, for the purpose of negating both extremes, he says "Those, <s>Subhūti</s>" and so forth.

body.text: paramārthataḥ skandhapudgalādīnāṃ satsvabhāvānupalambhāt na sattvāḥ ityanenādhyāropāntaniṣedhaḥ, avicāraikaramaṇīyatvena sadaiva vidyamānatvena nāsattvāḥ ityanenāpavādāntaniṣedhaḥ | bhaviṣyanti ityanayā deśanayā bhagavataḥ kīdṛgaviparītasmṛtyupasthānamiti sattvebhyo darśayitvā bhagavatastasyāṃ smṛtyupasthānasampadi bodhisattvena chanda-praṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti nirdiṣṭam | na te sattvāḥ nāsattvāḥ? ityanena yogasamāpattinirdiṣṭā |
body.translated_text: "They are not beings"—because ultimately the intrinsic nature of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>pudgala</s> (person), and the like is not apprehended; by this, the extreme of superimposition (<s>adhyāropa</s>) is negated. "They are not non-beings"—because they always exist in the manner of being delightful without analysis; by this, the extreme of nihilism (<s>apavāda</s>) is negated. "They will exist"—by this teaching, having shown to beings what kind of non-inverted mindfulness-establishing the <s>Bhagavān</s> has, it is indicated that a <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s excellence of establishing mindfulness through aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and resolve (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). "They are neither beings nor non-beings"—by this, <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) is indicated.

body.text: yadi na te sattvāḥ syustadā kathaṃ bhagavatā 'bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani śīlavanto guṇavantaśca te'; ityādyuktamityevaṃ parivitarkaṃ vicāryaṃ tatkasya hetoḥ? ityapṛcchat | asattvāste bhāṣitāḥ iti paramārthato 'sattvā eva, saṃvṛtisatskandhasadbhāvamāśritya bhāṣitāste | saṃvṛtau sattvāt tenocyante sattvā iti | anyathā saṃvṛtāvapyasattve na (te) bhāṣitāḥ syurityanena cittapragraho darśitaḥ | sarveṇa tāvadanena gāmbhīryamuktam | sarvasattvebhyo bhagavatāpratihatasmṛtyupasthānadeśanāt tāvadaudāryaṃ nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: If they were not beings, then how did the <s>Bhagavān</s> say "There will exist in the future those who are virtuous and endowed with qualities"?—reflecting thus and investigating, he asked "For what reason?" "They are spoken of as non-beings" means: they are ultimately non-beings indeed; they are spoken of in dependence on the existence of the <s>skandhas</s> in conventional [truth]. Since they exist conventionally, therefore they are called "beings." Otherwise, if they did not exist even conventionally, they would not have been spoken of—by this, the uplift of the mind (<s>cittapragraha</s>) is shown. By all of this, profundity has been stated. Through the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s unobstructed teaching of establishing mindfulness for all beings, vastness has been indicated.

body.text: 2. abhisambodhiḥ
body.translated_text: 2. Full awakening (<s>abhisambodhi</s>)

body.text: yadi na syād bhagavataḥ kācidapi dharmadeśanā, tadā na syāt (saḥ) samyaksambuddho 'pi tatastathāgatābhisambodhisiddhaye vyarthaḥ syād bodhisattvānāṃ yatnaḥ | yato 'bhisambuddhadharmā iṣyante, ato deśanāpi bhavatīti manvānebhyaḥ (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 202]

children.text: ) tebhyo 'bhisambodhim adhikṛtya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | āryasubhūtiḥ pūrvābhiprāyaṃ gṛhītvā nāsti saḥ ityudatarat | tadevaṃ manyate- paramārthābhiprāyeṇa bhagavatā dharmadeśanā pratiṣiddheti | yathā paramārthataḥ kasyāścidapi dharmadeśanāyā abhāvaḥ (tathā) abhisambuddhasyāpyabhāvaḥ, etat pūrvaṃ nirdiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: To them, addressing full awakening, he says "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?" and so forth. The noble <s>Subhūti</s>, having grasped the previous intent, answered "There is not that [<s>dharma</s>]." He thinks thus: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> has negated <s>Dharma</s>-teaching with the ultimate intent." Just as there is no <s>Dharma</s>-teaching whatsoever ultimately, so too there is no [one who has] fully awakened—this was previously indicated.

body.translated_text: If there were no <s>Dharma</s>-teaching whatsoever by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, then he would not be a perfectly awakened one (<s>samyaksambuddha</s>) either; and then the effort of <s>bodhisattvas</s> for the accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s full awakening would be pointless. For those who think "Since it is accepted that <s>dharmas</s> are fully awakened to, therefore teaching also exists,"

body.text: saṃvṛtitaḥ bhagavato dharmadeśanā, sambodhiḥ, taddhetupratipattiścāpi vidyanta eva, tasmād bodhisattvenānuttarasamyaksambodhestathyasaṃvṛtisvabhāvāyāḥ sādhanārthaṃ yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | anena bodhisattvena kathaṃ sthātavyamiti darśitam | pūrvamavavādaparyeṣaṇakāle bodhisattvānā 'abhisambodhi paramārthaḥ'; iti yo vikalpaḥ, sa apanoditaḥ, idānīṃ buddhabhūmiparyeṣaṇakāle pareṣāṃ tādṛgvikalpanirākaraṇānna bhavati punaruktidoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Conventionally, however, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, his full awakening, and the practice that is its cause do indeed exist. Therefore, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should make effort for the accomplishment of the unsurpassed perfect awakening, which is of the nature of authentic conventional truth (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>). By this, how a <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide has been shown. Previously, at the time of seeking instruction, the conceptual construction of <s>bodhisattvas</s> that "awakening is the ultimate" was removed; now, at the time of seeking the <s>Buddha</s>-ground, since others' similar conceptual constructions are refuted, there is no fault of repetition.

body.text: bhagavatā anuttarā samyaksambodhistathyasaṃvṛtau vyavasthāpitā, sā kīdṛśīti atra aṇurapi ityādyāha | yatra jñānaṃ pracarati (tatra) bhagavatā grāhyasvarūpasya svalakṣaṇasya sūkṣmo 'pi dharmasvabhāvo nopalabdhaḥ, sa tāvat samastadharmanairātmyāvabodhasvarūpā anuttarā sampaksambodhiḥ | tairthika-śaikṣāśaikṣajñānācchreṣṭhatvena 'anuttarā | sarvabhāvānāṃ tathatāyā yathāvadadhigamasvabhāvatvena ucyate samyaksambodhirityarthaḥ | tatra sarvadharmāṇāmanupalabdhiheto "na" ityuktam | yato hyasattvaṃ tato 'nupalambhaḥ | vidyamānatve nānupalabdhiḥ, satsu sarvadharmeṣu tathāgatasya ālambanajñānasyaiva jñāpakatvāt | anena dharmanairātmyāvabodhasvabhāvo nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has established the unsurpassed perfect awakening in authentic conventional [truth]—what is it like? To this, he says "even an atom" and so forth. Where knowledge operates, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has not apprehended even a subtle <s>dharma</s>-nature of the own-characteristic of what is to be grasped. That, then, is the unsurpassed perfect awakening, whose nature is the comprehension of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. "Unsurpassed" (<s>anuttarā</s>) because it is superior to the knowledge of <s>tīrthikas</s>, learners, and non-learners. It is called "perfectly full awakening" (<s>samyaksambodhiḥ</s>) because its nature is the realization of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all entities as they truly are. Among these, because of the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, "not" is said. For since [<s>dharmas</s>] are non-existent, there is non-apprehension. If they existed, there would not be non-apprehension, since when all <s>dharmas</s> exist, it would merely indicate the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s object-cognition. By this, the nature of the comprehension of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> has been indicated.

body.text: sāmprataṃ pudgalanairātmyāvabodhasvabhāvaṃ pratipādayituṃ api tu khalu punaḥ sūbhūte ityādyāha | samāḥ sa dharmaḥ iti tadavabodhiteṣu sarvadharmeṣu pudgalanairātmyasāmyāt | na tatra kiñcidviṣamam iti sarvatra tadaviparyayāt, ātmagrāhahetorbhāvābhiniveśasya prahīṇatvāt | bhagavatā tāvadātmagrāhaḥ savāsanaḥ prahīṇaḥ | tena saiva pudgalanairātmyajñānasvabhāvā sambodhiḥ, anuttarā samyaksambodhirityucyate, nānyā | kena rūpeṇa samaḥ sa dharma ityatra niḥsattvatvena ityādyāha | anena sarveṇa kathaṃ yogasamāpattyā pratipattavyamiti tannirdiṣṭam | sā kathamabhisambuddhyata ityāha kuśalairdharmaiḥ iti | sā puṇyajñānasambhārātmakaiḥ kuśalairdharmairabhisambuddhyata ityarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, in order to establish the nature of the comprehension of the selflessness of persons, he says "But moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>" and so forth. "That <s>dharma</s> is equal" means: because of the equality of the selflessness of persons among all <s>dharmas</s> that have been comprehended through that [awakening]. "There is nothing unequal therein" means: because of the absence of its opposite everywhere; because the attachment to [real] entities (<s>bhāvābhiniveśa</s>), which is the cause of grasping at self, has been abandoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has indeed abandoned the grasping at self together with its latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). Therefore, that very [awakening], whose nature is the knowledge of the selflessness of persons, is called the unsurpassed perfect awakening—and no other. "In what form is that <s>dharma</s> equal?"—to this, he says "through being without a self" and so forth. By all of this, how one should practice through <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) has been indicated. "How is it fully awakened to?" he says: "through wholesome <s>dharmas</s>." The meaning is: it is fully awakened to through wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have the nature of the accumulations of merit and knowledge.

body.text: yadyasattvād aṇurapi dharmo nopalabhyeta, kathaṃ nāma bhaveyuḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ? yatastairabhisambuddhyate 'taḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ ityādyāha | paramārthāstu ardhamā eva | saṃvṛtau sattvāt kuśalā dharmāḥ ityuktam | tasmāt kuśalerdharmairabhisambudhyata ityatra nāsti doṣaḥ | anena adhyāropāpavādāntagrāhavikṣepanirākaraṇena cittapragraho nirdiṣṭaḥ | etaiḥ sarvaḥ sthānaiḥ gāmbhīryamapi sandarśitam | aśeṣapudgaladharmanairātmyāvabodharūpasya samyaksambodhisvabhāvasya paridīpanena audāryamapi darśitam |
body.translated_text: If, because of non-existence, not even an atom of <s>dharma</s> is apprehended, how could there be wholesome <s>dharmas</s>? Since it is fully awakened to through them, he says "wholesome <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth. But ultimately, they are equal [i.e., essenceless]. Since they exist conventionally, it is said "wholesome <s>dharmas</s>." Therefore, there is no fault in saying "it is fully awakened to through wholesome <s>dharmas</s>." By this, through the refutation of the distraction of grasping at the extremes of superimposition and nihilism, the uplift of the mind has been indicated. Through all these stations, profundity too has been demonstrated. Through the illumination of the nature of the perfect awakening as the comprehension of the selflessness of both persons and <s>dharmas</s> without remainder, vastness too has been shown.

body.text: 3. mahādharmārthaprajñaptiḥ
body.translated_text: 3. Designation of the great <s>Dharma</s>-meaning (<s>mahādharmārthaprajñapti</s>)

body.text: bhagavataḥ sā samyaksambodhiḥ kathaṃ veditvayā? iti vicāryamāṇe mahārthadharmatayā prajñāpitatvena tatsattāṃ darśayituṃ yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 204]

children.text: ) ityādyāha | sumeravaḥ parvatarājānaḥ ityupalakṣaṇam | anantalokadhātūn ratnaiḥ paripūrya dānena yat puṇyaṃ tadapi upamāṃ naiva kṣamate | itaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ ityupalakṣaṇamātraparidīpanena sakalo mahāyānadharmaḥ parilakṣito bhavati | yāvad iti vacanena sahasratamī kalā- 'śatasahasratamī kalā .......... upamā-aupamyamityetāni'; saṃgṛhyante | evaṃ mahārthadharmaprajñapanena hetunā bhagavataścittasampadaḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ ānuttaryamavagamyate, tathāvidhasamyaksaṃbodhim antarā tathāvidhadharmadeśanāyā aśakyatvāt |
children.translated_text: and so forth, he says. '<s>Sumerus</s>, kings of mountains' is merely an illustrative term. The merit that would result from filling infinite world-realms with precious substances and giving them — even that does not suffice as a comparison. By the illustrative indication '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' alone, the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s> is encompassed. By the expression 'to the extent that' — 'not even a thousandth part... not even a hundred-thousandth part...'

body.translated_text: When examining "How is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s perfect awakening to be known?"—in order to show its existence through its having been designated by means of the <s>Dharma</s> of great meaning, "And moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>"

body.text:
tasmādetādṛkcittasampatsampādane chanda-praṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyam | sakalenānena kathaṃ sthātavyaṃ bodhisattveneti nirdiśyate, anenaivaudāryamapyabhihitam | sā ca sambodhiḥ tathyasaṃvṛtisvabhāvā draṣṭavyā, na tu paramārthataḥ, prāgevoktatvāt, sākṣādanuktamapi sāmarthyataḥ yogasamāpattiḥ, cittapragrahaḥ gāmbhīryaṃ ca nirdiṣṭam |
4. mahāvavādārthaprajñapti :
bhagavato lokottarajñānāvasthāyāṃ sattvasaṃjñā sarvathā na pravartate, atyantasamāhitatvāt, ado nāścaryam | sattvebhyo vimuktayupadeśakāle 'samāhitāvasthāyāṃ viśuddhalaukikajñānāvasthāyāmapi sattvādisaṃjñā na pravartata iti tannirdiśya avavādamahārthatvena prajñaptihetunā bhagavato 'nuttaracittasampadaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_205

children.text: ) pratipatsyamānāṃ darśayituṃ mahārthāvavādamadhikṛtya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | praśnasyottaramapratīkṣamāṇaḥ sapadi svataḥ na khalu punaḥ subhūte, evaṃ draṣṭavyam ityādyāha | tasmād bhagavataścittasampadastādṛśe mahārthāvavādahetau bodhisattvena chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti nirdiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: In order to show what [the <s>bodhisattva</s>] is to practice, addressing the teaching of great significance, he says: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so forth. Without waiting for the answer to the question, he immediately says on his own: 'Not so, <s>Subhūti</s>, it should not be regarded thus' and so forth. Therefore, it is indicated that the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide in aspiration and vow because of the cause of such a teaching of great significance from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s excellence of mind.

body.translated_text: Therefore, one should abide in aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for the accomplishment of such excellence of mind. By all of this, how the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide is indicated; by this same [passage], the magnanimity (<s>audārya</s>) is also expressed. And that perfect awakening (<s>sambodhi</s>) should be regarded as being of the nature of correct conventional [truth], not ultimately — since this has been stated previously. Although not stated directly, by implication [there is] yogic concentration, mental composure,

body.text: kiṃ sattvānāṃ sattve 'pi saṃkleśahetubhūtatayā tathā nābhipreyate tathāgatena? āhosvit sattvābhāvāditi cintayatāmāśayaṃ vijñāya tatkasya hetoḥ? iti papraccha | skandhātmakasya pudgalātmakasya ca kasyacit sattvasya paramārthato 'bhāvād evaṃ nopalabhyata iti darśayitumāha- nāstiṃ kaścit sattvo yastathāgatena parimocittaḥ iti | anena bodhisattvaiḥ kathamatra yogasamāpattyā pratipattavyamiti tannirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Does the <s>Tathāgata</s> not intend it thus because sentient beings, even in their existence, are causes of affliction? Or is it because sentient beings do not exist? — knowing the intention of those who reflect thus, he asked: 'For what reason?' Since no sentient being whatsoever — whether constituted by the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) or by a personal self (<s>pudgala</s>) — exists ultimately, in order to show that [a sentient being] is not apprehended thus, he says: 'There is no sentient being who [is so apprehended by] the <s>Tathāgata</s>...'

body.text: abhāvaḥ kathaṃ jñātavya ityatra yadi punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | ayamatrābhiprāyaḥ yathājñeyaṃ tathāgatasya jñānaṃ pravartate, anyathā aprahīṇāvaraṇatvena kathaṃ syāt tathāgatatvam | tasmād yadi sattvaḥ syāt tadā sandṛśyeta sa tathāgatena, ātmanaḥ pratyakṣopalabdhatayā viciakitsābhāvāt | sa eva tāvattasya pragāḍhaḥ ātmagrāhaḥ syāt | tataśca ātmagrāhahetutaḥ samutpannaṃ nikhilakleśajālabandhanamapyatidṛḍhaṃ syāt tadā rāgādyatipragāḍhabaddhasya āvaraṇāprahāṇena bhagavataḥ tathāgatapadaprāptirna syāt | bhagavatā ca tatpadaṃ prāptam, ataḥ prahīṇasakalāvaraṇaḥ saḥ | prahīṇāvaraṇayā aśeṣa ātmagrāhaśikharī viśīryate, tasmāt sattvābhāvo na jñāyate |
body.translated_text: Regarding 'How is non-existence to be known?', he says: 'If again, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth. The intent here is: the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge operates in accordance with what is to be known; otherwise, how could there be <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood if the obscurations were not abandoned? Therefore, if a sentient being existed, then it would be perceived by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, because of the absence of doubt due to the direct perception of the self. That very [being]

body.text: ātmanyasati kimātmadṛṣṭilakṣaṇa ātmagrāho na bhavati? kimarthaṃ bhagavatā ātmādisaṃjñā nocyate? ityatra ātmagrāha iti subhūte ityādyāha | yadi (bhagavatā) ātmādivastuna eva grahaṇaṃ syāttadā prahīṇāvaraṇasya tasya bhagavata (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_206

children.text: ) ātmagrāhaḥ samudbhavet, kasyāpyātmagrāhasyābhāvāt agrāha eṣa tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: self-grasping would arise. Since there is no self-grasping whatsoever, it is declared by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be 'non-grasping.'

body.translated_text: If the self does not exist, does not the self-grasping characterized by the view of self arise? For what reason does the <s>Bhagavān</s> not speak of perceptions such as self and the like? — regarding this, he says: 'Self-grasping, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth. If the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s grasping were indeed of the entity of self and the like, then for that <s>Bhagavān</s> whose obscurations have been abandoned,

body.text: atha kīdṛśa ātmagrāha iti? sa ca ityādyāha | śravaṇādivirahād heyopādeyayoranabhijñatvād bālāḥ, prekṣāvattvaviyogād āaryebhyaḥ pṛthaktvācca pṛthagjanāḥ | pṛthagjanā api kecit sacchāstraṃ śrutvā yoniśomanaskārasthitāḥ dharmanairātmyādhimuktāḥ satyamabhiniviśante, tadanātmagrāhavyavacchedato bālā ityāha | bālamātrakathanāt skandhādyabhijñā api tādṛśāḥ pṛthagjanā anupajātāryamārgatayā bālā eva | bālānāṃ vaiśiṣṭayamabhidhātuṃ vyāvṛtte 'pyātmagrāhe bālatvena teṣvātmagrāha ityavabhāsate, tasmāttadāśayavaśād ātmagrāha ityevaṃ nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Then, what kind of self-grasping [is it]? He says: 'And that...' and so forth. 'Childish ones' (<s>bāla</s>) — because of being devoid of hearing [the <s>Dharma</s>] and so forth, and because of not knowing what is to be abandoned and what is to be taken up. 'Ordinary persons' (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) — because of being separated from discernment, and because of being different from the noble ones (<s>ārya</s>). Even some ordinary persons, having heard the true teaching, and being established in proper mental attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>), convinced of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, grasp at the truth [of non-self]. To exclude their non-self-grasping, [the term] 'childish' is used.

body.text: na tanmātreṇa satyam, atiprasaṅgāt | anātmaśabdaprayogeṇāpi kathaṃ nātmādīnāṃ satyagrahaṇam, yadyātmā na syāttadā ke tāvat pṛthagjanā abhidhīyeran? iti vicintya bālapṛthagjanāḥ ityādyuktam | paramārthatastu ajanā eva, saṃvṛtimāśrityoktatvānna doṣaḥ | ebhiḥ sarvairadhyāropāpavādāntanirākaraṇena cittapragṛhīttatvaṃ darśitam | anena sarveṇa tāvat sākṣād gāmbhīryaṃ proktam | aśeṣasattvadhātubhyo mahārthāvavadaprajñapterhetutvadarśanena cittasampada ādauryamapi nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: It is not true merely by that much, because of overextension. Even with the usage of the word 'non-self,' how is there not a grasping at the truth of self and the like? If the self did not exist, then who would be called 'ordinary persons'? — reflecting thus, the words 'childish ordinary persons' and so forth are spoken. Ultimately, however, they are indeed unborn (<s>aja</s>); since [the designation] is stated in reliance on the conventional, there is no fault. By all of these [statements], through the refutation of both superimposition and denial, the mind

body.text: 5. dharmakāyaparigrahaṇam :
body.translated_text: 5. Appropriation of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body):

body.text: yadi bālapṛthagjanāḥ na syuḥ, kathaṃ tathāgatasya lakṣaṇānuvyañjanairalaṅkṛtāḥ kāyasampadaḥ sambhaveyuḥ? pṛthagjanāḥ svakaruṇāmūlakabodhicittamutpādya pāramitāsu prayatante (tataśca) lakṣaṇādibhīralaṅkṛtāstathāgatakāyasampattivanto bhavanti, tadabhāve mūlabhāvāt kathaṃ bhaveyuḥ tādṛyastathāgatakāyasampada iti? ye pāriṣadyāḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_207

children.text: ) kṛtānalpavikalpāḥ rūpādiṣu bhāvābhiniveśenaivaṃ cintayanti, tebhyo dharmakāyaparigrahamadhikṛtya tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | pūrvaṃ dharmakāyatayā na vyavasthāpitam, idānīṃ dharmakāyaṃ vyavasthāpayitumuktatvānna punaruktidoṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: [come about]? Those who make manifold conceptual constructions, with attachment to the existence of forms and the like, think thus — to them, regarding the appropriation of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, he says: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so forth. Previously it was not established as the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; now, since [the topic] is stated in order to establish the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, there is no fault of repetition.

body.translated_text: If childish ordinary persons did not exist, how would the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body-excellences, adorned with the [thirty-two] marks and [eighty] secondary marks, come about? [For] ordinary persons, generating the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) rooted in their own compassion, strive in the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), and [thereby] become adorned with the marks and the like, possessing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body-excellence. In their absence, since that would be the absence of the root, how would such <s>Tathāgata</s>-body[-excellences]

body.text: lakṣaṇasampadā tāvat paramārthavicāraṇāyāmavayavinaḥ paramāṇusaṃghātasya vā svabhāvenānupapattiṃ viditvā pūrvakamevābhiprāyaṃ gṛhṇan subhūtirāha no hīdam | evameva upapattyantaraṃ bhagavatā sacet punaḥ subhūte ityādinoktam |
body.translated_text: Regarding the excellence of marks, upon examining them from the standpoint of ultimate truth — knowing the impossibility by nature of a composite whole or an aggregate of atoms — <s>Subhūti</s>, grasping the very same intent as before, says: 'No, indeed not.' In the same manner, an alternative reasoning is stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the words: 'If again, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so forth.

body.text: yadi tathāgato lakṣaṇasampanmātreṇa prabhāvitaḥ syāt tadā vakṣyamāṇahetunā tulyatvād rājāpi cakravartī kathaṃ na bhavet tathāgataḥ? nanu sthānasthottaptapūrṇatvena viśiṣṭā bhagavato lakṣaṇasampad, na tu cakravartinaḥ, tataḥ sa nocyate tathāgata ityapi na yujyate, sthānasthādiviśeṣasyāpi jaḍasvabhāvatve nāsti kaścid viśeṣaḥ | tena yadi tathāgato jaḍasvabhāvairlakṣaṇādidharmaiḥ prabhāvito 'bhaviṣyat tadā cakravartī api tathāgato 'bhaviṣyat iti cet? na, tasmāttathāgastāvad aśeṣavastusvabhāvasya yathāvadadhigamamātreṇa prabhāvita ityabhiprāyaḥ | anena tathāvidhaṃ jñānahetukaṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ prati bodhisattvena chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: If the <s>Tathāgata</s> were realized merely through the perfection of marks, then — because of being equally [endowed with marks] by the reason to be stated — how would a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) not also be a <s>Tathāgata</s>? If [one objects:] 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s perfection of marks is distinguished by being situated in the [proper] place, heated [by practice], and complete, but not that of a <s>Cakravartin</s>; therefore he is not called a <s>Tathāgata</s>' — this is also untenable, since the distinction of place and the like is also of an insentient nature.

body.text: adhunā paramārthatastattathāgatajñāne 'pi nābhiniveṣṭavyamiti darśayituṃ dharmakāyo (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_208

children.text: ) vyavasthāpyate | bodhisattvena kathaṃ yogasamāpattyā pratipattavyamiti dvābhyāṃ gāthābhyāṃ pradarśyate |
children.translated_text: is established. How the <s>bodhisattva</s> should practice through yogic concentration is demonstrated by two verses.

body.translated_text: Now, in order to show that one should not be attached even to that <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge ultimately, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body)

body.text: tatra pūrvagāthayā kathaṃ tathāgato na draṣṭavyaḥ, kaiśca na dṛśyata etannirdiṣṭam | kathaṃ na draṣṭavya iti cet? darśanādivyavahāraprajñaptyā | ke na paśyantīti cet? mithyāprahāṇaprasṛtāḥ | rūpeṇa cādrākṣuḥ ityanena rūpe 'bhiniviṣṭāḥ pudgalāḥ pāramārthikalakṣaṇādibhiralaṅkṛtaṃ dharmarūpaṃ pudgalarūpaṃ ca paśyantīti vyavahāraprajñaptirnidiṣṭā | ghoṣeṇa cānvayuḥ iti māṃ śabdena evameva sa tathāgata iti jñātavanta ityarthaḥ | anena śravaṇavyavahāraprajñāptirnidiṣṭā | upalakṣaṇamātramimau vyavahārau | tena viśeṣabhedo vijñānaṃ cāpi saṃgṛhītam |
body.translated_text: Therein, by the first verse, how the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be seen, and by whom he is not seen — this is indicated. How should he not be seen? Through the conventional designation of seeing and so on. Who do not see [him]? Those who have set out upon the wrong path of abandonment. 'Through form...'

body.text: mithyāprahāṇaprasṛtāste janāḥ tāvad vitathāmārgasthitatvānna māṃ samyag rūpeṇa drakṣyanti | prahīyate 'neneti prahāṇaṃ mārga ityucyate, tacca viparītatvānmithyā | tadapyadarśanahetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Those people who have set out upon the wrong path of abandonment, because of being established on the false path, will not see me correctly through form. That by which one abandons is called 'abandonment' (<s>prahāṇa</s>), meaning the path; and that, being perverted, is wrong (<s>mithyā</s>). That too is a cause of non-seeing.

body.text: atha kathaṃ buddhā draṣṭavyā ityatra dharmataḥ ityādyāha | dharmāṇāṃ yo hyakṛtrimaḥ svabhāvaḥ, sa 'dharmatā'; ityucyate | sā ca yuktyāgamābhyāṃ siddhatvādāditaḥ śāntādisvabhāvā | saiva tathatā, dharmadhātuḥ, bhūtakoṭiḥ, animittaṃ paramārthaścetyādiparyāyairucyate |
body.translated_text: Then, how should the Buddhas be seen? To this he says 'through the <s>Dharma</s>-nature (<s>dharmatā</s>)' and so on. The uncreated intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> is called '<s>dharmatā</s>' (the nature of things). And that, being established through both reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>), is of a nature that is primordially peaceful and so on. That itself is suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), the <s>Dharma</s>...

body.text: sarvatra tathābhāvāt 'tathatā tadālambanena sarve buddhadharmāḥ sambhavanti | taddhetubhūtatvād 'dharmadhātu'; aviparītatvād bhūtaḥ, tatparyantatvād bhūtakoṭiḥ | (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_209

children.text: ) tatra nīlādisarvavastunimittānāmabhāvād animittaṃ | paramasya jñānasya gocaratvāt paramārthaḥ | kimiti sā dharmatayā draṣṭavyetyatrāha- dharmakāyāḥ iti | svabhāvārthaḥ kāyaśabda ucyate | tenāyamarthaḥ- samyagjñānanibandhanā ye tathāgateṣu vyavasthāpitāste paramārthato dharmasvabhāvāḥ | yo yatsvabhāvaḥ, sa tatsvabhāvena draṣṭavyaḥ, na tvanyasvabhāvena | yadyevaṃ tarhi dharmatā prakāśasvabhāvā bhavet, anyathā kathaṃ tallakṣitāste draṣṭuṃ śakyanta iti vicārya dharmatā ityādyāha |
children.translated_text: Therein, because of the absence of all signs (<s>nimitta</s>) such as blue and so on, [it is called] 'signless' (<s>animitta</s>). Because of being the domain of the supreme knowledge, [it is called] 'ultimate reality' (<s>paramārtha</s>). Why should [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] be seen through the <s>dharma</s>-nature? To this he says: '<s>dharmakāyas</s>' (truth-bodies). The word '<s>kāya</s>' (body) is said in the sense of 'intrinsic nature.' Thus the meaning is...

body.translated_text: Because of being thus everywhere, 'suchness' (<s>tathatā</s>) — from taking that as their object, all Buddha-qualities arise. Because of being their cause, [it is called] '<s>dharmadhātu</s>' (the element of <s>dharmas</s>). Because of being non-erroneous, [it is called] 'real' (<s>bhūta</s>). Because of being its ultimate point, [it is called] 'the limit of reality' (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>).

body.text: kimaśakyatvād aparijñeyā athavā parijñāne doṣasadbhāvāditi vicintya na śakyā ityādyāha | dharmisvabhāve siddhe taddharmatā vijñātuṃ śakyate, yadā dharmisvabhāva eva kaścit paramārthato na siddhastadā kathaṃ sā dharmatāpi vijñātuṃ śakyate kevalayā svasantatyā | nāsti sā kevaletyabhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Is [the <s>dharma</s>-nature] unknowable because it is impossible, or is there a fault in knowing it? — Reflecting thus, he says 'it cannot be...' and so on. When the nature of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is established, then its <s>dharmatā</s> (nature) can be known. But when no intrinsic nature whatsoever of the property-bearer is established ultimately, then...

body.text: yadyevaṃ samyagjñānasvabhāvānāṃ buddhanāmapi dharmiṇāṃ paramārthato 'siddhatvānna syād darśanam, tatkathaṃ dharmatā draṣṭavyeti cet? naiṣa doṣaḥ | ye paramārthataḥ sarvadharmiṇo na paśyanti ta eva dharmatāṃ paśyanti | dharmatā tāvadanutpannasvabhāvā, sā kathaṃ tadviparītotpādagrahaṇena grāhyā, na hi ghaṭagrahaṇena tadanutpādagrahaṇam | anena tathāgato na rūpakāyena draṣṭavyaḥ, api tu dharmakāyena draṣṭavya ityetannirdiśyate |
body.translated_text: If it is so — since even the Buddhas, who have the nature of correct knowledge, as property-bearers are not established ultimately, there would be no seeing [of them]; how then can it be said that the <s>dharma</s>-nature should be seen? There is no fault here. Those who do not see any property-bearers whatsoever ultimately — they alone see the <s>dharma</s>-nature...

body.text: asatyapi tathāgatasya lakṣaṇasampatsvabhāvatve yujyata eva lakṣaṇasampaddhetukaṃ tathāgatasyānuttarasamyaksambodhilakṣaṇam, gaṇakaiḥ (lakṣaṇajñaiḥ) bodhisattvasya lakṣaṇasampadaṃ draṣṭvā bhagavān anuttarasamyaksambodhau vyākṛta iti (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_210

children.text: ) yeṣāṃ saṃśayaḥ, tatparihārārthaṃ tatkiṃ manyase subhūte ityādyāha | yadi lakṣaṇasampad anuttarasamyaksambodherhetuḥ syāt tadā cakravartino 'pi syādityabhiprāyaḥ | gaṇakaistāvat tathāvidhaṃ lakṣaṇamātraṃ draṣṭvā vyākṛtam, na tu hetumityadoṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the removal of the doubt of those [who wonder], he says 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>?' and so on. The intent is: if the possession of marks were the cause of unsurpassed perfect awakening, then even a wheel-turning king (<s>cakravartin</s>) would [attain it]. The physiognomists saw such marks...

body.translated_text: Even though the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s possession of marks (<s>lakṣaṇasampad</s>) has no intrinsic nature, it is indeed tenable that the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s characteristic of unsurpassed perfect awakening has the possession of marks as its cause. Physiognomists (<s>gaṇakas</s>), having seen the possession of marks of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, [predicted that] the <s>Bhagavān</s> would [attain] unsurpassed [awakening]...

body.text: anena cittapragrahītatvaṃ nirdiṣṭam | anena tāvat sakalena sthānena gāmbhīryaṃ darśitam | saṃvṛtau cāśeṣavastusvabhāvādhimagalakṣaṇasya tathāgatajñānasya nirdeśena āudāryamapi nirdiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: By this, the uplift of the mind is indicated. By this entire section, the profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>) has been shown. And by the indication of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge, which has the character of realizing the nature of all entities conventionally, the vastness (<s>audārya</s>) is also indicated.

body.text: 6. saṃsāre nirvāṇe cāpratiṣṭhānam : (a) nirvāṇe 'pratiṣṭhānam
body.translated_text: 6. Non-abiding in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>: (a) Non-abiding in <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: paramārthataḥ sarvadharmāṇāmabhāvād yadi sā dharmatā vijñātuṃ na śakyata iti cet tata ucchedavādī bhavān syāt | tataśca tathāgatasyāpyabhāvād apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇamapi na sidhyatīti yadāśaṅkitaṃ tadarthaṃ saṃsāranirvāṇayoḥ apratiṣṭhānamadhikṛtya subhūte ..... evaṃ ..... bodhisattvayānasamprasthitaiḥ ....... ityādyāha | na ca bhūtavināśo 'pi prajñaptaḥ, dharmatāyā yathāvadavabodhāt | ata eva coktam-
body.translated_text: If, because all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately non-existent, that <s>dharma</s>-nature cannot be known — then you would be an annihilationist (<s>ucchedavādin</s>). And since the <s>Tathāgata</s> too would be non-existent, non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>) also would not be established — to address what was thus apprehended...

children.translated_text: Nothing is to be removed from this, and nothing whatsoever is to be added.
Reality should be seen as it truly is; the seer of reality is liberated.

body.text: anāgate dharmavṛttipratibandhakatvena ucchedo 'pi na prajñaptaḥ, yathābhūtadharmatāyā deśanāt | sarve dharmo avicāraramaṇīyatayā yathābhūtaiḥ pratyayairutpadyamānā abhyupeyante, ato bhagavatā buddhena tathyasaṃvṛtisvabhāvāyāḥ māhākaruṇāyā nirmāṇādau adhipatitvamādāya punarvineyebhyo yathāvadupāyopadarśanena (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_211

children.text: ) niravacchinnasaṃsārapravāho 'bhyupeyate | anena bhagavato nirvāṇe 'pratiṣṭhitatvaṃ nirdiṣṭam | tathāvidhe bhagavatkāye chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti tadapi nirdiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: an uninterrupted flow of <s>saṃsāra</s> is accepted. By this, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s non-abiding in <s>nirvāṇa</s> is indicated. That one should abide in such a body of the <s>Bhagavān</s> through aspiration and vow — that too is indicated.

body.translated_text: Annihilation is also not designated as an obstruction to the continuation of <s>dharmas</s> in the future, because of the teaching of <s>dharmatā</s> as it truly is. All <s>dharmas</s>, being delightful without analysis (<s>avicāraramaṇīya</s>), are accepted as arising from causes as they truly are. Therefore, by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>...

body.text: (ba) saṃsāre 'pratiṣṭhānam :
body.translated_text: (b) Non-abiding in <s>saṃsāra</s>:

body.text: yadyevaṃ bhagavān saṃsārapravṛttimabhyupaiti, tadā saṃsartā eva bhavatīti vikalpya saṃsāre 'pratiṣṭhitatvaṃ darśayituṃ yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | nirātmakeṣu iti māyāvat paratantratvāt, na svata ātmabhāvaḥ, nityasya kramakramābhyāṃ hetorvirodhāt, ahetukasya akiñcitkaratvāt | svaparayornādhiṣṭhānamapi, adhiṣṭhāturevāsambhāvāt, tasmāt sarvadharmāste ubhayavidhāḥ nirātmakāḥ |
body.translated_text: If the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus accepts the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>, then he would simply be a transmigrator — having considered this, to show non-abiding in <s>saṃsāra</s>, he says 'And moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>...' and so on. 'In the selfless' — because of being other-dependent like an illusion, not...

body.text: yathoktam : "ātmā ātmeti bhikṣavo bālo 'śrutavān pṛthgjanaḥ prajñaptimanupatitaḥ, na tvatrātmā vā ātmīyaṃ vā |" anena sarvadharmeṣu pudgalanairātmkṣāntiḥ sandarśitā | anutpattikeṣu ityanena dharmanairātmakṣāntinirdiṣṭā |
body.translated_text: As has been said: 'Self, self — O monks, the foolish, untaught worldling (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) falls into [mere] designation. But there is no self or anything belonging to self herein.' By this, the patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) regarding the selflessness of persons in all <s>dharmas</s> is demonstrated. By 'in the unoriginated' (<s>anutpattikeṣu</s>), the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>...

body.text: yadi bhāvānāmutpādo bhaved, ahetuko vā bhavet, sahetuko vā | sahetuke 'pi nityahetuko vā anityahetuko veti vikaladvayam | tatra na tāvat (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_212

children.text: ) prathamo vikalpaḥ kādācitkatvapratīteḥ | nirapekṣasya sadasadavasthāsamatvena sarvatra nirviśiṣṭatvāt nityaṃ sattvamasattvaṃ vā syāt |
children.translated_text: the first alternative, because of the experience of occasionality (<s>kādācitkva</s>). Because for something independent (<s>nirapekṣa</s>), the states of existence and non-existence being equal, it would be indistinguishable everywhere — it would either permanently exist or permanently not exist.

body.translated_text: If the origination of entities were to exist, it would be either without a cause or with a cause. If with a cause, there is a further dilemma: from a permanent cause or from an impermanent cause. In that case, not

body.text: ataśca kādācitkatvasambhavād dvitīyo 'pi pakṣastāvanna yujyate | nityasya itaraiḥ sahakāribhistāvanna kaścit sāmarthyaviśeṣaḥ kriyate | kutracidapyanapekṣaḥ san kimiva krameṇa kāryamutpādayenna yugapaditi | kāraṇe 'vikāle na kādācitkakāryatirodhānaṃ yujyate | kathaṃ krameṇotpādaḥ syāditi |
body.translated_text: And therefore, because of the possibility of occasionality, the second alternative too is not tenable. For a permanent [cause], no special capacity is produced through cooperation with other auxiliary [conditions]. Being independent of anything whatsoever, why would it produce the effect gradually rather than all at once?

body.text: ye svahetuṃ bhāvānāṃ vadanti, te 'pyarthato 'bhāvādevabhyupagacchanti | svabhāve siddhe heturapi syānna tvasiddhe, sarvasāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇatvāttasya | svābhave siddhe tasyāhetukasiddhirevābhyupagatā syāt, taditarānyahetau cānabhīṣṭe kathaṃ na nirhetukaḥ syāt | na bhāvaḥ svabhāvād bhinnaḥ | ataḥ sidhyati tatsiddhe, (phalataḥ) ahetuka eva syāt | anyathā tatsiddhe 'pyasiddhatvāt kathaṃ tadabhinnasvabhāvatvam | tato yo 'hetuvādī pakṣo nirastaḥ, sa atrāpi tulyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Those who posit an intrinsic cause of entities also effectively accept [origination] from non-existence. If the intrinsic nature were established, there could be a cause; but not when it is unestablished, since [non-existence] has the characteristic of being devoid of all causal capacity. If the intrinsic nature is [already] established, then its establishment without a cause is effectively accepted...

body.text: na tāvad yujyate tṛtīyapakṣo 'pi samānāsamānakālayoḥ kāraṇatvavirodhāt | tathā hi, hetau sati sa phalena (kāryeṇa) samānakālo vā bhaved bhinnakālo vā? na tāvat samānakālāt, svayaprāptātmasvabhāvasya sarvasāmarthyaśūnyatvāt kutrāpi phale yogābhāvāt | ātmasvabhāve ca (prāpte) tatsvabhāvavat phalasyāpi tatsamānakālabhāvitayā ātmasvabhāvatvameva | na tatra phalaṃ yujyate |
body.translated_text: The third position is also not tenable, because of the contradiction of being a cause at both simultaneous and non-simultaneous times. For thus: given a cause, would it be simultaneous with the effect (result), or at a different time? Not from a simultaneous [cause], because that which has already attained its own essential nature is devoid of all capacity and has no connection with any effect whatsoever. And since [the effect], being simultaneous with that [cause], would have [already] attained its own nature just like the nature of that [cause], it would simply be of the nature of its own essence. [Therefore,] an effect is not tenable there.

body.text: bhinnakāle 'pi tāvat taditarakālavyavadhānena vā bhaved, yathāvaibhāṣikairvipākaheturiṣyate, tathā | athavā avyavadhānena vā bhaved, yathāsautrāntikaiḥ kāryakāraṇayorutpādavināśau 'tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavad'; ucyete tathā syāditi? tatra taditarakālavyavadhānena phalotpāde sati vināśādevotpādaḥ abhyupagamyeta, sarvasāmarthyavirahitatvāttasya vināśasya na yujyate hetubhāvatvam, anyathā akārakasya vinaṣṭavastuno vināśāt kathaṃ (utpādaḥ) bhavet |
body.translated_text: Even at a different time, would [the effect arise] with an intervening period of other time, as the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> maintain regarding the ripening cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>)? Or would it be without an interval, as the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> say of the arising and ceasing of cause and effect — 'like the rising and falling of the arms of a balance'? Regarding the first: if the effect arises with an intervening period of other time, its arising would have to be admitted as [coming] from cessation alone; since that cessation is devoid of all capacity, it is not tenable for it to have the status of a cause — otherwise, how could arising occur from the cessation of a defunct entity that has no causal power?

body.text: avyavadhāneneti pakṣe 'pi yadi sarvātmanā avyabahitastadā tadeva samakālatvaṃ syāt | niravayavayordvayorvastunoḥ sarvātmanā avyavahitatve ekakālatvātiriktā nānyā gatiḥ | tasmāt sarvātmanā avyavahite sati pūrvaṃ yathā aṇumātrakam (iti prasaktam), tathaiva kalpasyāpi kṣaṇamātrakatvaṃ durnivāram |
body.translated_text: In the position 'without an interval' as well: if [cause and effect are] completely without separation in every respect, then that would just be simultaneity. For two entities without parts that are entirely without separation — there is no other possibility beyond being at the same time. Therefore, when there is complete non-separation, just as was entailed earlier [that something would be reduced to] the size of an atom, so too it is impossible to prevent even an aeon from being reduced to a mere moment.

body.text: ekadeśena cāvyavahite sāvayavatvaṃ prasajyate, ataḥ paramārthataḥ sarve bhāvā anutpannā eva | avicāraramaṇīyā mithyātvenotpannā iva pratīyanta eva, yathā bhrāntijñāne pratibhāsasvabhāvāḥ | (yadi) na syāt prasiddhamātraṃ pramāṇaṃ (tadā) 'kāryakāraṇayorāgopālaṃ prasiddhatvānna yujyate vimarśaḥ iti vādaḥ kathaṃ yujyeta, prasiddhasya rūpādeḥ pramāṇataḥ viśīrṇatvāt | tasmāduktaṃ bhagavatā candrapradīpasūtre (samādhirājasūtram)-
body.translated_text: And if there is non-separation in only one part, then partedness (<s>sāvayavatva</s>) would follow. Therefore, ultimately all entities are simply unoriginated. [Yet they appear] as falsely originated, charming when unexamined, just like the appearance-nature in erroneous cognition. If mere commonplace [perception] were not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), then the statement 'because the cause and effect [relationship] is commonly known down to the cowherd, analysis is not appropriate' — how would that be tenable, since commonly perceived form and the like are dissolved by valid means of knowledge? Therefore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated in the <s>Candrapradīpasūtra</s> (<s>Samādhirājasūtra</s>):

children.text: na cakṣu pramāṇaṃ na śrotragrāṇaṃ na jihvā pramāṇaṃ na kāyacittam |
children.translated_text: The eye is not a valid means of knowledge, nor is the ear or nose; neither is the tongue a valid means of knowledge, nor are the body or mind.

children.text: pramāṇaṃ yadyeta bhaveyurindriyāḥ kasyāryamārgeṇa bhavet kāryam ||
children.translated_text: If these sense faculties (<s>indriya</s>) were valid means of knowledge, for whom would there be any purpose of the noble path?

children.text: yasmādime indriya apramāṇā jadā svabhāvena avyākṛtaśca |
children.translated_text: Since these sense faculties are not valid means of knowledge, insentient by nature and indeterminate,

children.text: tasmād ya nirvāṇapathaiva ārthikaḥ sa āryamārgeṇa karotu kāryam ||
children.translated_text: therefore, one who desires the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> should accomplish [that] purpose through the noble path.

body.text: yatpratyakṣalakṣaṇamāhurācāryāstacca pratyakṣaṃ saṃvṛtitaḥ, paramārthe 'vatāraṇāya draṣṭavyam | na ca saṃvṛtau na samānaparyanuyogaḥ, tatastasya saṃvṛtāvuktatvānna parīkṣaṇaṃ kṣamate | ato bhagavatā śālistambādiṣu bhāvānāṃ svaparodayo niṣiddhaḥ | tathoktam āryalaṅkāvatāre-
body.translated_text: What the masters describe as the characteristic of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — that too is direct perception from the standpoint of conventional [truth], and should be seen as an entry into the ultimate. Nor is the same counter-argument [valid] in conventional [truth], because since it is stated in conventional [truth], it does not bear examination. Therefore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has prohibited the self-origination and other-origination of entities in the <s>Śālistamba</s> [<s>Sūtra</s>] and elsewhere. Thus it is stated in the noble <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s> [<s>Sūtra</s>]:

body.text: "sadasatorutpattivirahitatvānmahāmate, sarvadharmā anutpannāḥ |"
body.translated_text: "Because of the absence of origination from existent and non-existent, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are unoriginated."

body.text: vistṛtaprajñāpāramitāsuṃ coktam- "subhūte, na kaścid dharma utpannaḥ, sā (api) anutpannā" tatra yā prajñā, sānutpattikadharmakṣāntirityucyate |
body.translated_text: And in the extensive <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [<s>Sūtras</s>] it is stated: "<s>Subhūti</s>, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever has originated; that [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] too is unoriginated." Therein, that wisdom which [realizes this] is called <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-origination of <s>dharmas</s>).

body.text: tathoktaṃ ratnākaranāma(mahāyāna) sūtre-
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Ratnākara</s> (<s>Mahāyāna</s>) <s>Sūtra</s>:

children.text: sva eva yadā nāsti paro hetuḥ kathaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: When the self itself does not exist, how could there be another cause?
How could there be origination from self-nature? The <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) has declared [there is none] from another.

body.text: api ca,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

body.text: bhāvā jāyanti saṃvṛtyā paramārthe 'svabhāvakāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmas</s> arise conventionally; ultimately they are without own-nature.

body.text: yadyetat sarvaṃ parikalpitasvabhāvamadhikṛtyoktamiti cet? na, sarvasvabhāvānāṃ pramāṇato nirākṛtatvāt | anenāparo 'lpakuśalamūlo 'pi (jano yadā) saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ nānubhavati, (tadā) anutpattikadharmakṣāntiprāptatvāt mahājñānālokodayā labdhānuttarapuṇyaskandhā bodhisattvāḥ kathaṃ saṃsāraduḥkham anubhaveyurityevamāveditam |
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] 'Is all this stated with reference to the imagined nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>) only?' — No, because all own-natures have been refuted by valid means of knowledge. By this, [the following is conveyed:] if even others with few roots of merit do not experience the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> when they have attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-origination of <s>dharmas</s>), then how would <s>bodhisattvas</s>, in whom the great light of knowledge has arisen and who have obtained unsurpassed accumulations of merit, experience the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>? — this is what is being communicated.

body.text: dvividho hi saṃsāraduḥkhasyānubhavaḥ- kāyiko daurmanasyalakṣaṇaśca | tatra pūrvakastu pāpakarmaṇaḥ phalam, aparastu mohajaḥ, viparyastajñānasambhūta eva | tatrānutpanneṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiprāptyā bodhisattveṣu nāstyubhayavidho duḥkhahetuḥ, pāpaṃ mohaśceti | akāraṇānna sambhavati duḥkhasparśavihāraḥ | anena kathaṃ bodhisattvena pratipattavyamiti deśitam |
body.translated_text: For the experience of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> is twofold: physical, and that characterized by mental distress (<s>daurmanasya</s>). Of these, the first is the fruit of sinful action; the second arises from delusion, produced from perverted knowledge. When <s>bodhisattvas</s> have attained patient acceptance of the non-origination of <s>dharmas</s>, neither type of cause of suffering exists — neither sin nor delusion. Without a cause, an abiding in the contact of suffering is impossible. By this, how the <s>bodhisattva</s> should practice has been taught.

body.text: utpāditabahutarapuṇyaskandhā rūpāvacarādisattvā iva kiṃ (te) saṃsāra eva na bhavanti? kathaṃ vā bahutarapuṇyaskandhotpādamātreṇa saṃsāre 'pratiṣṭhitatvaṃ sandarśitamityāśaṅkya punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: Having generated a greater accumulation of merit, would they not [still remain] in <s>saṃsāra</s>, like beings in the <s>rūpāvacara</s> (form realm) and the like? Or how is non-establishment in <s>saṃsāra</s> demonstrated merely by the generation of a greater accumulation of merit? — anticipating this objection, he again says '<s>Subhūti</s>' and so forth.

body.text: anena tāvad utpannapuṇyaskandhe 'pi teṣāṃ mithyābhiniveśena puṇyaskandhaparigrahasya sarvasaṃkleśamūlaviparyāsasyāprahīṇatvam, ataḥ (te) viśiṣṭagatiṃ prāptā api saṃsāre vyavasthāpyante, bodhisattvānāṃ tu anutpattikadharmakṣāntiprāpteḥ puṇyaskandheṣu nāsti satyābhiniveśaḥ, atasteṣāṃ sarvasaṃkleśamūlasaṃmohasya prahīṇatvānna saṃsāre 'vasthānabhityevaṃ nirdiśyate | paravikalpanirākaraṇārthamāryasubhūtiraviditābhiprāya iva nanu parigrahītavyaḥ iti viparītamabhyadhāt |
body.translated_text: By this, [the following is shown:] even when a <s>puṇyaskandha</s> (accumulation of merit) has been generated, because of their false clinging to it, the <s>viparyāsa</s> (perversion) that is the root of all affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) — the grasping of the accumulation of merit — has not been abandoned; therefore, even having attained distinguished destinies, they are established in <s>saṃsāra</s>. But for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, because they have attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-origination of <s>dharmas</s>), there is no clinging to reality regarding the accumulations of merit; therefore, because the delusion that is the root of all affliction has been abandoned for them, 'there is no abiding in <s>saṃsāra</s>' — thus it is taught. For the purpose of refuting the conceptualization of others, the noble <s>Subhūti</s>, as if not knowing the intent, stated the contrary: 'it should surely be received.'

body.text: tadayamāśayaḥ- tattatsūtreṣu bhagavatā 'bodhisattvaḥ puṇyaskandhaṃ parigṛhṇāti'; ityuktam | atra na parigrahītavyaḥ iti vacanena kathaṃ na virodha iti? bhagavānapi yenābhiprāyeṇoktavān tadubhayamapi darśayitumāha- parigrahītavyaḥ iti | parigrahīta iti yadāha tattu parigrahalakṣaṇanaya upasaṃhāralakṣaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: The intent is this: in various <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated 'the <s>bodhisattva</s> receives the accumulation of merit.' Here, by the statement 'it should not be received,' how is there no contradiction? The <s>Bhagavān</s> too, in order to show both [aspects] and the intent with which he spoke, says 'it should be received.' When he says 'received,' that is by the method of the characteristic of reception, [meaning] having the characteristic of gathering.

body.text: viparītagrāhakalakṣaṇanirākaraṇena nātra virodhaḥ | vitathamārgagrāhakatvaṃ viparitagrahaṇamityanena tadvikalpaprahaṇāccittapragrahaṇaṃ darśitam | yaśca khalu- (

children.translated_text: <s>Vajraṭ</s>_216

children.text: ) punaḥ subhūte, kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prārabhya audāryamuktam, avaśiṣṭapūrvabhāgairgāmbhīryaṃ nirdiṣṭam | etena sakalena sthānena śāśvatocchedāntaṃ parihṛtya madhyamamārgo deśitaḥ, nirdiṣṭaṃ ca saṃsāre nirvāṇe cāpratiṣṭhitatvam |
children.translated_text: Again, '<s>Subhūti</s>, [if] a son or daughter of noble family...' — beginning with this, the nobility [of the teaching] has been stated; through the remaining preceding portions, the profundity has been taught. By this entire section, having avoided the extremes of eternalism and nihilism (<s>śāśvatocchedānta</s>), the middle path (<s>madhyamamārga</s>) has been taught, and non-establishment in both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been indicated.

body.translated_text: Through the refutation of the characteristic of perverted grasping, there is no contradiction here. Perverted grasping means grasping of the false path — by this, through the abandonment of that conceptual construction, the taking hold of the mind (<s>cittapragrahaṇa</s>) has been demonstrated. And indeed —

body.text: 7. prasthiti-pariśuddhiḥ
body.translated_text: 7. Purity of conduct (<s>prasthitipariśuddhi</s>)

body.text: prasthitiḥ pariśuddhirucyate | trividhastasyāḥ prabhedaḥ- 1. īryāpathena prasthitiḥ, 2. sattvabhājanalokādhipatyena prasthitiḥ, 3. asaṃkleśena prasthitiśca |
body.translated_text: Conduct (<s>prasthiti</s>) is called 'purity.' Its division is threefold: 1. Conduct through deportment (<s>īryāpatha</s>), 2. Conduct through mastery over the worlds of beings and environment (<s>sattvabhājanāloka</s>), and 3. Conduct through non-affliction (<s>asaṃkleśa</s>).

body.text: 1. īryāpathena prasthitiḥ
body.translated_text: 1. Conduct through deportment (<s>īryāpathena prasthiti</s>)

body.text: tatra yadi buddho draṣṭavyo dharmakāyena, na tu rūpakāyena, tadā bhagavataścaturīryāpathena janmābhiniṣkramaṇādinā cāgamaprasiddhena kathaṃ na virodha iti yo manyate tadarthaṃ prasthānasampada īryāpathena prasthitimadhikṛtya api tu khalu punaḥ subhūte yaḥ kaścid ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: If the <s>Buddha</s> should be seen through the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body) and not through the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body), then how is there no contradiction with the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s four modes of deportment (<s>caturīryāpatha</s>) — birth, renunciation, and so forth — which are well known from scripture? — for one who thinks thus, addressing the excellence of conduct, concerning conduct through deportment, he says 'but moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, whoever...' and so forth.

body.text: gacchati vā āgacchati vā ityetaddvayena caṅkramaṇam, tiṣṭhati ityādibhiḥ krameṇāvaśiṣṭā īryāpathā uktāḥ | īryāpathapirdeśastūpalakṣaṇamātram tena janmādīnāmapyatra nirdeśo draṣṭavyaḥ | bhagavata āgamena paridīpitānāmīryāpathādīnāṃ yaḥ samyaktayā śabdaśo 'bhiniveśastāsya viparītābhiniveśānna jānāti tathāgatena bhāṣitasyārtham |
body.translated_text: 'Goes or comes' — by these two, walking meditation (<s>caṅkramaṇa</s>) [is indicated]; by 'stands' and the rest, the remaining modes of deportment are stated in order. The mention of the modes of deportment is merely illustrative; by that, the indication of birth and the like should also be understood here. Whoever, regarding the modes of deportment and the like of the <s>Bhagavān</s> as illuminated by scripture, clings to the words literally with perverted attachment — he does not know the meaning of what was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: na ca bhagavān rūpakāyena prabhāvitaḥ, asau tu jñānapariśuddhaḥ, tasyāmūrtatvājjñānasya saṃvṛtāvapi gatyādayo na sambhavanti | gatyādayastu rūpaskandhasya sthānaviśeṣaprabhāvitatvāt | te ca bhagavato nirmāṇakāyamāśrityoktāḥ, na ca jñānakāyamāśritya, tatra saṃvṛtitaḥ paramārthato vā gatyādīnāmasambhavāt | tasmād evaṃvidhāyāṃ īryāpathaprasthitau bodhisattvena chandapraṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti sandarśitam |
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bhagavān</s> is not manifested through the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body); rather, he is purified through knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). Since that knowledge is immaterial (<s>amūrta</s>), even in conventional [truth], going and the like are not possible [for it]. Going and the like, however, pertain to the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (form aggregate), being produced by particular locations. And those are stated with reference to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body), not with reference to the <s>jñānakāya</s> (knowledge body), since going and the like are impossible there, whether conventionally or ultimately. Therefore, it has been demonstrated that the <s>bodhisattva</s> should abide through desire (<s>chanda</s>) and aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) in such conduct through deportment.

body.text: yadi tathāgate gatyādayo na saṃvidyante (tarhi) kathaṃ tathāgataḥ iti gatyā prabhāvita ivocyata iti cittāśayaṃ vitarkyāha- tatkasya hetoḥ? iti | na me sa bhāṣitasyārthamājānāti ityanena yojanīyam | atrottarārthaṃ tathāgataḥ ityādyāha |
body.translated_text: If going and the like are not found in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, then how is [the title] '<s>Tathāgata</s>' spoken as if characterized by going (<s>gati</s>)? — pondering this mental question, he asks 'for what reason?' This should be construed with 'he does not know the meaning of what I have spoken.' Here, for the purpose of answering, he says '<s>Tathāgata</s>' and so forth.

body.text: evamabhipreyate- vyapadeśo 'yaṃ na gatyā prabhāvitaḥ, api tu adhigamena prabhāvitaḥ gataḥ ityasyādhigatyarthatvāt | vastutattvaṃ yathāsthitiḥ, tathaivādhigamyate, adhigatatvāt tathāgataḥ | athavā pūrvakairbuddhairyathā vastutattvamadhigatamaviparyayeṇa tathaivānenāpyadhigatamityadhigatatvāt tathāgataḥ | sa ca tathyasaṃvṛtau jñānakāyatvena yujyate, na cānyatrāvikalpitatvāt | tacca gamanādi kvacit saṃvṛtāvapi na sambhavati, amūrtatvāt | paramārthe tu na sambhavatitarām, anutpannatvāt | tataḥ sa vastusvabhāvādhigatyā samastalokasya jyeṣṭhatvāt pūjanīyatvāt arhan ityucyate, samyagavabuddhatvāt samyaksambuddhaḥ ityucyate, anyathātvena jaḍasvabhāvena rūpakāyastu tathā nocyata iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The intent is this: this designation is not made effective by going, but rather is made effective by realization, since "gone" (<s>gata</s>) has the sense of "realized" (<s>adhigatya</s>). The true nature of reality as it abides is realized just as it is; because of having realized, [he is called] <s>Tathāgata</s>. Alternatively, just as the true nature of reality was realized without error by the previous <s>Buddhas</s>, so too it has been realized by this one as well—because of having realized in that way, [he is called] <s>Tathāgata</s>. And that [designation] is appropriate in authentic conventional [truth] as the knowledge-body (<s>jñānakāya</s>), and not elsewhere, because it is non-conceptual. And that going and the like is not possible anywhere, even in conventional [truth], because [the knowledge-body] is formless (<s>amūrta</s>). Ultimately, it is even less possible, because it is unoriginated. Therefore, because he is the most venerable in the entire world through his realization of the true nature of reality, he is called <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One); because he has correctly awakened, he is called <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One). The form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>), however, being of a different nature—inert—is not so called; that is the purport.

body.text: anena yogasamāpattiḥ cittapragrahaśca sandarśitaḥ | anena tāvat sakalasthānena gāmbhīryaṃ nirdiṣṭam | saṃvṛtau tathāgatasya nirmāṇakāyamāśritya anantalokadhātuṣu apratihatagamanādipradarśanena ādāryamapi pradarśitam |
body.translated_text: By this, <s>yogasamāpatti</s> (meditative attainment) and the uplift of the mind (<s>cittapragraha</s>) have been demonstrated. By this entire station, profundity has been indicated. By showing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s unobstructed going and the like in infinite world-realms, based on the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s emanation-body (<s>nirmāṇakāya</s>) in conventional [truth], the nobility has also been demonstrated.

body.text: 2. (a) bhājanalokādhipatyena prasthitiḥ
body.translated_text: 2. (a) The setting-forth through mastery over the vessel-world

body.text: yastathāgatasya nirmitarūpakāyaḥ, yaśca manomayakāyaḥ, tasyāpi ekānekasvabhāvavisaṃyogānmāyānirmitabuddhavat mṛṣātvaṃ darśayituṃ bhājanasattvalokabhāvavigamāt prasthitimadhikṛtya yaśca khalu punaḥ subhūte ityādyāha | pūrvaṃ tvadhimukticaryābhūmau bodhisattvasyābhāvo darśitaḥ, samprati buddhabhūmau bhagavataḥ prasthitidarśanānna punaruktiḥ |
body.translated_text: In order to show the falsity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s emanated form-body (<s>nirmitarūpakāya</s>) and mind-made body (<s>manomayakāya</s>)—like a magically created <s>Buddha</s>—through the separation from one-and-many nature, addressing the setting-forth through the non-existence of the vessel-world and sentient-being world, he says "And moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>" and so forth. Previously, the non-existence of the <s>bodhisattva</s> was shown on the ground of the practice of conviction (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>); now, since the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s setting-forth is shown on the <s>Buddha</s>-ground, there is no repetition.

body.text: atra punadvividhenopāyena ekānekasvabhāvaviyogāvabodhānnairātmyaṃ darśitam | tadyathāpi nāma maṣiṃ kuryāt....... paramāṇusañcayaḥ ityanena ekānekasvabhāvaviyogāvagamena tanukaraṇopāyo darśitaḥ | atrāpi pūrvavad vyākhyānaṃ (veditavyam) | nanu digbhāgabhedena paramāṇavo 'siddhā (tadā) kathaṃ te sañcitāḥ? iti sañcintya tatkasya hetoḥ? ityāśaṅkyottaramāha (pariharannāha) saced bhagavan iti vijñaya ekatvagrāhakanivṛttyupāyārthameva paramāṇuprabhedena (yaḥ) sañcayaḥ sa ukto na tu paramārthato 'navasthitatvāt, anyathā paramāṇusañcayaḥ sarvatra pratyakṣatvena prasiddhyeta | tasmāt na bhagavānavakṣyat paramāṇusañcaya iti abhāṣite 'pyevamākhyātatvāt | anena tathāgatasya rūpābhāvatvena tādṛśyāṃ sthitau chanda-praṇidhānābhyāṃ sthātavyamiti deśitam |
body.translated_text: Here again, the selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) is shown through the twofold method of comprehending the separation from one-and-many nature. "Just as one might make ink... the aggregation of atoms"—by this, the method of attenuation through the comprehension of the separation from one-and-many nature is shown. Here too, the explanation should be understood as before. Now, since atoms are unestablished through the division of directional parts, how are they aggregated? Reflecting thus and anticipating the objection "For what reason?", he gives the answer: "If, <s>Bhagavān</s>"—understanding that the division into atoms was stated solely for the purpose of removing the method of grasping at oneness, not ultimately, since [atoms] are not fixed; otherwise, the aggregation of atoms would be established everywhere as directly perceptible. Therefore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not have said "aggregation of atoms"—even though it was not stated, it is thus explained. By this, it is taught that since the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s form is non-existent, one should abide in such a state through aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and resolve (<s>praṇidhāna</s>).

body.text: yadi na syāt sañcayaḥ (tadā) api nu bahuḥ sa paramāṇusañcayo bhavet? iti kasmād bhagavānavakṣyadityāśayaṃ viditvā tatkasya hetoḥ? ityāha | asañcayaḥ saḥ iti pūrvottarādidigbhāgabhedena avasthitānāṃ teṣāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ svabhāvenāsiddhatvānna yujyate tattvataḥ sañcayaḥ | ekatvagrāhanirākaraṇāyaiva (

children.translated_text: [<s>Vajraṭ</s> 219]
It was spoken; therefore it is called "aggregation of atoms."

body.translated_text: If there were no aggregation, then why would the <s>Bhagavān</s> say "Would that aggregation of atoms be much?"—knowing this intent, he says "For what reason?" "That is non-aggregation" means: since those atoms, established in the division of directional parts such as east, west, and the like, are not established in their own nature, aggregation is not proper in reality. Solely for the refutation of the grasping at oneness

body.text: asati ca digbhāgabhede paramāṇavaḥ paramāṇvantaraiḥ pūrvāparordhvādhodigbhāgabhedena parivṛtā na syuḥ, tato na bhavedupacayaścittacaittādivat | bhāga eva bhavati paramāṇurityapi kathanaṃ na yujyate, tatrāpi tarkasāmyāt | evaṃbhūteniṣṭhito 'pi na yujyate | aniṣṭhitāḥ paramāṇavaḥ svabhāvena tarhi tvayā kiṃ sādhyate? aniṣṭhitasvabhāve bhāvo na sidhyati, tataḥ siddhamasmākaṃ matamiti | anekasvabhāvatvamaṇūnāṃ yadṛcchayāpi nocyate, (tadā) aniṣṭhite paramāṇau (anekasvabhāvatvaṃ) kathamupapadyeteti mayoktam | ye paramāṇavastvayā niravayavatvena vyavasthāpyante teṣāṃ pūrvottarādidigbhedābhyupetatvāt digbhāgabhedenābhyupagamyante, tena sāvayavāḥ [te] prasajyante | tataḥ prasaṅgasiddho hetorāśrayāsiddhiḥ, na ca kevalaṃ cittacaitasikābhyāmanaikāntikāḥ, amūrtatvātte na dikṣvavasthitāḥ, pūrvottarādidigbhirapi nāvatiṣṭhante |
body.translated_text: And if the division of directional parts did not exist, the atoms would not be surrounded by other atoms in the divisions of east, west, above, below, and the like; therefore, there would be no accumulation, like mind and mental factors. To say that "the atom is simply a part" is also not proper, because the same reasoning applies there too. Even if it were established in such a manner, it is not proper.
